sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: What must Tennessee drivers under eighteen complete before holding a full, unrestricted license?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Tennessee requires drivers under eighteen to build driving experience through graduated steps before they can hold a full, unrestricted license.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: What are the four stages of Tennessee's graduated licensing program in order?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: The four steps of the Graduated Driver License program are the Learner Permit, the Intermediate Restricted License, the Intermediate Unrestricted License and the Regular Driver License.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: Where on the card is the three-letter graduated program code printed during the first three stages?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.memory_hook: Printed in the bottom left corner
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: A license issued at any of the first three GDL steps shows GDL printed in its bottom left corner.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: Which two graduated stages include a separate Restriction Card to carry, and what information does it show?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.memory_hook: Lists current limits and advancement steps
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: Learner permit and Intermediate Restricted holders each receive a Restriction Card to carry, explaining their limits and what is needed to advance to the next level.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: What minimum age and two exam steps are required to get a Tennessee learner permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.memory_hook: Age fifteen plus written and vision
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: A learner permit requires being fifteen and passing the standard written exams and the vision screening.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: How many days must a teen hold the learner permit before advancing to an Intermediate Restricted License?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.memory_hook: Hold permit one hundred eighty days
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: A teen must hold the learner permit for one hundred eighty days before moving up to the Intermediate Restricted License.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: Who must ride with a learner permit driver, and where in the car must they sit?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.memory_hook: Licensed adult twenty-one in front seat
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: A permit holder may drive only when a licensed driver aged twenty-one or older rides in the front seat.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: Between which nighttime and early-morning hours is a learner permit holder barred from driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.memory_hook: No driving ten night to six
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: A permit holder may not drive between ten p.m. and six a.m.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: How does reaching six or more record points affect a teen's learner permit wait?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.memory_hook: Stay under six for one-eighty days
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: A learner permit holder whose record reaches six or more points must keep the permit until the record stays under six points for one hundred eighty consecutive days.

sec03-card-sec03-R16.front: How many months does a teen learner permit last, and what fee applies under age eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-R16.memory_hook: Twelve months for ten dollars fifty
sec03-card-sec03-R16.expected_back: The GDL review table shows a learner permit issued for twelve months, with a fee of ten dollars and fifty cents for any applicant under eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: What minimum age and behind-the-wheel test are required for the Intermediate Restricted License?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.memory_hook: Turn sixteen and pass road test
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: The Intermediate Restricted License requires being sixteen and passing the driving skills test, also called the road test.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: How many total and nighttime practice hours must be certified for the Intermediate Restricted License, and who can sign?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.memory_hook: Fifty hours total, ten at night
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: For the Intermediate Restricted License, a parent, legal guardian or licensed driving instructor must certify fifty hours of driving practice, ten of them at night, on the Department's form SF-one thousand two hundred fifty-six.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: What license class and yellow top-bar wording appear on both intermediate teen cards?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.memory_hook: Class D with yellow Intermediate header
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: Both intermediate levels list the license class as Class D and display Intermediate Driver License in the yellow header bar on the front.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: What minimum age and time in the Restricted stage are needed to reach the Intermediate Unrestricted License?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.memory_hook: Age seventeen after one restricted year
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: Moving up to the Intermediate Unrestricted License requires being seventeen and having held the Intermediate Restricted License for one year.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: Which crash or seatbelt infractions block the Intermediate Unrestricted upgrade, and are new exams required?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.memory_hook: At-fault crash or two belt tickets
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: The Intermediate Unrestricted License is refused after an at-fault traffic accident or two safety belt violations, and it needs no additional tests.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: Why do holders of the Intermediate Unrestricted License stop receiving a separate restriction card?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.memory_hook: Zero driving restrictions mean no card
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: The Intermediate Unrestricted level carries no driving restrictions, so no restriction card is issued for it.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: What fee applies when moving from Intermediate Restricted to Intermediate Unrestricted after one year?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.memory_hook: Two-dollar application fee after one year
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: Moving from the Intermediate Restricted to the Intermediate Unrestricted License costs a two dollars application fee after the one-year minimum.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: Which three milestones unlock a regular Class D license, and which age marking still stays on the card?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.memory_hook: Eighteen or graduation; keeps under-twenty-one mark
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: A teen can get the regular Class D license at eighteen or on graduating high school or earning a GED, whichever comes first, and the license drops the word Intermediate but keeps its Under twenty-one markings.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: At age eighteen, what two choices does a driver have regarding the word Intermediate on their card?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.memory_hook: Pay eight dollars or wait renewal
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: At eighteen a driver may pay an eight dollars duplicate fee for a license without the word Intermediate, or keep the Intermediate license until the end of its five-year renewal cycle.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: In what orientation has Tennessee printed every license issued to drivers under twenty-one since July two thousand eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: Since July one, two thousand eighteen, every license issued to someone under twenty-one has been printed in a vertical format.

sec03-card-sec03-F39.front: Which three paths allow an emancipated sixteen-year-old to obtain a regular Class D license directly?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.memory_hook: Active military, marriage, or court emancipation
sec03-card-sec03-F39.expected_back: A sixteen-year-old emancipated by active-duty military service, marriage or court order may obtain a regular Class D license.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.front: How many passengers may an Intermediate Restricted teen carry, and which two exceptions allow more?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.memory_hook: One passenger unless adult or siblings
sec03-card-sec03-F35.expected_back: An Intermediate Restricted driver may carry only one other passenger, unless a passenger is twenty-one or older with a valid unrestricted license, or the passengers are siblings living in the same home and the driver carries a parent's letter for school trips.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.front: During what hours may an Intermediate Restricted teen not drive, and which four exceptions allow trips?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.memory_hook: Eleven night to six, four exceptions
sec03-card-sec03-F36.expected_back: An Intermediate Restricted driver may not drive from eleven p.m. to six a.m. unless with a parent or guardian, with a written-designated licensed driver twenty-one or older, going to or from a school event or work with written permission, or going hunting or fishing between four a.m. and six a.m. with a valid license.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: How does the nighttime curfew start hour change between a learner permit and an Intermediate Restricted License?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.memory_hook: Ten for permits, eleven for restricted
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: The two curfews differ: a learner permit holder under eighteen may not drive from ten p.m. to six a.m., while an Intermediate Restricted driver is barred from eleven p.m. to six a.m.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: How does the role of a twenty-one-year-old licensed driver differ between the permit stage and the Restricted stage?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.memory_hook: Supervises permits, unlocks extra restricted passengers
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: The age twenty-one shows up twice: a permit holder needs a licensed driver twenty-one or older in the front seat, while a restricted driver may carry extra passengers when one passenger is twenty-one or older with a valid unrestricted license.

sec03-card-sec03-F40.front: During the permit and intermediate stages, which ages require seat belts and which require child restraints?
sec03-card-sec03-F40.memory_hook: Belts four to seventeen, restraints younger
sec03-card-sec03-F40.expected_back: At the permit and both intermediate levels, seat belts are mandatory for every passenger aged four through seventeen, and a child under four must ride in a child restraint device.

sec03-card-sec03-R14.front: Which type of crash happens most often in work zones, and what two habits prevent it?
sec03-card-sec03-R14.memory_hook: Rear-end crashes dominate; slow, stop tailgating
sec03-card-sec03-R14.expected_back: Most work zone crashes are rear-end collisions, so teens are told not to tailgate and to slow to the posted work-zone limit.

sec03-card-sec03-R15.front: What four actions should every driver take when approaching and driving through a work zone?
sec03-card-sec03-R15.memory_hook: Headlights on, merge early, obey flaggers
sec03-card-sec03-R15.expected_back: In a work zone, merge early, obey the flaggers, avoid lane changes unless directed, and switch on headlights before entering.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.front: Roughly how many minor traffic tickets add up to six points on a teen's driving record?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.memory_hook: Two minor tickets equal six points
sec03-card-sec03-F38.expected_back: Six points on the record is roughly the same as two minor traffic citations.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: Which two serious offenses revoke an Intermediate Restricted License and drop a teen back to a permit until eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.memory_hook: Forged parent note or fatal crash
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: A forged letter of parental approval, or contributing to a fatal accident, revokes the Intermediate Restricted License and leaves the teen with only a learner permit until age eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.front: What penalty follows a conviction for carrying a forged or fraudulent parental permission letter?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.memory_hook: Revokes restricted license until age eighteen
sec03-card-sec03-F37.expected_back: Being convicted of carrying a forged or fraudulent permission letter revokes the Intermediate Restricted License and leaves only a learner permit until age eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: Which three setbacks add ninety days onto the one-year Intermediate Restricted requirement?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.memory_hook: Six points, crash, or second belt
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: On the Intermediate Restricted License, six or more points, contributing to an accident, or a second seatbelt conviction adds ninety days to the one-year minimum, for one year and three months in total.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: How does hitting six or more points punish a learner permit holder differently than an Intermediate Restricted driver?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.memory_hook: Permits restart one-eighty; restricted adds ninety
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: Points penalties depend on the level: on a learner permit, six or more points restart a wait of one hundred eighty consecutive clean days, while on the Intermediate Restricted License the same points add ninety days to the one-year minimum.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: What extra requirement applies when an Intermediate Restricted teen gets convicted of a second moving violation?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.memory_hook: Complete certified driver education before advancing
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: A second moving-violation conviction on the Intermediate Restricted License requires finishing a certified driver education course before advancing.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: What happens if a violation from your Restricted period hits state records after you already upgraded to Unrestricted?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.memory_hook: Drops back to Restricted ninety days
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: If a violation from the Intermediate Restricted period reaches the Department only after the Unrestricted license is issued, the teen drops back to Intermediate Restricted for ninety days.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.front: Which mobile phone uses are banned while driving with a Tennessee learner permit or intermediate license?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.memory_hook: Zero mobile or car phone use
sec03-card-sec03-F32.expected_back: Tennessee bans any learner permit or intermediate license holder from using a cell phone, whether handheld, car phone or other mobile phone, while driving on a Tennessee road.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.front: What four consequences hit a teen convicted of violating the graduated driver cell phone ban?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.memory_hook: Fifty fine, six points, ninety-day delay
sec03-card-sec03-F33.expected_back: A teen convicted under the cell phone ban faces a Class C misdemeanor, a fifty dollars fine, six points on the record and a ninety-day delay in Intermediate Restricted eligibility.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.front: Who is barred from texting while driving in Tennessee, and how much can the fine and court costs reach?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.memory_hook: Every driver; fifty fine, ten costs
sec03-card-sec03-F34.expected_back: Since July one, two thousand nine, texting while driving has been banned for all drivers, with a fine of no more than fifty dollars plus court costs of no more than ten dollars.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: Which credential can a fifteen-year-old newcomer with an out-of-state permit get, and what must happen before Restricted?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.memory_hook: Learner permit until sixteen and one-eighty
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: A fifteen-year-old new resident holding a valid permit from another state qualifies only for a Tennessee learner permit and must reach one hundred eighty total days on a permit and turn sixteen before the Intermediate Restricted License.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: How can a newcomer teen credit prior out-of-state permit days toward Tennessee's one-hundred-eighty-day rule?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.memory_hook: Bring certified record within thirty days
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: Time on the previous state's permit can count toward the one hundred eighty days if the teen shows a certified driving record issued within the thirty days before the Tennessee application.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: What happens if a newcomer teen's out-of-state driving history shows an accident or traffic violation?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.memory_hook: Hold permit pending Driver Improvement review
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: If the previous state's record shows any violation or accident, the teen keeps a Tennessee learner permit until the Driver Improvement Section confirms the record meets the less than six points rule.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: Which Tennessee stage does a sixteen-year-old apply for when holding a valid out-of-state license for at least ninety days?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.memory_hook: Ninety days qualifies for Intermediate Restricted
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: A sixteen-year-old holding a valid out-of-state license issued at least ninety days before applying applies for the Intermediate Restricted License.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: How can a teen whose out-of-state license is under ninety days old still qualify for Intermediate Restricted?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.memory_hook: Clean record with one-eighty combined days
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: A teen whose out-of-state license is less than ninety days old gets the Intermediate Restricted License only with a clear record showing at least one hundred eighty combined days on a permit or license.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: Does prior driving time in another state shorten Tennessee's one-year Intermediate Restricted requirement?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.memory_hook: Never; full Tennessee year still applies
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: However long a license was held in another state, the Tennessee Intermediate Restricted License must still be held one year before the Unrestricted level.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: Which adults are eligible to sign a minor's financial-responsibility teen affidavit?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.memory_hook: Same-address parent, guardian, or authorized grandparent
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: Allowed signers of the teen affidavit are a parent, foster parent or step-parent sharing the applicant's address, a legal guardian, or a grandparent whom one of those adults has authorized.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: How can a teen complete the financial-responsibility affidavit when the signing adult cannot visit the Driver Service Center?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.memory_hook: Sign beforehand before a notary public
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: If the adult cannot come to the Driver Service Center, the teen affidavit can be completed ahead of time and signed in front of a notary public.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: What extra notarized paper must a grandparent bring when signing financial responsibility for a teen?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.memory_hook: Notarized authorization from parent or guardian
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: A grandparent taking on financial responsibility must bring a notarized authorization signed by the parent, step-parent, custodian or guardian.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: What must a parent or guardian sign again if a minor adds another vehicle class such as a motorcycle?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: A minor adding another license class, such as a motorcycle, needs the parent or guardian to sign a second teenage affidavit for that class.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: How do high school graduates versus currently enrolled Tennessee students prove school compliance, and how long does the form last?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.memory_hook: Original diploma, or thirty-day school form
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: A graduate proves school status with an original diploma or GED certificate, while an enrolled Tennessee student brings an original SF1010 form that is valid for thirty days after the school signs it.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: Can a teen use grade cards or school transcripts to prove school attendance at the licensing counter?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.memory_hook: Report cards and transcripts never count
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: Grade cards and school transcripts are never accepted as proof of school attendance or progress.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.front: How long is a school attendance form honored over summer break when signed during the final thirty days of school?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.memory_hook: Valid thirty days into next schoolyear
sec03-card-sec03-R11.expected_back: Over the summer, an SF1010 signed within the last thirty days of the school year is honored until thirty days after the next school year begins.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.front: What school proof do students bring from out-of-state or private schools that do not carry standard Tennessee forms?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.memory_hook: Principal letterhead confirming student not truant
sec03-card-sec03-R12.expected_back: A student at an out-of-state school, or at an approved private or church school without SF1010 forms, brings a letter on official school letterhead from the principal or headmaster confirming the student is not truant.

sec03-card-sec03-R13.front: Which two items must a home-schooled teen bring to prove school compliance?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.memory_hook: Director's intent letter plus parent form
sec03-card-sec03-R13.expected_back: A home-schooled applicant brings a letter from the local director of schools confirming the annual notice of intent to home school, plus Form SF-one thousand one hundred ninety-three signed by a parent or guardian.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: How does losing and regaining driving privileges differ between a student's first dropout and a second dropout?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.memory_hook: First re-enrolls; second waits until eighteen
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: A student fifteen or older who drops out loses driving privileges; after the first dropout the privilege returns on going back to school, but after a second dropout the student must wait until eighteen to apply.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.front: How much extra must a teen pay to reinstate driving privileges after returning to school?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.memory_hook: Twenty-dollar reinstatement fee plus card fees
sec03-card-sec03-F31.expected_back: A student reinstated after returning to school pays a twenty dollars reinstatement fee on top of the application and license fees.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: Which three authorized people on the road outrank posted signs and traffic signals whenever their instructions differ?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: Directions from police, highway construction workers or school crossing guards must be obeyed even when they differ from what the signals and signs show.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: How can you still identify a stop sign even when snow, mud, or tree branches hide its lettering?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: Every sign's shape and color announce its purpose, so a stop sign hidden by dirt, branches or snow is still known by its red octagon.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: What types of traffic messages appear on rectangular signs?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: A rectangular sign carries laws, regulations or instructions such as speed limits or lane use.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: Which five specific signs or route shields are the ONLY ones that use a red background?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: Red is the background only for stop signs, the four-way or all-way plates beneath them, do not enter and wrong way signs, and interstate route markers.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: For what sole purpose are orange road-sign backgrounds reserved?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: Orange backgrounds are reserved for construction and maintenance signs and are used for nothing else.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: Match yellow, brown, green, and blue sign backgrounds to their four road jobs?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: Yellow is the background for general warning signs, brown marks recreational and cultural points of interest, green is for guide signs and mileposts, and blue is for motorist services.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: What high-visibility color marks school zone signs in Tennessee?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: Fluorescent yellow-green is the color for school zone signs.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: Where else besides schools do fluorescent yellow-green signs appear — and in what weather do they excel?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Fluorescent yellow-green signs also mark pedestrian areas such as crosswalks and are easier to see in low light, fog and rain.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: What kind of roadside situation does a fluorescent pink — or coral — sign warn you about?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: Fluorescent pink, sometimes called coral, marks temporary traffic control for incidents such as crashes, wildfires, floods and hazardous material spills.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: How do black and white share duties across regulatory signs and colored sign legends?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: Black is used for regulatory signs and for the message on white, yellow and orange signs, while white also serves as the lettering on brown, green, blue, black and red signs.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: When the Tennessee manual describes part of a sign as white, what reflective finish counts as white too?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: Wherever the manual says a sign is white, that includes silver reflective coating or material that reflects white light.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: Who do temporary traffic control zones protect around an incident — and which five devices guide lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: Temporary traffic control zones let traffic move safely past an incident while protecting drivers, responders and equipment, and may use message signs, warning lights, flags, barricades and cones.

sec07-card-sec07-R33.front: Which national standard governs Tennessee's road signs — and why might you spot two versions of a sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R33.expected_back: Tennessee's signs and markings follow the federal Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices, so drivers may see both old and new designs during updates.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: Which sign is the ONLY eight-sided shape on the road, and where must your wheels stop for it?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: The octagon is the only eight-sided sign, always red with white letters, and requires a complete stop without passing the crosswalk.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: After making your full stop at a stop sign, how should you proceed if hedges or parked cars hide cross traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: If you cannot see cross traffic after stopping at a stop sign, creep forward carefully to where you can see and go only when it is safe.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: What does a small red ALL WAY plaque mounted beneath a stop sign tell you?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: A red ALL WAY plate under a stop sign means every direction of traffic at that intersection must stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: How do you handle a triangular yield sign when the cross road is empty versus heavy with traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: At a triangular yield sign, slow down and stop for cross traffic coming from either side; with no cars coming you may enter carefully without a full stop, but always stop in heavy traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: What does a round yellow warning sign announce ahead, and how should you respond?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: The round railroad advance sign warns that a grade crossing is ahead, so slow down and be ready to stop if a train is coming.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: Why do drivers lose races against locomotives — and over how many crossing crashes happen yearly?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: Never try to beat a train, because drivers usually misjudge its speed, and the manual counts more than two hundred crashes a year at railroad crossings.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: What does the white X-shaped crossbuck pinpoint, and what does the small number plaque beneath it warn?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: The X-shaped crossbuck stands at every railroad grade crossing and marks exactly where the tracks are, with a small sign below showing how many tracks there are.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: What three rules apply whenever red lights flash on a railroad crossbuck?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: Flashing lights on a crossbuck mean a train is coming: stop, stay stopped until it passes, and make sure every track is clear before crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: At a gated railroad crossing, when must you stop and when may you finally pull forward?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Where a crossing has gates, stop when the lights start flashing and before the gate comes down, and wait until the gates rise and the lights stop.

sec07-card-sec07-R37.front: What does a large white X and the letters RR painted directly on the lane warn?
sec07-card-sec07-R37.expected_back: A white crossbuck with the letters RR painted on the pavement warns of many railroad crossings ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: What do diamond-shaped signs alert you to, and what speed response do they usually call for?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards or unexpected conditions ahead and usually call for slowing down.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: What does a black line diagram drawn like a tiny map on a yellow diamond sign show?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: A diamond warning sign drawn as a small road map shows the kind of intersection ahead, such as a crossroad.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: What recommended speed cutoff separates a sharp-angled Turn warning sign from a rounded Curve sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: The turn sign marks a turn with a recommended speed of thirty miles per hour or less, while the curve sign marks curves rated between thirty and fifty-five miles per hour

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: What road geometry and spacing distance trigger a Reverse Turn sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: A reverse turn sign marks two turns in opposite directions less than six hundred feet apart.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: What does the small square number plaque mounted beneath a curve or ramp warning sign tell you?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: A small advisory speed plate under a warning sign gives the recommended top safe speed for that hazard.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: Where should your eyes actually scan when you pass a Falling Rocks warning sign — and why?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: The falling rocks sign warns of rocks lying on the road rather than rocks falling on you, so watch the pavement, not the hillside.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.front: Why are Stop Ahead, Yield Ahead, and Signal Ahead diamonds posted — and when should braking start?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.expected_back: Stop-ahead and yield-ahead signs warn of a stop or yield sign you cannot yet see, and you should begin slowing when you pass them; a traffic-light symbol version warns of a signal ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.front: Contrast your action at a Lane Ends sign against your courtesy move at a Merging Traffic sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.expected_back: At a lane-ends sign, signal and merge into the remaining lane, and at a merging-traffic sign, check behind you and move over if you can to give merging drivers room.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.front: What traffic squeeze does a Narrow Bridge diamond prepare you for?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.expected_back: A narrow bridge sign warns that the bridge may force passing cars to slow down.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.front: Between which two points is the height on a Low Clearance sign measured?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.expected_back: A low clearance sign gives the height from the road surface to the bottom of the bridge or overpass ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.front: What must you prepare to do at a T-intersection sign, and what do roadside chevron arrows emphasize?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.expected_back: A T-intersection sign means you must turn right or left ahead and be prepared to yield, while chevron signs emphasize a sharp change in direction.

sec07-card-sec07-R23.front: What kinds of fixed hazards right beside the pavement edge do striped object markers highlight?
sec07-card-sec07-R23.expected_back: Object markers flag things just off the road edge, such as bridge ends and underpass supports.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: Which three types of speed information can regulatory speed signs display?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: Speed signs show the maximum allowed, the minimum required or a coming change in the limit.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: How does a timer-controlled school speed sign show its lower limit is active, and where is it placed?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: A school speed sign run by a time clock flashes yellow lights while lighting up the limit, and it is posted wherever children may be walking across the street to or from school.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: On a multi-lane two-way road, what does Keep Right require — and which two moves allow leaving the right lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: On a road with more than one lane each way, the keep-right sign means stay in the far right lane unless passing a slower car or turning left.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: What engineering measurement determines where no-passing zones go — and which four features hide oncoming cars?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: No-passing zones are set by how far ahead you can see, allowing for hidden hazards such as hills, curves, intersections and driveways.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: What unique shape, colors, and side of the road distinguish the No Passing Zone sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: The triangular No Passing Zone sign, yellow or orange, is placed on the left side of the road.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: What universal message does a red circle with a diagonal slash over a black symbol deliver?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: A red circle with a diagonal line on a white sign means the action pictured behind it is forbidden.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: Is standing in the roadway to solicit a ride legal in Tennessee?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: Standing in the roadway to ask for a ride is illegal in Tennessee.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: What two kinds of lane assignments can regulatory lane-control signs enforce?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: Some lane control signs require trucks to use certain lanes or tell each lane to go straight or turn left, and they are sometimes mounted overhead.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: Which two vehicle categories qualify to use lanes marked with a High Occupancy Vehicle sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: A High Occupancy Vehicle sign marks lanes reserved for buses and vehicles carrying at least the number of people shown.

sec07-card-sec07-R27.front: Which three credentials authorize parking in a space marked with the blue handicap symbol?
sec07-card-sec07-R27.expected_back: Parking spaces with the blue handicap symbol are reserved for vehicles with disabled veteran or handicapped plates or a special decal, and others may not use them.

sec07-card-sec07-R16.front: What shapes and print color do work-zone signs use, and which five hazards do they flag?
sec07-card-sec07-R16.expected_back: Work zone signs are usually orange diamonds or rectangles with black letters or symbols, warning of workers, lower speeds, detours, slow equipment and lane closures.

sec07-card-sec07-R17.front: What legal weight do the signals of a work-zone flagger holding a paddle or flag carry?
sec07-card-sec07-R17.expected_back: In a work area you must obey a person directing traffic with a sign or flag.

sec07-card-sec07-R18.front: What does a large flashing arrow panel ahead warn of, and when should you merge?
sec07-card-sec07-R18.expected_back: A flashing arrow panel warns of a lane closure, and you must start merging into the open lane well before reaching it.

sec07-card-sec07-R19.front: What tool do flaggers normally hold versus emergencies — and do their hand gestures change?
sec07-card-sec07-R19.expected_back: Flaggers usually hold a paddle reading stop on one side and slow on the other, switching to red flags in emergencies, and the stop and proceed hand motions are the same either way.

sec07-card-sec07-R20.front: How should you position your car, set speed, and treat lane changes while threaded among cones and drums?
sec07-card-sec07-R20.expected_back: Among barricades, panels, barriers, drums and cones, keep to the middle of your lane at the posted speed, and do not change lanes until you are fully past the work zone.

sec07-card-sec07-R21.front: Which two fluorescent vest colors help you spot officers, flaggers, and road crews in rain or dusk?
sec07-card-sec07-R21.expected_back: Officers, flaggers and other workers directing traffic wear fluorescent yellow-green, along with fluorescent orange for workers, so drivers can see them in poor light and bad weather.

sec07-card-sec07-R22.front: What emblem marks farm tractors, work rigs, and buggies — and how does it show day versus night?
sec07-card-sec07-R22.expected_back: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a fluorescent orange triangle, highly visible by day, seen on farm tractors, construction equipment and horse-drawn vehicles, and it glows in headlights at night.

sec07-card-sec07-R24.front: What colors form a U.S. highway route marker, and how far does a U.S. route extend?
sec07-card-sec07-R24.expected_back: A U.S. route sign shows black numbers on a white shield set on a black background, and a U.S. route continues into other states.

sec07-card-sec07-R25.front: What highway network do red-and-blue shield markers identify?
sec07-card-sec07-R25.expected_back: Blue and red interstate route markers identify the national system of interstate and defense highways.

sec07-card-sec07-R26.front: What happens if you stay in a lane beneath a yellow MUST EXIT or EXIT ONLY interstate sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R26.expected_back: On interstate guide signs the arrows point to the lane you need to enter or leave the highway, and when a guide sign carries the must-exit marking, every vehicle in the lanes under those arrows must exit.

sec07-card-sec07-R28.front: How close together stand Tennessee's urban interstate reference markers — and in which five cities?
sec07-card-sec07-R28.expected_back: Interstate reference markers stand every one thousand feet on busy stretches in Nashville, Knoxville, Memphis, Jackson and Chattanooga, showing route, direction and log mile in tenths so callers can give their exact location.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: From top to bottom on a vertical signal head, in what order do red, yellow, and green sit?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: Traffic lights run red, yellow and green from top to bottom, and the red light always means stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: Under what three conditions may you turn right at a steady red light in Tennessee?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: On a steady red, stop behind the crosswalk or stop line; unless a sign forbids it, you may then turn right once no pedestrians or cross traffic are present.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: What does a steady yellow traffic light mean — and when is continuing through allowed?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: A yellow light means red comes next: slow to a smooth stop if you safely can, never speed up to beat it, and if you are already in the intersection keep going carefully.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: For at least how many seconds must a yellow signal shine before turning red under Tennessee law?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: Tennessee law requires the yellow light to show for at least three seconds before the red.

sec07-card-sec07-R29.front: Which cross-street driver mistake makes flooring the gas on a late yellow especially deadly?
sec07-card-sec07-R29.expected_back: Drivers who rush a yellow light risk colliding with cross-street drivers who jump the green early.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: Even on a circular green light, which three groups still earn your yield?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: A green light lets you go only if the intersection is clear: yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in it, and to oncoming traffic when turning left.

sec07-card-sec07-R30.front: Why shouldn't you creep into a jammed intersection before your exit lane opens?
sec07-card-sec07-R30.expected_back: Do not pull into a busy intersection to turn until your path is clear, or you may be stranded inside it.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.front: What right does a green turn arrow grant — and what yield duty still remains?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.expected_back: With a green turn arrow you have the right-of-way to turn only that way, after yielding to anyone already in the intersection.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.front: What do a yellow turn arrow and a steady red turn arrow each require?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.expected_back: A yellow turn arrow means get ready to yield to oncoming traffic, and a red arrow or red light in your lane bans all turns even when other lanes have green.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.front: What must you yield to before turning left on a flashing yellow arrow?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.expected_back: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn left only after yielding to all oncoming traffic and to bicyclists and pedestrians in the crosswalk.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.front: Contrast a flashing red intersection beacon against a flashing yellow beacon?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.expected_back: A flashing red light is the same as a stop sign, and a flashing yellow light means slow down and go through carefully.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.front: How does Tennessee law require you to treat an intersection whose traffic lights are completely dark?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.expected_back: When a traffic signal is not working, Tennessee law treats the intersection as an all-way stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.front: When two vehicles halt simultaneously at an all-way stop, which driver yields?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.expected_back: When two or more vehicles stop at an all-way stop at the same moment, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.front: Besides people walking on foot, whom else does Tennessee law classify as a pedestrian?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.expected_back: Tennessee law defines a pedestrian as anyone on foot or using a motorized or non-motorized wheelchair.

sec07-card-sec07-R31.front: What should a pedestrian already mid-street do before DON'T WALK appears — and how are some WALK phases triggered?
sec07-card-sec07-R31.expected_back: A pedestrian who has started across on WALK should finish crossing as quickly as possible before DON'T WALK appears, and some signals need a push button to show WALK.

sec07-card-sec07-R32.front: On which two kinds of roadways do overhead lane-control signals appear most often?
sec07-card-sec07-R32.expected_back: Lane control signals over each lane are mostly used where traffic direction changes by time of day, and they also show whether toll plaza lanes are open.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.front: Which paint color belongs on your right versus your left — and what if yellow sits on your right?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.expected_back: A solid white line marks the right edge of your lane, and a yellow line marks the left edge of lanes going your direction, so yellow on your right and white on your left means you are going the wrong way.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.front: What fundamental traffic split do yellow pavement lines always indicate?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.expected_back: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.front: When may you cross a single broken yellow center line?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.expected_back: A broken yellow center line may be crossed to pass when no traffic is coming and it is safe.

sec07-card-sec07-F42.front: While passing across double solid yellow lines is banned, what turn across them stays legal when safe?
sec07-card-sec07-F42.expected_back: Double solid yellow lines may not be crossed to pass from either direction, though you may cross a solid yellow line to turn into a driveway or side road when safe.

sec07-card-sec07-F43.front: Along a paired solid-and-broken yellow center line, when may YOU pass — and when must you finish?
sec07-card-sec07-F43.expected_back: With one solid and one broken yellow line, you may pass only when the broken line is on your side, and you must be back in your lane before the passing zone ends.

sec07-card-sec07-F44.front: Contrast broken white, single solid white, and double solid white lines between same-way lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F44.expected_back: White lines separate lanes going the same way: a broken white line may be crossed when safe, a solid white line means stay in your lane, and a double solid white line must not be crossed.

sec07-card-sec07-R34.front: Besides dividing opposing traffic, what fixed travel-path hazards do yellow lines outline?
sec07-card-sec07-R34.expected_back: Yellow lines also outline hazards along the travel path, such as bridge supports.

sec07-card-sec07-F45.front: Which pedestrians at a corner earn your yield — even where zero white crosswalk stripes exist?
sec07-card-sec07-F45.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians who are in a crosswalk or about to enter it, and remember that not every crosswalk is marked.

sec07-card-sec07-F46.front: Rank the three exact stopping landmarks in order — stop line, crosswalk, or bare corner?
sec07-card-sec07-F46.expected_back: Stop behind a painted stop line; with no stop line, stop before the first crosswalk line, and with neither, stop before your front bumper crosses the cross street's edge line.

sec07-card-sec07-F47.front: Contrast a lane painted with a curved arrow plus ONLY against a lane showing combined straight-and-curved arrows?
sec07-card-sec07-F47.expected_back: A lane marked with a curved arrow and the word ONLY must turn that way, while a lane showing both curved and straight arrows may turn or go straight.

sec07-card-sec07-R36.front: What rule separates single-headed pavement arrows from double- or triple-headed pavement arrows?
sec07-card-sec07-R36.expected_back: Double or triple pavement arrows allow more than one movement, while a single arrow allows only the one direction shown.

sec07-card-sec07-R35.front: How are Tennessee HOV lanes marked on pavement or separated — and what two facts do roadside signs post?
sec07-card-sec07-R35.expected_back: HOV lanes are marked by a diamond in the center of the lane or set apart by a barrier, and signs give the minimum passengers and the hours the limit applies.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: What must you do if a traffic officer waves you through a red light or orders another normally illegal move?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: You must obey a traffic officer at all times, even when told to do something normally illegal, such as driving through a red light behind a funeral procession.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: Why is coasting downhill in neutral or holding the clutch pedal down illegal and unsafe?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: Never coast downhill in neutral, and in a manual car never coast with the clutch pressed, because both reduce your control.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: Which direction do you travel around Tennessee traffic circles, roundabouts, and town squares?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Tennessee drives on the right, so you go to the right around traffic circles, roundabouts and town squares.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: Between what evening and morning times does Tennessee law require your headlights to stay on?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Headlights must be on from thirty minutes after sunset until thirty minutes before sunrise.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: Besides nighttime hours, what visibility limit and weather condition require turning on your headlights?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: Headlights are also required whenever you cannot clearly see people or vehicles two hundred feet ahead, and whenever rain, mist or snow keeps your wipers running.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: Within what distance of an oncoming car or a vehicle ahead of you must you dim your high beams?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle comes within five hundred feet or when you are within five hundred feet behind another vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: Which lights are illegal to drive with by themselves in poor visibility or when high beams must be dimmed?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Driving with only parking lights on when visibility is limited is illegal, and so is using fog or auxiliary lights alone or when high beams must be dimmed.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: Although driving on parking lights alone is illegal, when are parking lights actually required?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: A vehicle stopped or parked on the road or shoulder must show parking lights when visibility is limited, even though driving on parking lights alone is illegal then.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: For standard vehicles in Tennessee, which two colors are legal for steady front-facing lights?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Since January one, two thousand eighteen, steady lights showing to the front of a vehicle must be white or amber, with exceptions for certain vehicles.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: For ordinary vehicles, what is the only flashing front-facing light setup allowed under Tennessee law?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: Also since January one, two thousand eighteen, no flashing front-facing lights are allowed other than factory emergency flashers, again with some vehicle exceptions.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: How must a truck or trailer carry loose material or trash that could blow or fall onto the road?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: Any vehicle carrying litter or loose material that could fall or blow onto the highway must keep it enclosed or fully covered by a tarp.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: What fine range and cleanup hours can a Tennessee court impose for highway littering?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: Littering fines run from fifty dollars to three thousand dollars by amount, plus up to forty hours of litter pickup and, if the court chooses, up to eight hours at a recycling center.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: What two passing or lane moves are forbidden around a funeral procession on a two-lane Tennessee road?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: On a two-lane road you may not pass a funeral procession, and you may not drive between its vehicles unless an officer directs you to.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: Even where no minimum speed sign is posted, when does driving slowly violate Tennessee law?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: Driving below a posted minimum speed in normal conditions is illegal, and even with no minimum posted you may not drive so slowly that you block traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: At what speed below the limit do you count as a slow-moving vehicle, and how many trailing cars require pulling off?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: You count as a slow-moving vehicle at ten miles per hour or more below the speed limit, and with five or more vehicles lined up behind you, you must pull off when safe.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: Under which three roadway conditions is driving below a posted minimum speed limit permitted?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: Driving below a posted minimum is allowed in bad weather, heavy traffic or on a bad road.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: Is Tennessee's Basic Speed Rule a statute or a safety principle, and can you violate it below the posted limit?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: The Basic Speed Rule is a safety principle rather than a Tennessee law: your speed must fit current conditions, and driving faster than conditions allow breaks the rule even below the posted limit.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: Under the Basic Speed Rule, how far ahead must you always be able to bring your vehicle to a stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: Under the Basic Speed Rule your speed must always let you stop within the clear distance you can see ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: Which roadway, environment, and personal factors shape your safe speed under the Basic Speed Rule?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: The Basic Speed Rule weighs traffic volume and speed, pedestrians, road surface, width and layout, visibility, weather and your own ability.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: If the driver ahead slams on the brakes and you rear-end them while driving under the speed limit, what does that prove?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: If the car ahead stops suddenly and you cannot avoid hitting it, you were breaking the Basic Speed Rule or following too closely, even within the limit.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.front: How does the manual compare the crash risk of overly slow drivers against speeders?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.expected_back: The manual says slow drivers are as likely to crash as speeders, so keep pace with traffic that is moving within the limit.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: When no other speed sign is posted, what is the default limit on primary and secondary Tennessee state and federal highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Unless another limit is posted, primary and secondary state and federal highways have a fifty-five miles per hour speed limit.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: What is Tennessee's maximum rural interstate speed limit compared with typical congested urban interstate stretches?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Tennessee's top interstate speed limit is seventy miles per hour, posted on most rural interstate sections, while congested urban interstates are typically fifty-five miles per hour

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: In normal uncongested flow, what are the minimum legal speeds in the far-left interstate lane versus the right lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Driving under fifty-five miles per hour in the far left lane of an interstate is illegal unless congestion prevents it, and the minimum in the right lanes is forty-five miles per hour

sec08-card-sec08-R13.front: What should you do if driving at the interstate's minimum speed feels too fast for you or your vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.expected_back: If the interstate minimum speed is too fast for you, take another road.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.front: Which three levels of government set speed limits on their respective roads, and what limits are common in neighborhoods?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.expected_back: The state, counties and cities each set speed limits on their own roads, and some residential streets are limited to twenty-five or thirty-five miles per hour at all times.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: How does Tennessee law classify speeding in a school zone, and how many points land on your record?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Speeding in a school zone is treated by law as reckless driving and adds an automatic six points to your record, which triggers an advisory letter.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.front: During which three student periods do reduced school-zone speed limits apply?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.expected_back: School zone limits apply while children are going to or from school and during recess.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: What minimum and maximum fine range does Tennessee law set for speeding through an active highway work zone?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: Tennessee law sets a fine of at least two hundred fifty dollars and up to five hundred dollars for speeding in an active work zone.

sec08-card-sec08-R16.front: Beyond highway paving, what roadside jobs count as work zones, and what visual cues mark them?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.expected_back: Work zones include utility work, tree trimming and surveying, and are marked by orange or yellow-green signs, flashing equipment lights and brightly dressed workers.

sec08-card-sec08-R17.front: How many deaths, injuries, and property-damage crashes did the manual report for Tennessee work zones in twenty twenty-one?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.expected_back: The manual reports that Tennessee work zone crashes in two thousand twenty-one killed twenty-six people, injured one thousand one hundred five and caused three thousand ten property damage cases.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: How should you apply the brakes in everyday driving, and what two hazards come from slamming them late?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: Brake early, slowly and evenly; braking too hard can make you skid, and sudden stops make it harder for drivers behind you to stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: In a vehicle without anti-lock brakes, how do you recover if your wheels lock into a skid?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: In a car without anti-lock brakes, if you start to skid, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction of the skid when it is safe to do so.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: How should you brake and steer during a sudden emergency stop in a vehicle equipped with anti-lock brakes?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: With anti-lock brakes, press firmly and steadily, never pump the pedal, and steer around hazards while keeping your foot on the brake until you stop.

sec08-card-sec08-R20.front: What pedal feel is normal when anti-lock brakes engage, and what mistake shuts the system off?
sec08-card-sec08-R20.expected_back: Noise and vibration in the pedal are normal when anti-lock brakes work, and lifting off or pumping the pedal disengages them.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: What is the difference between covering the brake and riding the brake, and which one is safe?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: Covering the brake, holding your foot just above it for a quick response, is a safe habit, but riding the brake, resting your foot on it, is not.

sec08-card-sec08-R21.front: Which two mechanical and traffic problems happen when you ride the brake pedal?
sec08-card-sec08-R21.expected_back: Riding the brake wears out the brakes and falsely tells drivers behind that you are about to stop.

sec08-card-sec08-R18.front: How many independent ways of applying the brakes must every legal passenger car have?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.expected_back: By law every car needs two separate ways of applying the brakes, usually the foot brake and a parking or emergency brake.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.front: Before downshifting to slow a manual-transmission car for a stop, what should you do for drivers behind you?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.expected_back: In a manual car you can slow for a stop by first flashing your brake lights to warn drivers behind, then shifting to a lower gear.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: What driving mistake causes most rear-end collisions and also shrinks your view ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: Most rear-end crashes are caused by tailgating, which also blocks your view of the road ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-R22.front: How does Tennessee statute define illegal tailgating?
sec08-card-sec08-R22.expected_back: Tennessee law forbids following another vehicle more closely than is reasonable for the speed, traffic and road conditions.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: How do you measure your following distance using Tennessee's two-second rule?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: Under the two-second rule, start counting as the car ahead passes a fixed point; if you reach that point before two seconds, you are following too closely.

sec08-card-sec08-R23.front: What should you do right after a fixed-point count shows you are under two seconds behind the car ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-R23.expected_back: If the two-second count shows you are too close, ease off and recheck at another fixed point until you are at least two seconds back.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: In which four driving situations should you double your following gap to at least four seconds?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: Increase your following distance to at least four seconds in bad weather, at night, at interstate speeds and when following a motorcycle.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: Which three sequential stages make up total stopping time, and how long is average reaction time?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Stopping takes three steps: perception time to recognize danger, reaction time to start braking, which averages about two-thirds of a second, and braking time.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: In the manual's seventy-mile-per-hour deer example, how far does the car travel before braking starts and before stopping completely?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: The manual's example shows that at seventy miles per hour a driver who spots a deer travels one hundred twenty-eight feet before braking and needs about four hundred eighteen feet in all to stop.

sec08-card-sec08-R24.front: Which five road and vehicle conditions change how many feet your car needs to stop?
sec08-card-sec08-R24.expected_back: Stopping distance depends on the pavement, tires, brakes, shock absorbers and the vehicle's weight when loaded or towing.

sec08-card-sec08-R25.front: According to the National Safety Council figure in the manual, about how many feet does a light car need to stop from fifty miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-R25.expected_back: The manual cites the National Safety Council: a light passenger car at fifty miles per hour can stop in about two hundred feet.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: In exact priority order, where must you bring your front bumper to a halt at a stop sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: At a stop sign you must stop at a marked stop line or before the nearest side of the crosswalk; with neither, stop where you can see cross traffic but before entering the intersection.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: How does Tennessee law define a stop, and does that apply before turning right on red?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: Tennessee law defines a stop as the complete end of all movement, and a right turn on red also requires a full stop first.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: What visual cue tells you that you left enough space when stopped behind another car in traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: When stopped behind another vehicle, leave enough room to see its rear tires touching the pavement, giving you space to steer around it if needed.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: What two consequences can rolling slowly through a stop sign cost a Tennessee driver or applicant?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: A rolling stop is illegal and is grounds both for a ticket and for failing the road test.

sec08-card-sec08-R26.front: After making your full legal stop, what should you do if bushes or parked cars block your view of cross traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-R26.expected_back: If you cannot see cross traffic after stopping, edge forward slowly until you can see both ways, and wait for anyone in the crosswalk to finish crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-R27.front: Once the car ahead of you stops at a stop sign and drives off, may you follow right through behind it?
sec08-card-sec08-R27.expected_back: After the car ahead clears the intersection, pull up to the stop line and come to a full stop again yourself.

sec08-card-sec08-R28.front: What physical sensation inside the car tells examiners and officers that your vehicle came to a complete stop?
sec08-card-sec08-R28.expected_back: Officers and instructors say a car has fully stopped only when you feel it lurch forward after all motion ends.

sec08-card-sec08-R29.front: How must you treat a stop paddle or hand signal from a construction flagger compared with a police officer?
sec08-card-sec08-R29.expected_back: You must stop completely when a flagger at a construction site or a police officer signals you to stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: How fast should you approach a railroad crossing, and when is it safe to drive across multiple tracks?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: Drive at a speed that lets you stop before the nearest rail, and do not cross until every track is clear of trains.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: Within what exact distance range from the nearest rail must you stop when a train approaches?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: When a train is approaching, stop between fifteen and fifty feet from the tracks, never on them, and wait until it has passed and crossing is safe.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: How far out must trains blow their horn, and which four crossing warnings forbid driving onto the tracks?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: Trains must sound their horn about one thousand five hundred feet before a crossing, and flashing lights, a lowered gate, a flagger or a visible train all mean you must not cross.

sec08-card-sec08-R30.front: Which four pavement markings appear ahead of railroad tracks, and how are rail-signal violations penalized?
sec08-card-sec08-R30.expected_back: Railroad crossing pavement markings include a large X, the letters RR, a no-passing stripe and a stop line, and breaking railroad signals carries the same penalties as other traffic devices.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: Which three groups of vehicles must stop at every railroad crossing even when no train or flashing light is present?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: School and church buses, taxis and other passenger carriers for hire, and vehicles carrying flammable, explosive or hazardous cargo must stop at every railroad crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-R31.front: How do buses and hazmat tankers signal behind them as they prepare for a mandatory railroad-crossing stop?
sec08-card-sec08-R31.expected_back: A bus about to stop at a railroad crossing pulls right with its stoplights on, and tankers required to stop usually turn on emergency flashers.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: When meeting or trailing a school or church bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, how long must you remain stopped?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: Meeting or following a school or church bus with red lights flashing and stop arm out, you must stop and stay stopped until the arm is withdrawn and the bus moves.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: What do flashing yellow lights on a school bus tell drivers, and how should you respond?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: Flashing yellow lights on a school bus mean it is about to stop to load or unload children, so slow down and get ready to stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: What criminal offense grade and fine range hit a driver who illegally passes a stopped school bus?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: Passing a stopped school bus is a Class A misdemeanor with a fine of two hundred fifty dollars to one thousand dollars.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.front: When may oncoming traffic keep moving cautiously past a stopped school bus, and how does a shared center turn lane count?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.expected_back: On a highway divided by a median or barrier, oncoming drivers need not stop for a school bus but must go carefully; a center turn lane is not a barrier, so traffic both ways must stop.

sec08-card-sec08-R32.front: Why is passing a stopped school bus on the right especially deadly, and what three cues allow proceeding?
sec08-card-sec08-R32.expected_back: Never pass a stopped school bus on the right, where children get on and off; stay stopped until it moves, its driver waves you on or its signals go off.

sec08-card-sec08-R33.front: Who must stop when a school bus halts right at an intersection to load or unload students?
sec08-card-sec08-R33.expected_back: When a school bus stops at an intersection to load or unload children, drivers coming from every direction must stop.

sec08-card-sec08-R45.front: How do stopping and passing rules for a public transit bus differ from a school bus?
sec08-card-sec08-R45.expected_back: Unlike a school bus, a transit bus stopped for passengers does not require you to stop and may be passed, but watch for riders crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.front: Where do more crashes happen than anywhere else, and what share of total and fatal crashes involve them?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.expected_back: More crashes happen at intersections than anywhere else, and the manual says intersections are involved in thirty-three percent of all crashes and twenty-one percent of fatal crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.front: What scanning sequence should you use before entering an intersection, and whom should you check twice for?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.expected_back: Use the left-right-left rule at intersections: look left, then right, then left again just before moving, and look twice for motorcycles, bicycles and pedestrians.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.front: Where should your speed be lowest at an intersection, and what lane and passing rules apply?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.expected_back: Slow before an intersection, be at your slowest just before entering, get into the correct lane beforehand, and never pass another vehicle inside an intersection.

sec08-card-sec08-F39.front: Is getting trapped inside an intersection after the light changes ever legal if no 'Do Not Block' sign is posted?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.expected_back: Blocking an intersection after the light changes is always illegal, whether or not a sign says so.

sec08-card-sec08-F40.front: Does Tennessee law ever grant a driver the right-of-way?
sec08-card-sec08-F40.expected_back: The law never gives anyone the right-of-way; it only says who must yield, and you must still do everything possible to avoid a crash.

sec08-card-sec08-F41.front: In a marked school zone with warning flashers blinking, what is your duty when a pedestrian enters any crosswalk?
sec08-card-sec08-F41.expected_back: In a marked school zone with warning flashers on, you must stop for a pedestrian crossing in any crosswalk and stay stopped until they are across.

sec08-card-sec08-F42.front: What cues identify blind or deaf pedestrians with service animals, and how far back must you stop without honking?
sec08-card-sec08-F42.expected_back: For a pedestrian with a white or red-tipped cane or a guide dog, or a deaf walker whose dog wears a blaze orange leash, stop at least ten feet away and do not honk.

sec08-card-sec08-R37.front: When must you yield to walkers on corners or sidewalks, and when is driving on a sidewalk legal?
sec08-card-sec08-R37.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians crossing with the light when you turn a corner and when you cross a sidewalk from a driveway, alley or lot; driving on a sidewalk is illegal except to cross it.

sec08-card-sec08-R38.front: In which three everyday areas must you slow down and watch with extreme caution for playing children?
sec08-card-sec08-R38.expected_back: Drive with extreme caution where children may be playing, and slow down near schools, playgrounds and residential areas.

sec08-card-sec08-F43.front: To whom must you yield when turning left at an intersection versus pulling out of an alley or driveway?
sec08-card-sec08-F43.expected_back: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right, and when entering from a driveway or alley, yield to all traffic on the main road.

sec08-card-sec08-R39.front: Alongside roundabouts, curb pull-outs, and highway merges, what unusual emergency-station move requires yielding?
sec08-card-sec08-R39.expected_back: Yield to traffic already in a roundabout, to moving traffic when leaving a parked position, to highway traffic when merging, and to an emergency vehicle backing into a fire station.

sec08-card-sec08-F44.front: Who goes first at an all-way stop, and what tie-breaker applies both there and at uncontrolled intersections?
sec08-card-sec08-F44.expected_back: At an all-way stop the first vehicle to arrive goes first, and if two arrive together, yield to the vehicle on your right; at an uncontrolled crossing, also yield to the vehicle on your right.

sec08-card-sec08-R40.front: Whom must you let clear even after your light turns green, and who yields at a T-intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-R40.expected_back: Yield to any vehicle already in the intersection even on your green, and on the dead-end road of a T intersection yield to traffic both ways on the main road.

sec08-card-sec08-F45.front: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with a siren, air horn, or flashing red or blue lights?
sec08-card-sec08-F45.expected_back: Pull to the right edge and stop for any emergency vehicle using a siren, air horn or red or blue flashing light, and stay stopped until it passes or an officer waves you on.

sec08-card-sec08-R41.front: May a private civilian vehicle carry or flash blue—or blue and red—emergency lights?
sec08-card-sec08-R41.expected_back: Private vehicles may not carry or show blue, or blue and red, flashing emergency lights unless authorized.

sec08-card-sec08-R42.front: Which three actions are illegal around a fire truck answering an alarm or working at a fire scene?
sec08-card-sec08-R42.expected_back: Never follow a fire truck answering an alarm, never drive within the block where it has stopped, and never run over a fire hose without permission from the officer in charge.

sec08-card-sec08-R43.front: What should you do for an approaching emergency vehicle if you are already inside an intersection versus stopped at a red light?
sec08-card-sec08-R43.expected_back: For an emergency vehicle, clear the intersection before pulling over, avoid blocking a side road, and at a red light stay put even if it turns green before the vehicle passes.

sec08-card-sec08-R34.front: Where should you position and stop your car when a police officer signals you with blue lights or a siren?
sec08-card-sec08-R34.expected_back: When a police car signals you with flashing blue or blue and red lights or a siren, pull over close to the right edge, clear of any intersection, and stop.

sec08-card-sec08-R35.front: Which five safety steps should you and your passengers follow during a Tennessee traffic stop?
sec08-card-sec08-R35.expected_back: During a traffic stop keep your hands on the wheel, keep passengers' hands visible, tell the officer if you hold a handgun permit and are armed, stay inside, and switch on the interior light after dark.

sec08-card-sec08-R36.front: Why should you skip roadside arguments with officers, and what may you do if an unmarked car flashes lights at you?
sec08-card-sec08-R36.expected_back: Do not argue with an officer at the scene, since violations are decided in court, and if an unmarked car signals you, you may drive slowly to a nearby populated spot before stopping.

sec08-card-sec08-R44.front: What must you do when a metro transit bus signals to pull back into traffic from a curbside stop?
sec08-card-sec08-R44.expected_back: Yield to a metro transit bus that has signaled and is pulling back into traffic from a bus stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F46.front: On multi-lane roads, what does Tennessee's Move Over Law require near stopped flashing emergency, utility, maintenance, or tow rigs?
sec08-card-sec08-F46.expected_back: Under the Move Over Law, on a road with two or more lanes your way, move out of the lane next to a stopped emergency, utility, road maintenance or tow vehicle with flashing lights, or slow to a safe speed.

sec08-card-sec08-R46.front: What road layout and vehicle location trigger the lane-change duty under this chapter's Move Over rule?
sec08-card-sec08-R46.expected_back: The Move Over requirement applies only on roads with two or more lanes in your direction when the stopped vehicle is on your side of the road.

sec08-card-sec08-R47.front: Which five bad habits does the manual call out as the most common turning faults?
sec08-card-sec08-R47.expected_back: The most common turning faults are not signaling, signaling too briefly, not searching for hazards, turning from the wrong lane and turning improperly.

sec08-card-sec08-R48.front: Which lane should you start and finish a turn in, and does turning on your blinker give you right-of-way?
sec08-card-sec08-R48.expected_back: Turn from the lane closest to your direction of turn into the closest legal lane, and remember that signaling never gives you the right-of-way.

sec08-card-sec08-R49.front: When do hand signals help most, when do they fall short, and where should your hand be mid-turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R49.expected_back: Hand signals help in bright sun or heavy traffic but are hard to see at night, and you should pull your arm in to steer during the turn.

sec08-card-sec08-R50.front: How can you alert trailing drivers before braking to a stop, and what must you verify after gentle turns?
sec08-card-sec08-R50.expected_back: Tap the brakes a few times to flash your brake lights before stopping, and cancel your turn signal afterward so it does not mislead others.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: Which two lettered sections of the Tennessee manual supply questions for both the learner permit test and the driver license test?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Sections B and C of the manual are the study material for both the learner permit test and the driver license test.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: Why can't reading the manual alone teach you to drive — and what two things actually build skill?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: The manual by itself cannot teach you to drive; driving skill comes from a good instructor and lots of practice.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: How are Tennessee's online practice tests organized, and which manual chapters feed the Guidelines for Driving test?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: The online practice tests are grouped by topic, and the Guidelines for Driving practice test matches Chapters B-one and B-two of the manual.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: Which four chapters feed Rules of the Road — and which single chapters match Signs and Alcohol?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: The Rules of the Road practice test spans four chapters (B-four, B-five, B-six and B-eight), while Traffic Signs and Signals maps to B-three alone and Alcohol, Other Drugs and Driving to B-seven.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: Before opening the driver's door, what should you walk around the vehicle looking for?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: Before getting in, walk around the vehicle and look for small children, pets or anything else in the way.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: Which five vehicle condition items — from glass to pavement drips — belong in your outside walk-around?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: The outside check also covers the windows, lights, body damage, tire condition and any sign of fluid leaking.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: Right after sitting down inside, what should you do with the key, the doors, and unfamiliar controls?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: After getting in, put the key in the ignition, lock the doors and learn where every switch, gauge and pedal is and what it does.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: Which eight everyday and emergency controls must you locate before you ever need them in traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: You should know where the horn, turn signals, four-way flashers, headlight and dimmer switch, wiper and washer controls, parking brake and release, climate and defroster controls and gearshift are even before you need them.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: Why must you never drive with your seat reclined or even partly reclined?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Never drive with the seat reclined or partly reclined, because it cuts your view and slows your reaction in an emergency.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: How should you set seat distance so your right foot moves smoothly between gas and brake?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Set the seat so the pedals are easy to reach and your foot can glide from accelerator to brake while your heel stays on the floor.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: What seating or steering-column mistake makes turning the wheel awkward?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Do not slide the seat so far forward, or pull the steering column out so far, that steering becomes awkward.
