sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: Through which glass panels and mirrors must a properly adjusted driver's seat give a clear view?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: Your seat position should give a clear view through the windshield, both side windows and every mirror.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: Roughly how many inches should separate your body from the steering wheel — and why does airbag aim matter?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Keep your body roughly ten to twelve inches from the steering wheel whether or not the car has an air bag, so a deploying air bag strikes your chest instead of your chin or face.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: Relative to your shoulders, how high may the top of the steering wheel sit?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: The top of the steering wheel should sit no higher than the tops of your shoulders.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: How high should you raise your head restraint, and what rear-impact injury does it prevent?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: Raise the head restraint until it is level with the back of your head, because it is there to prevent whiplash when you are struck from behind.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: At what exact point in cabin setup should you adjust all three rearview mirrors, and with what goal?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: Adjust all three rearview mirrors only after the seat is set, and always before you start driving, aiming for the widest view and the smallest blind spots.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: How should you aim the inside rearview mirror, and what tiny rear landmark shows at its edge?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: Set the inside mirror to frame the rear window, turned so that only the edge of the right rear window post shows.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: Where do you lean your head — and what shows at the inner mirror edge — when setting the left outside mirror?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: For the left mirror, rest your head against the driver's window and set the mirror until the side of your car just barely shows at its inner edge.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: Where do you hold your head — and what shows at the inner edge — when aiming the right outside mirror?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: For the right mirror, hold your head just above the center console and set it until the side of your car just barely shows at its inner edge.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: As an overtaking car exits your inside mirror on the left, what should appear simultaneously in your left outside mirror?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: To check the mirrors, let a car pass on your left: as it leaves the inside mirror, its front bumper should appear in the left outside mirror.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: If leaning slightly back still shows lots of your car's rear corners in the outside mirrors, how should you adjust them?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: If leaning back a little still shows you more than a glimpse of your car's rear corners in the outside mirrors, turn those mirrors outward.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: When your car lacks power or remote mirror switches, how can you aim the right-side mirror accurately?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: A car without remote mirror controls may need a helper to set the passenger-side mirror correctly.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: Where should you get comfortable with wide-angle mirror settings before merging into live traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: Try new mirror settings while parked, for example along a street watching passing cars, before driving into traffic with them.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: Even with wide-set mirrors, why must you still turn your head before turning or changing lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Even perfectly adjusted mirrors leave some blind spots, so always turn your head to check before turning or changing lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: How should your lap and shoulder belts fit, and who must be secured before you shift out of park?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: Wear the lap belt snug across your hips and the shoulder belt snug across your shoulder, and make sure every passenger is belted or in a child restraint before you drive.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: What legal consequence can follow failing to buckle yourself or secure passengers in required child seats?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: Failing to belt yourself or to secure passengers in a car seat or booster seat can bring a fine, and the passenger-protection chapter covers the full rules.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: Compare pedal and gear positions for starting an automatic car versus starting a manual-transmission car?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: To start most cars, keep your foot on the brake with an automatic in PARK or a manual in NEUTRAL; a manual car needs the parking brake set and the clutch pressed before it will start.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: When you turn the ignition to ON, which dashboard indicators should you scan for warnings?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: With the key turned to on, check the dashboard lights and gauges, such as the antilock brake, air bag and fuel indicators, for warnings.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: Besides night and storms, how much farther away do low-beam headlights make your vehicle visible in normal daylight?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: Use low-beam headlights especially at night or in bad weather; even in normal daylight, headlights make a vehicle visible from twice as far away.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: What do R, D, and O stand for on an automatic shifter — and where does overdrive belong?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: In an automatic car, R is reverse and D is drive, and some newer cars add an O overdrive setting meant for interstates with little stop-and-go traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: In which three tough driving situations should you select automatic lower gears marked L, two, or one?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: The lower gears marked L, two or one are for special cases such as steep mountain descents, slow driving on ice or slippery roads, and slowing down if the brakes fail.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: How can a manual transmission spare your brakes when descending a steep hill?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: A manual transmission lets the driver use gears instead of brakes to help slow the car, and you should shift to a lower gear going down steep hills.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: During which three driving moments — including what stopping speed — must you press a manual clutch all the way down?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: With a manual transmission, push the clutch all the way down when starting, when shifting and once your speed falls below ten miles per hour while stopping.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: What is Tennessee's law on coasting in neutral — and where shouldn't your left foot rest between shifts?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: Coasting with the gears in neutral is illegal, and you should not rest your foot on the clutch when you are not changing gears.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: Why must you NEVER turn the ignition key to LOCK while a vehicle is still moving?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: In a car with a steering wheel interlock, never turn the ignition to lock while moving, because the wheel will lock and you will lose control.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: How firmly should both hands hold the wheel, and which two casual arm habits should you avoid?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: Keep both hands on the wheel with a relaxed but firm grip, and do not prop your elbow on the door or hang your arm out the window.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: How should your elbows look when your palm reaches the top of the steering wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: Your elbows should bend slightly when your palm reaches the top of the wheel, and you should never sit with your arms locked straight.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: For which three column or dash controls will one hand briefly leave its normal steering spot?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: Your hand position will change briefly while you work the turn signal, headlight dimmer or wiper controls.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.front: Beyond losing steering leverage, what catastrophic injury risks hitting an arm hung out the window?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.expected_back: An arm resting on the door or out the window gives you less control of the wheel and could be severed in a sideswipe.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: Where should your central gaze aim while steering, and what job does your peripheral side vision perform?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: You steer with your eyes as well as your hands: look where you want to go, and let your side vision help hold your lane position.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.front: At which clock numbers do your left and right hands belong on the wheel — and why?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.expected_back: Picture the wheel as a clock and put your left hand at nine o'clock and your right at three o'clock, a position that helps avoid air bag injuries.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: Instead of letting the rim spin loose through your fingers after a turn, how should you straighten out?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: Coming out of a turn, reverse the hand movements instead of letting the wheel slide through your fingers; this counter-steering also helps in skids and on snow and ice.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: Why does the manual allow crossing your wrists slightly in a turn while banning crossing your arms?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: Crossing your wrists during a turn is fine, but crossing your arms is not, because clothing or jewelry can snag and an air bag would injure you more.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: Which steering technique does Tennessee recommend, and what two advantages set it apart?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: The push-pull method is the recommended way to steer because it slows the turn and keeps both hands on the wheel the whole time.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.front: To which clock numbers do your hands travel during a push-pull left turn versus a right turn?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.expected_back: In a push-pull left turn the left hand pulls down to about seven o'clock while the right pushes up to about one o'clock; a right turn mirrors this, with the right hand pulling to about five and the left pushing to about eleven.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.front: What happens to your hands during hand-over-hand steering, and how must you manage speed when using it?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.expected_back: Hand-over-hand steering turns the wheel faster but crosses the hands at the top and sometimes leaves only one hand on the wheel, so keep your speed down when using it.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.front: Where do you grip and pull the rim during a hand-over-hand right turn before returning to nine and three?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.expected_back: For a hand-over-hand right turn, reach forward to grip the rim at one o'clock palm down, pull to five o'clock, repeat with the other hand, and return to nine and three before counter-steering out.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.front: Which three mistakes trip up new drivers most often when reversing?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.expected_back: New drivers backing up most often go too fast, steer too much or turn the wheel the wrong way.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.front: Where do your left hand, right arm, and eyes go to reverse — and which way turns the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.expected_back: To back up, hold the wheel at twelve o'clock with your left hand, put your right arm over the seat back and look through the rear window, turning the wheel toward the side you want to move to.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.front: What speed and eye discipline belong throughout every backing maneuver?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.expected_back: While backing, keep to idle speed or gentle acceleration and keep looking to the rear until the car has fully stopped.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.front: How far ahead should you aim your eyes when pulling away from a stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.expected_back: When pulling away, look at least one block ahead and steer toward a reference point.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.front: Walk through your checks, signal, and pedal touch right before pulling forward from a curb?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.expected_back: Before pulling forward, check ahead, to the sides and behind, signal if leaving a curb, then move your foot to the accelerator and press gently.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.front: Which collision type tops Tennessee crash statistics every single year?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.expected_back: Tennessee reports rear-end collisions as the most common type of crash each year, which is why smooth, planned stops matter.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.front: Put the mirror check and three foot movements of a smooth stop in order?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.expected_back: For a smooth stop, check your mirrors, ease off the accelerator, move your foot to the brake and press with steady pressure rather than stomping.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.front: Where must your bumper stop at a stop sign or red signal — with markings versus without?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.expected_back: At a stop sign or signal, stop before the crosswalk or marked stop line; if there is neither, stop where you can see traffic on the cross road before entering the intersection.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.front: Within how many inches of the curb must you park in Tennessee?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.expected_back: When parking at a curb, pull within eighteen inches of it.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.front: Once basic vehicle handling feels automatic, what single habit matters most for safety?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.expected_back: Once you become a competent driver, the safest habit is not letting your attention to driving slip.

sec05-card-sec05-F42.front: Why can't your senses detect deadly carbon monoxide — and which three situations commonly leak it into cabins?
sec05-card-sec05-F42.expected_back: Carbon monoxide from the engine can kill and cannot be tasted, smelled or seen; it tends to leak while the heater runs, when the exhaust system is faulty, or from other cars' fumes in heavy traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.front: Which two enclosed engine-running situations risk fatal carbon monoxide buildup?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.expected_back: Never run the engine in a closed garage, and never use the heater or air conditioner in a parked car with the windows shut.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.front: Which three maintenance, listening, and vent habits guard against carbon monoxide poisoning?
sec05-card-sec05-R18.expected_back: To guard against carbon monoxide, have the exhaust checked regularly, listen for unusual roaring under the car and close the fresh-air vent in heavy traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F44.front: Which two physical holding and messaging actions does the Hands Free Tennessee law forbid?
sec05-card-sec05-F44.expected_back: Under the Hands Free Tennessee law, a driver may not hold a phone or mobile device with any part of the body or write, send or read any text-based message.

sec05-card-sec05-R20.front: What seat-position reach and three video actions also violate Tennessee's hands-free law?
sec05-card-sec05-R20.expected_back: The hands-free law also forbids reaching for a device in a way that takes you out of your seated, belted position, and watching, recording or broadcasting video on it.

sec05-card-sec05-R19.front: What fine and court-cost caps — plus which responder exemptions — came with Tennessee's two thousand nine texting statute?
sec05-card-sec05-R19.expected_back: The older two thousand nine rule bans reading or sending written messages on a hand-held device while moving, with a fine of up to fifty dollars plus up to ten dollars court costs, and exempts on-duty police, firefighters and emergency workers.

sec05-card-sec05-F45.front: When school-zone warning flashers are active, what phone rule applies to moving drivers aged eighteen and older?
sec05-card-sec05-F45.expected_back: Since January one, two thousand eighteen, drivers aged eighteen or older commit an offense by using a hand-held phone while moving through a marked school zone with its warning flashers on, unless the phone is in hands-free mode.

sec05-card-sec05-R21.front: Does the school-zone hands-free allowance cover drivers under eighteen — and how is teen handheld use classified?
sec05-card-sec05-R21.expected_back: In a marked school zone the hands-free exception does not cover drivers under eighteen, for whom hand-held use is a delinquent act.

sec05-card-sec05-F46.front: Which screens are banned inside the driver's view while moving — and which three functional displays stay legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F46.expected_back: A video screen able to show television or video may not be installed where the driver can see it while the car is moving, though navigation, vehicle information and camera displays are allowed.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: At least how many feet ahead of a turn or lane change must you switch on your turn signal in Tennessee?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Turn on your turn signal at least fifty feet before a turn or lane change.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: When your driveway or turn sits right past an intersection, when should you click on your turn signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: If you plan to turn just past an intersection, wait until you are in the intersection to signal, so no one thinks you are turning at it.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: Which two well-meaning blinker habits does the Tennessee manual tell you never to use?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Do not use your turn signal to wave a driver behind you around, or to repeat the signals of cars ahead of you.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: Why must you signal every direction change even when the street looks completely deserted?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: Signal every time you change direction, even when no one seems to be around, because the car you do not see is the most dangerous.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How long should you run your turn signal before pulling away from a parked spot at the curb?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: When leaving a curb, signal long enough for oncoming traffic to know you are pulling out of the parked position.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: When should you get into your turn lane and pick your gear, and how should throttle feel through the corner?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: Move into the correct turn lane as early as possible, sooner on faster roads, choose your gear before the intersection and accelerate slightly through the turn.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: Where must you wait if backed-up traffic ahead could trap you mid-turn when the signal changes?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: Do not enter an intersection to turn if traffic ahead could keep you from finishing the turn before the light changes; wait behind the stop line.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: What is the right play if you realize at the last moment that you are in the wrong lane for your turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: If you are in the wrong lane for a turn, go on to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane there.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: Why must your front wheels stay pointed straight ahead while waiting for an opening to turn left?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: While waiting to turn left, keep your wheels pointed straight, because a rear-end hit with the wheels turned can push you into oncoming traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: Which braking, clutch, and gearshift actions should you avoid once you are actually turning inside an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: Do not brake or press the clutch during the turn itself, and do not shift gears in the intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: When you and an oncoming driver both turn left at the same intersection, how should your paths pass each other?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: When two drivers meet at an intersection and both turn left, each turns to the left of the other.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: How far forward into an intersection should you roll with straight wheels before starting to steer left?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: In a left turn, keep the wheels straight until you reach the turn point, just before the imaginary center of the intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: From which lane do you start a left turn on a two-way street, and which lane must you enter?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: For a left turn from a two-way street, approach in the lane next to the center line, then turn into the first lane just right of the center line of the new street, never wide into the right lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: If you are waiting behind the line to turn left and the signal turns yellow, what must you do?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: If the light turns yellow while you are waiting to turn left, do not pull into the intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: How can you tell instantly from center lane-line colors whether a street carries two-way or one-way traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: Center lines are yellow on two-way streets and white on one-way streets.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: Which lane must you turn into when making a left turn onto a one-way street?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Turning left onto a one-way street, turn sharply into the first lane, the one nearest the left curb.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: When driving on a one-way street, which lane must you use to set up a left turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: On a one-way street, approach a left turn from the lane farthest to the left.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: What lane rule governs dedicated left-turn lanes and side-by-side multiple turn lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: Where a lane is marked for left turns, turn only from that lane, and in multiple turn lanes stay in your starting lane all the way through.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: How do you execute a left turn from a one-way street onto a two-way street, and when may you move right?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: Turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street, enter the intersection before turning sharply into the first lane right of the yellow line, and move right only after signaling and checking.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: When is turning left on a red light from a one-way street onto a two-way street legal?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: Turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street is never allowed on a red light.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: Under what exact street combination and conditions is turning left on a red light legal in Tennessee?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: Turning left from one one-way street onto another, you may go on red after a full stop unless a No Turn on Red sign is posted.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: Which two red-light turns does Tennessee allow unless prohibited by a sign, and what must you do first?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: Tennessee allows a right turn on red, and a left turn on red from a one-way street onto a one-way street going left, unless a sign forbids it, after a full stop and yielding.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: When may drivers in a second adjacent lane make the same turn as the curb or inside lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: In a multiple turn lane setup, the second lane may make the same turn as the first only when a sign or pavement marking allows it.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: What purpose do curved white channel lines and pavement arrows serve inside wide intersections?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: White channel lines and arrows in an intersection guide you into the correct lane as you turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: How should you position your car before and after making a standard right turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: On a right turn, do not swing wide to the left; stay close to the right curb and turn into the lane nearest the right curb.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: Why is swinging wide to the left right before making a right turn dangerous?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: If you swing wide before a right turn, the driver behind may think you are turning left and try to pass you on the right.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: Which four traffic and vulnerable-user conflicts must you scan for before turning right?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: Before a right turn, look left and right for cross traffic and for oncoming vehicles also turning, and check for pedestrians and bicyclists.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: Why must you never squeeze past a large truck or bus on the right near an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: Large trucks and buses must swing wide when turning, so never pass one on the right if it may be turning right.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: Which direction does traffic move inside a roundabout, and who yields at the entrance?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: Always travel counterclockwise, to the right, around a roundabout, and yield to vehicles already circulating before entering.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: What posted speed range, passing rule, and exit-blinker rule govern driving inside a roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: Roundabout speeds are usually posted at fifteen to twenty-five miles per hour, you may not pass inside a multi-lane roundabout, and you signal right to exit.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: Which three safety and neighborhood goals prompt cities to install roundabouts?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: Roundabouts are used to slow traffic, cut crashes and discourage commuters from cutting through neighborhoods.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.front: Which side of the raised splitter island do you pass when entering a roundabout, and when may you stop inside?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.expected_back: Keep to the right of the splitter island when approaching a roundabout, and once inside do not stop unless a sign, signal or officer tells you to.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.front: What conflict must you watch for in a multi-lane roundabout, and what should you do if you miss your exit?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.expected_back: In a multi-lane roundabout be ready to yield to vehicles crossing in front of you from the inside lane to exit, and go around again if you miss your street.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: At what controlled intersections and below what clear sight distance are U-turns illegal in Tennessee?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: You may not make a U-turn at an intersection controlled by a signal or officer, or anywhere you cannot see five hundred feet of traffic both ways.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: Where else are U-turns banned on city streets, and what safer alternative does the manual recommend?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: U-turns are also banned between intersections in a city and wherever signs or markings forbid them; driving around the block is safer.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.front: Can Tennessee cities or towns outlaw U-turns across all of their municipal streets?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.expected_back: Some towns and cities ban U-turns on their streets entirely, so check with local police.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: Are U-turns allowed on interstates, and who is permitted to use paved median crossovers there?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: U-turns on interstates are illegal, and median emergency crossovers are only for emergency and maintenance vehicles.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.front: What must you do if you blow past your interstate exit or get caught in a freeway backup?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.expected_back: If you miss an interstate exit or are stuck in a jam, drive on to the next exit; cutting across the median is illegal.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: How much roadway space must you leave oncoming vehicles on a narrow road with no painted center line?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: On a road with no center line, give oncoming drivers at least half of the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: Which paint color belongs on your left versus your right, and what does seeing yellow on your right mean?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: White on your right, yellow on your left: if the yellow line is on your right, you are on the wrong side and must pull over at once.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.front: Which four situations allow driving left of the center line, and which side should pass a road crash?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.expected_back: Drive left of center only to pass, to get around an obstruction, on a one-way road or to turn left, and go around crashes to the right when possible.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: What is the sole legal purpose of the middle lane on a two-way street with three or five lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: The center lane of a two-way road with three or five lanes is used only for left turns.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: Which roadway of a divided highway must you drive on, and where is crossing the median legal?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: On a divided highway always use the road on the right, and cross the median only at an authorized crossover or intersection or when directed.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: What urgent warning are raised lane reflectors sending if they glow red in your headlights?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: Red reflectors facing you on the lane lines mean you are driving the wrong way and could hit someone head on.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.front: How do center and lane markings differ between a two-lane highway and an undivided four-lane highway?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.expected_back: A two-lane highway has a single broken yellow center line, while a four-lane highway has two solid yellow lines in the middle and dashed white lines between same-direction lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R20.front: How do public median crossovers on four-lane divided highways differ from interstates?
sec09-card-sec09-R20.expected_back: Median crossovers exist only at paved openings on four-lane highways; interstates have none for regular traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.front: Where must you wait if another car is already stopped inside a divided-highway median crossover?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.expected_back: When a car is already waiting in a highway crossover, stay stopped in the left lane with your signal on rather than pulling in behind it, which could cause a head-on crash.

sec09-card-sec09-R21.front: What does a pavement marking combining a straight arrow and a turn arrow allow, and what yield rules apply?
sec09-card-sec09-R21.expected_back: A lane with both a turn arrow and a straight arrow lets you go either way, following normal right-of-way rules unless a protected arrow is showing.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: What is prohibited in a shared center turn lane, and what is the maximum distance you may travel inside it?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: A shared center turn lane is only for left turns from either direction, may not be used for passing, and may not be driven in for more than three hundred feet.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: When two opposing drivers want the same stretch of a shared center turn lane, who has priority?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: When drivers from opposite directions enter a shared center turn lane, the first one in has the right-of-way.

sec09-card-sec09-R22.front: When should you pull into a shared center turn lane, what shortcut is banned, and how can side-street turners use it?
sec09-card-sec09-R22.expected_back: Enter a shared center turn lane just before your turn, never ride in it to reach a turn lane at the next intersection, and you may use it to wait before merging right from a side street.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: What does each overhead symbol—green arrow, red X, flashing yellow X, and steady yellow X—mean over a reversible lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: Over reversible lanes, a green arrow means you may use the lane, a red X means you may not, a flashing yellow X means turns only, and a steady yellow X means leave the lane soon.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: Which three groups may travel in a white-diamond reserved lane, and when may an ordinary solo car enter one?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: Reserved lanes marked by a white diamond are for buses, bicycles or HOV car pools only, though you may cross one to turn within the next half block.

sec09-card-sec09-R23.front: What occupancy minimum and schedule info do HOV-two signs communicate?
sec09-card-sec09-R23.expected_back: An HOV two sign means at least two people must be in the vehicle to use that lane, and signs give the days and hours the limit applies.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: What exact sequence of checks and signals should you follow every time you change lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: To change lanes, check your mirrors, signal, look over your shoulder toward your move, check blind spots, and then move over gradually.

sec09-card-sec09-R24.front: How should you respond when a driver slightly ahead in the next lane clicks on a blinker to merge over?
sec09-card-sec09-R24.expected_back: When the driver ahead signals a lane change, slow and leave room, and do not speed up or change lanes until they have finished.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.front: Before pulling out to pass on a two-lane road, how should you treat any oncoming car visible in the distance?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.expected_back: Before passing, assume that any oncoming vehicle you can see is too close, and when in doubt stay in your lane.

sec09-card-sec09-R25.front: What crash happens if you cut back in too early after passing versus waiting too long?
sec09-card-sec09-R25.expected_back: Passing crashes are often fatal: cutting back too soon risks a sideswipe, and cutting back too late risks a head-on collision.

sec09-card-sec09-R26.front: Why must you never nose across the center line just to peek past the vehicle ahead before passing?
sec09-card-sec09-R26.expected_back: Do not swing across the center line to look ahead before passing; needing to do so means you are following too closely or lack the sight distance to pass.

sec09-card-sec09-R27.front: Why does the manual warn against passing at night on unfamiliar two-lane roads?
sec09-card-sec09-R27.expected_back: Avoid passing at night on unfamiliar roads, because it is harder to see where the passing zone ends.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.front: When is it safe to pull back into the right lane after passing a car, and what final step finishes the pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.expected_back: Return to your lane after passing only when you can see the whole passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, and then cancel your signal.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.front: Is passing several cars in one move legal in Tennessee, and what hundred-foot clearance rule applies?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.expected_back: Passing several vehicles at once is not illegal in Tennessee but is generally unsafe, and should only be tried if you can be back in your lane one hundred feet before a no-passing marking or oncoming car.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.front: Under which two roadway conditions may you legally pass on the right, and what surface rule never bends?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.expected_back: You may pass on the right only when the car ahead is turning left or the road has room for two or more moving lanes your way, and never by leaving the pavement.

sec09-card-sec09-R28.front: Which three special lanes are illegal for right-side passing, and who gets blamed if the car ahead turns right?
sec09-card-sec09-R28.expected_back: Never pass on the right in a bike lane, a parking lane, or an emergency lane within sight of a signal or stop sign; the driver passing on the right is at fault if the car ahead turns right.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.front: Around which six roadway features is passing prohibited because sightlines or escape room vanish?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.expected_back: Do not pass near an intersection, railroad crossing, narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel, or when approaching a hill or curve.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.front: Why must you never overtake a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.expected_back: Never pass a car that has stopped for pedestrians in a crosswalk, a frequent cause of pedestrian deaths.

sec09-card-sec09-R29.front: What center-line marking and bus signal strictly forbid passing?
sec09-card-sec09-R29.expected_back: Do not pass when the solid yellow line is on your side or when a school or church bus has its lights flashing and stop arm out.

sec09-card-sec09-R30.front: About how far back should you stop for a crosswalk on a multi-lane street, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-R30.expected_back: On a multi-lane road, stop about thirty feet before a crosswalk so you do not hide crossing pedestrians from drivers in other lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.front: Does passing a 'Do Not Pass' zone's end sign mean it is automatically safe to pull out and pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.expected_back: The end of a no-passing zone only means you can see farther; you still must judge whether passing is safe.

sec09-card-sec09-R31.front: Even inside a marked no-passing zone, when may you legally cross a solid yellow line?
sec09-card-sec09-R31.expected_back: In a no-passing zone you may still cross the solid yellow line to turn left into or out of an alley, intersection, private road or driveway.

sec09-card-sec09-R32.front: What does Tennessee law say about using the right shoulder to pass or weaving back and forth through lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-R32.expected_back: Do not pass on the right shoulder, and do not weave from lane to lane to get ahead of traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.front: What three duties apply to you while another driver is passing your vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.expected_back: When someone is passing you, stay in your lane, keep to the right and hold your speed, never speeding up to block them.

sec09-card-sec09-R33.front: If an oncoming car pops over a hill while someone is halfway past you, what should you do?
sec09-card-sec09-R33.expected_back: If an oncoming car appears while you are being passed, slow down so the passing driver can pull back in ahead of you.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.front: At least how many feet of side clearance does Tennessee law require when passing a bicyclist riding your direction?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.expected_back: Tennessee law requires at least three feet of space when passing a bicycle going your way, kept until you are safely past.

sec09-card-sec09-R34.front: In which two tight situations must you wait behind a bicyclist instead of trying to squeeze past?
sec09-card-sec09-R34.expected_back: Never pass between a bicyclist and oncoming traffic on a two-lane road, and do not pass where it would squeeze the rider toward parked cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F42.front: How can you tell instantly whether a tractor-trailer driver can see your car, and why avoid cruising beside one?
sec09-card-sec09-F42.expected_back: If you cannot see a truck's side mirrors, its driver cannot see you, and lingering beside a truck keeps you in its blind spot.

sec09-card-sec09-R35.front: Why is pulling right in front of a heavy truck or bus and braking so dangerous?
sec09-card-sec09-R35.expected_back: Never pull in front of a truck or bus and slow down, because it removes the truck driver's safety cushion.

sec09-card-sec09-R36.front: How do flat roads, uphill climbs, and downhill grades change passing a heavy truck, and what speed cap stays firm?
sec09-card-sec09-R36.expected_back: Passing a truck takes longer on level ground, is easier on an upgrade where it slows, and may need more speed on a downgrade, but you still may not exceed the limit.

sec09-card-sec09-F43.front: What is the only reason to back into a live travel lane, and why should road-test applicants drill backing?
sec09-card-sec09-F43.expected_back: Never back into a travel lane except into a parallel parking space, and remember that backing is the maneuver new drivers most often fail on the road test.

sec09-card-sec09-R37.front: What check comes before entering your car to back up, and how should you look once reversing?
sec09-card-sec09-R37.expected_back: Before backing, check behind the vehicle before getting in, then look through the rear window instead of relying only on mirrors or leaning out the door.

sec09-card-sec09-F44.front: Which two high-conflict places are explicitly illegal to back into or reverse along?
sec09-card-sec09-F44.expected_back: Backing from a driveway into an intersection is illegal, and so is backing up on an interstate.

sec09-card-sec09-R38.front: May you stop inside a moving travel lane if you get lost, drop off a friend, or feel car trouble starting?
sec09-card-sec09-R38.expected_back: Do not stop in a travel lane for any reason, such as being lost, a breakdown or dropping off a passenger; keep going until you can pull off.

sec09-card-sec09-R51.front: Which way does your front bumper swing as you steer while backing out of an angled parking space, and when do you recheck?
sec09-card-sec09-R51.expected_back: When backing out of an angle space, the front of the car swings opposite to the turn; stop and look again once you can see past the cars beside you.

sec09-card-sec09-F45.front: What wheel-placement, open-road width, and visibility distances apply when parking outside city limits?
sec09-card-sec09-F45.expected_back: Outside city limits, park with all four wheels off the pavement if possible, leave at least eighteen feet of road for traffic, and be visible for two hundred feet both ways.

sec09-card-sec09-R39.front: What brake and transmission habit should you use every single time you park?
sec09-card-sec09-R39.expected_back: Set the parking brake every time you park, leaving a manual car in gear or an automatic in park, especially on hills or near schools and playgrounds.

sec09-card-sec09-R40.front: What does Tennessee law say about leaving an unattended parked car running, and what two steps secure it?
sec09-card-sec09-R40.expected_back: Leaving the engine running in an unattended parked car is illegal; take the keys and lock the doors.

sec09-card-sec09-R41.front: Which three actions are mandatory whenever you pull out of a parallel or lot parking space?
sec09-card-sec09-R41.expected_back: Look, signal and yield whenever you pull out of any parking space, including a parallel space.

sec09-card-sec09-F46.front: Which way do you turn your front wheels when parking downhill, on any curbless hill, or uphill with a curb?
sec09-card-sec09-F46.expected_back: On a downhill with a curb, or on any hill without a curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road; uphill with a curb, turn them away from the curb.

sec09-card-sec09-F47.front: How many feet must you stay clear when parking near a fire hydrant, crosswalk, stop sign or signal, and railroad crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-F47.expected_back: Parking is illegal within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant, within twenty feet of a crosswalk, within thirty feet of a traffic signal or stop sign, and within fifty feet of a railroad crossing.

sec09-card-sec09-R42.front: Is stopping side-by-side next to a curbed car ever legal, and when should four-way flashers come on after dark?
sec09-card-sec09-R42.expected_back: Double parking is illegal, and four-way flashers may be used after dark when a vehicle is disabled or creates a hazard.

sec09-card-sec09-R43.front: Which everyday access points, structures, and freeway spots ban non-emergency parking?
sec09-card-sec09-R43.expected_back: Parking is also illegal in front of a driveway, in an intersection or fire lane, on a sidewalk, bridge or tunnel, on interstate ramps unless disabled, and on an interstate shoulder except in an emergency.

sec09-card-sec09-R44.front: How far must you park from a fire-station driveway on the same side of the street versus across the street?
sec09-card-sec09-R44.expected_back: Keep at least twenty feet from a fire station driveway when parking on its side of the street, and at least seventy-five feet when parking across from it.

sec09-card-sec09-R45.front: Which three levels of stopping or loading restrictions can painted curbs establish?
sec09-card-sec09-R45.expected_back: Painted curbs set special rules: some allow stopping only to pick up or drop off passengers, some only to load or unload with the driver staying, and some forbid stopping at all.

sec09-card-sec09-R46.front: How do you line up beside the forward car and angle back when starting a parallel park?
sec09-card-sec09-R46.expected_back: To start parallel parking, stop beside the car ahead of the space, bumpers even, no closer than two feet, then back slowly with the wheel turned sharply right to about a forty-five-degree angle.

sec09-card-sec09-R47.front: Within how many inches of the curb must a completed parallel park sit, and what comes before opening your door?
sec09-card-sec09-R47.expected_back: A finished parallel park should leave you no more than eighteen inches from the curb, and check traffic before opening the driver's door.

sec09-card-sec09-R48.front: If your car dies and cannot roll off the pavement, which four steps warn traffic and secure the vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-R48.expected_back: If your car breaks down and cannot leave the road, raise the hood or tie a cloth to the left door handle or antenna, turn on the flashers and lock up.

sec09-card-sec09-R49.front: Is walking along a Tennessee interstate legal if your car breaks down?
sec09-card-sec09-R49.expected_back: Walking on an interstate is illegal, so except in an extreme emergency stay in a disabled car until an officer or helper arrives.

sec09-card-sec09-R50.front: Who may legally use an accessible parking space, and what penalties hit violators?
sec09-card-sec09-R50.expected_back: Handicap spaces are only for a vehicle with a valid placard or plate that is carrying its holder; anyone else parking there commits a misdemeanor with a one hundred dollars fine and may be towed.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: Why does driving after dark turn extra hazardous along poorly lit highways and rural roads?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Night driving is especially risky on poorly lit highways and country roads, because you see clearly over a much shorter distance and dark animals, cars and people in dark clothing are hard to spot.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: How do your odds of a serious crash at night compare with daytime driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Even though traffic is lighter at night, the chance of a serious crash is much greater than during the day.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: Which three specific visual skills weaken once daylight fades?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Most of a driver's reaction time depends on eyesight, and depth perception, color recognition and side vision all weaken after dark.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: Which two nights of the week record more fatal traffic crashes than any other days?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: More fatal crashes happen on Friday and Saturday nights than on any other day of the week.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: What is the foundational speed rule for driving safely after dark?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: The basic rule of night driving is never to outrun your headlights, which means driving slowly enough to stop within the distance your lights show you.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: How must your stopping distance compare with sight distance at night, and what car factors matter?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: At night, keep your stopping distance shorter than your sight distance and weigh how strong your lights are and how well your brakes respond.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: Where should your eyes scan beyond your main beams while driving after dark?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Look beyond the reach of your headlight beams for dark shapes, and glance left and right now and then to locate the pavement edge and oncoming cars.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: Where should you look instead of staring straight into bright oncoming headlights?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: Do not look straight into oncoming headlights, which can blind you for a moment; instead watch the right edge of the road and steer by the white edge line.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: Why should you avoid flashing your high beams to warn another motorist?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Do not flash your high beams to warn another driver, because it can distract that driver and lead to a crash.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: At least how far ahead must Tennessee headlights reveal a person on the highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Tennessee law requires headlights that let you clearly see a person on the highway at least two hundred feet ahead, so they must work properly, be aimed correctly and have clean lenses.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: Why must headlights stay in peak working order to meet legal seeing distance?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Headlight power fades sharply with distance, which is why the lights must be in good working order to meet the legal seeing distance.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: Which two resources can help ensure your headlights are aimed accurately?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: Check your owner's manual for how to aim your headlights, or have a mechanic at a reputable garage or dealership align them.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: What happens to your eyes and road vision during glare recovery time after bright lights pass?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: Glare recovery time is the pause after an oncoming car passes while your narrowed pupils adjust back to dim light, and during it you are close to driving blind.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: Does sharp daytime vision speed glare recovery, and which drivers usually recover slowest?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: Glare recovery time does not depend on how sharp your eyesight is; it differs from person to person and is usually worse for older drivers and people in poor physical condition.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: What cleaning habits help cut down night glare on windshields, glasses, and lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: To fight glare, keep the windshield clear on both sides along with your eyeglasses, and clean your headlights and windows inside and out at least once a month.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: What is the effect of headlights aimed too high or too far outward?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Headlights pointed too high or too far outward do not help you see the road; they only add glare for drivers you meet or follow.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: Within what distance must you dim high beams when meeting or following another vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: Switch to low beams whenever you meet an oncoming vehicle or come up behind one within five hundred feet.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: Which beam setting belongs in cities and towns, and what curve habit protects oncoming traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: Use low beams at all times when driving in cities and towns, and avoid blasting an oncoming driver with high beams on curves or turns to the right.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: Why must you never leave full headlights burning while parked at night, even briefly?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: Never leave your headlights on while parked at night, even briefly, because a stopped car's lights can blind approaching drivers and mislead them about where the road runs.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: When do lit headlights on a parked vehicle create the worst deception for approaching drivers?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: A parked car's lit headlights are a bigger hazard when the car sits on the wrong side of the road.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: Which two lighting systems should stay on if you must park beside a highway at night?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: Whenever you park on or beside a highway at night, leave your emergency flashers and parking lights on.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: When is stopping allowed on an interstate shoulder versus on an entrance or exit ramp?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Parking on an interstate shoulder is banned except in an emergency, and you may not park on any paved or unpaved part of an entrance or exit ramp unless the vehicle is disabled.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: Why must you drop speed at the very first sign of rain?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: Wet pavement can be as dangerous as ice, so slow down at the first sign of rain, since you will need more stopping distance and may skid on sharp turns.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: Why are roads usually slickest during the first minutes after rain begins?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: Roads are usually most slippery right after rain begins, because dirt and oil mix with the water into a greasy film that robs your tires of grip.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: Why should you wait a few seconds after raindrops start before switching on windshield wipers?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: Keep your wiper blades in good shape, and wait a few seconds after rain begins before turning them on so there is enough water to clear the glass rather than smear grime.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: Which two climate controls keep windows and mirrors clear during damp or stormy weather?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: Use the defroster or the air conditioner to keep your windows and mirrors clear in bad weather.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: How should you adjust turn signaling and braking timing during rainy weather?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Rain calls for signaling turns and lane changes early and braking well ahead of a stop so drivers behind know what you plan.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.front: Why does rain starting on a hot day make asphalt extraordinarily slick at first?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.expected_back: When rain starts on a hot day, heat-raised oil in the asphalt makes the pavement extremely slippery for the first few minutes, until the rain washes it away.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: Which headlight setting must you use in fog or mist, and why are high beams dangerous?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: In fog or mist, use low beams and never high beams, because high-beam light bounces back into your eyes.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: What is the safest overall decision regarding driving in thick fog or wildfire smoke?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: The best advice for fog or smoke is not to drive in it; Tennessee can see forest-fire smoke and temperature-driven fog in any season.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.front: If you cannot avoid driving in fog or smoke, which light combinations are required or banned?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.expected_back: If you must drive in fog or smoke, use low beams, never drive with only parking lights or fog lights on, and reduce your speed.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: Why should you silence or lower the radio and stay off your phone in fog or smoke?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: In fog or smoke, keep the radio off or low and do not use a cell phone, so you can hear the traffic around you.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: Which lane, passing, crossing, and stopping rules keep you safer inside fog?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: In fog, be patient, keep to the right, avoid passing, avoid crossing traffic unless you must, and do not stop on the roadway unless it is truly necessary.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.front: What should you do if fog grows so thick that you lose sight of the road edge?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.expected_back: If you cannot see the edge of the road in fog, pull off far to the right, completely clear of the travel lane, and switch on your emergency flashers.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: What personal safety step should you take if your car breaks down or stalls in fog or smoke?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: If your car stalls or breaks down in fog or smoke, move away from it to avoid being hurt.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.front: Besides postponing travel until fog lifts, what roadside controls should you watch for in fog zones?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.expected_back: In fog, consider putting off your trip until it clears, and obey the warning devices set up in fog-prone areas.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.front: During which three daytime weather conditions does Tennessee law require turning on low-beam headlights?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.expected_back: Tennessee law requires you to turn on low-beam headlights when driving in daylight through dense fog, heavy rain or snow, which also helps oncoming drivers see you.

sec11-card-sec11-R38.front: Why should you switch headlights on whenever bad weather cuts visibility?
sec11-card-sec11-R38.expected_back: Use your headlights whenever weather limits visibility, so other drivers can see you.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.front: What happens between your tires and the road during hydroplaning, and why is it unstable?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.expected_back: Hydroplaning happens when heavy water makes your tires lose all contact with the pavement, so a small steering change or a gust of wind can send the car into a skid or spin.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.front: How must you slow down if your tires start hydroplaning on standing water?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.expected_back: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, slow down gradually by easing off the gas, and do not slam on the brakes.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.front: How severely can hydroplaning multiply stopping distance and affect steering?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.expected_back: Hydroplaning can triple your stopping distance and reduce or eliminate steering control.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.front: Does hydroplaning happen only at freeway speeds, or can it occur slower?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.expected_back: Hydroplaning is more likely at higher speeds, but tires can hydroplane at any speed under the right conditions.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.front: What tire condition defines a skid, and what driver mistake triggers it?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.expected_back: Skids happen when the tires can no longer grip the road, and they are caused by drivers going too fast for conditions.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.front: What should your feet and hands do if your car's rear end slides left in a skid?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.expected_back: In a skid, stay off the brake and steer in the direction you want the car to go; if the rear slides to the left, steer to the left.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.front: What steering adjustment is crucial the moment a skidding vehicle begins straightening out?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.expected_back: Once a skidding car begins to straighten, turn the wheel back the other way, or the car may swing around and start a new skid in the opposite direction.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.front: How should you steer right after catching the main slide of a skid?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.expected_back: Keep making small left and right steering corrections after a skid until the vehicle is moving down the road under your control again.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.front: What proactive habit is the single best defense against ever entering a skid?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.expected_back: The best defense against skids is to avoid them by watching the weather and slowing down well before your stopping point.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.front: What must you do immediately if your right wheels drop off the paved roadway edge?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.expected_back: If your wheels drop off the paved road, lift your foot off the gas without braking suddenly and keep a firm grip without jerking the wheel back toward the pavement.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.front: How should you brake and when should you steer back onto pavement after a wheel drop-off?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.expected_back: After running off the pavement, brake lightly and briefly instead of slamming or holding the pedal, and steer back on only once nearby traffic is clear and you have slowed.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.front: What is the primary job of painted edge rumble stripes, and what is the buzz-and-shake?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.expected_back: Rumble stripes are edge lines painted over a row of indentations; their main job is to make the edge line easier to see on wet nights, while the vibration and noise are a side effect.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.front: Which thunderstorm hazard kills more people each year than lightning, wind, or hail?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.expected_back: Each year flooding kills more people than any other thunderstorm hazard, and many victims are drivers who try to cross flooded roads.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.front: What depth of fast-moving floodwater knocks down an adult versus sweeps away most cars?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.expected_back: Just six inches of fast-moving floodwater can knock a person down, and moving water of eighteen to twenty-four inches deep is enough to sweep away most cars.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.front: Why do heavy pickups and SUVs still fail to protect drivers in flooded roadways?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.expected_back: A heavy vehicle is no protection in a flood, because cars float through buoyancy and trucks or SUVs gain only six to twelve more inches of clearance.

sec11-card-sec11-R21.front: What often happens once floodwater sweeps a car downstream, leaving only seconds to escape?
sec11-card-sec11-R21.expected_back: Once swept downstream, a car often rolls or flips and the driver has only a few seconds to get out, and many panicked drivers are later found still belted in.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.front: Why does Turn Around, Don't Drown warn against trusting shallow-looking floodwater?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.expected_back: Turn Around, Don't Drown: stay out of flooded roads, because the water may be much deeper than it looks where the roadbed has washed out.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.front: What two legal and financial penalties can hit a driver who knowingly bypasses flood barricades?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.expected_back: A driver who knowingly ignores clearly visible flood warning signs or barricades and drives into a flooded road can be charged with reckless driving and made to repay the cost of the rescue.

sec11-card-sec11-R22.front: How shallow can water be when you lose car control, and what depth floats most vehicles?
sec11-card-sec11-R22.expected_back: As little as six to twelve inches of water can cost you control of the car, while about two feet is enough to float most cars downstream.

sec11-card-sec11-R23.front: What must you do immediately if your vehicle stalls inside floodwater?
sec11-card-sec11-R23.expected_back: Never drive through floodwater or across a flowing stream, and if your vehicle stalls in water, leave it right away and head for higher ground.

sec11-card-sec11-R24.front: Which road features collect floodwater fastest, and when are hidden floods hardest to spot?
sec11-card-sec11-R24.expected_back: Watch for flooding at highway dips, low spots and around bridges, do not camp or park beside streams when storms threaten, and take special care at night when flood dangers are harder to see.

sec11-card-sec11-R25.front: What simple in-car habit keeps you informed during severe thunderstorms?
sec11-card-sec11-R25.expected_back: During severe thunderstorms, listen to your car radio and stay alert.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.front: What must you do instead of trying to outrun a visible tornado in your car?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.expected_back: If you spot a tornado, do not try to outrun it; get out of the car, find a ditch or low spot and lie face down to protect yourself from flying debris.

sec11-card-sec11-R45.front: According to the Tennessee manual, where should you seek shelter during a hailstorm or sleet?
sec11-card-sec11-R45.expected_back: In a hailstorm or sleet, the manual says to seek shelter by driving under an overpass or bridge.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.front: How should you position and adjust speed when a large truck or bus passes on your left?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.expected_back: When a large truck or bus passes you on the left, move as far right in your lane as you can and slow down to handle its wind gusts.

sec11-card-sec11-R26.front: Which four vehicle profiles struggle most in strong crosswinds and need slower speeds?
sec11-card-sec11-R26.expected_back: Strong crosswinds make a vehicle harder to control, especially a camper, a large recreational vehicle, a car towing a trailer or a lightweight vehicle, so slow down.

sec11-card-sec11-R27.front: Where along a highway do sudden crosswind gusts hit hardest?
sec11-card-sec11-R27.expected_back: Watch for crosswinds that can push you toward the side or middle of the road when you come out of a sheltered stretch into open space.

sec11-card-sec11-R28.front: How do you keep a towed trailer from jackknifing in the wind wake of a passing truck?
sec11-card-sec11-R28.expected_back: When towing a trailer, wind from a passing truck or bus can make your rig jackknife, so accelerate slowly once it passes to keep the trailer tracking straight.

sec11-card-sec11-R29.front: How do strong headwinds versus strong tailwinds change throttle, steering, and braking needs?
sec11-card-sec11-R29.expected_back: A headwind may require more gas and makes steering harder, while a tailwind raises your speed, so you must slow and begin braking sooner.

sec11-card-sec11-R30.front: When is sun glare worst ahead, and which three tools help cut it down?
sec11-card-sec11-R30.expected_back: Driving toward the sun in early morning or late afternoon creates glare, which sunglasses, clean windows and sun visors reduce.

sec11-card-sec11-R31.front: Why must you stay extra defensive even when low sun shines comfortably from behind you?
sec11-card-sec11-R31.expected_back: When the sun is behind you, oncoming drivers face the glare and may not see your turn signals or even your car.

sec11-card-sec11-R32.front: How should your gear, front wheels, and gas pedal be set when starting out of mud or snow?
sec11-card-sec11-R32.expected_back: To free a car stuck in mud or snow, shift to low gear with the front wheels straight, press the gas gently without spinning the wheels, and drive forward as far as you can.

sec11-card-sec11-R33.front: After creeping forward as far as possible in mud or snow, how do you rock the car free?
sec11-card-sec11-R33.expected_back: Then shift to reverse and back up slowly as far as possible, and repeat this forward and backward rocking until the car rolls free.

sec11-card-sec11-R34.front: What safety rule applies before wedging boards or branches under tires stuck in deep mud or snow?
sec11-card-sec11-R34.expected_back: In deep mud or snow you can put boards or branches under the tires, but never while the wheels are spinning or the vehicle is in gear.

sec11-card-sec11-R35.front: Where and when should you install tire chains to avoid getting stuck?
sec11-card-sec11-R35.expected_back: Carrying tire chains year-round can keep you from getting stuck; pull far to the right before fitting them, and put them on before driving into snow or mud.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.front: Why do tree-shaded or building-shaded road sections hide surprise ice on cold wet days?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.expected_back: On cold, wet days, spots shaded by trees or buildings can hide ice, because they freeze first and dry out last.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.front: Why do highway bridges and overpasses ice over earlier than solid-ground roads?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.expected_back: Bridges and overpasses can hide ice because they tend to freeze before the rest of the road.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.front: How does traction on ice right near the freezing point compare with much colder sub-zero ice?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.expected_back: Close to the freezing point, an icy road can be more slippery than it is at colder temperatures.

sec11-card-sec11-R36.front: What are the three classic driver overreactions on snow-covered or icy roads?
sec11-card-sec11-R36.expected_back: Most drivers' three big errors on snow and ice are overpowering and spinning the wheels, over-braking and sliding them, and over-steering into a skid.

sec11-card-sec11-R37.front: What must you clear off before winter driving, and what tool belongs in the car?
sec11-card-sec11-R37.expected_back: Before driving in winter, clear snow, ice and frost from every window, and carry a quality ice scraper with a brush for windows, lights and outside mirrors.

sec11-card-sec11-R39.front: How should you pull away from a stop and hold pace on snow or ice?
sec11-card-sec11-R39.expected_back: On ice or snow, start slowly and avoid spinning the wheels, and keep your speed steady and slow but not too slow.

sec11-card-sec11-R40.front: What helps carry a vehicle through deeper snow, and what improves winter steering?
sec11-card-sec11-R40.expected_back: In deeper snow you often need the car's momentum to keep moving, and good front tire treads or snow tires improve steering.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.front: What happens to steering control if continuous hard braking locks your front wheels on ice?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.expected_back: On snow or ice, continuous hard braking can lock the front wheels and take away your steering control.

sec11-card-sec11-F41.front: On snow or ice without pumping, how do you modulate brake pressure near wheel lockup?
sec11-card-sec11-F41.expected_back: On snow or ice, brake firmly to just short of lockup, ease off slightly if the wheels lock, then reapply and hold steady pressure without pumping.

sec11-card-sec11-F42.front: How should you press the pedal with antilock brakes during an icy emergency stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F42.expected_back: With antilock brakes, keep constant, firm pressure on the pedal, and in an emergency stop push it all the way to the floor if needed, even on wet or icy roads.

sec11-card-sec11-R41.front: How far can stopping stretch from just twenty miles per hour on a low-traction icy surface?
sec11-card-sec11-R41.expected_back: On a low-traction surface at twenty miles per hour, your stopping distance can stretch to two hundred feet or more.

sec11-card-sec11-R42.front: How can road conditions flip abruptly between the sunny side and shady side of a winter hill?
sec11-card-sec11-R42.expected_back: The sunny side of a hill may be merely wet while the shady side is covered with thin ice.

sec11-card-sec11-R43.front: Besides bridges freezing early, what icy trap can lurk right behind a car stopped ahead?
sec11-card-sec11-R43.expected_back: Ice usually forms on bridges before the roads leading up to them, and a long ice patch behind a car that stopped ahead of you can make you skid into it.

sec11-card-sec11-R44.front: What does stop-and-go traffic do to fresh snow, and where can your tires find better bite?
sec11-card-sec11-R44.expected_back: Where stop-and-go traffic packs fresh snow hard, it soon becomes extremely slippery, and steering to one side of the packed track can help you avoid the slickest part.

sec17-card-sec17-R01.front: How does the manual describe earning a driver license as a teen steps toward adulthood?
sec17-card-sec17-R01.expected_back: Getting a license is often called a modern rite of passage into adulthood, and a dangerous one that demands serious preparation.

sec17-card-sec17-F01.front: What is the single most important thing a supervising adult can do while teaching someone to drive?
sec17-card-sec17-F01.expected_back: The most important thing you can do when teaching someone to drive is to drive safely yourself, because the new driver copies your habits.

sec17-card-sec17-F02.front: How do teens frequently justify bad road-test habits like rolling stops to license examiners?
sec17-card-sec17-F02.expected_back: Examiners often hear young drivers defend habits such as rolling stops by saying that is how their parent drives.

sec17-card-sec17-F04.front: Which two traffic choices are shaped directly by a new driver's behind-the-wheel attitude?
sec17-card-sec17-F04.expected_back: Attitude decides whether a new driver will cooperate or compete in traffic and whether the driver accepts high risk or practices defensive driving.

sec17-card-sec17-F05.front: Which three personal qualities make a supervising adult an effective driving mentor?
sec17-card-sec17-F05.expected_back: A mentor's patience, courtesy and willingness to improve are the best assets, and setting that example may do more than anything else for a teen's safety.

sec17-card-sec17-R02.front: What sequence does Tennessee's graduated program establish for beginners of any age?
sec17-card-sec17-R02.memory_hook: Book study first, supervised driving next
sec17-card-sec17-R02.expected_back: The graduated license rules call for book learning first and then a minimum amount of supervised driving before solo driving, a sound approach for new drivers of any age.

sec17-card-sec17-F03.front: How many days must an applicant under eighteen hold a learner permit before taking the road test?
sec17-card-sec17-F03.expected_back: People under eighteen must hold a learner permit for one hundred eighty days and qualify under the graduated license program before they can take the road test.

sec17-card-sec17-F06.front: How can narrating your own thoughts aloud while driving coach a passenger learner safely?
sec17-card-sec17-F06.expected_back: Talking out loud while you drive, about tricky signs, yellow-light decisions, surrounding traffic and the two-second rule, uses teachable moments without overloading the learner.

sec17-card-sec17-R03.front: How should a parent or mentor react when narration prompts friendly critique of their own driving?
sec17-card-sec17-R03.expected_back: Teaching out loud may lead your learner to offer friendly criticism of your own driving, which you should accept with good humor.

sec17-card-sec17-R05.front: What active role must a mentor maintain from the front passenger seat during practice drives?
sec17-card-sec17-R05.expected_back: Stay alert as a mentor, anticipating problems and being ready to react to prevent unsafe situations.

sec17-card-sec17-F07.front: Why must mentors map out every practice drive beforehand rather than wandering aimlessly?
sec17-card-sec17-F07.expected_back: Plan every practice session in advance, because aimless driving can be dangerous for a novice, especially early on.

sec17-card-sec17-R07.front: Why should a driving mentor keep spoken commentary brief while the beginner is behind the wheel?
sec17-card-sec17-R07.expected_back: Everything a mentor says is also a distraction for the driver, so keep comments sparing and avoid situations the learner is not ready for.

sec17-card-sec17-F14.front: How should a mentor time route directions and choose pedal or control words?
sec17-card-sec17-F14.expected_back: Give directions well ahead of time and use the same words every time, such as always saying gas pedal rather than switching to accelerator.

sec17-card-sec17-F15.front: Why must a mentor respond calmly instead of yelling or fussing over routine beginner mistakes?
sec17-card-sec17-F15.expected_back: Do not yell and fuss over every mistake; respond calmly, because criticism can quickly erode a new driver's confidence.

sec17-card-sec17-F16.front: What should a mentor and learner do right after a serious behind-the-wheel mistake?
sec17-card-sec17-F16.expected_back: After a major mistake, stop as soon as you safely can while it is fresh, and discuss what happened and what the safest response would have been.

sec17-card-sec17-F08.front: Why must hand-and-foot coordination be solid before a beginner ever enters live street traffic?
sec17-card-sec17-F08.expected_back: Before practicing in traffic, make sure the learner has good hand and foot coordination, since a novice unsure of the pedals may hit the wrong one in a panic.

sec17-card-sec17-R04.front: What single foundation should the earliest behind-the-wheel sessions focus on building?
sec17-card-sec17-R04.expected_back: Even in early lessons, nothing replaces real experience on the road, but first sessions should focus simply on gaining control of the vehicle.

sec17-card-sec17-F09.front: Where is the ideal place to run phase-one beginner driving practice?
sec17-card-sec17-F09.expected_back: In phase one, practice basic car control somewhere safe and away from traffic, and a large empty parking lot is ideal.

sec17-card-sec17-F10.front: Which foundational cabin, pedal, backing, and lane-holding skills belong inside phase one?
sec17-card-sec17-F10.expected_back: Phase one skills include buckling up, adjusting the seat and mirrors, using the gearshift and pedals, backing up, pulling forward, turning and staying within an imaginary lane.

sec17-card-sec17-F11.front: Into what neighborhood setting does phase two move, and which four traffic skills get added?
sec17-card-sec17-F11.expected_back: In phase two, in a quiet residential area, add pulling into traffic, simple intersections, lane position with a two-second following gap, and easy lane changes.

sec17-card-sec17-R06.front: Why should a learner's first left turns wait for a quiet street when even right turns demand five steps?
sec17-card-sec17-R06.expected_back: Do not hit a beginner with everything at once; even a simple right turn involves mirrors, signaling, lane use, braking and turning, so save a first left turn for a calm area.

sec17-card-sec17-F12.front: Which five tougher maneuvers and parking skills enter during phase three in heavier traffic?
sec17-card-sec17-F12.expected_back: In phase three, once basic control is mastered, move to heavier traffic and add parallel and hill parking, multiple-turn-lane intersections, U-turns and quick stops.

sec17-card-sec17-F13.front: Which four high-demand environments round out phase-four supervised practice?
sec17-card-sec17-F13.expected_back: In phase four, practice everything on high-speed highways or interstates, in different weather, at night in good and bad weather, and in city or heavy traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-F17.front: What relationship have safety researchers found between supervised practice miles and solo crash rates?
sec17-card-sec17-F17.expected_back: Researchers find that the more supervised miles new drivers log before driving alone, the fewer crashes they have.

sec17-card-sec17-R08.front: Roughly how many supervised miles does transportation research recommend before a novice drives solo?
sec17-card-sec17-R08.expected_back: The University of Michigan Transportation Research Institute recommends about three thousand supervised miles, although each new driver differs.

sec17-card-sec17-F18.front: How many supervised driving hours does Tennessee's graduated program require before an intermediate license?
sec17-card-sec17-F18.expected_back: Tennessee's graduated license program requires minors to drive fifty hours before they can move up to the intermediate license.

sec17-card-sec17-R09.front: What easy method does the manual suggest for keeping track of a teen's supervised practice hours?
sec17-card-sec17-R09.expected_back: Track supervised hours in a simple notebook kept in the glove compartment, or copy the manual's sample log.

sec17-card-sec17-R10.front: Which four practical topics can a written family driving agreement spell out ahead of time?
sec17-card-sec17-R10.expected_back: A family driving agreement can cover where and when the teen may drive, how the car is returned, who pays for gas, maintenance and insurance, and the consequences of tickets, damage and moving violations.

sec17-card-sec17-F19.front: Roughly what share of sixteen-year-old male and female drivers crash during their first year licensed?
sec17-card-sec17-F19.expected_back: In their first year of driving, about one in five sixteen-year-old male drivers and about one in ten sixteen-year-old female drivers will have a crash.

sec17-card-sec17-F20.front: Which two high-risk factors combine in many of the worst teen crashes, explaining graduated limits?
