sec17-card-sec17-F20.expected_back: Some of the worst teen crashes happen at night and with a group of young people in the car, which is why the graduated license program restricts both.

sec17-card-sec17-R11.front: What happens to crash risk when alcohol or drug impairment joins nighttime teen group driving?
sec17-card-sec17-R11.expected_back: Alcohol or any other impairment multiplies the crash risk of driving at night with a group of young passengers several times over.

sec17-card-sec17-F21.front: What mindset becomes a new driver's worst enemy soon after mastering basic vehicle controls?
sec17-card-sec17-F21.expected_back: A beginner's worst enemy is overconfidence after quickly learning the basics, so skill-building must continue after the license.

sec17-card-sec17-R12.front: Why are caution and raw years behind the wheel not enough by themselves for defensive driving?
sec17-card-sec17-R12.expected_back: Good defensive driving takes more than caution or experience alone; the driver must keep working at good technique after passing the license exam.

sec17-card-sec17-F22.front: What spoken communication requirement must every applicant meet before starting a Tennessee road test?
sec17-card-sec17-F22.expected_back: Every applicant must understand and speak enough English to communicate safely with the examiner before a road test can be given.

sec17-card-sec17-R13.front: How can a mentor prepare a learner whose first language is not English for traffic signs?
sec17-card-sec17-R13.expected_back: When teaching a driver whose first language is not English, have the driver study traffic signs and signals thoroughly and help translate them while driving together.

sec17-card-sec17-R14.front: How can a mentor rehearse the road examiner's role during practice sessions?
sec17-card-sec17-R14.expected_back: Practice the examiner's role by giving simple English instructions such as turn left, slow down or go straight at the next intersection.

sec17-card-sec17-F23.front: Roughly how briefly does an examiner ride with a teen, and what can passing never guarantee?
sec17-card-sec17-F23.memory_hook: Under thirty minutes; zero habit guarantee
sec17-card-sec17-F23.expected_back: A license examiner rides with your child for less than thirty minutes, and passing that test does not guarantee safe habits afterward.

sec17-card-sec17-R15.front: Why does passing the skills test not prove a teen will drive safely once alone?
sec17-card-sec17-R15.expected_back: Most applicants drive at their best during the road test, so passing it does not mean they will keep using safe procedures once the examiner is gone.

sec17-card-sec17-F24.front: How do the examiner's job and the parent's or mentor's job divide, even after a license is issued?
sec17-card-sec17-F24.expected_back: The examiner judges competence, but teaching the child to drive is the parent's or mentor's responsibility, so keep monitoring a teen's driving after licensing.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: What are the three parts of Tennessee's driver license examination?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.memory_hook: Vision screening, knowledge test, road test
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: The Tennessee driver license examination has three parts: a vision screening, a knowledge test and a road test.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: Which Driver Service Centers do not offer license exams, and how are written knowledge tests queued?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.memory_hook: Skip express centers; knowledge walks in
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: Every Driver Service Center gives license tests except the express service centers, and knowledge tests are handled first-come, first-served.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: Why must behind-the-wheel road tests always be scheduled ahead of time rather than walk-in?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.memory_hook: Road tests run strictly by appointment
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: Road tests take long enough to administer that they are given only by appointment.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: How do the required tests for an original Class D or hardship applicant compare with a learner permit applicant?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.memory_hook: Three for licenses, two for permits
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: An original Class D or Class H applicant takes the knowledge test, the road skills test and the vision screening, while a Class PD applicant takes only the vision screening and knowledge test.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: Which exams apply when trading a Tennessee learner permit for Class D compared with renewing or replacing a card?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.memory_hook: Vision plus road; renewals take zero
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: Exchanging a Class PD permit for a Class D license needs only the vision screening and road skills test, while a duplicate or renewal needs no test at all.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: Which two screenings or exams are required when adding a For-Hire endorsement?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: Adding a For-Hire endorsement requires the vision screening and a knowledge test.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: When does a new resident take only the vision check versus taking all three Tennessee exams?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.memory_hook: Valid state card vision; otherwise three
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: A new resident with a current, valid out-of-state license takes only the vision screening, but one whose license is expired, or who comes from another country or never held a license, takes all three tests.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: What visual acuity score must you meet in each eye and both eyes together, with or without corrective lenses?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.memory_hook: Twenty over forty, each and together
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: The vision screening requires at least twenty over forty vision in each eye alone and in both eyes together, with or without glasses or contact lenses.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: What step must an applicant take if they cannot pass the counter vision screening?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.memory_hook: Bring an eye specialist's completed statement
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: An applicant who cannot pass the vision screening must have an eye specialist of their choice complete an eye statement for the Department to evaluate.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: Which manual sections feed the multiple-choice knowledge test, and how is it divided across four topics?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.memory_hook: Sections B and C, four quarters
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: The knowledge test is multiple choice, built from Sections B and C of the manual, and is expected to split roughly twenty-five percent each among traffic signs and signals, safe driving principles, rules of the road, and drugs and alcohol.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: How are knowledge tests normally administered, and which three non-English languages run on computerized terminals?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.memory_hook: Computer terminals; Spanish, Korean, and Japanese
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: Knowledge tests run on computerized testing machines, with written versions only in very limited cases, and computerized centers also offer Spanish, Korean and Japanese versions.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: What translation help may non-native English speakers use during testing, and what devices or helpers are banned?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.memory_hook: Clean dictionary; no electronics or interpreters
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: An applicant whose first language is not English may use a translation dictionary free of notes or handwriting, but phones, PDAs and electronic dictionaries are banned and interpreters may not help with any test.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: Who can schedule an oral knowledge exam at selected centers, and what extra proof must minors under eighteen bring?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.memory_hook: Reading or learning barriers; doctor's note
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: Oral knowledge tests are offered by appointment at selected centers for applicants who cannot read or have a learning disability, and an applicant under eighteen must first supply a physician's or educational specialist's written statement.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: How does the Department of Safety assist a deaf applicant who requests an oral knowledge test?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: When a deaf applicant asks for an oral knowledge test, the Department of Safety supplies a certified sign language interpreter to help administer it.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.front: Which age group may take the written knowledge exam online, and who supervises through the state proctor app?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.memory_hook: Teens fifteen to seventeen, parent proctored
sec04-card-sec04-F37.expected_back: Teens aged fifteen to seventeen who must take the written test may take it online, supervised by a parent or legal guardian acting as proctor through the Tennessee Proctor Identification (PID) App.

sec04-card-sec04-R17.front: How does the Tennessee proctor app verify an adult before they supervise an online teen knowledge test?
sec04-card-sec04-R17.memory_hook: Matches secure identity against state records
sec04-card-sec04-R17.expected_back: The Tennessee PID App lets an eligible proctor obtain a secure personal identification verified against the proctor's own Department of Safety record before supervising an online knowledge test.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: Can an applicant retake a failed Tennessee driver license exam later on that same day?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.memory_hook: Never repeat any test same day
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: No test may be repeated on the same day it was taken.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: How much must you pay again each time you fail a learner permit, Class D, or hardship exam?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.memory_hook: Pay the two-dollar application fee again
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: Each time you take and fail a PD, D or H test you pay the two dollars application fee again.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: How long must you wait to retry after failing a knowledge test the first time or on later attempts?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.memory_hook: Wait at least one full day
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: After failing any knowledge test you must wait at least one day before trying again, and the same wait applies after every later failure.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: What two immediate consequences hit anyone caught cheating on a required license exam?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: Any cheating on a required examination means automatic failure and a thirty-day wait before the test may be attempted again.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: How does the mandatory waiting period compare between failing a knowledge test honestly and getting caught cheating?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.memory_hook: One-day miss versus thirty-day cheat ban
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: Waiting periods differ by cause: a failed knowledge test means a one-day wait, while being caught cheating means a thirty-day wait before another attempt.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: What paperwork must you bring back to the center whenever you return to retake a failed exam?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.memory_hook: Bring every required original document again
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: Anyone returning to retake a test must bring all the required original documents again.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: Which three kinds of actions during an exam are treated as cheating?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.memory_hook: Hidden notes, talking, or test stand-ins
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Forms of cheating include written notes on paper, clothing, the body or devices, talking during the test including phone use, and trying to have someone else take the exam.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: Which personal communication devices must be switched completely off during both the written and road tests?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.memory_hook: Switch off phones, pagers, messaging devices
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: All cell phones, pagers and text messaging devices must be switched off during both the written test and the road test.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: By what two methods can you schedule a road test, and how many days ahead does booking open?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.memory_hook: Online or toll-free, forty-five days ahead
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: Road test appointments can be booked online or by toll-free phone up to forty-five days ahead of the desired test date.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: What happens to your road test appointment if you have not already passed the written knowledge test?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.memory_hook: Pass knowledge first or appointment cancels
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: You must already have passed the knowledge test before your road test appointment, or the appointment is canceled.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: What status document must an applicant without a valid Tennessee learner permit bring to the road test?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.memory_hook: Bring citizenship, residency, or legal-stay proof
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: An applicant without a valid Tennessee learner permit must bring proof of US citizenship or lawful permanent residency to the road test appointment, or current proof of temporary legal presence when getting a TDL.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: How much English proficiency must an applicant have when taking the behind-the-wheel road test?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.memory_hook: Enough English to understand examiner directions
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: Road test applicants must speak and understand enough English to communicate with the examiner during the drive.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: At least how many minutes before your scheduled road test should you arrive, and why?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.memory_hook: Arrive fifteen minutes early for paperwork
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: Plan to arrive at least fifteen minutes before the road test appointment so paperwork and documents can be processed.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: What happens if you check in more than five minutes past your scheduled road test time?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.memory_hook: Over five minutes late cancels test
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: Arriving more than five minutes late for a road test appointment cancels the test, and you must reschedule for a later date.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.front: How many minutes does a Tennessee road test average, and when does lateness force rescheduling?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.expected_back: Road tests average twenty to twenty-five minutes, and arriving five or more minutes late means the appointment must be rescheduled.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: Which severe weather conditions and winter time-of-day rule halt Tennessee road tests?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.memory_hook: No extreme storms or winter darkness
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Road tests are not given in extreme weather such as heavy rain or snow, dense fog, hail, high winds or icy roads, and in the winter months they are not given after dark.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: Which mild weather lets road tests proceed versus which severe conditions shut them down?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.memory_hook: Light precipitation proceeds; storms, floods cancel
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: Road tests go ahead in light to moderate rain, fog or snow but not in heavy rain, thunderstorms, thick fog, flooded or snow- and ice-packed roads, or during severe weather warnings.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.front: Under what two broad situations may the Department cancel scheduled road test appointments?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.memory_hook: Emergencies or dangerous weather cancel slots
sec04-card-sec04-R11.expected_back: The Department may cancel road test appointments during emergencies or dangerous weather.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.front: Who is allowed inside the car during a road test, are pets allowed, and will examiners ever ask for illegal moves?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.memory_hook: Applicant and examiner only, zero tricks
sec04-card-sec04-F32.expected_back: Only the applicant and the examiner, or other authorized personnel, may ride in the road test vehicle, no animal is allowed, and you will never be asked to do anything illegal.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: Does the state provide a road-test car, or what must the applicant bring?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.memory_hook: Supply your own fully working vehicle
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: You must supply your own road test vehicle, with all its operating equipment and safety features in working order.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: Starting with which model year must a passenger test car have working seat belts for both you and the examiner?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.memory_hook: Nineteen sixty-nine and newer, both seats
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: Any passenger vehicle built in nineteen sixty-nine or later must have safety belts in good working condition for both the applicant and the examiner.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: Which two separate braking systems must every car have by Tennessee law?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.memory_hook: Regular foot brake plus parking brake
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: By law every car needs two separate ways to apply the brakes: a regular foot brake and a parking brake.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: What minimum and maximum number of white headlights may a motor vehicle carry?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.memory_hook: Two minimum, four maximum white headlights
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: A motor vehicle must carry at least two and no more than four white headlights.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: Which five rear lights must work on a passenger car brought for testing?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.memory_hook: Plate light, two tails, two brakes
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: A passenger vehicle needs a rear license plate light, two red tail lights and two red brake lights.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: How many windshield wipers should a vehicle have, and when is a single wiper acceptable?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.memory_hook: Two wipers unless one sweeps full
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: A vehicle with a windshield should have two wipers, unless a single wiper clears to within one inch of the inside of the windshield.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: What mirror must every test vehicle have, and when are two outside mirrors also required?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.memory_hook: Unblocked rearview; two outside for impairments
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: The test vehicle needs at least one rearview mirror that does not block the driver's rear view, and two outside mirrors are also required for applicants with certain vision or hearing impairments.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: Beyond lights and brakes, what audible warning device and registration item must work and be current on your test car?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.memory_hook: Working horn and current registration tags
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: Every motor vehicle used for the road test must have a working horn and valid registration tags.

sec04-card-sec04-R13.front: What exhaust, dashboard, and front-door rules must your road-test car pass before driving?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.memory_hook: Quiet muffler, working speedometer, two-way doors
sec04-card-sec04-R13.expected_back: The test vehicle needs a muffler to prevent excessive noise and smoke, a working speedometer, and driver and passenger doors that open from both inside and outside.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: What window-tint limit applies to a passenger car's windshield and side or rear windows?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.memory_hook: Zero windshield tint, thirty-five percent windows
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: No tint may be applied to the windshield, and on a passenger car no window material may let through less than thirty-five percent of visible light.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.front: On a sport-utility or multi-purpose vehicle, which windows skip tint limits and which still follow the passenger-car rule?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.memory_hook: Rear windows exempt; front sides regulated
sec04-card-sec04-R12.expected_back: On a multi-purpose vehicle, windows behind the front seat are exempt from tint limits, but the windows to the driver's left and right follow the passenger car rule.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: Between what ground heights must bumpers sit on a passenger car versus a four-by-four recreational vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: Passenger car bumpers must sit fourteen to twenty-two inches above the ground, and 4x4 recreational vehicle bumpers fourteen to thirty-one inches.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: How many vehicle controls must you demonstrate before driving off, including which glass-clearing control?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.memory_hook: Demonstrate eight controls including windshield defroster
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: Before the road test the applicant must show how to use eight equipment items, including the windshield defroster and fan to defog the glass.

sec04-card-sec04-R16.front: Why should you bring a familiar car to the road test, and which six systems plus registration must be ready?
sec04-card-sec04-R16.memory_hook: Familiar car with working safety systems
sec04-card-sec04-R16.expected_back: Bring a familiar vehicle whose horn, lights, belts, brakes, signals and wipers all work and whose registration is current.

sec04-card-sec04-R14.front: Which core driving habits—from starting and backing to intersections, spacing, and signaling—does the road examiner grade?
sec04-card-sec04-R14.memory_hook: Every control, turn, stop, and signal
sec04-card-sec04-R14.expected_back: The examiner watches how you prepare and start, control the car, handle intersections and turns, obey signals and signs, drive in traffic, stop, back up, judge distance, signal to others, share the road and adjust speed.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.front: Which four actions end a Tennessee road test in immediate failure regardless of error count?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.memory_hook: Law violation, refusal, danger, or crash
sec04-card-sec04-F33.expected_back: A road test ends in immediate failure for any traffic law violation, refusing to cooperate or follow directions, any dangerous action, or contributing to an accident.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.front: How many road-test errors still pass, and what retest waits apply at seven-to-nine, ten-to-twelve, and thirteen-to-fifteen errors?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.memory_hook: Up to six passes; waits climb
sec04-card-sec04-F34.expected_back: On the road test, one to six errors is a pass, seven to nine errors means a retest the next day, ten to twelve errors means seven days, and thirteen to fifteen errors means fourteen days.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.front: How long must you practice before retesting after sixteen or more road-test errors or an automatic failure?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.expected_back: Sixteen or more road test errors, or an automatic failure, means a thirty-day practice period before a retest.

sec04-card-sec04-R15.front: What feedback does the examiner give you right after a failed road test?
sec04-card-sec04-R15.memory_hook: Explains mistakes, fixes, and practice maneuvers
sec04-card-sec04-R15.expected_back: After a failed road test the examiner explains the errors, how to correct them and which maneuvers to practice before returning.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: Under Tennessee law, at least what percentage of knowledge-test questions must cover impaired driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Tennessee law requires that no less than twenty-five percent of knowledge test questions deal with driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: Between ten at night and two in the morning, roughly what fraction of drivers are intoxicated?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Researchers estimate that between ten p.m. and two a.m., about one in every ten drivers on the road is intoxicated.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: What type of drinkers account for nearly half of all DUI arrests?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: Nearly fifty percent of drivers arrested for DUI are social or moderate drinkers rather than heavy drinkers.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: Where had more than one-third of late-night intoxicated drivers been drinking beforehand?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: Of the drivers estimated to be intoxicated late at night, more than one-third had been drinking at someone else's home.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: How soon after swallowing a drink does alcohol begin entering your bloodstream?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Alcohol begins passing into the bloodstream within one to two minutes after you drink it.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: How does drinking faster than your liver can oxidize alcohol affect blood concentration and intoxication?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: You become intoxicated when you drink alcohol faster than your liver can oxidize it, and the higher the share of alcohol in your blood, the more intoxicated you are.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: Roughly how fast does the liver oxidize alcohol, and do coffee, showers, or exercise help?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: The liver can oxidize only about one drink per hour, and coffee, exercise or a cold shower cannot speed that up; only time sobers a drinker.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: Roughly what share of alcohol does the liver break down, and how does liver disease change BAC?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: The liver breaks down roughly ninety percent of the alcohol in the body, so a damaged or diseased liver keeps BAC higher for longer.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: What health damage can chronic heavy drinking inflict across organs and specifically on the liver?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: Heavy, long-term drinking can harm nearly every organ, and its effect on the liver can lead to hepatitis and cirrhosis.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: What does blood alcohol concentration measure, and what does a higher number mean?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Blood alcohol concentration, or BAC, measures the percentage of alcohol in the blood, and the higher the number, the more impaired the person.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: Which BAC level is always illegal in Tennessee, and how many drops per ten thousand is it?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: In Tennessee a BAC of point zero eight is the intoxication level that is always illegal, which equals eight drops of alcohol for every ten thousand drops of blood.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: Which three primary variables govern how high your BAC climbs?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: Your BAC depends on your body weight, how long you have been drinking and how much alcohol you have had.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: Does body weight or drink category stop each drink within an hour from pushing BAC upward?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: Every drink taken within an hour pushes your BAC higher, whatever you weigh and whatever kind of alcoholic drink it is.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: How do three drinks finished inside one hour compare with three drinks spaced across three hours?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: Three drinks in one hour affect you more than the same three drinks spread over three hours.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: Between two drinkers of identical scale weight, why does the one with higher body fat show intoxication sooner?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: Because alcohol dissolves in water and not in fat, of two people with the same weight, the one with more body fat will show intoxication first.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: What happens when a smaller-framed person matches drink-for-drink with larger friends?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: A smaller person who tries to keep pace with larger friends' drinking will usually feel impaired judgment and lowered inhibitions sooner.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: How does eating beforehand affect alcohol absorption, and does food block alcohol from reaching your blood?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: Food in the stomach slows how fast alcohol is absorbed, but all of the alcohol still reaches the blood eventually.

sec12-card-sec12-F42.front: How does the alcohol inside a twelve-ounce beer compare with a one-ounce shot of whiskey?
sec12-card-sec12-F42.expected_back: A twelve-ounce bottle of beer holds about as much alcohol as a one-ounce shot of whiskey.

sec12-card-sec12-F43.front: Roughly how much time is needed to clear one drink versus three drinks?
sec12-card-sec12-F43.expected_back: It takes about one hour to cancel the effects of one drink and about three hours for three drinks.

sec12-card-sec12-R35.front: According to reliable studies, how many drinks within three hours impair driving for most people?
sec12-card-sec12-R35.expected_back: Reliable studies show that two or three drinks in three hours or less impair the driving of most people.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: Compared with sober driving, how many times likelier is causing a crash at point one zero, point one five, and point one seven BAC?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: Compared with a sober driver, a driver at point one zero BAC is seven times more likely to cause a crash, at point one five about twenty-five times, and at point one seven about fifty times.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: How low can BAC be when skill, judgment, and vision already suffer greatly, especially in young drinkers?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: Every person at a point one zero BAC is too impaired to drive safely, and driving skill, judgment and vision are greatly impaired at levels as low as point zero three and point zero four, especially in young drinkers.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: What estimated share of Americans will be involved in an alcohol-related crash during their lifetime?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: An estimated two in every five Americans, or forty percent, will be in an alcohol-related crash at some point in their lives.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: Which two abilities matter most for safe driving, and how much alcohol does it take to hurt both?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: Judgment and vision are the two abilities most important to driving, and small amounts of alcohol affect both.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: After how many drinks does your ability to judge speed, time, and distance begin changing?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: Your ability to judge speed, time and distance changes after only one drink.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: Which four reckless behind-the-wheel behaviors commonly reveal alcohol-impaired judgment?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: Alcohol-impaired judgment shows up as needless risks such as speeding, passing without enough clear distance, rushing around curves and showing off.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: How severely does alcohol cut clear night vision and affect headlight-glare recovery?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: Alcohol cuts your ability to see clearly at night by more than half and slows your recovery from headlight glare.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: What does alcohol do to your eye muscles that degrades focusing and glare vision?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: Alcohol relaxes the eye muscles so they cannot focus properly, which also makes glare vision poor.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: Why does alcohol ruin depth and distance judgment and raise head-on and rear-end crash risk?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: Alcohol makes each eye receive a slightly different picture, which throws off judgment of depth and distance and raises the risk of head-on and rear-end crashes.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: Almost what percentage of all driving information reaches you through your eyes?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: The eyes supply almost ninety percent of the information a driver uses, so any loss of vision can be disastrous.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: By roughly what percentage does peripheral side vision shrink at point zero five BAC?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: At a point zero five BAC, your side vision shrinks by about thirty percent.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: At how low a BAC do reaction time and physical coordination begin suffering?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: Reaction time and coordination start to suffer at a BAC as low as point zero two.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: What happens simultaneously to alertness, concentration, reactions, and coordination as drinking continues?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: As drinking increases, alertness and concentration fade while reaction time and coordination keep getting worse, a deadly combination behind the wheel.

sec12-card-sec12-R34.front: Which mental faculty is the very first thing alcohol impairs upon reaching the brain?
sec12-card-sec12-R34.expected_back: Alcohol quickly reaches the brain and disrupts the parts that control judgment, emotions and confidence, and judgment is the first thing affected.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: Is alcohol chemically a stimulant or a depressant, and why do small doses feel lively?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: Alcohol in any amount is a depressant, not a stimulant; the lift people feel from small doses comes from lowered inhibitions.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.front: How does alcohol affect nerve impulses and body functions needed for focused driving?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.expected_back: Alcohol slows all nerve impulses and body functions, which limits a driver's ability to stay alert and concentrate.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: What happens when alcohol mixes with another depressant like a tranquilizer or sedative?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: When alcohol is combined with another depressant such as a tranquilizer or sedative, the effects multiply rather than simply add together.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: Does holding a valid doctor's prescription legally excuse driving under that drug's influence?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: Having a prescription for a drug is no legal defense for driving under its influence.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.front: What question should you always ask when a doctor prescribes a sedative or tranquilizer?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.expected_back: If your doctor prescribes a tranquilizer or sedative, ask how it will affect your ability to drive safely.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: Which three impairing ingredients can hide inside over-the-counter cold, cough, and allergy remedies?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Over-the-counter cold tablets, cough syrups and allergy remedies can contain antihistamines, alcohol or codeine, so read the label warnings before driving.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.front: Which two classic bottle warnings flag driving risk, and whom should you ask when unsure?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.expected_back: Watch for medicine label warnings such as may cause drowsiness or do not operate machinery, and ask a doctor or pharmacist about any drug or drug combination you are unsure of.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.front: Which two essential driving faculties do studies show marijuana and other drugs impair?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.expected_back: Studies show marijuana and other drugs also affect judgment and motor skills, so driving under their influence is dangerous too.

sec12-card-sec12-R37.front: How can cold remedies fool sick drivers, and what happens if antihistamines mix with alcohol?
sec12-card-sec12-R37.expected_back: Cold medicines can make you feel well enough to drive while still dulling alertness, judgment, coordination and vision, and combining alcohol with antihistamines can be more dangerous than either alone.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: Where beyond public roads, and under what states of control or drug influence, does Tennessee DUI law apply?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: In Tennessee it is illegal to drive or be in physical control of a motor vehicle on a public road or in a place open to the public, such as a shopping center or apartment complex, while under the influence of any intoxicant, marijuana, narcotic or stimulant drug.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: At what blood or breath alcohol percentage is driving or physical control automatically illegal in Tennessee?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: It is also illegal in Tennessee to drive or be in physical control of a vehicle when your blood or breath alcohol concentration is point zero eight percent or higher.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: Can you still be convicted of DUI below point zero eight, or even at point zero zero BAC?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: A BAC under point zero eight does not clear you of DUI, and a driver can even be convicted with a BAC of point zero zero if drugs impaired the driving.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: Which three driver groups face stricter legal alcohol cutoffs below the standard point zero eight?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: Lower legal alcohol levels apply to younger drivers, commercial drivers and repeat offenders than the general point zero eight level.

sec12-card-sec12-R15.front: What speed or lane behaviors give police legal grounds to pull you over for a DUI check?
sec12-card-sec12-R15.expected_back: Erratic driving or a speed that is too fast or too slow is enough reason for an officer to stop a vehicle and investigate for DUI.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: What agreement do you automatically make under Tennessee's Implied Consent Law whenever you drive?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: Under the Implied Consent Law, driving in Tennessee means you have agreed to be tested for alcohol or drugs in your blood when an officer with reasonable grounds asks.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: How long will a court likely suspend your driving privileges if you refuse testing after arrest?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: If you are arrested and refuse the test an officer requests, the court will likely suspend your driving privileges for twelve months.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: What authority does Tennessee's No Refusal law give police investigating suspected impaired drivers?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: Tennessee's No Refusal law, passed in two thousand twelve, lets officers seek search warrants for blood samples from suspected impaired drivers.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: How do Tennessee DUI penalties for prescription, OTC, or illegal drugs compare with alcohol DUI?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: DUI penalties are the same whether the driver used alcohol or drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter drugs.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: What roadside probation duty and vest message apply to every Tennessee DUI conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: Any DUI conviction requires, as a probation condition, picking up litter for three eight-hour shifts while wearing clothing that says I am a DRUNK DRIVER.

sec12-card-sec12-R16.front: How must the state mark a photo ID issued to someone whose license is revoked for DUI?
sec12-card-sec12-R16.expected_back: If a person whose license was revoked for DUI applies for a photo ID during the revocation, the department must mark the ID to show the holder is a DUI offender.

sec12-card-sec12-R17.front: In which county does a Tennessee resident complete mandatory DUI litter-pickup shifts?
sec12-card-sec12-R17.expected_back: For a Tennessee resident, the DUI litter pickup is done in the offender's home county.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.front: What mandatory jail and fine minimums are added on top of DUI penalties with a passenger under eighteen?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.expected_back: Driving under the influence with a child under eighteen in the vehicle adds a mandatory minimum of thirty days in jail and a mandatory minimum one thousand dollars fine on top of other penalties.

sec12-card-sec12-R19.front: Which felony grades apply when a DUI seriously injures versus kills an accompanying child?
sec12-card-sec12-R19.expected_back: Under the Drunk Driving Child Protection Act, a DUI that seriously injures an accompanying child is a Class D felony, and one that kills the child is a Class C felony.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.front: Which criminal charges can follow an impaired crash that kills someone versus injures someone?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.expected_back: A driver under the influence who causes a crash that kills someone may be charged with vehicular homicide, and one that injures someone may bring an aggravated assault charge.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.front: After how many DUI convictions within what timeframe will Tennessee seize the offender's vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.expected_back: A driver's vehicle will be seized after two DUI convictions within five years when both events happened after January nineteen ninety-seven.

sec12-card-sec12-R18.front: What can happen to the car if someone already revoked for DUI gets caught driving on that revoked license?
sec12-card-sec12-R18.expected_back: A vehicle can be seized when a driver whose privileges are already revoked for DUI is charged with driving on that revoked license.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.front: How long after reinstatement must someone with two DUIs in five years use an ignition interlock?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.expected_back: A person with two DUIs within a five-year period must drive a vehicle with an ignition interlock device, which keeps the car from starting when the driver's BAC is too high, for six months after reinstatement.

sec12-card-sec12-R20.front: When must a judge order a formal drug-and-alcohol treatment assessment for a DUI offender?
sec12-card-sec12-R20.expected_back: A judge will also order a drug and alcohol treatment assessment, with treatment as needed, for an offender who had a prior DUI within the five years before the current one.

sec12-card-sec12-R21.front: Which three additional obligations can a court impose alongside standard DUI jail and fines?
sec12-card-sec12-R21.expected_back: Other court-ordered DUI requirements can include an alcohol safety DUI school where available, rehabilitation for second and later convictions, and restitution to injured victims when the offender can pay.

sec12-card-sec12-R22.front: Which out-of-pocket expenses push the real price of a DUI into several thousand dollars?
sec12-card-sec12-R22.expected_back: Beyond fines and court costs, a DUI can bring bond, attorney fees, lost work time, alcohol course and treatment fees and higher insurance premiums, adding up to several thousand dollars.

sec12-card-sec12-R23.front: What jail time, high-BAC jail boost, fine range, and revocation apply to a first DUI conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-R23.expected_back: The DUI penalty table lists a first conviction as forty-eight hours in jail, or seven days with a BAC of zero point two zero percent or more, a fine of three hundred fifty dollars to one thousand five hundred dollars and a one-year revocation.

sec12-card-sec12-R24.front: What jail span, fine range, and license revocation apply to a second DUI conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-R24.expected_back: The DUI penalty table lists a second conviction as forty-five days to eleven months and twenty-nine days in jail, a fine of six hundred dollars to three thousand five hundred dollars and a two-year revocation.

sec12-card-sec12-R25.front: How does Tennessee's DUI penalty table classify a fourth or subsequent DUI conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-R25.expected_back: According to the DUI penalty table, a fourth or later DUI conviction is a Class E felony.

sec12-card-sec12-R26.front: What is the leading cause of death among young people, and what share involves alcohol?
sec12-card-sec12-R26.expected_back: Traffic crashes are the leading killer of young people, and nearly half of those crashes involve alcohol.

sec12-card-sec12-R27.front: How high must BAC climb before most teenagers become intoxicated?
sec12-card-sec12-R27.expected_back: Most teenagers become intoxicated at low BAC levels.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.front: Why do young drivers face far higher crash odds than older drivers between point zero one and point zero eight?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.expected_back: Young drivers have a much higher crash risk than older drivers at BAC levels from point zero one to point zero eight, because of low alcohol tolerance and limited driving experience.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.front: What license loss hits an eighteen-to-twenty-year-old for buying or possessing alcohol, even away from any car?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.expected_back: If you are eighteen, nineteen or twenty and are convicted of buying, trying to buy or possessing alcohol, you lose your driving privilege for one year, or two years for a second offense, even if no vehicle was involved.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.front: How long do thirteen-to-seventeen-year-olds lose driving rights for first-offense alcohol or drug possession?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.expected_back: A person aged thirteen to seventeen found to have possessed, consumed or sold alcohol or drugs loses driving privileges for one year or until turning seventeen, whichever period runs longer, even without ever having held a license.

sec12-card-sec12-R28.front: For ages thirteen through seventeen, how long is the suspension on a second substance conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-R28.expected_back: A second juvenile alcohol or drug conviction for someone aged thirteen to seventeen brings a suspension of two years or until age eighteen, whichever is longer.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.front: At what BAC do sixteen-to-twenty-year-old drivers commit underage driving while impaired, and what penalties apply?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.expected_back: A driver aged sixteen to twenty found driving with a point zero two BAC or under the influence of alcohol or another intoxicant is convicted of underage driving while impaired, with a one-year license loss and a two hundred fifty dollars fine.

sec12-card-sec12-R29.front: What extra requirement can courts add to license loss and fines for underage driving while impaired?
sec12-card-sec12-R29.expected_back: Underage driving while impaired can also include public service work in addition to the license loss and fine.

sec12-card-sec12-R30.front: How does the designated-driver plan work, and how do many venues support that friend?
sec12-card-sec12-R30.expected_back: The designated driver approach, where friends agree in advance who will stay completely sober, is one of the most successful recent programs, and many night clubs give that driver free non-alcoholic drinks.

sec12-card-sec12-R31.front: Why must you decide not to drive before taking your very first drink?
sec12-card-sec12-R31.expected_back: Alcohol-related crashes are not accidents but preventable events, so decide before you start drinking that you will not drive, since the decision gets harder after a drink or two.

sec12-card-sec12-R32.front: Which three practical group habits keep drinkers off the driver's seat?
sec12-card-sec12-R32.expected_back: To avoid drinking and driving, go out in groups with a driver who agrees not to drink, ride with a sober friend, or hand your keys to a sober person before you start.

sec12-card-sec12-R33.front: What simple response works best when someone offers you alcohol and you are driving?
sec12-card-sec12-R33.expected_back: If someone offers you a drink and you plan to drive, simply decline and say you are driving.

sec12-card-sec12-R36.front: Which preventable hazard causes more deaths below age forty than any other cause?
sec12-card-sec12-R36.expected_back: Alcohol-related crashes are the number one killer of people under age forty.

sec12-card-sec12-R38.front: In the manual's two-thousand-twenty Tennessee data, what share of traffic deaths involved alcohol and also drugs?
sec12-card-sec12-R38.expected_back: In two thousand twenty, three hundred twenty-six Tennessee traffic deaths, or twenty-seven percent, were alcohol-related, and one hundred twenty-two of them also involved a driver who had used drugs.

sec12-card-sec12-R39.front: For two thousand twenty-one, what approximate shares of fatalities involved alcohol versus drugs or alcohol?
sec12-card-sec12-R39.expected_back: For two thousand twenty-one the manual reports about twenty-four percent of fatalities as alcohol-related and about forty-one percent as involving a driver impaired by drugs or alcohol.

sec12-card-sec12-R40.front: Nationwide in two thousand twenty, roughly what percentage of all US traffic deaths were alcohol-related?
sec12-card-sec12-R40.expected_back: Nationwide in two thousand twenty, eleven thousand six hundred fifty-four traffic deaths, about thirty percent of the total, were alcohol-related.

sec12-card-sec12-R41.front: Which addiction-services hotline listed in the manual offers toll-free alcohol and drug referrals?
sec12-card-sec12-R41.expected_back: The chapter was written with the Tennessee Association of Alcohol, Drug and Other Addiction Services, and its toll-free Redline at one-eight hundred-eight hundred eighty-nine-nine thousand seven hundred eighty-nine offers information and referrals.

sec12-card-sec12-R42.front: Why shouldn't you memorize only the chapter's end-of-section sample questions for your written knowledge exam?
sec12-card-sec12-R42.expected_back: The sample questions at the end of the chapter are only study aids, and the real knowledge test may use entirely different questions.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: Which drivers are recorded inside the National Driver Register?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: The National Driver Register lists people whose licenses were canceled, denied, revoked or suspended, or who were convicted of certain serious traffic violations.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: Which pointer system does Tennessee run against all fifty-one US jurisdictions before issuing a license?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Before issuing a license, Tennessee uses the Problem Driver Pointer System to search the National Driver Register, a national file of problem drivers reported by all fifty-one U.S. jurisdictions.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: Can Tennessee issue or renew your license while another state still reports an unresolved problem?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: If the search shows you have an unresolved problem in another state, Tennessee cannot issue you a license, even a renewal, until that state's matter is cleared.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: What limited info can Tennessee examiners give you about another state's hold, and whom must you call?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: Examiners can only tell you which state reported a problem and give a phone number for it; for details you must contact that state, because Tennessee does not hold them.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: Can both a DUI conviction and refusing an implied-consent blood-alcohol test cost you your Tennessee license?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: A Tennessee license may be revoked or suspended for DUI, including refusing a blood alcohol test under implied consent.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: What happens to your driving privilege if you lend your license out or fraudulently alter one?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: Letting someone else use your license or ID, or fraudulently altering a license, can cost you your license.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: What license consequence follows leaving a crash with injuries or death, or failing to stop and render aid?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: Leaving the scene of a crash that injures or kills someone, or failing to stop and give aid, is grounds for losing your license.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: How many reckless-driving violations in twelve months—or what street-racing offense—can trigger suspension or revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: Two reckless driving violations within twelve months, or drag racing, can lead to suspension or revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: What can happen to your driver license if you drive away from a gas station without paying?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: Driving away from a gas station without paying for fuel is grounds for losing your license.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: During which two roadside encounters can lacking active coverage proof trigger a Tennessee suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: Failing to show proof of insurance or financial responsibility to an officer after a crash or a moving violation charge can lead to suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: Which health conditions that interfere with safe control can result in suspension or revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: Mental or physical conditions that interfere with safe driving, such as Alzheimer's disease, seizures or loss of consciousness, can lead to suspension or revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: What license penalty applies to perjury or giving false ownership, use, or license-application facts?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: Perjury or giving false information about a vehicle's use or ownership or on a license application is grounds for losing your license.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: Which three serious criminal offenses behind the wheel are automatic grounds for revocation or suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: A felony involving a vehicle, evading arrest while driving, and manslaughter or vehicular homicide are all grounds for revocation or suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: What happens to habitual moving-violation offenders or drivers who ignore court crash-damage judgments?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: Being a habitual recipient of moving violations, or not complying with a court judgment for crash damages, can lead to losing your license.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: Which two non-driving legal violations can still cost you your Tennessee driver license?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: Buying or possessing alcohol under age twenty-one, or failing to meet child support requirements, can cost you your license.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: Having how many grams or more of methamphetamine inside a vehicle triggers license revocation or suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: A driver found with five or more grams of methamphetamine in a vehicle can have the license revoked or suspended.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: Must a drug or alcohol offense happen inside a car to cost a minor under eighteen driving privileges?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: A driver under eighteen can lose driving privileges for any drug or alcohol conviction, whether or not it happened while driving.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: Which three school-related issues can strip driving privileges from a driver younger than eighteen?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: A driver under eighteen can lose driving privileges for dropping out of school, failing to make satisfactory progress in school, or carrying weapons on school property.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: How many unexcused absences in a row—or total across a semester—count as dropping out under eighteen?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: For the under-eighteen rule, dropping out means ten days in a row or fifteen total days of unexcused absence in a semester.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.front: How many subjects must a driver under eighteen generally pass each grading period to keep driving?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.expected_back: For the under-eighteen rule, satisfactory school progress generally means passing three subjects each grading period.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: Within how many days must you surrender a suspended or revoked license, and what fine hits late returns?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: A suspended or revoked license must be turned in to the Department of Safety within twenty days, and failing to surrender it brings a seventy-five dollars fine on top of other fines and costs.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.front: Which three return options give you official credit for turning in a suspended Tennessee license?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.expected_back: You can turn in a suspended license at any Tennessee Highway Patrol office or Driver License Service Center to get credit for returning it, or mail it to the department.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: Except after final court convictions or judgments, what two steps precede license suspension or revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: Before suspending, revoking or canceling a license, the department notifies the driver in writing and offers a hearing, except in cases of final judgments and convictions.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.front: After an administrative hearing, which four corrective tools might the department try before suspending you?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.expected_back: After a hearing, the department may try education, re-examination, license restrictions and probation to improve poor driving habits before turning to suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: What is Tennessee's day-count deadline and three ways to file an address move?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: You must report a new address to the Department of Safety within ten days, and you can do it online, by letter or with a form at any Driver License Service Center.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.front: Must you get a reprinted plastic card immediately after reporting an address move?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.expected_back: Your new address may not appear on the card until a new, renewed or reinstated license is issued, but it must be correct on the official driver license file.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.front: What two problems can hit you if you fail to keep a current address on file?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.expected_back: Without a correct address on file you may miss important notices about your license status, and you could be ticketed.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: Under the Non-Resident Violator Compact, what happens if you ignore a ticket in Tennessee or a member state?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: Under the Non-Resident Violator Compact, if you ignore a traffic citation from Tennessee or another member state, your driving privileges will be suspended, revoked or canceled.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: How long does a Non-Resident Violator Compact suspension remain active?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: A compact suspension lasts until the court tells the department that the citation has been properly handled and the fees are paid.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: Which two official report sources add point values onto your Department of Safety driving record?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: Every traffic violation or crash on your Department of Safety record carries a point value, based on court reports and officers' crash reports.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: At how many points within twelve months does an adult driver aged eighteen or older face proposed suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: An adult driver aged eighteen or older who builds up twelve or more points within twelve months receives a notice of proposed suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: What twelve-month point total triggers a mailed advisory warning letter for an adult driver?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: An adult driver with six to eleven points within any twelve months is mailed an advisory letter as a warning.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: For a driver under eighteen, what twelve-month point counts trigger an advisory letter versus proposed suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: A juvenile driver under eighteen who builds up six or more points within twelve months receives a notice of proposed suspension, and one with one to five points is mailed an advisory letter.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.front: How often may you use a Defensive Driving Course to avoid or shorten a point suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.expected_back: A Defensive Driving Course can help you avoid a point suspension or shorten it, but that option is available only once in any five-year period.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.front: What payments and insurance filings are required to restore a license after a frequent-violation suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.expected_back: After a suspension for frequent violations, you must pay reinstatement fees and file proof of insurance, with SR-twenty-two insurance required for adults, before getting your regular license back.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.front: What determines your exact reinstatement steps, and which state office handles clearing records?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.expected_back: Reinstatement steps depend on why you lost your license and what else is on your record, and the department's Financial Responsibility office handles clearing a record.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.front: What two consequences hit if you get caught driving while your license is suspended?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.expected_back: Driving while your license is suspended extends the suspension and can lead to criminal prosecution.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: How many points hit your record for passing a stopped school, church, or youth bus loading passengers?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: Passing a stopped school, church or youth bus that is loading or unloading passengers carries eight points.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.front: How many points are assigned for failing to stop as required at a railroad crossing?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.expected_back: Failing to stop at a railroad crossing carries eight points.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.front: How many points do reckless driving versus careless or negligent driving add to your record?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.expected_back: Reckless driving carries six points, and careless or negligent driving carries four points.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.front: What point penalty hits a minor under eighteen caught using a phone behind the wheel?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.expected_back: Using a cell phone while driving under age eighteen carries six points.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.front: How many points apply for failing to yield to emergency vehicles or move over for roadside responders?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.expected_back: Failing to yield to emergency vehicles, or failing to change lanes or slow down for authorized vehicles on the roadside, carries six points.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.front: How many points apply when you contribute to a crash causing property damage, bodily injury, or death?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.memory_hook: Damage three, injury four, death eight
sec13-card-sec13-F30.expected_back: Contributing to a crash that causes property damage carries three points, one that causes bodily injury four points, and one that causes another person's death eight points.

sec13-card-sec13-R15.front: How many points apply to speeding one to five miles per hour over on normal roads versus work zones?
sec13-card-sec13-R15.expected_back: Speeding one to five miles per hour over the limit carries one point, or two points in a construction zone.

sec13-card-sec13-R16.front: How many points apply for speeding six to fifteen miles per hour over normally versus in construction zones?
sec13-card-sec13-R16.expected_back: Speeding six to fifteen miles per hour over the limit carries three points, or four in a construction zone.

sec13-card-sec13-R17.front: At sixteen through twenty-five over the limit, what points apply on open roads versus construction zones?
sec13-card-sec13-R17.expected_back: Speeding sixteen to twenty-five miles per hour over the limit carries four points, or five in a construction zone.

sec13-card-sec13-R18.front: What point totals apply at twenty-six to thirty-five, thirty-six to forty-five, and forty-six-plus over?
sec13-card-sec13-R18.expected_back: Speeding twenty-six to thirty-five miles per hour over carries five points, thirty-six to forty-five miles per hour over carries six, and forty-six miles per hour or more over carries eight.

sec13-card-sec13-R19.front: How many points do driving below a posted minimum speed or driving too fast for conditions each carry?
sec13-card-sec13-R19.expected_back: Driving below the posted minimum speed or too fast for conditions carries three points each.

sec13-card-sec13-R20.front: How many points are assigned to failing to yield right-of-way and to improper passing?
sec13-card-sec13-R20.expected_back: Failing to yield the right of way carries four points, and improper passing carries four points.

sec13-card-sec13-R21.front: Which four common tailgating, turning, backing, and blinker mistakes each carry three points?
sec13-card-sec13-R21.expected_back: Following too closely, an improper turn, improper backing and failing to signal each carry three points.

sec13-card-sec13-R22.front: How many points apply to vehicular reckless endangerment, fleeing police, and child endangerment?
sec13-card-sec13-R22.expected_back: Reckless endangerment by vehicle, fleeing a law enforcement officer and child endangerment each carry eight points.

sec13-card-sec13-R23.front: How do points compare between driving while suspended or revoked versus simply forgetting your card at home?
sec13-card-sec13-R23.expected_back: Driving when the required license is suspended, revoked or canceled carries eight points, while driving without your license in your possession carries two points.

sec13-card-sec13-R24.front: How many points apply for breaking printed license restrictions versus failing to report a crash?
sec13-card-sec13-R24.expected_back: Violating the restrictions printed on your license carries six points, and failing to report a crash carries four points.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.front: What limited driving does a restricted license permit during a suspension or revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.expected_back: A restricted license lets a driver whose license was suspended or revoked, but who needs to drive for work or school, drive only for the specific purposes written on it.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.front: Which prior convictions bar a driver from ever receiving a DUI restricted license?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.expected_back: A DUI restricted license is not available to a driver with a prior DUI or adult driving while impaired conviction within ten years, or a prior vehicular homicide, aggravated vehicular homicide or vehicular assault.

sec13-card-sec13-R25.front: Which six essential destinations can a court-ordered DUI restricted license authorize?
sec13-card-sec13-R25.memory_hook: Work, college, worship, probation, treatment, interlock
sec13-card-sec13-R25.expected_back: A driver convicted of DUI may get a court-ordered restricted license covering trips such as work, full-time college, worship, probation meetings, treatment programs and interlock appointments.

sec13-card-sec13-R26.front: When during a two-year DUI revocation may an offender seek an interlock-equipped restricted license?
sec13-card-sec13-R26.expected_back: After the first year of a two-year DUI revocation, a driver may apply for a restricted license by installing an ignition interlock for the rest of the revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-R27.front: Where does an adult suspended for frequent violations apply for a restricted license, and what is required?
sec13-card-sec13-R27.expected_back: An adult suspended for frequent traffic violations may apply to the Driver Improvement Section for a restricted license, with an approval letter, SR-twenty-two proof, tests and fees.

sec13-card-sec13-R28.front: Who can grant a restricted license after suspensions for implied consent, drag racing, or gas drive-offs?
sec13-card-sec13-R28.expected_back: A person suspended by the court for implied consent, drag racing or a gas drive-off may ask the trial judge for a restricted license for work, full-time college and interlock appointments.

sec13-card-sec13-R29.front: What limited travel can a minor suspended for drugs or alcohol request from the trial judge?
sec13-card-sec13-R29.expected_back: A minor who loses a license over drug or alcohol charges may ask the trial judge for a restricted license to drive to and from school or work.

sec13-card-sec13-R30.front: What limited driving relief is available during a suspension for an unsatisfied traffic citation?
sec13-card-sec13-R30.expected_back: A person suspended for an unsatisfied citation can get a certified court order allowing driving to and from work only, showing the fines paid or a payment plan.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.front: How many days do you have after departmental notice to submit a doctor's medical driving report?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.expected_back: When the department learns that a physical or mental condition affects someone's driving, that driver must send a doctor's medical report within thirty days of being notified.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.front: How long must a driver remain episode-free after losing consciousness from epilepsy, heart syncope, or diabetes?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.expected_back: A driver who loses consciousness or control from epilepsy, cardiac syncope, diabetes or a similar condition must be suspended and stay episode-free for at least six months before reinstatement.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.front: What happens if your driving ability is questioned and you ignore a re-exam or medical-report notice?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.expected_back: A driver whose ability is in question may be told to take a full or partial driver examination, and ignoring a request for an exam or medical report brings a suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-R31.front: How long does suspension last when a submitted medical report comes back unfavorable?
sec13-card-sec13-R31.expected_back: If a driver's medical report is unfavorable, the driving privilege stays suspended until the condition improves.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.front: What does liability insurance cover compared with collision insurance and uninsured-motorist coverage?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.expected_back: Liability insurance covers damage you cause to others, collision insurance covers damage to your own vehicle, and uninsured motorist insurance covers damage caused by uninsured drivers.

sec13-card-sec13-F36.front: Is collision coverage mandatory, and when must Tennessee drivers show proof of financial responsibility?
sec13-card-sec13-F36.memory_hook: Collision optional; proof at stops, crashes
sec13-card-sec13-F36.expected_back: Collision insurance is not required in Tennessee, but the Financial Responsibility Law requires you to show proof of financial responsibility whenever you are charged with a violation or are in a crash, whoever was at fault.

sec13-card-sec13-R32.front: Whom does Tennessee's Financial Responsibility Law protect the public against?
sec13-card-sec13-R32.expected_back: The Financial Responsibility Law protects the public from financially irresponsible drivers and from drivers with repeated violations or obvious disregard for traffic laws.

sec13-card-sec13-R33.front: Which two policy paperwork items count as valid proof of financial responsibility?
sec13-card-sec13-R33.expected_back: Accepted proof of financial responsibility includes your insurance policy declaration page or an insurance binder.

sec13-card-sec13-R34.front: Besides a declarations page or binder, which three items prove Tennessee financial responsibility?
sec13-card-sec13-R34.expected_back: Proof of financial responsibility can also be an insurance card from a company authorized in Tennessee, a commissioner's certificate for a cash deposit or bond, or proof of self-insurance.

sec13-card-sec13-F37.front: Which two state privileges get blocked after a conviction for failing to show financial responsibility?
sec13-card-sec13-F37.expected_back: Being convicted of failing to show proof of financial responsibility suspends your driving privileges and blocks renewal of your vehicle tags and registration.

sec13-card-sec13-R39.front: When a crash claim is filed with the state against you, which three options prevent losing license and tags?
sec13-card-sec13-R39.expected_back: When a claim against you is filed with the department, you must show you had liability insurance, get notarized releases from claimants, or post a cash or surety bond, or lose driving and registration privileges.

sec13-card-sec13-R40.front: Before a financial-responsibility revocation starts, how and when must you ask for a hearing?
sec13-card-sec13-R40.expected_back: You may request an administrative hearing before a financial responsibility revocation if you ask in writing on or before its effective date.

sec13-card-sec13-F38.front: Which crashes require immediate notice to local police, county sheriff, or Highway Patrol?
sec13-card-sec13-F38.expected_back: You must immediately notify local police, or the county sheriff or nearest Highway Patrol outside a city, of any crash causing death, injury or property damage over fifty dollars.

sec13-card-sec13-F39.front: What injury or single-person property-damage threshold makes a crash reportable to the Department of Safety?
sec13-card-sec13-F39.expected_back: A crash that kills or injures anyone, or damages any one person's property by more than four hundred dollars, is a reportable crash that must be reported to the Department of Safety.

sec13-card-sec13-R35.front: Who must handle reporting a crash if injuries leave the driver unable to give notice?
sec13-card-sec13-R35.expected_back: If the driver cannot give the crash notice because of injury, a passenger who is able must make or arrange the notice.

sec13-card-sec13-R36.front: What must you do if you strike an unattended vehicle or domestic animal and cannot locate its owner?
sec13-card-sec13-R36.expected_back: If a crash involves an unattended vehicle or a domestic animal and you cannot find the owner, report it to the police.

sec13-card-sec13-R38.front: Which two privileges can be suspended if you fail to file a required crash report?
sec13-card-sec13-R38.expected_back: Not reporting a crash may lead to suspension of both your driving and registration privileges.

sec13-card-sec13-F41.front: Where must you stop immediately after a crash, and why turn off the ignition?
sec13-card-sec13-F41.expected_back: Tennessee law requires drivers in a crash to stop immediately at or as near the scene as possible without blocking traffic, and to turn off the ignition to prevent a fire.

sec13-card-sec13-F42.front: When are you allowed to move an injured person out of a wrecked vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F42.expected_back: Do not move an injured person from a wrecked vehicle unless you have medical or rescue training or there is immediate danger such as fire.

sec13-card-sec13-R41.front: What immediate action is needed if a crashed vehicle catches fire?
sec13-card-sec13-R41.expected_back: If your car is on fire after a crash, help the people out and move them away from the vehicle in case it explodes.

sec13-card-sec13-R42.front: Whom should you call quickly after a crash, and what mindset and location are required?
sec13-card-sec13-R42.expected_back: Call nine one one to report a crash as quickly as possible, and remain calm and stay at the scene.

sec13-card-sec13-R43.front: Which details should you exchange with drivers and record from injured people and witnesses?
sec13-card-sec13-R43.expected_back: Exchange names, addresses and license numbers with other drivers, and get plate numbers plus the names and addresses of anyone injured and of each witness.

sec13-card-sec13-R44.front: Whose ownership and policy numbers must you also record, and whom should you notify promptly?
sec13-card-sec13-R44.expected_back: Also collect other vehicle owners' names, addresses and insurance policy numbers, and notify your own insurance company right away.

sec13-card-sec13-F43.front: If you encounter a crash without rescue training, how should you help without causing trouble?
sec13-card-sec13-F43.expected_back: If you come upon a crash and are not trained to give aid, call nine one one and keep driving slowly past so you do not get in the way of police and rescue crews or cause a secondary collision.

sec13-card-sec13-R45.front: What three steps should you take if you actually witnessed a crash happen?
sec13-card-sec13-R45.expected_back: If you saw the crash happen, pull safely off the road, turn on your emergency flashers and tell the officer or trooper that you are a witness.

sec13-card-sec13-R46.front: What driver behavior near an active crash scene triggers secondary collisions?
sec13-card-sec13-R46.expected_back: Secondary crashes near a crash scene are caused by drivers slowing to gaze at it out of curiosity.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.front: Besides people walking on foot, which mobility users count as pedestrians under Tennessee law?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.expected_back: Under Tennessee law, anyone on foot or using a motorized or non-motorized wheelchair counts as a pedestrian.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.front: Where do pedestrians generally hold right-of-way, and do unpainted intersections still contain crosswalks?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.expected_back: Pedestrians generally have the right-of-way at all intersections, and every intersection has a crosswalk even when no lines are painted.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.front: Even when technical right-of-way favors your car, what legal duty still governs driving near pedestrians?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.expected_back: Whatever the right-of-way rules say, the law requires drivers to use great care and extreme caution to avoid hitting pedestrians.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.front: Why must no part of your bumper sit across a crosswalk while waiting on red or turning?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.memory_hook: Blocking crosswalks forces walkers into traffic
sec16-card-sec16-F04.expected_back: Do not stop with any part of your vehicle over the crosswalk at a red light or while waiting to turn, because it forces pedestrians around your car.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.front: Which four groups of pedestrians suffer the highest share of car-pedestrian collisions?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.expected_back: Young, elderly, disabled and intoxicated pedestrians are the most frequent victims of car-pedestrian crashes, so watch for them especially.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.front: At what positions inside a crosswalk does a pedestrian trigger your legal duty to yield?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.memory_hook: Your road half or approaching closely
sec16-card-sec16-R02.expected_back: Yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk who is on your half of the road, or so close to it from the other half as to be in danger.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.front: Which side of your car needs special pedestrian checks, particularly during right turns?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.expected_back: Watch for pedestrians on your right, especially when you are making a right turn.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.front: Which pedestrians are hardest to see and least predictable, and near what five places must you slow?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.expected_back: Children are the least predictable and hardest-to-see pedestrians, so take extra care near school zones, bus stops, playgrounds, parks and snack vendors.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.front: Who gets right-of-way across driveways, alleys, or garage exits, and what horn or engine move is forbidden?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.memory_hook: Yield sidewalks; never honk or rev
sec16-card-sec16-R05.expected_back: Yield to people on the sidewalk when you enter or leave a driveway, alley, parking lot or garage across it, and never honk or rev your engine to rush a pedestrian.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.front: How long must you remain stopped for a crossing pedestrian when school-zone warning flashers are active?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.expected_back: In a marked school zone with its warning flashers on, you must stop for a pedestrian crossing in a marked crosswalk or at an intersection without one, and stay stopped until the pedestrian has crossed your roadway.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.front: Which two visual cues identify a blind pedestrian who always receives full right-of-way?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.memory_hook: Red-tipped white cane or guide dog
sec16-card-sec16-F06.expected_back: Always yield to a blind pedestrian carrying a white or metallic cane with a red tip or using a guide dog.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.front: May pedestrians walk in the street alongside an available sidewalk?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.expected_back: Where sidewalks exist, pedestrians must use them, and walking in the road there is illegal.
