sec16-card-sec16-R07.front: On which side and in what formation should pedestrians walk when no sidewalk exists?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.memory_hook: Left edge facing traffic, single file
sec16-card-sec16-R07.expected_back: Where there is no sidewalk, walk on the left side of the road facing oncoming traffic, in single file when walking with others.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.front: Why is wearing headphones risky while walking or jogging along busy streets?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.expected_back: Walking or jogging beside busy roads with headphones on can keep you from hearing traffic warnings.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.front: What four-part look sequence should a pedestrian complete at the curb before stepping out?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.expected_back: Before crossing, stop at the curb or road edge and look left, right and left again, then check over your shoulder for turning vehicles.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.front: Why should pedestrians waiting at an intersection corner step back when a bus or truck turns right?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.expected_back: Trucks and buses make wide right turns that can run up onto the corner of the sidewalk, so pedestrians on corners should step back.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.front: Why must a pedestrian never cut behind a truck that is backing up?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.expected_back: Never walk behind a truck that is backing up, because its driver cannot see directly behind it.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.front: What clothing should night walkers wear, and what handheld item gives the best visibility?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.expected_back: At night, pedestrians should wear bright or reflective clothing, and carrying a flashlight is the safest way to be seen.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.front: Does a green traffic light or white walk signal guarantee that stepping into the street is safe?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.expected_back: A WALK signal or a green light means it is your turn to cross, not that it is safe; look first and cross only if it is safe.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.front: What should you do if the don't-walk signal begins flashing after you are already halfway across?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.expected_back: If the DON'T WALK signal starts flashing while you are mid-street, keep walking, because you will have time to finish crossing.

sec16-card-sec16-R12.front: During which three signal phases are pedestrians barred from starting across unless a walk signal faces them?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.expected_back: Pedestrians may not cross on a red or yellow light, or on a mixed red and green turn light, unless facing a WALK signal.

sec16-card-sec16-R13.front: Why does the law forbid pedestrians from stepping off a curb directly in front of a close-approaching vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-R13.expected_back: Pedestrians must not step off the curb into the path of a vehicle so close that it is an immediate hazard, because vehicles cannot stop at once.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.front: Which two turning mistakes by motorists cause the majority of car-bicycle collisions?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.memory_hook: Turning left or right across riders
sec16-card-sec16-F10.expected_back: The most common car-bicycle crashes happen when a driver turns left in front of an oncoming bicycle or turns right across a bicycle's path.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.front: How should you time a left turn with an oncoming cyclist or a right turn with a cyclist on your right?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.expected_back: When turning left with a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction, wait for the rider to pass; when turning right with a bicyclist approaching on your right, let the rider through first.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.front: What legal status do bicyclists hold on most Tennessee streets, and from which highways are they barred?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.expected_back: On most roads bicyclists have the same rights and duties as other road users, but they are banned from limited-access highways, expressways and certain marked roads.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.front: On which side and in what direction must bicyclists ride on Tennessee roadways?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.expected_back: Bicyclists must ride on the right side of the road in the same direction as traffic, as far right as practical while avoiding hazards.

sec16-card-sec16-R14.front: Why is a bicyclist riding properly when moving toward lane center alongside a row of parked cars?
sec16-card-sec16-R14.expected_back: When a bicyclist rides away from parked cars toward the center of the lane, the rider is riding properly to avoid opening doors.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.front: How much side clearance and what pace does Tennessee law require when overtaking a bicycle?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.memory_hook: Pass slowly with three feet minimum
sec16-card-sec16-F14.expected_back: Tennessee law requires you to pass a bicycle going your way slowly and with at least three feet of clearance, keeping that space until you are safely past.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.front: What should you do instead of squeezing between a bicyclist and an oncoming car on a two-lane road?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.expected_back: Never pass between a bicyclist and oncoming traffic on a two-lane road; slow down and wait until it is safe.

sec16-card-sec16-R15.front: How do you handle sharing a left-turn lane with a cyclist versus preparing for a right turn near bikes?
sec16-card-sec16-R15.expected_back: If you share a left turn lane with a bicyclist, stay behind the rider until the turn is complete, and before a right turn merge with bicycle traffic rather than cutting across it.

sec16-card-sec16-R16.front: In which two tight street setups must you hold back instead of overtaking a bicycle?
sec16-card-sec16-R16.expected_back: Never pass a bicycle where the street is too narrow or the pass would push the rider close to parked cars.

sec16-card-sec16-R17.front: How should you alert an unaware cyclist before overtaking on a narrow road?
sec16-card-sec16-R17.expected_back: Before passing a bicycle on a narrow road when the rider may not know you are there, tap the horn gently and briefly instead of blasting it.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.front: May motorists use a signed and marked bicycle-only lane to turn, pass, or park?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.memory_hook: Never turn, pass, or park inside
sec16-card-sec16-F16.expected_back: A marked and signed bicycle-only lane must never be used by drivers for turning, passing or parking.

sec16-card-sec16-R20.front: How must you set your headlights at night when meeting an oncoming bicyclist?
sec16-card-sec16-R20.expected_back: At night, do not use your high beams when you see an oncoming bicyclist.

sec16-card-sec16-R18.front: How does a rider signal a left turn versus the two ways to signal a right turn by hand?
sec16-card-sec16-R18.memory_hook: Left straight; right bent-up or straight
sec16-card-sec16-R18.expected_back: Hand signals: a left turn is the left arm straight out, and a right turn is the left arm bent up at the elbow or the right arm straight out.

sec16-card-sec16-R19.front: What arm and palm position signals that a rider or driver is slowing down or stopping?
sec16-card-sec16-R19.expected_back: The hand signal for stopping or slowing is an arm held out and bent downward at the elbow, with the palm facing back.

sec16-card-sec16-R21.front: In which three situations may a bicyclist legally occupy the entire traffic lane?
sec16-card-sec16-R21.memory_hook: Passing, road hazards, or narrow lanes
sec16-card-sec16-R21.expected_back: A bicyclist may take the full lane when passing another vehicle, when the road has hazards such as potholes, debris or parked cars, or when the lane is too narrow to share.

sec16-card-sec16-R22.front: Which three protective habits does the manual stress for bicycle riders?
sec16-card-sec16-R22.memory_hook: Wear helmets, ride right, avoid curb-squeezing
sec16-card-sec16-R22.expected_back: Bicyclists should wear a helmet, never slip between a truck or bus and the curb, and ride on the right with the flow of traffic.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.front: What front and rear lighting or reflector visibility distance does Tennessee law require on bicycles at night?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.memory_hook: White front, red rear, five-hundred feet
sec16-card-sec16-F17.expected_back: Tennessee law requires a bicycle ridden at night to have a front lamp showing white light visible for at least five hundred feet and a red reflector or red lamp visible from five hundred feet behind.

sec16-card-sec16-R23.front: Why must drivers expect sudden turns and wobbles whenever children ride bicycles nearby?
sec16-card-sec16-R23.memory_hook: Young riders misjudge speed and traffic
sec16-card-sec16-R23.expected_back: Children on bicycles cannot judge traffic well, so expect erratic moves and sudden turns wherever children may be riding.

sec16-card-sec16-R24.front: From which concealed roadside spots can bicycles emerge abruptly into traffic?
sec16-card-sec16-R24.expected_back: Watch for bicycles coming out of driveways or from behind parked cars and other obstructions.

sec16-card-sec16-R25.front: What does an orange or red pennant mounted on a bicycle often tell approaching drivers?
sec16-card-sec16-R25.expected_back: A red or orange pennant flag on a bicycle commonly means the rider has impaired hearing, so slow down.

sec16-card-sec16-R26.front: How does a motorcycle's slim outline affect a car driver's eyes in traffic?
sec16-card-sec16-R26.memory_hook: Slim profile hides speed and distance
sec16-card-sec16-R26.expected_back: A motorcycle's narrow, short profile makes it harder to see and makes its distance and speed harder to judge.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.front: What error by automobile drivers causes two-thirds of car-motorcycle collisions?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.memory_hook: Turning across an unseen oncoming motorcycle
sec16-card-sec16-F18.expected_back: Research shows two-thirds of car-motorcycle crashes are caused by the car driver turning in front of the motorcycle, often without ever seeing it.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.front: How much lane width belongs to a motorcycle, and may a car drive beside one in the same lane?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.expected_back: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane, so never try to share a lane with one.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.front: Why must you avoid passing a motorcycle too closely or at excessive speed?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.memory_hook: Wind gusts shove riders off balance
sec16-card-sec16-F20.expected_back: Pass a motorcycle as you would a car, but not too close or too fast, because the blast of air can push the rider out of control.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.front: At least how many seconds of following distance must you maintain behind a motorcycle?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.memory_hook: Keep at least two seconds back
sec16-card-sec16-F21.expected_back: Allow at least a two-second following distance behind a motorcycle so the rider has time to maneuver or stop.

sec16-card-sec16-R27.front: Why are blind-spot head checks especially critical for spotting motorcycles before changing lanes?
sec16-card-sec16-R27.memory_hook: Motorcycles vanish easily inside blind spots
sec16-card-sec16-R27.expected_back: Motorcyclists riding alongside a lane of cars are often out of view, so check your blind spots before changing lanes.

sec16-card-sec16-R28.front: Why should you wait at an intersection until a motorcyclist's actual turn or straight move becomes unmistakable?
sec16-card-sec16-R28.memory_hook: Confirm rider's move before pulling out
sec16-card-sec16-R28.expected_back: At intersections, where most motorcycle crashes happen, wait until the rider's intention to turn or go straight is clear before pulling into the rider's path.

sec16-card-sec16-R29.front: Why is a motorcycle harder to judge after dark, and what beam courtesy still applies?
sec16-card-sec16-R29.memory_hook: Single lamp blends; dim high beams
sec16-card-sec16-R29.expected_back: At night a motorcycle's single headlight or taillight can blend with other lights and make its distance hard to judge, so dim your high beams for it as for any vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-R30.front: Which five weather, wind, or bridge surfaces make stability hardest for motorcyclists?
sec16-card-sec16-R30.memory_hook: Rain, crosswinds, truck gusts, rails, grates
sec16-card-sec16-R30.expected_back: Wet roads, crosswinds, truck wind blasts, railroad crossings and metal grated bridges all cause extra trouble for motorcyclists, so give them more room.

sec16-card-sec16-R31.front: Which road vehicles accelerate fastest off the line, and which accelerate slowest?
sec16-card-sec16-R31.expected_back: Motorcycles accelerate faster than any other vehicle, while trucks and buses are the slowest.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.front: In fatal collisions involving passenger cars and large trucks, who suffers seventy-eight percent of the deaths?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.expected_back: In crashes between cars and large trucks, the people in the car, usually the driver, suffer seventy-eight percent of the deaths.

sec16-card-sec16-R33.front: What single piece of safety equipment provides your strongest protection in a crash with a large truck?
sec16-card-sec16-R33.memory_hook: Buckling your safety belt protects most
sec16-card-sec16-R33.expected_back: A safety belt is the single most important protection in a crash with a large truck.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.front: How can you tell instantly whether a large truck's driver can see your car?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.memory_hook: No driver reflection means you're invisible
sec16-card-sec16-F23.expected_back: If you cannot see the truck driver in the truck's mirror, the truck driver cannot see you.

sec16-card-sec16-F24.front: Up to how much can a loaded semi weigh, and how does fifty-five-mile-per-hour stopping compare between cars and semis?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.memory_hook: Eighty thousand pounds; four-fifty-foot truck stops
sec16-card-sec16-F24.expected_back: A loaded tractor-trailer may weigh up to eighty thousand pounds, and a car at fifty-five miles per hour can stop in about two hundred forty feet while a truck at that speed needs about four hundred fifty feet or more.

sec16-card-sec16-R34.front: Roughly what share of American communities rely solely on trucks for freight, and how long can rigs stretch?
sec16-card-sec16-R34.memory_hook: Seventy-seven percent communities; over seventy feet
sec16-card-sec16-R34.expected_back: Trucks are the only delivery and pickup method for about seventy-seven percent of America's communities, and a tractor-trailer combination can be longer than seventy feet.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.front: Why do large trucks swing left before turning right, and why must you never slip beside them?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.memory_hook: Wide setups hide right-side blind zones
sec16-card-sec16-F25.expected_back: Trucks must swing wide to the left to make a right turn, and they cannot see cars or motorcycles directly behind or beside them.

sec16-card-sec16-R32.front: Why is darting sharply in front of a moving bus or tractor-trailer so dangerous?
sec16-card-sec16-R32.expected_back: Cutting in front of a truck or bus can force an emergency stop it cannot make in time, so look for its front in your mirror before pulling in.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.front: When may you pull back ahead of a passed truck, and what must your speed do afterward?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.memory_hook: See whole cab front; keep pace
sec16-card-sec16-F26.expected_back: After passing a truck, do not move back in front of it until you can see the whole front of the truck in your rearview mirror, and do not slow down once you are ahead.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.front: Which four areas around a tractor-trailer make up its blind spots, and how far back does the rear one stretch?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.memory_hook: Front, both sides, two-hundred feet back
sec16-card-sec16-F27.expected_back: A truck's blind spots cover the area right in front of it, along both sides and up to two hundred feet behind it.

sec16-card-sec16-R36.front: How many feet directly ahead of a conventional long-hood bumper can disappear from the trucker's view?
sec16-card-sec16-R36.memory_hook: Ten to twenty feet hidden ahead
sec16-card-sec16-R36.expected_back: A trucker with a long hood may not see the first ten to twenty feet in front of the bumper.

sec16-card-sec16-R35.front: How should you take an upcoming highway exit when traveling near a truck or bus?
sec16-card-sec16-R35.memory_hook: Ease off and exit behind trucks
sec16-card-sec16-R35.expected_back: Do not drive directly behind a truck or bus, and if you are exiting, slow down and exit behind the truck instead of cutting in front of it.

sec16-card-sec16-R38.front: How does a truck's or bus's large size trick approaching drivers into misjudging its speed?
sec16-card-sec16-R38.memory_hook: Large vehicles appear slower than reality
sec16-card-sec16-R38.expected_back: Because of their size, trucks and buses often look slower than they really are.

sec16-card-sec16-R39.front: What does a truck or bus driver communicate by blinking headlights after you overtake them?
sec16-card-sec16-R39.memory_hook: Clear to return once mirror confirms
sec16-card-sec16-R39.expected_back: If a truck or bus driver blinks the headlights after you pass, it signals that you may move back in, once you can see the truck's front in your mirror.

sec16-card-sec16-R37.front: Which lane should you vacate when passing a highway commercial weigh station, and why?
sec16-card-sec16-R37.memory_hook: Clear right lane for merging trucks
sec16-card-sec16-R37.expected_back: Avoid the right lane near a commercial vehicle weigh station so slow trucks can merge back onto the road.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.front: Where should you position your car when stopped uphill behind a large truck?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.memory_hook: Stay left with extra rollback space
sec16-card-sec16-F28.expected_back: On an uphill grade, keep to the left side of your lane while waiting behind a truck so its driver can see you, and leave extra room in case it rolls back.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.front: How should you position your car and manage speed while a truck or bus overtakes you?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.memory_hook: Hold far side and ease speed
sec16-card-sec16-F29.expected_back: When a truck passes you, keep to the far side of your lane and slow slightly, and never speed up while a truck or bus is passing.

sec16-card-sec16-R40.front: Where should you steer when meeting an oncoming semi on a two-lane road, and what wind force hits?
sec16-card-sec16-R40.memory_hook: Keep far right against air push
sec16-card-sec16-R40.expected_back: When meeting a truck from the opposite direction, keep as far right as you can, because the wind turbulence between vehicles pushes them apart.

sec16-card-sec16-R41.front: How does hill grade change a truck's speed, and what must you avoid after passing one downhill?
sec16-card-sec16-R41.memory_hook: Slow uphill, fast downhill; maintain pace
sec16-card-sec16-R41.expected_back: Trucks lose speed climbing hills but travel faster downhill, so after passing one on a downgrade keep your speed instead of slowing in front of it.

sec16-card-sec16-R42.front: How should you adjust lane position when heavy truck tire spray obscures your windshield in rain?
sec16-card-sec16-R42.memory_hook: Position farthest away inside your lane
sec16-card-sec16-R42.expected_back: In rain or standing water, a truck's spray can badly cut your vision, so move as far from it as you can within your lane.

sec16-card-sec16-F30.front: Why must you never slip behind a truck stopped to back into a dock or driveway?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.memory_hook: Rear blind spots hide your car
sec16-card-sec16-F30.expected_back: Never cross behind a truck that is getting ready to back up, since you will be in the driver's blind spots.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.front: What emergency do smoking wheels or runaway speed on a downhill truck warn of, and how should you react?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.memory_hook: Failed brakes; drop back, never pass
sec16-card-sec16-F31.expected_back: If a truck going downhill has smoking wheels or is moving too fast, it may have lost its brakes, so fall back and do not pass.

sec16-card-sec16-R43.front: Why do hazardous-materials trucks demand extra following room?
sec16-card-sec16-R43.memory_hook: Hazmat rigs stop frequently at tracks
sec16-card-sec16-R43.expected_back: Do not follow too closely behind trucks carrying hazardous materials, which make frequent stops such as at railroad crossings.

sec16-card-sec16-R44.front: Why is stopping or parking near a highway runaway truck ramp strictly forbidden?
sec16-card-sec16-R44.expected_back: Never stop or park in a runaway truck ramp, which exists to stop out-of-control trucks and buses on steep downgrades.

sec16-card-sec16-F32.front: Which age group suffers most school-bus fatalities, and how do those tragedies happen?
sec16-card-sec16-F32.memory_hook: Walkers five to seven near buses
sec16-card-sec16-F32.expected_back: Most children killed in school bus crashes are pedestrians aged five to seven, hit by the bus or by drivers illegally passing a stopped school bus.

sec16-card-sec16-R45.front: During what exact moment do nearly three-quarters of school-bus pedestrian fatalities occur?
sec16-card-sec16-R45.memory_hook: While children board or exit buses
sec16-card-sec16-R45.expected_back: Nearly three of every four school bus pedestrian deaths happen while children are getting on or off the bus.

sec16-card-sec16-F33.front: How many feet and giant steps away from a school bus are children taught to walk, requiring drivers to stop well back?
sec16-card-sec16-F33.memory_hook: Ten feet, or five giant steps
sec16-card-sec16-F33.expected_back: Children are taught to stay ten feet from a school bus and take five giant steps away from it, so drivers must stop far enough back to leave that space.

sec16-card-sec16-F34.front: Which three types of low-speed traffic must mount a reflective orange triangle on the rear?
sec16-card-sec16-F34.expected_back: Animal-drawn vehicles, most farm vehicles and construction equipment must display the slow-moving vehicle emblem, a fluorescent or reflective orange triangle, on the rear.

sec16-card-sec16-F35.front: What speed and two turning quirks make farm equipment tricky to overtake?
sec16-card-sec16-F35.expected_back: Farm machinery usually has no turn signals, may swing wide left before turning right, and usually travels under twenty-five miles per hour

sec16-card-sec16-R46.front: What legal road rights and traffic duties apply to animal-drawn carriages and wagons?
sec16-card-sec16-R46.memory_hook: Same roadway rights and traffic rules
sec16-card-sec16-R46.expected_back: Animal-drawn vehicles have the same rights to the road as motor vehicles and must follow the same rules.

sec16-card-sec16-R47.front: What must you confirm before pulling out to pass a slow tractor near farm fields?
sec16-card-sec16-R47.expected_back: Slow-moving vehicles may turn into unmarked entrances, so make sure the driver has seen you and knows you intend to pass before you go around.

sec16-card-sec16-F36.front: How must you control speed, spacing, horn, and engine noise when passing a horse on the road?
sec16-card-sec16-F36.memory_hook: Slow, wide, zero horn or revving
sec16-card-sec16-F36.expected_back: When approaching or passing a horse being ridden or led along the road, use due care, keep a reasonable speed and distance, and do not honk or rev your engine.

sec16-card-sec16-R48.front: What background color and message identify temporary highway construction and maintenance signs?
sec16-card-sec16-R48.memory_hook: Orange background warns road work ahead
sec16-card-sec16-R48.expected_back: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols, and the color orange always means road work ahead, slow down.

sec16-card-sec16-F37.front: Up to how much can a Tennessee speeding fine reach inside a reduced-speed work zone with workers present?
sec16-card-sec16-F37.expected_back: In Tennessee, speeding in a reduced-speed work zone where transportation or construction workers are present brings a fine of up to five hundred dollars.

sec16-card-sec16-R49.front: At sixty miles per hour, how many seconds remain before reaching cones after passing a fifteen-hundred-foot warning sign?
sec16-card-sec16-R49.memory_hook: Eighty-eight feet per second leaves seventeen
sec16-card-sec16-R49.expected_back: A car going sixty miles per hour covers eighty-eight feet per second, so a Road Work one thousand five hundred Feet sign leaves you only seventeen seconds before the work zone.

sec16-card-sec16-F38.front: When should you merge after spotting a work-zone lane-closure sign, and what risks hit last-second mergers?
sec16-card-sec16-F38.memory_hook: Merge immediately; late mergers risk tickets
sec16-card-sec16-F38.expected_back: Merge as soon as you learn a lane is closing ahead in a work zone; a last-chance merger can be ticketed and blamed for a crash.

sec16-card-sec16-R50.front: What lighting and lane-holding rules apply as you enter and travel through a work zone?
sec16-card-sec16-R50.expected_back: Turn on your headlights before entering a work zone, and do not change lanes inside it unless told to.

sec16-card-sec16-F39.front: Which collision type dominates work zones, and what spacing prevents it?
sec16-card-sec16-F39.expected_back: Most work zone crashes are rear-end collisions, so do not tailgate and keep a safe distance from barriers, equipment and workers.

sec16-card-sec16-R51.front: How long must you obey mobile work-zone signs for mowing, patching, or striping even before seeing crews?
sec16-card-sec16-R51.memory_hook: Obey signs past End Road Work
sec16-card-sec16-R51.expected_back: Mobile work zones such as line painting, patching and mowing mean workers may be ahead even if not yet visible, so heed the signs until you pass the End Road Work sign.

sec16-card-sec16-F40.front: Who always holds right-of-way at rail crossings, and how far does a fifty-five-mile-per-hour freight train take to stop?
sec16-card-sec16-F40.memory_hook: Always trains; full mile to stop
sec16-card-sec16-F40.expected_back: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to trains, because a train cannot stop quickly; one going fifty-five miles per hour needs a full mile to stop.

sec16-card-sec16-R52.front: Roughly how many times higher is fatality risk in a train collision than in a car or truck crash?
sec16-card-sec16-R52.memory_hook: Thirty times deadlier than road crashes
sec16-card-sec16-R52.expected_back: Your chance of dying in a crash with a train is about thirty times higher than in a crash with a car or even a large truck.

sec16-card-sec16-R53.front: At what kind of crossings and within how many miles of home do most train-car wrecks occur?
sec16-card-sec16-R53.expected_back: Over half of train-car collisions happen at crossings with lights, bells or gates, and most occur within twenty-five miles of the driver's home.

sec16-card-sec16-F41.front: Between what maximum and minimum distances from the nearest rail must you stop when crossing signals activate?
sec16-card-sec16-F41.memory_hook: Stop fifteen to fifty feet back
sec16-card-sec16-F41.expected_back: At a railroad crossing with electric or mechanical signals, a driver who must stop has to do so within fifty feet but no closer than fifteen feet from the nearest rail.

sec16-card-sec16-R54.front: What exact sequence is required at a railroad crossing posted with a red stop sign?
sec16-card-sec16-R54.memory_hook: Complete stop, then check both ways
sec16-card-sec16-R54.expected_back: At a railroad crossing with a stop sign, come to a complete stop and cross only after looking both ways for a train.

sec16-card-sec16-F42.front: When is it legal to drive around lowered railroad gates, and when may you roll forward?
sec16-card-sec16-F42.memory_hook: Never weave; wait until lights stop
sec16-card-sec16-F42.expected_back: Never drive around lowered crossing gates; stay stopped until the gates are fully up and the lights have stopped flashing.

sec16-card-sec16-F43.front: What must you do if warning lights flash or gates start lowering after your car is already on the rails?
sec16-card-sec16-F43.expected_back: If the lights start flashing or the gates begin to lower while you are already on the tracks, keep moving across and never back up.

sec16-card-sec16-R55.front: What hidden danger must you check for after a train clears a multi-track crossing?
sec16-card-sec16-R55.memory_hook: Check both ways for second train
sec16-card-sec16-R55.expected_back: Where there is more than one track, make sure a second train is not coming from either direction before you cross after a train passes.

sec16-card-sec16-F44.front: What immediate steps apply if your vehicle stalls dead on railroad tracks, even with no train visible?
sec16-card-sec16-F44.memory_hook: Evacuate everyone immediately, call blue sign
sec16-card-sec16-F44.expected_back: If your vehicle stalls on the tracks, everyone should get out at once and move away from the tracks, even if no train is in sight, then call the number on the blue Emergency Notification System sign or nine one one.

sec16-card-sec16-F45.front: In what direction and angle should you run if a train is approaching your stalled car on the tracks?
sec16-card-sec16-F45.expected_back: If a train is coming toward your stalled vehicle, run toward the train at a forty-five-degree angle away from the tracks to avoid flying debris.

sec16-card-sec16-F46.front: Which three vehicle types must stop at every rail crossing, and what passing ban applies on two-way roads?
sec16-card-sec16-F46.memory_hook: School, passenger buses, hazmat; never pass
sec16-card-sec16-F46.expected_back: School buses, passenger buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials must stop at every railroad crossing, and you must never pass them there on a two-way road.

sec16-card-sec16-R56.front: Under what sole condition may you pass a stopped bus or hazmat truck at a multi-lane railroad crossing?
sec16-card-sec16-R56.memory_hook: Only when crossing signals stay inactive
sec16-card-sec16-R56.expected_back: On a multi-lane road, do not pass a bus or hazardous materials truck stopped at a crossing unless the crossing's signals or gates are clearly not activated.

sec16-card-sec16-F47.front: Which occupants inside a fifteen-passenger van must wear safety belts under Tennessee law?
sec16-card-sec16-F47.memory_hook: Every occupant buckled at all times
sec16-card-sec16-F47.expected_back: Tennessee law requires every occupant of a fifteen-passenger van to wear a safety belt at all times.

sec16-card-sec16-R57.front: Does Tennessee require a special commercial endorsement to drive a fifteen-passenger van, and what is advised?
sec16-card-sec16-R57.memory_hook: No special endorsement; training strongly advised
sec16-card-sec16-R57.expected_back: No special endorsement or license is needed to drive a fifteen-passenger van in Tennessee, but the driver should be trained and experienced.

sec16-card-sec16-R58.front: How should you seat riders and handle roof cargo or trailers to keep a fifteen-passenger van stable?
sec16-card-sec16-R58.memory_hook: Seat riders forward; skip trailers, roof-loads
sec16-card-sec16-R58.expected_back: In a fifteen-passenger van, seat passengers as far forward as possible and do not tow trailers or load the roof, which raise rollover risk.

sec16-card-sec16-R59.front: Which heavy road vehicles do recreational vehicles handle like in stopping distance and visibility?
sec16-card-sec16-R59.memory_hook: Recreational vehicles handle like large trucks
sec16-card-sec16-R59.expected_back: Recreational vehicles handle more like large trucks, need longer stopping distances and have many blind spots.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: Which everyday vehicles are covered under a Tennessee Class D driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.memory_hook: Class D covers everyday passenger cars
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: Class D is the license for ordinary passenger vehicles that are not used for commercial purposes, other than the vehicles that fall into Classes A, B, C or M.
pills: NOT A B C OR M

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: Which types of two-wheeled vehicles belong under Class M on Tennessee's license chart?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.memory_hook: Class M covers motorcycles and cycles
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: Class M on the license chart covers motorcycles and motor-driven cycles.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: What does Class P represent on Tennessee's license chart, and how is it paired when issued?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.memory_hook: Class P pairs with another class
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: Class P on the license chart is an instructional permit, issued together with a Class A, B, C, D or M license.
pills: A B C D OR M

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: Who qualifies for a Class H license on Tennessee's chart, and why is it granted?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.memory_hook: Class H serves young hardship cases
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: Class H on the license chart is a hardship license for drivers aged fourteen to sixteen who face special hardship.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: How does the meaning of the letter H change between a license class and an endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.memory_hook: Class H hardship, endorsement H hazmat
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: The letter H means two different things on the license chart: Class H is the hardship license for young drivers, while the H endorsement covers hazardous materials.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: How does Class P differ from the P endorsement on Tennessee's license chart?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.memory_hook: Class P permit, endorsement P passengers
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: The letter P also does double duty: Class P is an instructional permit, while the P endorsement covers vehicles designed to seat sixteen or more people including the driver.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: When must a Class D driver add the F endorsement to their Tennessee license?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.memory_hook: Hired mainly to haul needs F
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: The F (For Hire) endorsement applies when a Class D vehicle is driven by someone employed mainly to drive it as a public or common carrier of people or property.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: What cargo types are covered by the N endorsement versus the X endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.memory_hook: N hauls tanks, X adds hazmat
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: The N endorsement covers tanks holding one thousand gallons or more, and the X endorsement combines tanks with hazardous materials.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: Which specialized vehicles require the T endorsement versus the S endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.memory_hook: T pulls multiples, S drives schoolbuses
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: The T endorsement covers double and triple trailers, and the S endorsement covers school buses.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: Can a Tennessee Class M credential stand by itself, or must it share a card with another class?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.memory_hook: Standalone Class M or combined card
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: Class M can be issued as a license on its own or alongside another primary class on the same card.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: How does engine size in cubic centimeters divide a regular Class M license from a Class M limited license?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.memory_hook: One twenty-five splits full from limited
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: A motorcycle above one hundred twenty-five cubic centimeters calls for a Class M license, while one below one hundred twenty-five cubic centimeters calls for a Class M limited license.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: What three restrictions apply to off-road vehicles on road tests, highways, and roadway crossings?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.memory_hook: No tests, no highways, ninety-degree crossings
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: Off-road vehicles and ATVs cannot be used for the road test, may not be driven on Tennessee or federal highways, and may cross a roadway only at a ninety-degree angle.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: At what minimum vehicle weight must a driver hold a Class A, B, or C commercial license?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.memory_hook: Twenty-six thousand one triggers commercial class
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: Vehicles weighing twenty-six thousand one pounds or more require a Commercial Driver License in Class A, B or C.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: Which everyday vehicles does a commercial license cover automatically, and which two-wheeler still needs its own class?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.memory_hook: Commercial covers Class D, never motorcycles
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: A valid Class A, B or C commercial license also covers Class D vehicles, so no separate Class D is needed, but riding a motorcycle still requires adding Class M, as in Class AM.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: Which two state-issued credentials allow a Tennessee resident to legally operate a motor vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.memory_hook: Hold a Tennessee license or temporary
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: Every Tennessee resident who drives a motor vehicle needs either a valid Tennessee driver license or a Temporary Driver License (TDL).

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: Which three milestones require a newcomer holding an out-of-state license to apply for a Tennessee credential?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.memory_hook: Thirty days, local job, voter status
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: A newcomer with a valid license from another state or country must apply for a Tennessee license or TDL after living in Tennessee more than thirty days, upon working in Tennessee, or once they would qualify as a registered Tennessee voter.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: What is the maximum vehicle weight you may legally drive with a Tennessee Class D license?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.memory_hook: Class D caps at twenty-six thousand
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: A Class D license lets you drive any vehicle weighing up to twenty-six thousand pounds at most.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: Which three uses push a vehicle under twenty-six thousand pounds out of Class D and into Class C?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.memory_hook: Hazmat, sixteen riders, or school bus
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: A vehicle under twenty-six thousand pounds still needs a Class C license, not Class D, if it hauls hazardous materials, carries sixteen or more people counting the driver, or serves as a school bus.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: What minimum age and three tests apply to Class D, plus what extra system governs applicants under eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.memory_hook: Sixteen, three exams, intermediate teen rules
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: To get a Class D license you must be at least sixteen and pass a vision screening, a knowledge test and a driving test, and anyone under eighteen must also meet the Intermediate Class D rules.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: Which Class D workers, such as shuttle, ambulance, taxi, or courier drivers, must carry a For-Hire endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: Drivers whose main job is carrying people or property in a Class D vehicle, such as taxi, shuttle or ambulance drivers and couriers, must add a For-Hire endorsement.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Do tradespeople like plumbers, engineers, or meter readers need a state For-Hire endorsement to drive on the job?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.memory_hook: Incidental work driving skips state For-Hire
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: People who drive only in the course of another job, such as plumbers, meter readers and engineers, generally do not need the For-Hire endorsement, although an employer may still require it.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: What fee, vehicle class, driving experience, and age rules are required to add the For-Hire endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.memory_hook: Four-fifty, two years, eighteen or family
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: Adding the For-Hire endorsement costs four dollars and fifty cents and requires operating a Class D vehicle, having two years of unrestricted driving experience, and being at least eighteen, or sixteen for exclusive family-business deliveries.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: How old must a For-Hire applicant normally be, and when can a sixteen-year-old qualify?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.memory_hook: Eighteen normally, sixteen for family deliveries
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: For-Hire applicants must be at least eighteen, or sixteen when the vehicle belongs to their family business and is used only for that business's deliveries.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: Which two screenings or exams must an applicant pass to earn the For-Hire endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.memory_hook: Pass vision plus Section B exam
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: For-Hire applicants take a vision screening plus a separate knowledge test built from Section B of the manual.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: Between which two license categories does the Tennessee manual place the For-Hire endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.memory_hook: Bridge between private and commercial licenses
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: The manual describes the For-Hire endorsement as a bridge between the regular license for private travel and the commercial license needed for tractor-trailers, large trucks and buses.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: What minimum age and two exam steps are required to earn a Tennessee passenger learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.memory_hook: Turn fifteen, pass written and vision
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: A Class PD learner permit requires being at least fifteen and passing the Class D written knowledge test and vision screening.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: Who must accompany a passenger learner permit holder while driving, and which seat must they occupy?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.memory_hook: Licensed adult twenty-one right beside you
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: A Class PD holder may drive only with a licensed driver who is at least twenty-one and sits in the seat beside them.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: What test trades a passenger learner permit for Class D, and how long must teens under eighteen hold the permit first?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.memory_hook: One eighty permit days, road test
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: Trading a Class PD for a Class D requires a road skills test, and drivers under eighteen must first have held the PD for one hundred eighty days under the Graduated Driver License law.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: When does a learner permit holder advancing to Intermediate Class D have to retake the written knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.memory_hook: Expired past twelve months triggers retest
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: A PD holder moving up to an Intermediate Class D skips the knowledge test unless the permit expired more than twelve months before the driving skills test.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: At what minimum age can a Class H hardship license be granted, and for which vehicles and situations?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.memory_hook: Age fourteen for family hardship needs
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: A Class H hardship license can be issued to a fourteen-year-old for a Class D vehicle, a Class M motorcycle or both, but only for family hardship and limited needs.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: Roughly what share of minor driver licenses issued in Tennessee are Class H hardship credentials?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.memory_hook: Under one percent of minor licenses
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: Hardship licenses are rare: fewer than one percent of the licenses issued to minors are Class H.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: Where must a hardship applicant mail proof and forms first, and what arrives if approved?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.memory_hook: Mail administrative office, wait for letter
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: A hardship applicant mails proof of hardship with the application to the Driver Services Administrative Office, and approval brings a letter authorizing the application.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: Which exams must a hardship applicant pass for cars or motorcycles, and what engine limit caps a hardship bike?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.memory_hook: Full exams plus one-twenty-five cycle cap
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: A hardship applicant must pass vision, knowledge and road tests for a Class D vehicle, adds the Class M knowledge and driving tests to ride a motorcycle, and is then limited to one hundred twenty-five cubic centimeters.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: During what hours and to which destinations may a Class H hardship holder legally drive?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.memory_hook: Daylight hours to approved places only
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: A Class H license is good only during daylight and only for trips to the places named in the approval letter.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: What extra driving privilege does a Class H hardship holder gain upon turning fifteen?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.memory_hook: Age fifteen unlocks learner permit rides
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: A hardship license holder who is at least fifteen gets the same privileges as a Class PD holder when riding with one of the adults allowed for PD drivers.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: On what exact milestone does every Tennessee Class H hardship license expire?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: Every hardship license expires on the holder's sixteenth birthday, whatever age they were when approved.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: What must a teen do at sixteen if their hardship license was approved less than six months before that birthday?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.memory_hook: Switch to permit until one-eighty days
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: If a hardship license is approved with less than six months left before the sixteenth birthday, the holder must renew a Class PD at expiration and keep it until reaching one hundred eighty days of combined driving experience.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: When may Armed Forces or National Guard personnel drive in Tennessee without holding a Tennessee driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: Members of the armed forces, National Guard included, need no Tennessee license while driving a vehicle owned or leased by the military.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: Which heavy equipment or agricultural operators are exempt from needing a Tennessee driver license on a highway?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.memory_hook: Road machinery and temporary farm tractors
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: Operators of road machinery, farm tractors or other farm equipment moved temporarily along a highway need no Tennessee license.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: When may an out-of-state or foreign visitor legally drive in Tennessee without getting a Tennessee license?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.memory_hook: Valid home license matching vehicle class
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: Visitors carrying a valid license from their home state or country, equivalent to the matching Tennessee class, may drive without a Tennessee license.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: Under what exact condition may an unlicensed student drive during an approved school or commercial driver training course?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: Students in a Department-approved driver training course at a school or licensed driving school may drive unlicensed only while a certified instructor accompanies them.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: Which three conditions require Tennessee to refuse a driver license application?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.memory_hook: Suspended elsewhere, uninsured, or unsafe disability
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: A license is refused to anyone suspended or revoked in any state, anyone who has not shown required proof of insurance or financial responsibility, and anyone the Commissioner finds unable to drive safely because of a mental or physical disability.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: How long may non-citizens working in managerial or technical roles in Tennessee drive on another valid license before applying?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.memory_hook: Six months before applying in Tennessee
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: Non-US citizens working in managerial or technical jobs in Tennessee may drive on another valid license for six months and must then apply for a Tennessee license.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.front: Which two school-related failures make an applicant under eighteen ineligible for a Tennessee driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.memory_hook: Dropping out or failing school progress
sec01-card-sec01-F37.expected_back: Anyone under eighteen who has dropped out of school before graduating, or who is not making satisfactory progress in school, is not eligible for a license.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.front: What happens if an applicant cannot prove United States citizenship, permanent residency, or temporary legal presence?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.memory_hook: No legal presence, no state card
sec01-card-sec01-F38.expected_back: Applicants who cannot prove US citizenship, lawful permanent residency or temporary legal presence cannot receive a driver license or an ID-only license.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: What misdemeanor class, maximum fine, and jail term apply to driving while your license is suspended, revoked, or canceled?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.memory_hook: Class B misdemeanor, thousand, six months
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: Driving while your license is revoked, canceled or suspended is a Class B misdemeanor carrying a fine of up to one thousand dollars, up to six months in jail, or both.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: When must you carry and display your license while driving, and what penalty applies if you leave it behind?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.memory_hook: Always carry, Class D fine otherwise
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: You must carry your license or TDL whenever you drive and show it to any officer on request; failing to have it is a Class D misdemeanor with a fine from two dollars to fifty dollars.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: Does a Tennessee identification-only license require exams, what proof does it demand, and does it permit driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.memory_hook: Same identity proof, zero driving allowed
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: An ID-only license involves no testing but demands the same proof of identity and residency as a driver license, and it never authorizes driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: Who may obtain an Expiring Identification License, and at what age does it stop expiring?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.memory_hook: Anyone unlicensed; never expires at sixty-five
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: The Expiring Identification License can go to anyone without a valid driver license, and once the holder is sixty-five or older it no longer expires.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: Who qualifies for a free, non-expiring permanent identification license, and what medical proof is required?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.memory_hook: Doctor-certified disability earns free permanent card
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: A permanent identification license, free and non-expiring, is available to a person who is mentally challenged or physically disabled with a licensed doctor's certified statement that they cannot drive.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.front: What two things must an applicant supply if they have never been issued a Social Security number?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.memory_hook: Sworn perjury affidavit plus status document
sec01-card-sec01-R13.expected_back: An applicant who has never had a Social Security number signs an affidavit under penalty of perjury and supplies a certified US birth certificate or valid US passport, or USCIS proof of permanent residence.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.front: How young can a child be to receive a Tennessee identification-only license if documentation rules are met?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.memory_hook: Even infants qualify with proper documents
sec01-card-sec01-R14.expected_back: Families may get identification-only licenses for children, even infants, as long as each child meets the documentation requirements.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.front: Which letter starts every Temporary Driver License class code, and what sets the card's expiration date?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.expected_back: TDL class codes begin with the letter X, such as XD, XM and XPD, and a TDL expires on dates tied to the holder's legal presence documents.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.front: Who uses a Temporary Identification License, how is its class shown, and what is its maximum duration?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.memory_hook: Non-drivers with temporary stay, five years
sec01-card-sec01-F40.expected_back: A Temporary Identification License, shown as Class XID, serves non-driving applicants with temporary legal presence and can be issued for no more than five years.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.front: Which federal cards or passport-and-visa combinations prove temporary legal presence, including extra student or exchange forms?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.memory_hook: Federal cards or passport plus visa
sec01-card-sec01-R15.expected_back: Temporary legal presence is usually proven with an I-five hundred fifty-one, I-six hundred eighty-eight or I-seven hundred sixty-six card or a valid foreign passport with visa and I-ninety-four, and F one or F two holders add a SEVIS I-twenty while J one or J two holders add a DS-two thousand nineteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.front: Which permit or combined forms can a Temporary Driver License take, and what two things does it serve to prove?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.memory_hook: Permits or combos, driving and identity
sec01-card-sec01-R16.expected_back: A TDL can be issued as a learner permit (XPD, XMPD) or a combination type (XDM), proves the holder passed Tennessee's Class D or M requirements, and also works as identification.

sec01-card-sec01-F41.front: Which minors aged thirteen through seventeen are eligible to register as organ and tissue donors in Tennessee?
sec01-card-sec01-F41.memory_hook: Teens thirteen to seventeen holding credentials
sec01-card-sec01-F41.expected_back: Minors aged thirteen to seventeen who hold a driver license, permit or state ID may register as organ and tissue donors.

sec01-card-sec01-R17.front: What does circling yes for organ donation accomplish legally, and how can someone later remove the red heart?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.memory_hook: Legal registry consent; duplicate removes heart
sec01-card-sec01-R17.expected_back: Circling YES for donation on a license or ID application places you on the Donate Life Tennessee registry as legal consent, and removing the red heart later requires a duplicate license at a Driver Service Center.

sec01-card-sec01-R18.front: How can an honorably discharged service member get Veteran printed on a Tennessee driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-R18.memory_hook: Certify application and show discharge proof
sec01-card-sec01-R18.expected_back: An honorably discharged veteran can have Veteran printed on the license by certifying it on the application and showing a certified DD-two hundred fourteen, a NAVPERS-six hundred sixty discharge certificate or a DD Form two (Retired) card.

sec01-card-sec01-F42.front: Who should you contact immediately if your voter registration card does not arrive within thirty days of applying?
sec01-card-sec01-F42.memory_hook: Call your County Election Commission promptly
sec01-card-sec01-F42.expected_back: If no voter registration card arrives within thirty days of applying at a Driver Service Center, contact your County Election Commission right away.

sec01-card-sec01-R22.front: Why does a Driver Service Center forward your voter application rather than handing you a voter registration card?
sec01-card-sec01-R22.memory_hook: Only the Election Registrar issues cards
sec01-card-sec01-R22.expected_back: The Driver Service Center only forwards a voter application to the County Election Commission, because only the Election Registrar can issue a voter registration card.

sec01-card-sec01-R21.front: What three duties apply to registered sexual or violent sexual offenders when applying, renewing, and traveling?
sec01-card-sec01-R21.memory_hook: Inform examiner, file declaration, always carry
sec01-card-sec01-R21.expected_back: Registered sexual or violent sexual offenders must tell the examiner when applying or renewing, complete a Sex Offender Declaration and Supplemental Application, and carry their license or ID at all times.

sec01-card-sec01-F43.front: What age and license status must a United States citizen have to get an International Driving Permit, and how long does it run?
sec01-card-sec01-F43.memory_hook: Eighteen, unrevoked license, valid one year
sec01-card-sec01-F43.expected_back: A US citizen must be at least eighteen and hold a valid license that is not revoked or suspended to obtain an International Driving Permit, which lasts one year from issuance.

sec01-card-sec01-R19.front: Why can an International Driving Permit never be used by itself or for driving inside the United States?
sec01-card-sec01-R19.memory_hook: Translation booklet only, carry home license
sec01-card-sec01-R19.expected_back: An International Driving Permit is only a translation of a home license, must travel with that license, and is never valid by itself or for driving inside the United States.

sec01-card-sec01-R20.front: Where must Tennessee residents and foreign visitors obtain an International Driving Permit since state centers never issue them?
sec01-card-sec01-R20.memory_hook: Automobile club locally, home country abroad
sec01-card-sec01-R20.expected_back: Tennessee Driver Service Centers do not issue International Driving Permits; residents ask a local AAA office, and foreign visitors must obtain one in their home country before arriving.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: Which versions of checklist documents are accepted at a Driver Service Center, and which copies are rejected?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.memory_hook: Originals or certified copies, never photocopies
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: Every document on the application checklist must be an original or a certified copy; faxes and photocopies are turned away.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: Why does Tennessee require every license applicant to prove their full legal name and date of birth?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.memory_hook: Confirm true identity and prevent fraud
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: The Department asks every applicant to prove full legal name and date of birth so it can confirm identity and reduce fraud.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: Who may the state verify your application documents with, and how can that step affect your card?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.memory_hook: Issuing-agency checks can delay your card
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: Every document is subject to verification with the agency that issued it, and that verification can delay issuance of a permit, license or ID.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: What kinds of documents belong on the Primary identification list compared with the Secondary list?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.memory_hook: Core government records versus supporting items
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: Primary identification includes items such as a certified birth certificate, a valid passport, a military ID or a photo license from another state, while Secondary identification covers supporting items such as check stubs, union cards, work IDs and tax forms.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: Under what exact condition does a computerized check stub qualify as secondary identification?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: A computerized check stub counts as secondary identification only when the applicant's full name is pre-printed on it.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: Which version of a Social Security card is accepted as identification, and which versions are banned?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.memory_hook: Original paper card, never metal replicas
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: A Social Security card used as identification must be the original, never a metal or plastic replica.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: How many identity documents must an original applicant bring, and which list must supply at least one?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: The examiner asks for two identity items, and an original applicant must supply at least one from the Primary list, with the second from either list.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: Which identity lists can an existing Tennessee holder pull from when requesting a duplicate or renewal?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.memory_hook: Renewals and duplicates pick any two
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: Applicants for a duplicate or renewal of an existing Tennessee license or ID may supply any two identity items from either list.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: What must new residents do with their former state's driver license, and what if that card was lost?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.memory_hook: Surrender old license or prove twice
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: New residents must hand in the license from their former state, and if it was lost they provide the same two identity items as an original applicant.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: Which birth certificates pass Tennessee inspection, and which souvenir or church versions get turned away?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.memory_hook: Vital-statistics sealed copy, never hospital certificates
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: A birth certificate must be certified, sealed and issued by an authorized agency such as the Bureau of Vital Statistics, and hospital-issued or baptismal certificates are refused.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: Are expired passports accepted, and what must accompany a birth certificate, passport, or license written in another language?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.memory_hook: Unexpired passports only, plus certified translation
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: An expired passport is not accepted, and a passport, birth certificate or license not written in English must come with a Certificate of Accurate Translation.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: What does a valid driver license from your former state prove, and what status can it never prove?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.memory_hook: Proves identity, never citizenship or residency
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: A new resident's valid license from the former state can prove identity, but it never proves US citizenship or lawful permanent residency.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: Which four groups of applicants must bring proof of United States citizenship or lawful permanent residency?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: Proof of US citizenship or lawful permanent residency is required of first-time applicants, new and returning residents, anyone reinstating after a revocation, suspension or cancellation, and anyone licensed since January one, two thousand one who is renewing for the first time.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: Which four official documents are accepted to prove United States citizenship or lawful permanent residency?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.memory_hook: Birth record, passport, citizenship, resident card
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: Accepted proof of citizenship or permanent residency includes a certified birth certificate from a US state or territory, a valid US passport, a Certificate of Citizenship or Naturalization, and an I-five hundred fifty-one Permanent Resident card.

sec02-card-sec02-R13.front: Why is mail or online renewal blocked at the first renewal for anyone originally licensed after January first, two thousand one?
sec02-card-sec02-R13.memory_hook: Must show citizenship papers in person
sec02-card-sec02-R13.expected_back: Anyone first issued a Tennessee license or photo ID after January one, two thousand one must show citizenship or permanent-residency documents at the first renewal and cannot renew that time by mail or online.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: Which credentials may an applicant obtain when they hold temporary legal presence rather than citizenship or permanent residency?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.memory_hook: Temporary driver or identification license only
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: An applicant who has only temporary legal presence cannot get a regular license or ID, but may qualify for a Temporary Driver License or Temporary Identification License by proving authorized stay.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Do applicants seeking a temporary car or motorcycle license face different Tennessee exams than regular applicants?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.memory_hook: Every standard Tennessee exam still applies
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: A TDL or TID applicant must still meet every Tennessee examination requirement for driving Class XD or Class XM vehicles.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: How long can a temporary license or identification run, and what base rate applies regardless of stay length?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.memory_hook: Up to five years, twenty-eight dollars
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: A Temporary Driver License or Temporary Identification License runs for the authorized stay up to five years at a fixed twenty-eight-dollar base rate regardless of duration, plus any applicable GDL, motorcycle, or multi-type fees.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: How many Tennessee residency proofs must you bring, what address is banned, and how recent must they be?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.memory_hook: Two street-address proofs within four months
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: Applicants bring two proofs of Tennessee residency showing their name and street address, with no post office boxes, and each must be current, meaning dated within the last four months.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: Which everyday bills, financial records, registrations, or tax forms qualify as proof of Tennessee residency?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.memory_hook: Utility bills, leases, statements, tax forms
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: Acceptable residency proofs include a current utility bill with its postmarked envelope, a bank statement, a signed lease or mortgage, an insurance policy, Tennessee vehicle or voter registration, a W-two, or a property tax receipt from within the last year.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: Which three common financial or insurance items are specifically rejected as proof of Tennessee residency?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.memory_hook: Deposit receipts, bank checks, wallet cards
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: A utility initial deposit receipt, bank checks and insurance wallet cards do not count as proof of residency.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: Does holding a Tennessee license years ago before moving away exempt a returning resident from proving residency again?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.memory_hook: Returning residents still prove street residency
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: Residency proof is demanded from first-time, new-resident and returning-resident applicants for every ID, TDL, permit and license class, even if they once held a Tennessee license before moving away.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: When residency bills are in a spouse's or parent's name, how can an applicant or minor use them?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.memory_hook: Pair family bills with relationship certificate
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: Residency documents may name the applicant, the applicant's spouse, or for a minor a parent or legal guardian, and relationship is then shown with a certified marriage certificate or long-form birth certificate.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: When must you list a Social Security number on your application, and does Tennessee print it on your card?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: Tennessee law requires your Social Security number on the application whenever the US Government has issued you one, and the number is kept on your record but never printed on the license.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: What happens if the Social Security number on your application fails to match federal records?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.memory_hook: Extra proof or Social Security visit
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: If the Social Security number does not match federal records, the examiner asks for more proof and may send you to the Social Security Administration before accepting the application.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: What must an applicant who has never had a Social Security number sign in person, and how often?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.memory_hook: Sworn perjury affidavit every single application
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: Someone never issued a Social Security number must sign a sworn affidavit in person before an examiner or notary, under penalty of perjury, and must sign a new one with every later application.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: Beyond an original Social Security card, which four everyday records can verify your full Social Security number?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.memory_hook: Tax form, stub, bank, health card
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: A Social Security number can be proven with an original card, a W-two showing the full number, an employer payroll stub or bank statement with the number, or a health insurance card showing name and number.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: What responsibility form must an applicant under eighteen bring, and when are custody, adoption, or marriage papers added?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.memory_hook: Teenage Affidavit plus guardian relationship proof
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen also needs a Teenage Affidavit for financial responsibility, plus proof of relationship such as custody, adoption or marriage papers when the signing guardian or step-parent is not named on school attendance records.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: Who signs a minor's school attendance form, and how recently must it be dated when brought in?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.memory_hook: Principal or counselor within thirty days
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen needs proof of school attendance or progress, such as Form SF1010 completed by the principal or guidance teacher, signed and dated within the past thirty days.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: How many behind-the-wheel hours and how many permit months must a teen certify before stepping past a learner permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.memory_hook: Fifty certified hours after six months
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: A teen moving past the learner permit must submit form SF-one thousand two hundred fifty-six certifying fifty hours of behind-the-wheel experience, after holding the permit for six months.

sec02-card-sec02-F41.front: Which applicants by age or education are exempt from Tennessee's Graduated Driver License program?
sec02-card-sec02-F41.expected_back: The Graduated Driver License program does not apply to anyone eighteen or older, or to anyone under eighteen who has graduated high school or earned a GED.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: What kind of legal papers are required for a license name change, and is mail service allowed?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.memory_hook: Original or certified papers in person
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: Every supporting document for a name change must be an original or certified legal paper, and name changes are never accepted by mail.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: Why must you bring a registered marriage certificate rather than a marriage license to change your name?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.memory_hook: Registered wedding certificate, never marriage license
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: For a marriage name change, the certificate must be the original or certified copy registered after the wedding, not the license that authorized it.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: What distinguishes an acceptable court-document copy from one that a Driver Service Center refuses?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.memory_hook: Original live seal, never photocopied stamp
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: A court-document copy is acceptable only if the original signature or seal is affixed to it, and a copy with a copied seal or signature is refused.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: Within how many days of establishing Tennessee residency must an out-of-state driver switch to a Tennessee license?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.memory_hook: Switch licenses within thirty residency days
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: New or returning residents holding another state's license must get a Tennessee license within thirty days of establishing residency.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: Which screening must every single new or returning Tennessee resident complete at the Driver Service Center?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: Every new or returning resident takes a Tennessee vision screening at the Driver Service Center.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: How long must an out-of-state license be expired before a new resident has to take all three Tennessee exams?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.memory_hook: Expired past six months triggers retesting
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: A new or returning resident whose out-of-state license expired more than six months ago must pass the knowledge exam, the road skills test and the vision screening.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: How does the thirty-day newcomer rule differ from the six-month rule for out-of-state licenses?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.memory_hook: Thirty days switches, six months retests
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: Two look-alike new-resident limits: a newcomer has thirty days after establishing residency to switch to a Tennessee license, but only an out-of-state license expired more than six months triggers the full knowledge, road and vision testing.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: Which exams must new residents arriving from another country pass, and what happens to their foreign license?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.memory_hook: All three exams, keep foreign card
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: New residents arriving from other countries take the vision screening, knowledge exam and road skills test, and they may keep their foreign license.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: When does a United States Armed Forces member's Tennessee license remain valid beyond its printed expiration date?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.memory_hook: Active duty outside Tennessee, clean status
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: A Tennessee license held by a member of the US Armed Forces stays valid past its printed expiration while the person is on active duty based outside Tennessee and the license is not surrendered, canceled or suspended.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: How can active-duty troops stationed outside Tennessee mark their license to show it does not expire?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.memory_hook: Show military orders, add Code thirty
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: Active-duty personnel stationed outside Tennessee may have Code thirty added to the license to show it does not expire, by bringing their military orders and paying the fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: How soon must troops renew after discharge or reassignment back to Tennessee, and how is Fort Campbell treated?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.memory_hook: Sixty days back; Fort Campbell counts
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: After discharge, separation or reassignment back to Tennessee, the service member must renew within sixty days, and Fort Campbell counts as a Tennessee assignment.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.front: Which two military-connected groups are excluded from using Tennessee's active-duty license extension?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.memory_hook: National Guard and military dependents excluded
sec02-card-sec02-R12.expected_back: Members of the National Guard and family members of military personnel cannot use the active-duty license extension.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: How long do Tennessee licenses for drivers over twenty-one last since two thousand sixteen, and how did expiration dates change?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.memory_hook: Eight years from issue, off birthdays
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: Since January one, two thousand sixteen, licenses for people over twenty-one run eight years from the issue date, so they usually no longer expire on a birthday.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.front: When did pre-two-thousand-sixteen Class D licenses expire compared with the standard term of a learner permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.expected_back: A Class D license issued before January one, two thousand sixteen normally expires after five years on your birthdate, while permits normally expire one year after issuance.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: On the eight-year fee chart, what do a Class D license at sixteen and a minor's one-year permit at fifteen cost?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.memory_hook: Twenty-eight Class D, ten-fifty teen permit
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: On the standard eight-year fee table, a Class D operator license costs twenty-eight dollars with a minimum age of sixteen, and a learner permit for someone under eighteen costs ten dollars and fifty cents for one year with a minimum age of fifteen.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.front: How does the one-year learner permit fee differ between applicants under eighteen and applicants over eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.expected_back: A learner permit for someone under eighteen costs ten dollars and fifty cents for one year, while a permit for someone over eighteen costs five dollars and fifty cents for one year.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: Which six payment methods are accepted at Tennessee Driver Service Centers?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.memory_hook: Cash, check, money order, three cards
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: Driver Service Centers accept cash, check, money order, MasterCard, Visa and Discover for a license or ID.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: Where can lost credentials be replaced, and which two temporary cards can never be replaced online?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.memory_hook: Centers or online, never temporary credentials
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: A lost, stolen or destroyed license, permit or ID can be replaced at any Driver Service Center or sometimes online, but TDLs and TIDs cannot be replaced online.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.front: How far ahead of expiration does Tennessee mail a courtesy renewal notice, and is that notice required to renew?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.memory_hook: Eight to ten weeks; optional notice
sec02-card-sec02-F36.expected_back: The Department mails a courtesy renewal notice eight to ten weeks before your license expires, though you can renew without it.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.front: How do late renewal penalties escalate past thirty days, past six months, and past five years expired?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.memory_hook: Five dollars, ten dollars, full retest
sec02-card-sec02-F37.expected_back: A license expired more than thirty days carries a five dollars late fee, which doubles to ten dollars after six months, and after five years you must also pass the vision, knowledge and skills tests.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.front: How much grace time do you get to keep driving after your Tennessee license expires, and what penalty applies?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.memory_hook: Zero grace period, unlicensed driving penalties
sec02-card-sec02-F38.expected_back: There is no grace period: once your license expires you may not drive, and you face the same penalties as someone never licensed.

sec02-card-sec02-R14.front: At what age may drivers choose a non-photo license remotely, and why might keeping a photo card still help?
sec02-card-sec02-R14.memory_hook: Sixty skips photo; travel needs one
sec02-card-sec02-R14.expected_back: Drivers sixty or older may choose a non-photo license by mail or internet, though a photo license helps with boarding flights, Amtrak and cruise ships.

sec02-card-sec02-F39.front: How soon must you report a residential address change, even if postal or emergency renumbering caused it?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.memory_hook: Report within ten days, even renumbering
