sec02-card-sec02-F39.expected_back: State law requires you to report a residence address change to the Department of Safety within ten days, even when the change comes from the Postal Service or a nine-one-one district renaming rather than a move.

sec02-card-sec02-F40.front: What address details must appear on your Tennessee license, and why is a post office box alone refused?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.memory_hook: Physical street address, never post box
sec02-card-sec02-F40.expected_back: Your license must show a legal residential address with house or apartment number, street, city and zip code, and a post office box alone is refused.

sec02-card-sec02-R15.front: When your address changes, what must be updated within ten days, and what does not have to be replaced?
sec02-card-sec02-R15.memory_hook: Update state file; keep plastic card
sec02-card-sec02-R15.expected_back: Two look-alike address rules: the Department record must be updated within ten days of an address change, but the printed license itself does not have to be reissued.

sec02-card-sec02-R16.front: How does the federal Driver Privacy Protection Act guard personal details on your Tennessee driving record?
sec02-card-sec02-R16.memory_hook: Blocks personal data release without consent
sec02-card-sec02-R16.expected_back: The federal Driver Privacy Protection Act bars release of personal information from your driving record without your express consent.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: May a Tennessee officer pull you over and ticket you SOLELY for a safety-belt or child-restraint violation?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Tennessee law requires safety belts, child safety seats and booster seats, and an officer may stop and ticket a driver for a belt or child restraint violation alone.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: Which front-row occupants must wear a safety belt whenever a vehicle is moving in Tennessee?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: Every driver and every front-seat passenger must wear a safety belt whenever the vehicle is moving.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: Under what age must back-seat passengers always wear safety belts in Tennessee?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: Back-seat passengers under seventeen years old must also wear safety belts.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: When the driver holds a learner permit or intermediate license, which back-seat age group must wear safety belts?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: When the driver holds a learner permit or an intermediate license, back-seat passengers aged four to seventeen must be belted.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: Compare Tennessee's general back-seat belt age rule against the rule for permit and intermediate drivers?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: Back-seat belt rules depend on who is driving: passengers under seventeen must belt in any case, and with a permit or intermediate driver the rule covers back-seat passengers aged four to seventeen.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: What historic national first did Tennessee achieve in child passenger safety legislation?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Tennessee was the first state to pass a Child Passenger Protection Law requiring children to ride in car seats and booster seats.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: Which two groups of young children — by age OR weight — must ride in a rear-facing car seat?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: A child under one year old, or any child under twenty pounds, must ride in a rear-facing car seat.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: What age range AND weight requirement place a child into a forward-facing car seat?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: A child aged one through three who weighs more than twenty pounds must ride in a forward-facing car seat.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: What age span AND height cutoff require a child to use a belt-positioning booster seat?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: A child aged four through eight who is shorter than four feet, nine inches must ride in a belt-positioning booster seat while wearing a seat belt.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: Walk through all three Tennessee child-restraint stages from rear-facing to forward-facing to booster?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: Car seat direction turns on age and weight: rear-facing below one year or twenty pounds, forward-facing from one through three above twenty pounds, then a booster from four through eight while under four feet, nine inches.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: In which row must a child in a booster ride when available — and what standards govern seats?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: A child in a booster seat must ride in the back seat whenever the vehicle has one, and every car seat and booster must meet federal safety standards and be used as its maker and the vehicle maker direct.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: When a child uses a medically prescribed modified restraint, what document should stay inside that vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: A child may ride in a medically prescribed modified restraint, but a copy of the doctor's prescription should stay in that vehicle at all times.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: Normally, who answers legally for unrestrained children under sixteen — and what dollar fine applies?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: The driver is responsible for restraining every child under sixteen and can be charged and fined fifty dollars when such a child is not properly restrained.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: What shifts legal responsibility off the driver when a child's parent or legal guardian rides as a passenger?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: When a child's parent or legal guardian is in the car but not driving, that parent or guardian is responsible for the child's restraint and can be fined.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: What criminal grade and mandatory class can hit for skipping a required car seat or booster under age nine?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Failing to use a required car seat or booster seat for a child under nine, or one shorter than four feet, nine inches, can be charged as a Class C misdemeanor, with a required class on safely transporting children plus fees and fines.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: Contrast when Tennessee's plain fifty-dollar restraint fine applies versus the heavier Class C misdemeanor?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: The plain fifty dollars fine applies to a driver who fails to restrain a child under sixteen, while missing a required car seat or booster seat carries the heavier Class C misdemeanor penalty.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: Name the five physical ways safety belts shield your body during a crash?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: Safety belts protect in five ways: they prevent ejection, shift crash forces onto the strongest bones, spread forces over a wide area, hold you in driving posture, and protect the head and spinal cord.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: Even when a severe crash still makes a belted rider touch the wheel or dash, how does the belt help?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: Belted occupants who do strike the wheel, dashboard or windshield usually hit with far less force and suffer less serious injury.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: Which two crash advantages let a belted driver keep handling an unfolding emergency?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: A belted driver stays in the seat in a crash and is less likely to be knocked unconscious, so is better able to handle the emergency.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: By what percentages do lap-and-shoulder belts cut death and moderate-to-critical injury for front-seat car occupants?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: The manual reports that proper lap and shoulder belt use cuts the risk of death for front-seat car occupants by forty-five percent and of moderate-to-critical injury by fifty percent.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: By what even larger percentages do belts cut death and moderate-to-critical injury for light-truck occupants?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: For light truck occupants, the manual says correct belt use lowers the risk of death by sixty percent and of moderate-to-critical injury by sixty-five percent.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: How many times more likely were unbelted crash occupants to die — and to suffer serious injury?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: The manual reports that unbelted occupants were thirty-two times more likely to die and three times more likely to be seriously injured in a crash.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: Which single safety behavior contributes to more traffic deaths than any other according to the Tennessee manual?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: According to the manual, not wearing a safety belt contributes to more traffic deaths than any other single safety behavior.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: How fast does a safety belt release, and how common are crashes ending in fire or deep water?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: The idea that belts trap you is a myth: a belt unbuckles in under a second, and crashes rarely end in fire or deep water.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: What tiny percentage of crashes actually end in fire or submersion — and why does buckling still help there?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: According to the manual, only one-half of one percent of crashes end in fire or submersion, and staying conscious because of the belt improves your chance of escaping.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: Compared with riders who stay inside the cabin, how much more likely are ejected occupants to be killed?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: The manual says people thrown from a vehicle are four times as likely to be killed as those who stay inside it.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: What fraction does the Tennessee manual give for the chance of being killed once ejected from a vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: Being ejected from a vehicle sharply raises the chance of death or serious injury, and the manual puts the chance of being killed by ejection at one in eight.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: When your car is T-boned from the side, which direction do loose items and unbelted passengers slide?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: In a side impact the car moves sideways and everything loose inside, passengers included, slides toward the point of impact, not away from it.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: How many traffic deaths on Tennessee roads in two thousand sixteen does the manual cite to show why buckling matters?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: The manual says crashes on Tennessee roads killed one thousand thirty-nine people in two thousand sixteen, many of whom might have lived had they buckled up.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: Where across your lower body should the lap belt sit?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: Wear the lap belt low over the pelvis so its lower edge rests snugly on the tops of the thighs.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: Where must the shoulder belt cross, which two body zones are off-limits, and how tight should it stay?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: The shoulder belt goes over the shoulder and across the chest, never under the arm or across the abdomen, and must not be so loose that it slips off.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: How should a pregnant driver or passenger position both parts of her safety belt?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: A pregnant woman should wear the lap belt below her abdomen and the shoulder belt above the belly.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: What posture check against the vehicle seat shows a child is finally tall enough for adult belts?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: A child is big enough for the adult lap and shoulder belt once they can sit with their back against the seat back and their knees bend over the seat edge.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: Once a child graduates to adult belts, where must the lap and shoulder straps rest — and never go?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: On a child, the lap belt should sit low and snug on the upper thighs and the shoulder belt should cross the chest between neck and shoulder, never behind the back or under the arm.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: Which two bones take pressure under 'belts-to-bones' — and what happens if straps touch stomach, face, or neck?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Under the belts-to-bones rule the pelvis and collarbone should take the belt's pressure, so if the belt rides on the stomach or crosses the face or neck, the child goes back to a booster seat.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.front: Where specifically must the lap belt sit once a child moves out of a booster into vehicle belts?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.expected_back: Once a child transitions out of a safety seat to vehicle belts, position the lap belt firmly across the upper thighs so it stays low and snug over the hips.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: What share of otherwise-fatal crashes do properly secured infants survive — and how about toddlers?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: The manual says infants properly secured in safety seats survive almost seventy-five percent of crashes that would otherwise kill them, and toddlers survive more than half.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.front: Out of every ten deaths and ten serious injuries under age four, how many could proper child restraints prevent?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.expected_back: The manual states that correct use of child restraints could prevent nine of ten deaths and eight of ten serious injuries among child passengers under four.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.front: Why does your own seat-belt consistency directly shape whether children stay buckled?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.expected_back: Children copy their parents in the car, so buckling up yourself every trip sets the habit for your child.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.front: What do the manual's two thousand twenty CDC figures identify as the leading cause of fatal injury for ages three to fourteen?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.expected_back: The CDC figures in the manual name motor vehicle crashes as the leading cause of fatal injury for children aged three to fourteen in two thousand twenty.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: What pairing delivers the strongest crash protection available in a car, SUV, or truck?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: Air bags work best combined with safety belts, which together are the best protection available in a car, SUV or truck.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: What cabin strikes do airbags prevent, and how fast do they inflate and deflate?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: Air bags are meant to keep occupants from striking the steering wheel or dashboard, and they inflate and deflate faster than a blink.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.front: More than how many lives does the manual credit airbags with saving between nineteen eighty-seven and two thousand twelve?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.expected_back: The manual credits air bags with saving more than thirty-nine thousand nine hundred seventy-six lives between nineteen eighty-seven and two thousand twelve, citing NHTSA estimates.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: Through what age are children safest riding properly restrained in the back seat — with or without a passenger airbag?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: Children aged twelve and under are safest in the back seat, properly restrained, whether or not the car has a passenger air bag.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: Where must you avoid installing a child safety seat whenever a vehicle has a rear row?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: Do not put a child safety seat in the front seat of a car with a passenger air bag; place it in a rear seat if one exists.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.front: Where do infants in rear-facing seats belong when a car has a front passenger airbag and a back seat?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.expected_back: Infants in rear-facing seats belong in the rear seat of a vehicle that has a passenger air bag, if a rear seat is available.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: If a child MUST ride up front — like in a two-seat pickup with a passenger airbag — what two steps apply?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: If a child must ride in front, as in a pickup truck with a passenger air bag, move the seat as far back as possible and buckle the child properly.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.front: How many inches should adults keep between their breastbone and the airbag cover while wearing both belt straps?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.expected_back: Adults should always wear both lap and shoulder belts and sit far enough back to leave ten to twelve inches between the chest and the air bag cover, as NHTSA recommends.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.front: How should you angle an adjustable tilt steering wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.expected_back: Keep an adjustable steering wheel tilted down toward a level position.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.front: Which age group is ALWAYS banned from pickup beds in Tennessee — and where are ages six to twelve banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.expected_back: Tennessee forbids any child under six from riding in a pickup truck bed, and forbids children aged six to twelve from riding there on any state or interstate highway.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.front: Which two activities allow children in a pickup bed — and what speed ceiling governs parades?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.expected_back: A child may ride in a pickup bed during an organized parade or ceremony moving no faster than twenty miles per hour, or during farm work.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.front: Even off state highways, why might ages six to twelve still be barred from riding in a pickup bed?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.expected_back: Cities and counties may pass ordinances barring children aged six to twelve from pickup beds on local roads too.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.front: Under what child age, supervisor age, and three risk triggers is leaving a child in a parked public vehicle a crime?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.expected_back: It is an offense to knowingly leave a child under seven in a vehicle in a public place without supervision by someone at least thirteen if conditions risk the child, the engine is running or the keys are inside.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.front: What misdemeanor class and first-versus-repeat fines punish leaving a child under seven unattended in a car?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.memory_hook: Class B; two hundred, five hundred
sec06-card-sec06-F37.expected_back: Leaving a young child unattended this way is a Class B misdemeanor fined two hundred dollars for a first offense and five hundred dollars for any later offense.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.front: On a sunny summer day, how fast can heat inside a parked car start harming a child?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.expected_back: On a sunny summer day a car's interior can reach deadly heat within minutes, and harm can begin in as little as ten minutes.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.front: Even on a mild seventy-three-degree day, how hot can an SUV reach in ten and thirty minutes — and at ninety outside?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.expected_back: On a mild seventy-three-degree day an SUV can heat to one hundred degrees in ten minutes and one hundred twenty degrees in thirty minutes, and at ninety degrees outside the interior can reach one hundred sixty degrees within several minutes.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.front: Above which temperatures do heat exhaustion and heat stroke set in — and why are kids extra vulnerable?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.expected_back: Heat exhaustion can set in above ninety degrees and heat stroke above one hundred five degrees, and children's still-developing breathing systems make them especially vulnerable.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.front: Why shouldn't even a quick errand tempt you to leave a child behind — and what check belongs at every stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.expected_back: Never leave a child alone in a vehicle, even for a quick errand, and check that everyone, including sleeping babies, is out when unloading.

sec06-card-sec06-R20.front: Why must you lock parked cars at home and keep keys and fobs away from children?
sec06-card-sec06-R20.expected_back: Children can put a vehicle in motion, so always lock the car and keep keys and remote entry devices away from them.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.front: What should you do immediately if a child gets locked inside a car or you spot a child or pet left alone?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.expected_back: If a child is locked inside a car, or you see a child or animal left alone in one, call nine one one.

sec06-card-sec06-R21.front: Under Tennessee child-abuse law, how does knowingly injuring a child shift charges when the victim is six or younger?
sec06-card-sec06-R21.expected_back: Under Tennessee child abuse law, knowingly injuring a child under eighteen is a Class A misdemeanor, but it becomes a Class D felony when the child is six or younger.

sec06-card-sec06-R22.front: Contrast the jail-and-fine range of a Tennessee Class A misdemeanor against a Class A felony?
sec06-card-sec06-R22.expected_back: A Class A misdemeanor can bring up to eleven months, twenty-nine days in jail, a fine up to two thousand five hundred dollars, or both, while a Class A felony carries fifteen to sixty years and a possible fine up to fifty thousand dollars.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Which three surface-street hazards are absent on interstates, and how does traffic get on and off?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Interstates are controlled-access roads with no stop signs, railroad crossings or traffic lights, and drivers get on and off only at interchanges without crossing other traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: Which deadly crash type have interstates and divided highways largely wiped out, and how is road geometry built?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: Interstates and divided highways have largely eliminated the risk of head-on collisions, and they usually have few steep hills or sharp curves.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: What route details and gauge should you check before rolling onto an interstate, especially in rural areas?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Plan your entrance, direction and exit ahead of time, and check your fuel first, since rural exits can be many miles apart.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: What should you do if you are unwilling or unable to maintain at least the interstate's minimum speed?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: If you cannot or do not want to drive at least the minimum speed, do not use the interstate.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: How do you use an interstate entrance ramp and acceleration lane to merge cleanly into freeway traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Unlike entering most busy roads, entering an interstate means speeding up: use the acceleration lane to reach traffic speed, signal left and merge when the way is clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: Between a driver entering on an on-ramp and vehicles already cruising on the interstate, who must legally yield?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: The entering driver must yield the right-of-way to vehicles already on the interstate.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: Even though ramp traffic must legally yield, what should drivers already on the interstate do near on-ramps?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Drivers already on the interstate should, for their own safety, make room for vehicles trying to enter, even though the entering driver must yield.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: Why must you never stop at the tip of an on-ramp, and how should you time tight traffic gaps instead?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Do not stop at the end of an on-ramp; if you must wait for a gap, slow down on the ramp so you still have room to build speed, because stopping invites rear-end crashes.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: What does an interstate 'Lane Added' sign tell both entering ramp drivers and right-lane freeway drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: A lane added sign means the ramp becomes a new lane so entering traffic need not merge at once, and through drivers should avoid moving right there.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: What does an interstate 'Merge' sign tell drivers, unlike a 'Lane Added' sign?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: A merge sign means traffic from the right must merge into the existing right lane, so drivers already on the interstate should watch for it.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: What extra allowance should you give heavy trucks and buses accelerating down an interstate entrance ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: Trucks and buses joining the interstate may need extra time and space to fit into traffic, so give it to them.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: Which lane stays open for overtaking on multi-lane interstates, and where should you avoid cruising beside other cars?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: On multi-lane interstates, leave the far left lane for faster traffic, and do not ride alongside other vehicles where you sit in their blind spots.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: What are the three downsides of constant freeway lane-hopping compared with holding an even speed?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: Driving at an even speed reduces the need to change lanes, and lane-hopping raises crash risk, feeds road rage and rarely saves real time.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: Why should you avoid cruising bunched inside tight clusters of freeway cars?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: Avoid traveling in packs of cars and keep a space cushion around you for emergency moves.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: What minimum following gap applies on interstates in clear conditions versus storms, darkness, or fast rural stretches?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: On the interstate stay at least two seconds behind the vehicle ahead, and at least four seconds in bad weather, at night and on higher-speed rural stretches.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.front: What bad habit triggers many multi-car interstate chain-reaction crashes?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.expected_back: Following too closely causes many multiple-car crashes, and higher interstate speeds call for longer gaps.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: How many seconds down the road should your eyes scan while cruising on an interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Scan about fifteen to twenty seconds ahead for vehicles braking, entering or leaving.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: How should you alert fast-approaching drivers behind you when interstate traffic ahead suddenly slows or stops?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: If traffic ahead slows or stops, tap your brake pedal lightly several times to warn the drivers behind you.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: May you break the posted speed limit just to match faster interstate traffic, and where belong slower drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: Keep pace with traffic but never exceed the posted limit to stay with the flow, and if you drive slower than the flow, use the right lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Why does Tennessee law outlaw driving too slowly on an interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: Driving too slowly on an interstate is illegal because it is as dangerous as speeding.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: What is the far-left interstate lane reserved for, and what must you do when a faster vehicle closes behind you?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: The left lane is for passing only; if a faster driver comes up behind you there, move one lane to the right.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: On multi-lane interstates, drivers in which lanes should stay ready to yield rightward for overtaking traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: Drivers in every lane except the right-hand slow lane should be ready to move over so faster traffic can pass.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: During which weekday rush-hour windows are Tennessee HOV lanes restricted, and which vehicles qualify?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: During the morning peak of seven to nine a.m. and the evening peak of four to six p.m., the HOV lane is reserved for vehicles with two or more people, motorcycles, buses and emergency vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: Does an infant in a car seat count toward HOV occupancy, and may a solo driver duck into the HOV lane to pass?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: A baby in a car seat counts as a passenger for the HOV lane, and a single driver may not use it during peak hours even to pass.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: How do HOV lanes operate on weekends and off-peak hours, and what fine hits peak-hour violators?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: Outside peak weekday hours and on weekends, the HOV lane works as an ordinary lane, and an HOV violation brings a fifty dollars fine plus court costs.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: Where do Tennessee interstate HOV lanes sit, and how do you enter one from an on-ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: HOV lanes sit at the far inside of the interstate, so to use one you merge onto the highway normally and then move across to the far inside lane.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: At peak HOV hours, how does the occupant rule for a bus compare with a motorcycle?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Buses need two or more occupants to use the HOV lane at peak hours, while a motorcycle qualifies with just its rider.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: What must you plan early if your exit comes up before the inside HOV lane ends?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: If you plan to exit before the HOV lane ends, you must carefully move back across to the exit lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: When should you move into the right-hand lane ahead of your planned interstate exit?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Move to the right lane early when you plan to exit, to avoid last-second lane changes.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: How far ahead do advance interstate exit signs typically appear, and how does heavy traffic change your timing?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: Exit signs usually appear at least one mile before the exit, and in heavier traffic you should get into the exit lane sooner.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: When exiting an interstate, at what exact point should you start slowing down?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: Keep your speed until you are in the deceleration lane, then slow to the ramp's posted speed and on to the limit of the road you are joining.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: What pavement marker pattern typically outlines an interstate exit's deceleration lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: The deceleration lane at an exit is usually outlined by a row of white reflectors.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: What are the only two legal reasons to drive onto an interstate's paved shoulder?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: Do not drive on the interstate's paved shoulder except where marked for slowing down or in an emergency.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: When is parking on any part of an interstate entrance or exit ramp legal?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: Parking on any part of an entrance or exit ramp is illegal unless the vehicle is disabled.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: At a standard diamond interchange, where does the exit ramp split off, and how do you turn onto the crossroad?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: At a diamond interchange the exit ramp always comes before you pass over or under the cross road, and you then obey its sign or signal and turn as at any intersection.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: Driving along the surface crossroad at a diamond interchange, where do you find the right-turn on-ramp versus the left-turn on-ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: From the cross road at a diamond interchange, the right-turn entrance ramp comes before you cross the interstate and the left-turn ramp after it, never the other way around.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: How do you end up going left at a cloverleaf interchange where every ramp exits to the right?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: At a cloverleaf interchange every turn is a right turn: to go left, take the right-hand ramp just after the overpass.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: At a cloverleaf interchange, which ramp takes you right onto the cross highway?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: At a cloverleaf, turning right means taking the right-hand ramp before the overpass, and the loop for a left turn leaves you heading as if you had turned left.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: What traffic-flow advantage does a full cloverleaf interchange provide?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: A cloverleaf's advantage is that no turn crosses the path of other traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: What makes a weaving interchange one of the riskiest spots on an interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: A weaving interchange, where entering and exiting traffic share one lane, is among the most hazardous spots and calls for give-and-take from every driver.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.front: How should entering and exiting drivers handle conflict inside a weaving interchange?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.expected_back: At a weaving interchange, follow routine on-ramp entry procedures while watching for interstate vehicles moving right toward the exit ramp, with both drivers yielding and sharing in an equal give-and-take manner.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: Which three turn-around moves are illegal if you miss your interstate exit?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: Backing up, making a U-turn or crossing the median on an interstate is illegal; if you miss your exit, go on to the next one.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.front: When is a left turn or U-turn ever legal on an interstate, and who may use unmarked median strips?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.expected_back: Left turns and U-turns on the interstate are allowed only through an opening provided and marked for them, and only emergency and maintenance crews may cross the median.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: What rules cover unsignaled lane changes, blind-spot cruising, and improvised interstate entries?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: On the interstate you may not change lanes without signaling, drive in another driver's blind spot, or get on except through a provided entrance.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.front: Where is non-emergency stopping or parking allowed along an interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.expected_back: Stopping or parking on the interstate is allowed only in areas provided for it, and parking on the shoulder only in an emergency.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.front: Which four ongoing checks and spacing habits keep long interstate drives trouble-free?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.expected_back: Good interstate habits include signaling well ahead, checking mirrors often, keeping a safe following distance and checking your speed and fuel gauges often.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.front: Which three unexpected living or traffic hazards must you stay alert for even on controlled-access interstates?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.expected_back: Watch for pedestrians from broken-down vehicles, animals on the road and drivers going the wrong way.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.front: What updates appear on overhead TDOT SmartWay Dynamic Message Signs, and what does a blank board mean?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.expected_back: Dynamic Message Signs on urban Tennessee interstates, part of TDOT's SmartWay system, show real-time crash, weather and construction news, travel times and Amber Alerts, and are blank when not in use.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.front: Why is nighttime driving far deadlier per mile than daytime driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.expected_back: Night driving is far more dangerous per mile than daytime driving, mainly because of fatigue and poor vision, and drinking drivers are more often out at night.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.front: What causes 'interstate hypnosis' on long freeway drives?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.expected_back: Interstate hypnosis is drowsiness or unawareness brought on by long monotonous driving and the steady sound of wind, engine and tires.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.front: Which three actions combat interstate hypnosis, and why must drowsiness trigger an immediate stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.expected_back: To fight interstate hypnosis, keep your eyes moving, keep the car cool, and stop as soon as you feel drowsy, since drowsiness is the first step to falling asleep.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.front: How often should you stop and stretch on long highway trips, and what daily driving cap does the manual advise?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.expected_back: Stop and step out of the car for a rest at least every two hours or about every one hundred miles, and avoid driving more than eight hours a day.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.front: Which four everyday driver habits cause both interstate crashes and phantom traffic jams?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.expected_back: Rubbernecking, tailgating, needless lane changes and inattention all cause crashes and add to congestion.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.front: How do empty gas tanks and skipped maintenance affect everyone else on an interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.expected_back: Vehicles that run out of gas or break down from poor maintenance can cause bottlenecks, so watch your fuel and maintain your car.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.front: On highways with two or more same-direction lanes, what does the Move Over Law require near flashing stopped work or emergency rigs?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.expected_back: The Move Over Law requires you to leave an empty lane next to a stopped emergency, utility, maintenance or recovery vehicle with flashing lights on an interstate or other highway with two or more lanes your way.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.front: Does Move Over apply to left-median shoulders too, and when is slowing in your lane allowed instead of moving over?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.expected_back: Moving over applies whichever shoulder the vehicle is on, and you may simply slow down in your lane only when a lane change would be unsafe.

sec10-card-sec10-R21.front: Which lane do you shift into when a flashing vehicle sits on the right shoulder versus the left median shoulder?
sec10-card-sec10-R21.expected_back: When the stopped vehicle is on the right shoulder, move into the left lane; when it is on the left shoulder, move into the right lane, leaving the nearest lane empty.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.front: Does Tennessee's Move Over protection extend to ordinary civilian cars and pickups stopped with hazard flashers blinking?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.expected_back: The Move Over rule also covers any stopped vehicle on the shoulder, emergency lane or median that is showing flashing lights, including ordinary cars and trucks.

sec10-card-sec10-R22.front: Which six categories of official and service fleets are protected under Tennessee's Move Over Law?
sec10-card-sec10-R22.expected_back: The Move Over Law covers police and Highway Patrol cars, ambulances and fire vehicles, utility and sanitation trucks, tow trucks, TDOT HELP and maintenance vehicles, and road contractors.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.front: What are your immediate first two moves when your car loses power or blows a tire on an interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.expected_back: With car trouble, get onto the right shoulder or an emergency stopping area quickly and switch on your flashers.

sec10-card-sec10-R23.front: How do you signal visibly that your broken-down vehicle needs assistance, and where should you wait?
sec10-card-sec10-R23.expected_back: If your car breaks down and you need help, raise the hood and tie a white cloth to the hood or antenna, and if possible wait in or near the car on the side away from traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-R24.front: Why should families stay with a disabled vehicle instead of walking the interstate shoulder for help?
sec10-card-sec10-R24.expected_back: Walking along the interstate is dangerous, so keep children away from traffic, and a passing officer not on another call will stop to help a driver who stays with the vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-R25.front: In which four major Tennessee metro areas do yellow TDOT HELP trucks patrol to assist stranded motorists?
sec10-card-sec10-R25.expected_back: In Memphis, Nashville, Chattanooga and Knoxville, yellow TDOT HELP trucks may also assist stranded drivers.

sec10-card-sec10-R26.front: What authority do TDOT HELP operators hold over vehicles blocking lanes, and how must you treat their directions?
sec10-card-sec10-R26.expected_back: HELP operators may remove any vehicle that obstructs or endangers traffic, and you must follow their directions as you would a police officer's.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.front: After an interstate crash with no serious injuries or fatalities, what does Tennessee law let you do with a drivable car?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.expected_back: After an interstate crash with no serious injuries or deaths, Tennessee law lets you move a drivable vehicle to the emergency lane to wait for police.

sec10-card-sec10-R27.front: How do Tennessee's stay-at-the-scene duty and TDOT shoulder signs work together after a minor wreck?
sec10-card-sec10-R27.expected_back: While waiting at a crash scene you must stay, but you should not block traffic unnecessarily; TDOT signs remind drivers to move damaged vehicles to the shoulder when no one is seriously hurt.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.front: Which three actions must you never take after a serious or fatal crash?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.expected_back: Never move a seriously injured person unless emergency personnel tell you to, never disturb a fatal crash scene, and never leave the scene of any crash.

sec10-card-sec10-R28.front: Which core tire, power, safety, signaling, and document items belong in a suggested roadside emergency kit?
sec10-card-sec10-R28.expected_back: A suggested roadside emergency kit includes an excellent spare tire, jack and tire iron, tire pressure gauge, flashlight with spare batteries, first aid kit, fire extinguisher, jumper cables, three fuses or reflectors, insurance and registration papers, and a cell phone.

sec10-card-sec10-R29.front: Which extra items should join your emergency kit for winter road trips versus hot summer drives?
sec10-card-sec10-R29.expected_back: For winter trips also carry a blanket, a small portable heater, an ice scraper and snow tires or chains, and in summer carry bottled water.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: Which two broad topics are covered in Section C of the Tennessee driver manual?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: Section C of the manual is devoted to safety tips for safe driving and for sharing the road with others.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: Does your duty to learn traffic rules end once you earn a license, or how long does it last?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: Learning traffic laws and safe habits does not end with your license; drivers are responsible for keeping up with new laws, rules and safety practices for life.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: How does a new driver turn written manual rules into automatic behind-the-wheel habits?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: New drivers need practice and experience to turn the manual's written guidance into habits, so the manual advises reviewing it often.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: What does aiming high in steering require you to do with your eyes?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: Aim high in steering: look as far down the road as you can to pick up the traffic information you need for good decisions.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: How should you use your eyes instead of staring at a single spot in traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: Keep your eyes moving: scan instead of staring, shifting your gaze constantly so you keep up with changing traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: What spacing habit lets you get the big picture and judge real hazards around your car?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: Get the big picture by keeping a proper following distance so you can judge the real hazards around your vehicle, and do not tailgate.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: Where must you keep open space around your car so you always leave yourself an out?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: Leave yourself an out by keeping open space in front of your vehicle and on at least one side so you can escape a conflict.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: Which three vehicle tools help you catch eye contact so drivers and pedestrians notice you?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: Make sure others see you by using your horn, lights and signals to make eye contact with drivers and pedestrians.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: Beyond signaling with horn and lights for eye contact, what should you confirm about nearby drivers and walkers?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: Communicate in traffic using your horn, lights, and signals to make eye contact with motorists and pedestrians, and be reasonably sure of people's intentions.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: Which four ongoing actions define defensive driving before an obstacle or car becomes a crash?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: Defensive driving means staying constantly aware of conditions, planning ahead, anticipating dangers and acting in time to avoid hitting any obstacle or vehicle.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: What should a defensive driver expect from other motorists while keeping their own driving consistent?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: Driving defensively means expecting other people's errors and being ready to make up for them, while behaving predictably yourself so you do not confuse others.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: Which two attitudes toward fellow road users does the manual rank as the key to safe driving?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: The manual calls courtesy and consideration toward others the most important driving attitudes and the key to safe driving.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: What financial and legal headaches can hit you even after a minor collision with zero injuries?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: Even a collision with no injuries brings inconvenience and repair bills and can lead to court, fines and higher insurance rates, so a clean record protects you financially.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: What assumption should you make about another driver's next move, and what should you keep ready?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: Expect the other driver to do the wrong thing, and have a plan ready to counter the mistake.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: Roughly what percentage of behind-the-wheel road information enters through a driver's eyes?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: Drivers take in about ninety percent of their information about the road and surroundings through their eyes.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: Which three mental distractions does the manual warn have zero place behind the wheel?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: Concentration is one of the most important parts of safe driving, so daydreaming, sightseeing and distracting conversations have no place behind the wheel.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: How many seconds—and roughly what city distance—ahead should a defensive driver aim their focus?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: Defensive drivers focus their eyes about ten to fifteen seconds ahead, roughly one city block, so they see trouble early and have more time to react.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: Which three visual clues warn that a parked or stopped car is about to pull into your lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: Watch for exhaust smoke, brake or backup lights and turned wheels, which signal that a vehicle may pull into your path.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: What three things should you sweep for from side to side as you travel down a street?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: Scan from side to side for directional signs and for cars or people that could be in the road by the time you get there.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: Which hidden entrances, terrain features, and surface shifts require extra alertness on rural roads?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: In rural areas, watch for hidden intersections and driveways, curves, hills and changing road surfaces such as pavement turning to gravel or a narrowing road.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: In what exact sequence should you look before entering an intersection, and why does that side come first?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: Before entering any intersection, look left first because cars from the left are closer, then look right, then take one more quick look left.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: How regularly should you monitor your rearview mirrors, and before what lateral move is a check mandatory?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: Check your rearview mirrors constantly, and always check them before you change lanes.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: Roughly how often should you flick a brief glance to your rearview mirror, and what are you checking for?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: Check your rearview mirror about every ten seconds to spot anyone closing too fast or tailgating, without taking your eyes off the road ahead for more than a brief glance.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: During which four specific maneuvers or road grades must you check traffic behind your car?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.memory_hook: Lane changes, backing, hard braking, downgrades
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: Look at the traffic to your rear before a lane change, before backing, before braking hard and on long steep downgrades.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: What two details about surrounding vehicles let you make fast, safe choices when emergencies pop up?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: When you track how fast and where the traffic is on every side of your car, you can decide quickly and safely in most situations.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: Why must you avoid lingering in another vehicle's blind spot?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: Stay out of other drivers' blind spots so that another vehicle does not turn into you.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: How do you measure the two-second following rule using a roadside object?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: Follow the two-second rule: pick a fixed object ahead and count one thousand one, one thousand two; if you pass it before finishing, you are too close and should slow down.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: To how many seconds should your following gap expand on fast interstates, behind large rigs, or in bad weather?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.memory_hook: Stretch gap three to four seconds
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: On high-speed interstates, behind large trucks or buses, and in bad weather or poor visibility, increase your following gap to at least three to four seconds.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: What bad habit causes common rear-end crashes, and where besides normal travel should you leave extra stopped buffer?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: Rear-end crashes are very common and are caused by tailgating, so keep at least two seconds of space ahead, with extra room at railroad crossings and when stopped behind a vehicle on a hill or curve.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: Which four directions around your car make up a complete defensive safety cushion?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: Keep a safety cushion of space in front, behind and on each side of your vehicle so you have an escape route in an emergency.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: How should you clear a tailgater on a multi-lane road versus on a single-lane road?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: If someone tailgates you, move to the right lane if there is one; otherwise, once the way ahead is clear and a pass would be legal, ease off your speed gradually so the tailgater goes around.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: Why must you never tap or slam your brakes suddenly to scare off a tailgater?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: Never brake suddenly to discourage a tailgater, because it only raises your risk of being hit from behind.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.front: Which two smooth habits help the driver behind you maintain a safe following gap?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.expected_back: You can help keep a following driver at a safe distance by holding a steady speed and signaling early before you slow down or turn.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: What is the real safety goal of communicating in traffic with drivers and pedestrians?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.memory_hook: Show moves early to avoid crashes
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: Communicating in traffic means making your next move clear to drivers and pedestrians in time for them to avoid a collision.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: Which direction changes require a turn signal, and does an apparently empty street let you skip signaling?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: Use your turn signal any time you change direction, including lane changes, turns, entering an interstate and pulling to or from the curb, even when no other vehicle is in sight.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.front: What restriction still applies when you speed up or slow down to manage space around your car?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.expected_back: Controlling the space around you may mean slowing down or speeding up, but only within lawful limits.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: Where inside your lane should you position your car when meeting oncoming traffic on a two-lane road?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: When meeting oncoming traffic on a two-lane road, keep a little right of center in your lane so you do not crowd the centerline.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: When splitting the difference between two hazards like parked cars and an oncoming semi, who gets extra space?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.memory_hook: Favor extra room from deadlier hazards
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: Split the difference between two hazards by steering a middle course, but give more room to the more dangerous one, such as an oncoming semi-truck rather than parked cars.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: How do you handle overtaking a bicyclist when an oncoming car will reach you at the same moment?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: Take hazards one at a time: when overtaking a bicyclist with an oncoming car approaching, slow down, let the car pass, then move left to give the bicycle room.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.front: Which roadside cars and people need extra side clearance, and which age group needs the most?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.expected_back: Leave extra space between your vehicle and parked cars, pedestrians and bicyclists at the roadside, especially children.

sec14-card-sec14-R18.front: What should you add when bushes, sun glare, or umbrellas block sightlines for you or others?
sec14-card-sec14-R18.memory_hook: Add extra space around blind views
sec14-card-sec14-R18.expected_back: Allow extra space when vision is blocked for you or another driver, for example by bushes at an intersection, glaring sun or pedestrians with umbrellas.

sec14-card-sec14-R19.front: How should you adjust space around drivers or walkers absorbed in phones, sightseeing, or children?
sec14-card-sec14-R19.expected_back: Allow extra space around drivers or pedestrians who are distracted by phones, roadside attractions, sightseeing or tending to children.

sec14-card-sec14-R20.front: Which clues reveal a confused driver or pedestrian who needs extra space?
sec14-card-sec14-R20.expected_back: Allow extra space around confused drivers or pedestrians, such as those weaving between lanes, hunting for street names or reading maps.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: At least how many seconds of gap do you need to merge or change lanes, and how do you cross multiple lanes?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.memory_hook: Four-second gap, one lane per move
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: You need a gap of at least four seconds to change lanes, enter a roadway or merge, and you should cross several lanes one at a time, never cutting across them all at once.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.front: What courteous move should you make on a multi-lane road when ramp traffic is trying to merge?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.memory_hook: Move left to open merging space
sec14-card-sec14-R13.expected_back: On multi-lane roads, be courteous and move to the left lane when other vehicles are trying to merge into traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-R15.front: What three traffic consequences can result from cutting across several lanes at once?
sec14-card-sec14-R15.memory_hook: Jams traffic, wrecks you or others
sec14-card-sec14-R15.expected_back: Cutting across several lanes at once can tie up traffic, cause you to crash, or cause a crash between other drivers trying to avoid you.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: When must you stay out of an intersection even if the traffic light is green?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: Do not enter an intersection unless you can get all the way across, and never block it or leave part of your vehicle in a lane of approaching traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.front: Roughly how long does passing at fifty-five miles per hour take, and may you break the speed limit to pass?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.expected_back: Passing at fifty-five miles per hour takes about ten seconds, so you need a ten-second gap in oncoming traffic and enough sight distance, and passing never allows you to exceed the speed limit.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.front: What visual check in your rearview mirror tells you it is safe to pull back in after passing a car?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.expected_back: After passing, wait to move back into the driving lane until both headlights of the passed vehicle show in your rearview mirror.

sec14-card-sec14-R16.front: How many vehicles should you generally pass at once, and what space ahead must exist before starting?
sec14-card-sec14-R16.memory_hook: One vehicle with return gap open
sec14-card-sec14-R16.expected_back: As a general rule, pass only one vehicle at a time, and do not pass unless there is room to return to the driving lane.

sec14-card-sec14-R17.front: Why must you never count on the driver you are passing to create space for your return?
sec14-card-sec14-R17.expected_back: When finishing a pass, do not count on the other driver to make room for you; you need enough space behind you to return safely.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.front: How should you react when another driver misjudges a pass and runs low on room?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.expected_back: When another driver makes a mistake, such as passing without enough room, do not make it worse; slow down and give that driver room to get back into the lane.

sec14-card-sec14-R21.front: At which three road features should you slow down and expect abrupt lane merges?
sec14-card-sec14-R21.expected_back: Slow down and leave room for drivers merging suddenly around road hazards, from ending lanes, or onto and off expressways.

sec14-card-sec14-R22.front: Which three roadside situations can push a neighboring driver abruptly into your lane?
sec14-card-sec14-R22.memory_hook: Other mergers, work zones, emergency vehicles
sec14-card-sec14-R22.expected_back: Slow down and leave room for drivers who may be forced into your lane by another merging vehicle, road construction or emergency vehicles on the roadside.

sec14-card-sec14-R23.front: Roughly what share of annual traffic fatalities does the manual link to aggressive driving behaviors?
sec14-card-sec14-R23.expected_back: The manual cites the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration as saying about sixty-six percent of yearly traffic deaths are caused by aggressive driving such as passing on the right, running red lights and tailgating.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.front: Which behaviors—from following distance and horn use to extreme violence—count as aggressive driving?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.expected_back: Aggressive driving includes tailgating, honking, rude gestures, yelling, speeding, cutting others off and even using firearms.

sec14-card-sec14-R24.front: How are police departments and auto insurers responding to aggressive drivers?
sec14-card-sec14-R24.expected_back: Law enforcement agencies and insurance companies are getting much tougher on aggressive drivers.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.front: What three emotional and attention rules keep you from escalating a road-rage confrontation?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.expected_back: To avoid road rage, give driving your full attention, control your emotions and do not join a confrontation, even by honking or glaring.

sec14-card-sec14-R25.front: Which five everyday driving habits keep you out of road-rage triggers?
sec14-card-sec14-R25.memory_hook: Relaxed, lawful speed, space, needed passes
sec14-card-sec14-R25.expected_back: To avoid road rage, obey the law, drive defensively, drive relaxed and within the speed limit, do not tailgate, and pass only when you need to.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.front: How should you respond around an angry driver instead of taking bad traffic behavior personally?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.expected_back: Give an angry driver plenty of space, and do not take traffic problems personally; stay polite even when others are rude.

sec14-card-sec14-R27.front: What does the manual warn about a motorist who habitually gets angry behind the wheel?
sec14-card-sec14-R27.expected_back: A driver who tends to get angry behind the wheel must change that attitude and behavior, or becomes a crash waiting to happen.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.front: Where should you drive if another motorist starts following you aggressively?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.memory_hook: Head to police or public help
sec14-card-sec14-F36.expected_back: If a driver follows you, go to a police station or another public place where you can get help.

sec14-card-sec14-R26.front: What detail should you note and what action should you take if someone harasses you in traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-R26.expected_back: If you are harassed on the road, try to get the offender's license plate number and report the incident to the authorities.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.front: Does bad weather cause most traffic collisions, or in what weather do most crashes actually occur?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.memory_hook: Most crashes happen in clear weather
sec15-card-sec15-F01.expected_back: Most crashes happen in clear weather rather than in snow, rain or fog, so a pleasant day can be just as deadly.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.front: How do many motorists react right before an impending crash, and why is that reaction wrong?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.memory_hook: Never freeze; act to reduce impact
sec15-card-sec15-F02.expected_back: When a collision seems about to happen, many drivers panic and do nothing, yet there is almost always some action that can avoid the crash or lessen it.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.front: What are the three physical actions a driver can use to avoid an impending collision?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.expected_back: To avoid a collision a driver has three options: stop, turn, or speed up.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.front: Why should you check your vehicle owner's manual regarding your car's braking system?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.memory_hook: Know how your antilock system stops
sec15-card-sec15-R01.expected_back: Read your vehicle owner's manual to learn how its antilock braking system works, since antilock brakes let you stop without skidding.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.front: How should you use the brake pedal during a sudden emergency stop with antilock brakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.memory_hook: Stomp firmly and hold steady pressure
sec15-card-sec15-F04.expected_back: To stop quickly with antilock brakes, press the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep firm pressure on it, without letting up even when the pedal pushes back.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.front: How hard should you press the pedal in an emergency stop when your car lacks antilock brakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.memory_hook: Press hard just short of lockup
sec15-card-sec15-F05.expected_back: To stop quickly without antilock brakes, brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels, since braking too hard or too long can cause a skid.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.front: What pedal action restores rolling grip if your wheels lock up without antilock brakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.memory_hook: Ease off briefly, then squeeze again
sec15-card-sec15-F06.expected_back: Without antilock brakes, if the wheels lock and you feel a skid, let up on the pedal quickly, then press down again once the skid stops, repeating until the car stops.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.front: How does steering control during hard emergency braking differ with antilock brakes versus without them?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.memory_hook: Antilock keeps steering; locked wheels slide
sec15-card-sec15-F07.expected_back: In an emergency with antilock brakes the wheels do not lock and the car can still be steered, while without them all wheels may lock and the skidding car cannot be steered properly.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.front: Why must you never pump an antilock brake pedal when you feel rapid pulsing underfoot?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.memory_hook: Never pump; system pulses faster automatically
sec15-card-sec15-F22.expected_back: Never pump the brake pedal in a car with antilock brakes, even when the pedal pulses; the pulsing is the system pumping the brakes faster than you could.

sec15-card-sec15-R13.front: What happens if rattle or vibration startles you into easing off an antilock brake pedal?
sec15-card-sec15-R13.memory_hook: Easing off ruins antilock stopping power
sec15-card-sec15-R13.expected_back: With antilock brakes, keep your foot firmly on the pedal despite the pulsing and noise, because easing off ruins the system's advantage.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.front: Does having antilock brakes justify following closer or driving more aggressively?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.memory_hook: Never drive more aggressively with antilock
sec15-card-sec15-F24.expected_back: Never drive a car with antilock brakes more aggressively than one without them.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.front: Why should you steer around an obstacle rather than rely on braking alone when stopping room runs short?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.memory_hook: Cars turn faster than they stop
sec15-card-sec15-F08.expected_back: In most cases you can turn your vehicle faster than you can stop it, so if you cannot stop in time, steer around the hazard and brake only if you must.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.front: Where on the steering wheel should your hands sit for quick evasive steering and airbag safety?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.expected_back: For quick turns, grip the wheel with both hands on opposite sides at about the nine o'clock and three o'clock positions, which also keeps your wrists and forearms out of the air bag's main impact area.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.front: How do your right and left hands move on the wheel during a quick evasive turn to the left?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.memory_hook: Right swings across; left slides low
sec15-card-sec15-R02.expected_back: For a quick evasive turn to the left, the right hand swings from three o'clock toward nine o'clock as far as needed while the left hand slides toward the bottom of the wheel to steady the grip.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.front: What steering sequence brings your car straight into the lane after swerving left past a hazard?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.memory_hook: Steer right, straighten left, reset hands
sec15-card-sec15-R03.expected_back: As you clear the hazard, turn the wheel back to the right to regain your lane, then left just enough to straighten out, returning your hands to nine and three; for a quick right turn, mirror every step.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.front: Why must you stay poised to steer immediately after dodging an initial road hazard?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.memory_hook: Stay controlled to prevent secondary crashes
sec15-card-sec15-F10.expected_back: After steering away from a hazard, be ready to keep control and steer where you want the car to go, because some drivers dodge one crash only to cause another.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.front: What advantage do antilock brakes provide when you must swerve and slow down simultaneously?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.memory_hook: Steer and brake together without skidding
sec15-card-sec15-F11.expected_back: With antilock brakes you can steer while braking without skidding, which helps when you must swerve and stop or slow quickly.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.front: In what order must you handle the brake pedal and steering wheel for a quick turn without antilock brakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.expected_back: Without antilock brakes, to turn quickly you must let up on the brake pedal and then turn the wheel.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.front: How does braking right before releasing to turn help a car without antilock brakes corner faster?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.memory_hook: Braking shifts grip onto front tires
sec15-card-sec15-R04.expected_back: Braking before a quick turn without antilock brakes slows the car and shifts weight onto the front tires, which lets it turn faster.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.front: What two mistakes cause front tires to lose steering bite and plow straight forward?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.memory_hook: Locked front brakes or over-cranked steering
sec15-card-sec15-F13.expected_back: Stop braking if you feel the front wheels lock, and do not turn so sharply that the car can only plow straight ahead.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.front: When forced to choose between leaving the roadway and hitting an oncoming vehicle head-on, which is safer?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.memory_hook: Drive off-road rather than hit head-on
sec15-card-sec15-F14.expected_back: It is generally better to drive off the road than to crash head-on into another vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.front: In what crash setup is speeding up the safest choice, and what should follow once clear?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.memory_hook: Accelerate past side or rear hits
sec15-card-sec15-F15.expected_back: Speeding up can be the right move when another vehicle is about to hit you from the side or behind and there is room ahead, but slow down once the danger passes.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.front: What severe danger comes from jerking the steering wheel violently during an emergency?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.memory_hook: Jerking triggers rollovers or off-road wrecks
sec15-card-sec15-F23.expected_back: Do not freeze at the wheel or jerk it suddenly in an emergency, because a jerk can send you into another object or off the road and into a rollover.

sec15-card-sec15-R14.front: How do you combine antilock braking and steering all the way past a sudden obstacle?
sec15-card-sec15-R14.memory_hook: Hold brake, steer past to safety
sec15-card-sec15-R14.expected_back: Use the antilock system's nonskid ability to steer around the obstacle that made you brake, and keep steering to a safe place once past it.

sec15-card-sec15-R15.front: Where and at what speed does the manual suggest practicing antilock panic stops and swerves?
sec15-card-sec15-R15.memory_hook: Empty lot around twenty miles hourly
sec15-card-sec15-R15.expected_back: To practice antilock braking, use a big empty lot without curbs or many light poles, drive about twenty miles per hour, slam the brakes and steer, later steering around a cardboard box as a target.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.front: Which season brings the highest risk of deer collisions, and what two seasonal triggers cause it?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.memory_hook: Autumn mating and hunting stir deer
sec15-card-sec15-F16.expected_back: Fall is the peak season for deer crashes, because autumn's mating and hunting seasons make deer more active and likely to wander.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.front: Which animal accounts for the most dangerous and expensive wildlife collisions on highways?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.memory_hook: Deer cause costliest, deadliest animal crashes
sec15-card-sec15-F17.expected_back: Crashes with deer are generally the most dangerous and costly kind of animal crash.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.front: At what two times of day and near which two landscape features should you watch hardest for deer?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.memory_hook: Dusk and dawn near woods, water
sec15-card-sec15-F18.expected_back: Be especially alert for deer at dusk and dawn, when they come out to feed, and near woods and water.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.front: What should you expect immediately whenever a single deer crosses or stands near the road?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.memory_hook: One deer means others trail close
sec15-card-sec15-F19.expected_back: If you see one deer, expect that several others may be close by.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.front: Are animal collisions limited to autumn nights and deer, or when and with what animals can they happen?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.memory_hook: Any animal, any season, any hour
sec15-card-sec15-R05.expected_back: Animal crashes can happen in any season and with any animal, from opossums and rabbits to dogs, and while many deer crashes occur at night, they can happen at any hour.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.front: Has any device or barrier proven completely foolproof at keeping deer and wildlife off highways?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.expected_back: No foolproof method has been found to keep deer and other wild animals off highways.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.front: What three habits—using signs, scanning, and nighttime lighting—help you spot deer before they jump out?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.memory_hook: Heed signs, scan wide, high beams
sec15-card-sec15-R07.expected_back: To avoid deer, heed deer crossing signs, look far down the road and well off to each side, and at night use high beams when you can to light the road edges.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.front: What glowing clue along dark roadsides reveals a deer standing near the pavement?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.memory_hook: Headlight beams reflecting off deer eyes
sec15-card-sec15-R08.expected_back: Scan the roadsides for your headlights reflecting in a deer's eyes.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.front: Which three steps should you take when you spot an animal ahead with time to react?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.memory_hook: Slow down, tap brakes, honk horn
sec15-card-sec15-R09.expected_back: If you have time to avoid an animal ahead, slow down, tap your brakes to warn drivers behind you, and sound your horn.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.front: Why can flashing your headlights at a deer in the roadway backfire?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.expected_back: Deer tend to fixate on headlights, so flashing your lights at one may make it freeze in the road.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.front: How firmly should you brake for an animal when your mirror shows nobody following closely behind?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.expected_back: If no vehicle is close behind you, brake hard for an animal but do not lock the wheels into a skid.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.front: Why must you hold your lane rather than swerve when striking an animal cannot be avoided?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.memory_hook: Never swerve; stay straight on pavement
sec15-card-sec15-F20.expected_back: If hitting an animal seems unavoidable, do not swerve, since swerving may raise your risk of injury; keep the car under control and on the road.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.front: Whom must you notify after a collision with a deer or livestock?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.expected_back: Report a crash with a large animal such as a deer or farm animal to the police.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.front: What courteous step should you take if you accidentally strike a household pet near homes?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.expected_back: If you hit a domestic pet near homes, try to let the owner know if you can.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.front: What single root cause drives most traffic collisions, led by which three driver mistakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.memory_hook: Human error; speed, inattention, bad swerves
sec15-card-sec15-F25.expected_back: Human error is the single most common cause of traffic crashes, and the leading factors are excessive speed, lack of concentration and improper evasive action.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.front: Which three connected elements make up the highway safety system?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.expected_back: Safe driving depends on three parts of the highway system, the driver, the vehicle and the road, and neglecting any of them contributes to most crashes.

sec15-card-sec15-R17.front: Which three commitments separate a responsible driver from a careless one?
sec15-card-sec15-R17.memory_hook: Maintain vehicle, obey laws, respect others
sec15-card-sec15-R17.expected_back: A good driver takes pride in caring for the vehicle, obeys traffic laws and respects others, while a careless driver neglects all three.

sec15-card-sec15-R18.front: Roughly how many reported Tennessee crashes each year does the manual trace to poor driving habits?
sec15-card-sec15-R18.memory_hook: One hundred sixty thousand yearly crashes
sec15-card-sec15-R18.expected_back: The manual attributes about one hundred sixty thousand crashes reported to the Department of Safety each year to poor driving habits.

sec15-card-sec15-R19.front: Which four personal conditions show a motorist is physically and mentally fit to drive?
sec15-card-sec15-R19.expected_back: Being in shape to drive means seeing clearly, being rested, being free of drugs, and being healthy and emotionally fit.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.front: How can everyday states like worry, frustration, fatigue, anger, or a head cold affect your driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.memory_hook: Everyday moods and colds impair safety
sec15-card-sec15-F27.expected_back: Temporary conditions such as anger, worry, frustration, fatigue or even a cold can make you an unsafe driver.

sec15-card-sec15-R26.front: What should you do when a stiff neck, coughing spell, or sore leg makes physical control uncomfortable?
sec15-card-sec15-R26.expected_back: If you feel unwell, even from a stiff neck, cough or sore leg, let someone else drive.

sec15-card-sec15-F33.front: Under what two medical conditions may a Tennessee resident with epilepsy hold driving privileges?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.memory_hook: Doctor's care plus six seizure-free months
sec15-card-sec15-F33.expected_back: In Tennessee, a person with epilepsy may drive if under a doctor's care and seizure-free for at least six months.

sec15-card-sec15-R27.front: When must a driver taking insulin for diabetes stay out from behind the wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-R27.expected_back: A diabetic on insulin should stay off the road whenever an insulin reaction, blackout, convulsion or shock is possible, for example after skipping a meal.

sec15-card-sec15-R28.front: Which heart, blood-pressure, or circulation patients must not drive, and whom should treated heart patients consult?
sec15-card-sec15-R28.memory_hook: No blackout risk; consult your doctor
sec15-card-sec15-R28.expected_back: People with heart disease, high blood pressure or circulation problems who risk blackouts, fainting or a heart attack should not drive, and anyone treated for a heart condition should ask a doctor about driving.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.front: How should you handle strong anger before driving, and how do impatient drivers beat the urge to speed?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.memory_hook: Cool off first; leave extra time
sec15-card-sec15-F34.expected_back: If you are angry or excited, give yourself time to calm down before driving, and if you are impatient, plan extra time for trips so delays do not tempt you to speed.

sec15-card-sec15-R29.front: Can years of driving experience make someone safe behind the wheel when buzzed on alcohol or drugs?
sec15-card-sec15-R29.expected_back: No one, regardless of skill or experience, can drive safely when buzzed or impaired by alcohol or drugs.

sec15-card-sec15-R20.front: How does darkness affect every driver's eyesight, and what oncoming light adds extra trouble?
sec15-card-sec15-R20.memory_hook: Darkness dims everyone; glare blinds worse
sec15-card-sec15-R20.expected_back: Everyone sees worse at night, and some drivers struggle with the glare of oncoming headlights.

sec15-card-sec15-R21.front: What sensible habit should you adopt if you have difficulty seeing clearly at night?
sec15-card-sec15-R21.expected_back: If you have trouble seeing at night, limit night driving to what is necessary and be very careful when you do.

sec15-card-sec15-R22.front: During which two highway maneuvers does judging vehicle speed and distance matter most?
sec15-card-sec15-R22.expected_back: Judging distance and speed takes practice and matters most when merging and when judging gaps to pass on two-lane roads.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.front: How often does the manual recommend having an eye specialist examine your vision?
