sec15-card-sec15-F28.memory_hook: Check vision every year or two
sec15-card-sec15-F28.expected_back: Because seeing well is so important, have your eyes checked by an eye specialist every year or two.

sec15-card-sec15-F29.front: What does restriction code one on your Tennessee license require, and what happens if you drive without them?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.memory_hook: Wear corrective lenses or face fines
sec15-card-sec15-F29.expected_back: If your license shows the corrective lens restriction, code one, you must wear your glasses or contacts at all times while driving, or you could be ticketed and fined.

sec15-card-sec15-R23.front: Should corrective-lens wearers skip glasses on quick neighborhood errands, and what backup belongs in the car?
sec15-card-sec15-R23.memory_hook: Wear every trip; stash spare glasses
sec15-card-sec15-R23.expected_back: If you need glasses or contacts, wear them even on short trips, and keep a spare pair in the vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.front: Why must you never wear dark sunglasses or tinted contact lenses while driving after sunset?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.expected_back: Do not wear dark sunglasses or tinted contact lenses at night, since they cut the light you need to see.

sec15-card-sec15-R24.front: Which three audible traffic warnings does hearing catch, and how do hearing-impaired drivers make up for it?
sec15-card-sec15-R24.expected_back: Hearing helps you notice horns, sirens and screeching tires, and hearing-impaired drivers can compensate with their vision.

sec15-card-sec15-R25.front: Which four pre-trip choices help prevent highway drowsiness before a long drive?
sec15-card-sec15-R25.memory_hook: Sleep well, eat light, skip sedatives
sec15-card-sec15-R25.expected_back: To avoid fatigue, get a normal night's sleep, eat lightly before a long trip, avoid medicine that causes drowsiness, and try not to drive when you would normally be asleep.

sec15-card-sec15-F31.front: At least how often should you pull over to stretch and refresh during a long highway trip?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.expected_back: On long drives, stop for a break every hour or more often if needed, walking around and getting fresh air and a drink.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.front: What is the only safe move when you start feeling sleepy behind the wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.expected_back: Never drive while sleepy; pulling over for a few hours of sleep beats gambling that you can stay awake.

sec15-card-sec15-R30.front: Which four warning signs mean a mechanic should inspect your brakes immediately?
sec15-card-sec15-R30.memory_hook: Weak feel, noise, smell, sinking pedal
sec15-card-sec15-R30.expected_back: Have a mechanic check your brakes if they seem weak, are noisy, smell odd or the pedal sinks to the floor.

sec15-card-sec15-R31.front: From where must you inspect your car's headlights, taillights, brake lamps, and turn signals?
sec15-card-sec15-R31.expected_back: Check turn signals, brake lights, taillights and headlights from outside the vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-R32.front: In what weather do car batteries lose charge fastest, and what emergency gear belongs in your trunk?
sec15-card-sec15-R32.memory_hook: Cold, damp weather; carry jumper cables
sec15-card-sec15-R32.expected_back: Batteries run down faster in cold or damp weather, and keeping jumper cables in the car can get you started again.

sec15-card-sec15-R33.front: Why must cracked windshields and streaking wiper blades be repaired or replaced promptly?
sec15-card-sec15-R33.memory_hook: Cracks shatter easily; bad wipers smear
sec15-card-sec15-R33.expected_back: Repair or replace a damaged windshield, since cracked glass can break in a minor collision, and replace wiper blades that no longer clear the glass.

sec15-card-sec15-R34.front: What two visibility checks should you perform every time you stop for fuel?
sec15-card-sec15-R34.memory_hook: Top antifreeze washer fluid, scrub glass
sec15-card-sec15-R34.expected_back: Check the non-freezing washer fluid level each time you fill up with gas, and clean the windshield at gas stops so sun or headlights do not blur your view.

sec15-card-sec15-F35.front: Which four hazards rise sharply when you drive on worn or bald tire tread?
sec15-card-sec15-F35.expected_back: Worn or bald tires lengthen stopping distance, make turning harder on wet roads, raise the chance of a flat and can cause hydroplaning.

sec15-card-sec15-F36.front: How do you run the penny tread test, and what fraction of an inch marks an illegal, unsafe tire?
sec15-card-sec15-F36.memory_hook: Full Lincoln head means under two-thirty-seconds
sec15-card-sec15-F36.expected_back: In the penny test, insert a penny head first into the tread; if the tread does not reach Lincoln's head, two thirty-seconds inch, the tire is illegal and unsafe and must be replaced.

sec15-card-sec15-R35.front: How do underinflated or unbalanced wheels hurt your tires, gas tank, and vehicle control?
sec15-card-sec15-R35.memory_hook: Faster wear, wasted fuel, sloppy handling
sec15-card-sec15-R35.expected_back: Unbalanced tires and low pressure wear tires faster, waste fuel and make the vehicle harder to steer and stop.

sec15-card-sec15-F37.front: Where is your car's recommended tire pressure listed, and why should you ignore the number molded on the tire sidewall?
sec15-card-sec15-F37.memory_hook: Follow door-jamb sticker, never sidewall maximum
sec15-card-sec15-F37.expected_back: Use the recommended tire pressure on the sticker in the driver's door jamb, not the pressure printed on the tire, which is only the tire's maximum.

sec15-card-sec15-R36.front: Whom should you ask for proper inflation pressure after mounting aftermarket tires in a non-factory size?
sec15-card-sec15-R36.memory_hook: Consult the tire maker or installer
sec15-card-sec15-R36.expected_back: If you have put on aftermarket tires of a different size, ask the tire maker or installer for the right pressure, since the door-jamb figure no longer applies.

sec15-card-sec15-R37.front: What car behavior after hitting a bump or stopping tells you a mechanic should inspect the shocks?
sec15-card-sec15-R37.expected_back: If the car keeps bouncing after a bump or a stop, or is hard to control, have a mechanic check the shocks and suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F38.front: What happens mechanically if you twist the ignition key to the lock position while rolling?
sec15-card-sec15-F38.memory_hook: Steering wheel locks, losing all control
sec15-card-sec15-F38.expected_back: Never turn the ignition to the lock position while the car is moving, because the steering wheel will lock and you will lose control.

sec15-card-sec15-F39.front: Besides ordinary tiredness, what deadly mechanical problem can sudden sleepiness inside a car warn of?
sec15-card-sec15-F39.memory_hook: Sudden drowsiness can signal exhaust leaks
sec15-card-sec15-F39.expected_back: A sleepy feeling while driving or riding may mean an exhaust leak, which must be fixed at once because exhaust gases can kill inside a vehicle in a very short time.

sec15-card-sec15-F40.front: In which enclosed or stuck situations must you never leave a vehicle engine running?
sec15-card-sec15-F40.expected_back: Never run the engine in a closed garage or wherever the tailpipe may be blocked, including when the car is stuck in mud or snow.

sec15-card-sec15-R38.front: What window rule applies during long idling, and what is forbidden during extended rest-stop naps?
sec15-card-sec15-R38.memory_hook: Crack windows; never nap engine running
sec15-card-sec15-R38.expected_back: When idling for a long time, open a window for fresh air, and never sleep or sit with the engine running during an extended rest stop.

sec15-card-sec15-R39.front: Under what engine-temperature condition may you check the radiator, and why maintain proper coolant fullness?
sec15-card-sec15-R39.memory_hook: Check cold only; blocks boilover, freezing
sec15-card-sec15-R39.expected_back: Check the radiator only when the engine is cool, and keep coolant at the level the owner's manual recommends to prevent overheating or freezing.

sec15-card-sec15-F41.front: At least how full should your gas tank be before setting out on any substantial trip?
sec15-card-sec15-F41.expected_back: Make sure your vehicle has at least a half tank of gas before any trip of significant length.

sec15-card-sec15-R40.front: What two hazards do loose water bottles or unsecured gear inside the cabin create?
sec15-card-sec15-R40.memory_hook: Jam brake pedals or become projectiles
sec15-card-sec15-R40.expected_back: Keep loose objects off the floor where they could roll under the brake pedal, and secure items that could hit someone in a sudden stop.

sec15-card-sec15-R41.front: For what single purpose should a vehicle's horn be sounded?
sec15-card-sec15-R41.memory_hook: Sound horn strictly to warn others
sec15-card-sec15-R41.expected_back: Use the horn only as a warning to others.

sec15-card-sec15-R16.front: How much minimum time cushion belongs ahead in normal conditions, and when must you stretch it?
sec15-card-sec15-R16.memory_hook: Two seconds minimum, wider in hazards
sec15-card-sec15-R16.expected_back: Keep at least a two-second cushion behind the vehicle ahead, and more when conditions are hazardous.

sec15-card-sec15-R42.front: Why does matching the surrounding traffic flow cut multi-vehicle crash risk?
sec15-card-sec15-R42.expected_back: Vehicles moving the same direction at the same speed cannot hit one another, and multi-vehicle crashes often happen when drivers go faster or slower than traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-R43.front: Which four busy traffic clues or districts call for easing off your speed early?
sec15-card-sec15-R43.memory_hook: Distant brake lights, malls, downtown, rush-hour
sec15-card-sec15-R43.expected_back: Slow down where people and traffic gather, such as when brake lights come on several cars ahead, in shopping centers and downtown areas, and at rush hour.

sec15-card-sec15-R44.front: Why must you adjust your speed when entering narrow bridges or highway tunnels?
sec15-card-sec15-R44.memory_hook: Tighter clearances put oncoming cars closer
sec15-card-sec15-R44.expected_back: On narrow bridges and in tunnels, approaching vehicles pass closer together, so adjust your speed.

sec15-card-sec15-F42.front: What unpredictable hazard must you scan for constantly near schools, playgrounds, and residential blocks?
sec15-card-sec15-F42.memory_hook: Children darting or riding out unannounced
sec15-card-sec15-F42.expected_back: Near schools, playgrounds and residential streets, always watch for children who may cross, run or ride into the street without looking.

sec15-card-sec15-R45.front: Which two clearances must you verify before starting across railroad tracks, plus how do you handle rough rails?
sec15-card-sec15-R45.memory_hook: No train, clear exit, slow bumps
sec15-card-sec15-R45.expected_back: At railroad crossings, make sure no train is coming and you have room to get across, and slow down on bumpy crossings.

sec15-card-sec15-R46.front: Why should experienced drivers still read a new state's driver manual even when written exams are waived?
sec15-card-sec15-R46.memory_hook: Learn local laws and periodic updates
sec15-card-sec15-R46.expected_back: Good drivers review the manual periodically for law changes and study the driver manual of any new state they move to, even when no test is required.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: What must Tennessee drivers under eighteen complete before holding a full, unrestricted license?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Graduated stages phase in higher-risk nighttime and passenger situations slowly while new teen drivers build real traffic judgment.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: What are the four stages of Tennessee's graduated licensing program in order?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Test questions scramble the two intermediate stages to check that Restricted comes right after the permit and before Unrestricted.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: Where on the card is the three-letter graduated program code printed during the first three stages?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Officers can spot graduated status immediately from the three-letter program mark stamped in the card's bottom left corner.
sec03-card-sec03-F03.must_match_memory_hook: Printed in the bottom left corner

visual_sync.text_span: Printed in the bottom left corner

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: Which two graduated stages include a separate Restriction Card to carry, and what information does it show?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Both permit and Intermediate Restricted teens carry that extra card so driving limits and upgrade requirements stay clear.
sec03-card-sec03-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Lists current limits and advancement steps

visual_sync.text_span: Lists current limits and advancement steps

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: What minimum age and two exam steps are required to get a Tennessee learner permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Turning fifteen and clearing both the standard written exam and vision check opens the door to supervised driving.
sec03-card-sec03-F04.must_match_memory_hook: Age fifteen plus written and vision

visual_sync.text_span: Age fifteen plus written and vision

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: How many days must a teen hold the learner permit before advancing to an Intermediate Restricted License?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Even if you turn sixteen tomorrow, you cannot advance until your learner permit hits the full one-hundred-eighty-day mark.
sec03-card-sec03-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Hold permit one hundred eighty days

visual_sync.text_span: Hold permit one hundred eighty days

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: Who must ride with a learner permit driver, and where in the car must they sit?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Solo driving or letting a supervising adult nap in the back seat breaks Tennessee's permit supervision law.
sec03-card-sec03-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Licensed adult twenty-one in front seat

visual_sync.text_span: Licensed adult twenty-one in front seat

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: Between which nighttime and early-morning hours is a learner permit holder barred from driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Learner permit driving shuts down completely at ten in the evening until six in the morning when crash risk spikes.
sec03-card-sec03-F07.must_match_memory_hook: No driving ten night to six

visual_sync.text_span: No driving ten night to six

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: How does reaching six or more record points affect a teen's learner permit wait?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Hitting six points freezes advancement until your driving record stays below six points for one hundred eighty straight days.
sec03-card-sec03-F21.must_match_memory_hook: Stay under six for one-eighty days

visual_sync.text_span: Stay under six for one-eighty days

sec03-card-sec03-R16.question_text: How many months does a teen learner permit last, and what fee applies under age eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-R16.teaching_text: Knowing the twelve-month validity and ten-dollar-fifty fee prevents confusion with the cheaper adult permit rate.
sec03-card-sec03-R16.must_match_memory_hook: Twelve months for ten dollars fifty

visual_sync.text_span: Twelve months for ten dollars fifty

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: What minimum age and behind-the-wheel test are required for the Intermediate Restricted License?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Clearing the on-road skills exam at age sixteen moves a teen from full-time supervision into limited solo driving.
sec03-card-sec03-F08.must_match_memory_hook: Turn sixteen and pass road test

visual_sync.text_span: Turn sixteen and pass road test

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: How many total and nighttime practice hours must be certified for the Intermediate Restricted License, and who can sign?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Without a parent, guardian, or licensed instructor certifying fifty practice hours including ten after dark, road-test upgrades stop.
sec03-card-sec03-F09.must_match_memory_hook: Fifty hours total, ten at night

visual_sync.text_span: Fifty hours total, ten at night

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: What license class and yellow top-bar wording appear on both intermediate teen cards?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Both intermediate tiers carry Class D privileges while displaying Intermediate Driver License across the front yellow banner.
sec03-card-sec03-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Class D with yellow Intermediate header

visual_sync.text_span: Class D with yellow Intermediate header

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: What minimum age and time in the Restricted stage are needed to reach the Intermediate Unrestricted License?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Both conditions apply together, meaning a teen must be at least seventeen and complete twelve months in Restricted.
sec03-card-sec03-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Age seventeen after one restricted year

visual_sync.text_span: Age seventeen after one restricted year

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: Which crash or seatbelt infractions block the Intermediate Unrestricted upgrade, and are new exams required?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Clean Restricted drivers advance without taking another exam, whereas an at-fault wreck or second seatbelt ticket blocks promotion.
sec03-card-sec03-F11.must_match_memory_hook: At-fault crash or two belt tickets

visual_sync.text_span: At-fault crash or two belt tickets

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: Why do holders of the Intermediate Unrestricted License stop receiving a separate restriction card?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Once passenger and curfew caps lift at the Unrestricted tier, carrying an extra restriction insert becomes unnecessary.
sec03-card-sec03-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Zero driving restrictions mean no card

visual_sync.text_span: Zero driving restrictions mean no card

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: What fee applies when moving from Intermediate Restricted to Intermediate Unrestricted after one year?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Upgrading after your restricted year skips testing fees and requires only a two-dollar application charge.
sec03-card-sec03-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Two-dollar application fee after one year

visual_sync.text_span: Two-dollar application fee after one year

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: Which three milestones unlock a regular Class D license, and which age marking still stays on the card?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Graduating high school or turning eighteen removes the word Intermediate, though under-twenty-one indicators remain until twenty-one.
sec03-card-sec03-F12.must_match_memory_hook: Eighteen or graduation; keeps under-twenty-one mark

visual_sync.text_span: Eighteen or graduation; keeps under-twenty-one mark

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: At age eighteen, what two choices does a driver have regarding the word Intermediate on their card?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Turning eighteen makes removing the Intermediate label optional, letting you either buy an eight-dollar duplicate or ride out five years.
sec03-card-sec03-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Pay eight dollars or wait renewal

visual_sync.text_span: Pay eight dollars or wait renewal

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: In what orientation has Tennessee printed every license issued to drivers under twenty-one since July two thousand eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Vertical orientation gives officers and clerks an instant visual check that the cardholder was under twenty-one when issued.

sec03-card-sec03-F39.question_text: Which three paths allow an emancipated sixteen-year-old to obtain a regular Class D license directly?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.teaching_text: Legal emancipation through military service, marriage, or court order lets a sixteen-year-old hold regular Class D status.
sec03-card-sec03-F39.must_match_memory_hook: Active military, marriage, or court emancipation

visual_sync.text_span: Active military, marriage, or court emancipation

sec03-card-sec03-F35.question_text: How many passengers may an Intermediate Restricted teen carry, and which two exceptions allow more?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.teaching_text: Extra teen friends spike crash risk, so exceptions cover only a licensed adult twenty-one-plus or household siblings on lettered school trips.
sec03-card-sec03-F35.must_match_memory_hook: One passenger unless adult or siblings

visual_sync.text_span: One passenger unless adult or siblings

sec03-card-sec03-F36.question_text: During what hours may an Intermediate Restricted teen not drive, and which four exceptions allow trips?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.teaching_text: Late-night trips need a parent, a designated licensed adult twenty-one-plus, written school or work permission, or licensed early-morning hunting or fishing.
sec03-card-sec03-F36.must_match_memory_hook: Eleven night to six, four exceptions

visual_sync.text_span: Eleven night to six, four exceptions

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: How does the nighttime curfew start hour change between a learner permit and an Intermediate Restricted License?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Exam questions swap ten and eleven at night to test whether you know permits park one hour earlier than restricted drivers.
sec03-card-sec03-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Ten for permits, eleven for restricted

visual_sync.text_span: Ten for permits, eleven for restricted

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: How does the role of a twenty-one-year-old licensed driver differ between the permit stage and the Restricted stage?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: On a permit an adult twenty-one-plus is mandatory up front, whereas on Restricted that adult lifts the one-passenger cap.
sec03-card-sec03-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Supervises permits, unlocks extra restricted passengers

visual_sync.text_span: Supervises permits, unlocks extra restricted passengers

sec03-card-sec03-F40.question_text: During the permit and intermediate stages, which ages require seat belts and which require child restraints?
sec03-card-sec03-F40.teaching_text: Teen drivers are responsible for buckling every rider four through seventeen and securing children under four in proper restraints.
sec03-card-sec03-F40.must_match_memory_hook: Belts four to seventeen, restraints younger

visual_sync.text_span: Belts four to seventeen, restraints younger

sec03-card-sec03-R14.question_text: Which type of crash happens most often in work zones, and what two habits prevent it?
sec03-card-sec03-R14.teaching_text: Sudden construction slowdowns punish tailgaters with rear-end collisions unless you drop to the posted work-zone speed early.
sec03-card-sec03-R14.must_match_memory_hook: Rear-end crashes dominate; slow, stop tailgating

visual_sync.text_span: Rear-end crashes dominate; slow, stop tailgating

sec03-card-sec03-R15.question_text: What four actions should every driver take when approaching and driving through a work zone?
sec03-card-sec03-R15.teaching_text: Turning headlights on ahead of cones, merging early, staying in your lane, and obeying flaggers prevents sudden work-zone sideswipes.
sec03-card-sec03-R15.must_match_memory_hook: Headlights on, merge early, obey flaggers

visual_sync.text_span: Headlights on, merge early, obey flaggers

sec03-card-sec03-F38.question_text: Roughly how many minor traffic tickets add up to six points on a teen's driving record?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.teaching_text: Realizing that just two routine moving tickets hit the six-point penalty threshold shows how fast teen setbacks trigger.
sec03-card-sec03-F38.must_match_memory_hook: Two minor tickets equal six points

visual_sync.text_span: Two minor tickets equal six points

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: Which two serious offenses revoke an Intermediate Restricted License and drop a teen back to a permit until eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Faking parental permission or contributing to a fatal wreck wipes out solo teen driving privileges until age eighteen.
sec03-card-sec03-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Forged parent note or fatal crash

visual_sync.text_span: Forged parent note or fatal crash

sec03-card-sec03-F37.question_text: What penalty follows a conviction for carrying a forged or fraudulent parental permission letter?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.teaching_text: Forging a curfew or sibling permission note costs every solo driving privilege and locks you on a permit until eighteen.
sec03-card-sec03-F37.must_match_memory_hook: Revokes restricted license until age eighteen

visual_sync.text_span: Revokes restricted license until age eighteen

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: Which three setbacks add ninety days onto the one-year Intermediate Restricted requirement?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Any of those three infractions stretches your Restricted stage from twelve months out to one year and three months.
sec03-card-sec03-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Six points, crash, or second belt

visual_sync.text_span: Six points, crash, or second belt

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: How does hitting six or more points punish a learner permit holder differently than an Intermediate Restricted driver?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Written exams contrast these penalties directly: permits restart a one-hundred-eighty-day clean streak while Restricted tacks ninety days onto the year.
sec03-card-sec03-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Permits restart one-eighty; restricted adds ninety

visual_sync.text_span: Permits restart one-eighty; restricted adds ninety

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: What extra requirement applies when an Intermediate Restricted teen gets convicted of a second moving violation?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: A second moving ticket blocks upgrading until you finish a state-certified driver education course.
sec03-card-sec03-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Complete certified driver education before advancing

visual_sync.text_span: Complete certified driver education before advancing

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: What happens if a violation from your Restricted period hits state records after you already upgraded to Unrestricted?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Delayed court reporting never lets you dodge accountability; state records roll your license back to Restricted for ninety days.
sec03-card-sec03-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Drops back to Restricted ninety days

visual_sync.text_span: Drops back to Restricted ninety days

sec03-card-sec03-F32.question_text: Which mobile phone uses are banned while driving with a Tennessee learner permit or intermediate license?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.teaching_text: Whether handheld or built into the car, any mobile phone call or use while driving breaks Tennessee's teen phone law.
sec03-card-sec03-F32.must_match_memory_hook: Zero mobile or car phone use

visual_sync.text_span: Zero mobile or car phone use

sec03-card-sec03-F33.question_text: What four consequences hit a teen convicted of violating the graduated driver cell phone ban?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.teaching_text: One phone ticket delivers six points at once plus a fifty-dollar Class C misdemeanor fine and ninety extra restricted days.
sec03-card-sec03-F33.must_match_memory_hook: Fifty fine, six points, ninety-day delay

visual_sync.text_span: Fifty fine, six points, ninety-day delay

sec03-card-sec03-F34.question_text: Who is barred from texting while driving in Tennessee, and how much can the fine and court costs reach?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.teaching_text: Texting behind the wheel is illegal for adults and teens alike, carrying up to fifty dollars plus ten-dollar court costs.
sec03-card-sec03-F34.must_match_memory_hook: Every driver; fifty fine, ten costs

visual_sync.text_span: Every driver; fifty fine, ten costs

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: Which credential can a fifteen-year-old newcomer with an out-of-state permit get, and what must happen before Restricted?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Even with prior out-of-state practice, a fifteen-year-old starts on a Tennessee permit until reaching age sixteen and one hundred eighty permit days.
sec03-card-sec03-F13.must_match_memory_hook: Learner permit until sixteen and one-eighty

visual_sync.text_span: Learner permit until sixteen and one-eighty

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: How can a newcomer teen credit prior out-of-state permit days toward Tennessee's one-hundred-eighty-day rule?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Only an official certified driving history dated within thirty days before applying lets examiners credit your former state's permit time.
sec03-card-sec03-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Bring certified record within thirty days

visual_sync.text_span: Bring certified record within thirty days

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: What happens if a newcomer teen's out-of-state driving history shows an accident or traffic violation?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Examiners issue only a learner permit until Driver Improvement verifies that your out-of-state history stays below six points.
sec03-card-sec03-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Hold permit pending Driver Improvement review

visual_sync.text_span: Hold permit pending Driver Improvement review

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: Which Tennessee stage does a sixteen-year-old apply for when holding a valid out-of-state license for at least ninety days?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Holding another state's full teen license at least ninety days lets a sixteen-year-old step straight into Intermediate Restricted.
sec03-card-sec03-F17.must_match_memory_hook: Ninety days qualifies for Intermediate Restricted

visual_sync.text_span: Ninety days qualifies for Intermediate Restricted

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: How can a teen whose out-of-state license is under ninety days old still qualify for Intermediate Restricted?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Combining clean permit and license time to reach one hundred eighty total days bridges an out-of-state card held under ninety days.
sec03-card-sec03-F18.must_match_memory_hook: Clean record with one-eighty combined days

visual_sync.text_span: Clean record with one-eighty combined days

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: Does prior driving time in another state shorten Tennessee's one-year Intermediate Restricted requirement?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Test questions trap newcomers into subtracting prior months, when every teen must still hold Tennessee's Restricted card one full year.
sec03-card-sec03-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Never; full Tennessee year still applies

visual_sync.text_span: Never; full Tennessee year still applies

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: Which adults are eligible to sign a minor's financial-responsibility teen affidavit?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Only a parent, step-parent, or foster parent at your address, a legal guardian, or an authorized grandparent can accept liability.
sec03-card-sec03-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Same-address parent, guardian, or authorized grandparent

visual_sync.text_span: Same-address parent, guardian, or authorized grandparent

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: How can a teen complete the financial-responsibility affidavit when the signing adult cannot visit the Driver Service Center?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Getting the teen affidavit notarized ahead of time saves a wasted appointment when a parent's work schedule prevents attending.
sec03-card-sec03-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Sign beforehand before a notary public

visual_sync.text_span: Sign beforehand before a notary public

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: What extra notarized paper must a grandparent bring when signing financial responsibility for a teen?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: A grandparent cannot sign solo without a notarized permission slip from the parent, step-parent, custodian, or guardian.
sec03-card-sec03-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Notarized authorization from parent or guardian

visual_sync.text_span: Notarized authorization from parent or guardian

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: What must a parent or guardian sign again if a minor adds another vehicle class such as a motorcycle?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Liability on a passenger car does not automatically extend to motorcycles, so adding a new class requires its own signed affidavit.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: How do high school graduates versus currently enrolled Tennessee students prove school compliance, and how long does the form last?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Graduates bring an original diploma or equivalency certificate, while enrolled students carry a school compliance form valid thirty days.
sec03-card-sec03-F28.must_match_memory_hook: Original diploma, or thirty-day school form

visual_sync.text_span: Original diploma, or thirty-day school form

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: Can a teen use grade cards or school transcripts to prove school attendance at the licensing counter?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: Bringing a printed report card or transcript gets rejected every time because examiners accept only official compliance forms or diplomas.
sec03-card-sec03-F29.must_match_memory_hook: Report cards and transcripts never count

visual_sync.text_span: Report cards and transcripts never count

sec03-card-sec03-R11.question_text: How long is a school attendance form honored over summer break when signed during the final thirty days of school?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.teaching_text: Grabbing your signed form in the final month before summer break keeps you covered until thirty days after fall classes start.
sec03-card-sec03-R11.must_match_memory_hook: Valid thirty days into next schoolyear

visual_sync.text_span: Valid thirty days into next schoolyear

sec03-card-sec03-R12.question_text: What school proof do students bring from out-of-state or private schools that do not carry standard Tennessee forms?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.teaching_text: Official school letterhead signed by the principal or headmaster substitutes cleanly when a school lacks Tennessee's standard attendance form.
sec03-card-sec03-R12.must_match_memory_hook: Principal letterhead confirming student not truant

visual_sync.text_span: Principal letterhead confirming student not truant

sec03-card-sec03-R13.question_text: Which two items must a home-schooled teen bring to prove school compliance?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.teaching_text: Home-schooled teens need both the local school director's annual intent confirmation and the state home-school form signed by a parent.
sec03-card-sec03-R13.must_match_memory_hook: Director's intent letter plus parent form

visual_sync.text_span: Director's intent letter plus parent form

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: How does losing and regaining driving privileges differ between a student's first dropout and a second dropout?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: Re-enrolling restores eligibility after dropping out once, whereas a second dropout locks out driving privileges until age eighteen.
sec03-card-sec03-F30.must_match_memory_hook: First re-enrolls; second waits until eighteen

visual_sync.text_span: First re-enrolls; second waits until eighteen

sec03-card-sec03-F31.question_text: How much extra must a teen pay to reinstate driving privileges after returning to school?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.teaching_text: Returning after a dropout requires a twenty-dollar reinstatement charge on top of standard application and license fees.
sec03-card-sec03-F31.must_match_memory_hook: Twenty-dollar reinstatement fee plus card fees

visual_sync.text_span: Twenty-dollar reinstatement fee plus card fees

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: Which three authorized people on the road outrank posted signs and traffic signals whenever their instructions differ?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Live officers, flaggers, and school crossing guards see real-time hazards that fixed bulbs cannot.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: How can you still identify a stop sign even when snow, mud, or tree branches hide its lettering?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Recognizing the unique red eight-sided silhouette lets you stop safely before reading a single letter.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: What types of traffic messages appear on rectangular signs?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Speed limits, turn rules, and lane assignments use vertical or horizontal rectangles to state enforceable rules.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: Which five specific signs or route shields are the ONLY ones that use a red background?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Red always commands immediate stopping, prohibited entry, or tops the red-and-blue interstate route shield.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: For what sole purpose are orange road-sign backgrounds reserved?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Spotting orange ahead tells you immediately that construction or maintenance crews and equipment are near.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: Match yellow, brown, green, and blue sign backgrounds to their four road jobs?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Yellow flags general hazards, brown points to parks, green guides exits, and blue lists services.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: What high-visibility color marks school zone signs in Tennessee?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Bright fluorescent yellow-green stands out sharply along tree-lined neighborhood streets during morning bell hours.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: Where else besides schools do fluorescent yellow-green signs appear — and in what weather do they excel?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Fluorescent pigments glow vividly at dawn, dusk, fog, and rain where pedestrians step into crosswalks.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: What kind of roadside situation does a fluorescent pink — or coral — sign warn you about?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Unplanned emergencies like wildfires, hazmat spills, floods, or major wrecks use coral-pink temporary signs.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: How do black and white share duties across regulatory signs and colored sign legends?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: High contrast pairs black print onto white, yellow, and orange backgrounds while white letters top dark boards.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: When the Tennessee manual describes part of a sign as white, what reflective finish counts as white too?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Daytime silver sheeting bounces crisp white light straight back into your headlights after dark.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: Who do temporary traffic control zones protect around an incident — and which five devices guide lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Cones, barricades, flags, lights, and message boards channel cars cleanly around vulnerable rescue crews.

sec07-card-sec07-R33.question_text: Which national standard governs Tennessee's road signs — and why might you spot two versions of a sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R33.teaching_text: Adopting updated national traffic-control sign standards gradually means older and newer sign faces coexist during replacement cycles.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: Which sign is the ONLY eight-sided shape on the road, and where must your wheels stop for it?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Rolling past the painted crosswalk line while braking counts as failing to stop properly.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: After making your full stop at a stop sign, how should you proceed if hedges or parked cars hide cross traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Stop legally behind the line first, then inch forward carefully until you see a safe gap.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: What does a small red ALL WAY plaque mounted beneath a stop sign tell you?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Knowing cross traffic also faces stop signs lets you follow turn-taking right-of-way rules.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: How do you handle a triangular yield sign when the cross road is empty versus heavy with traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Yielding allows rolling carefully into an open road, while requiring a full stop whenever cars approach.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: What does a round yellow warning sign announce ahead, and how should you respond?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Circular signs warn exclusively of railroad grade crossings ahead so you ease speed early.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: Why do drivers lose races against locomotives — and over how many crossing crashes happen yearly?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Large locomotives create an optical illusion of slow movement, fueling over two hundred crossing wrecks yearly.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: What does the white X-shaped crossbuck pinpoint, and what does the small number plaque beneath it warn?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Multi-track plaques warn that a second train can hide right behind the caboose of the first.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: What three rules apply whenever red lights flash on a railroad crossbuck?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Pulling out before checking every parallel track invites getting struck by an unseen second train.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: At a gated railroad crossing, when must you stop and when may you finally pull forward?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Driving around lowered gates or rolling before red lights stop flashing is deadly and illegal.

sec07-card-sec07-R37.question_text: What does a large white X and the letters RR painted directly on the lane warn?
sec07-card-sec07-R37.teaching_text: Roadway paint reinforces roadside warning signs where drivers stare down at traffic ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: What do diamond-shaped signs alert you to, and what speed response do they usually call for?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Spotting a diamond gives you early runway to scrub speed before reaching curves or narrows.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: What does a black line diagram drawn like a tiny map on a yellow diamond sign show?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Seeing whether a side road meets at a crossroad, T, or Y prepares your scan early.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: What recommended speed cutoff separates a sharp-angled Turn warning sign from a rounded Curve sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Right-angle arrow diamonds mean thirty miles per hour or slower, whereas sweeping arrows span thirty to fifty-five.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: What road geometry and spacing distance trigger a Reverse Turn sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Two sharp turns bending opposite ways inside six hundred feet require staying slow between bends.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: What does the small square number plaque mounted beneath a curve or ramp warning sign tell you?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Advisory plaques post the dry-road safe ceiling engineered specifically for that curve or ramp.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: Where should your eyes actually scan when you pass a Falling Rocks warning sign — and why?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Staring up at the bluff misses boulders already sitting across your lane around the bend.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: Why are Stop Ahead, Yield Ahead, and Signal Ahead diamonds posted — and when should braking start?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Hills, trees, or curves hide the stop line or red light until too late at full speed.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.question_text: Contrast your action at a Lane Ends sign against your courtesy move at a Merging Traffic sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.teaching_text: Ending lanes require signaling over, while approaching ramps benefit when through cars step left.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.question_text: What traffic squeeze does a Narrow Bridge diamond prepare you for?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.teaching_text: Lost shoulders on old rural bridges leave bare inches when two wide vehicles meet.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.question_text: Between which two points is the height on a Low Clearance sign measured?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.teaching_text: Box trucks, RVs, or rooftop cargo taller than the posted clearance will strike steel girders.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.question_text: What must you prepare to do at a T-intersection sign, and what do roadside chevron arrows emphasize?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.teaching_text: Your road dead-ends at a T cross-street, while rows of chevrons trace a tight curve.

sec07-card-sec07-R23.question_text: What kinds of fixed hazards right beside the pavement edge do striped object markers highlight?
sec07-card-sec07-R23.teaching_text: Reflective striped panels keep drivers from clipping concrete bridge parapets or support columns at night.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: Which three types of speed information can regulatory speed signs display?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Interstates post minimums alongside maximums, while reduced-speed signs warn before town limits drop.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: How does a timer-controlled school speed sign show its lower limit is active, and where is it placed?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Lit numerals paired with amber flashers protect cross-streets during arrival and dismissal walks.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: On a multi-lane two-way road, what does Keep Right require — and which two moves allow leaving the right lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Keeping slower cruisers right leaves inner lanes clear for passing cars and left-turn setups.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: What engineering measurement determines where no-passing zones go — and which four features hide oncoming cars?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Hills, bends, intersections, and hidden driveways shrink clear forward sight below safe overtaking room.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: What unique shape, colors, and side of the road distinguish the No Passing Zone sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Mounting the sideways pennant on the LEFT road edge keeps it visible right as you peek out behind a truck.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: What universal message does a red circle with a diagonal slash over a black symbol deliver?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Whether over a U-turn arrow, left arrow, or bicycle, the red slash means no.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: Is standing in the roadway to solicit a ride legal in Tennessee?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Stepping into active asphalt lanes to thumb rides endangers both walkers and swerving drivers.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: What two kinds of lane assignments can regulatory lane-control signs enforce?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Overhead white panels sort heavy trucks or lock specific approach lanes into left-only or straight-only paths.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: Which two vehicle categories qualify to use lanes marked with a High Occupancy Vehicle sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Checking the posted minimum passenger count upfront prevents expensive solo-driver carpool lane tickets.

sec07-card-sec07-R27.question_text: Which three credentials authorize parking in a space marked with the blue handicap symbol?
sec07-card-sec07-R27.teaching_text: Leaving wide blue-marked stalls strictly to authorized plates or decals preserves ramp access.

sec07-card-sec07-R16.question_text: What shapes and print color do work-zone signs use, and which five hazards do they flag?
sec07-card-sec07-R16.teaching_text: Black print on orange warns of workers, lower speeds, detours, slow machinery, and closed lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-R17.question_text: What legal weight do the signals of a work-zone flagger holding a paddle or flag carry?
sec07-card-sec07-R17.teaching_text: Disobeying a work-zone flagger invites head-on crashes along single-lane alternating highway construction stretches.

sec07-card-sec07-R18.question_text: What does a large flashing arrow panel ahead warn of, and when should you merge?
sec07-card-sec07-R18.teaching_text: Racing to the barrels before cutting over pinches traffic and endangers cone crews.

sec07-card-sec07-R19.question_text: What tool do flaggers normally hold versus emergencies — and do their hand gestures change?
sec07-card-sec07-R19.teaching_text: Whether holding an octagonal STOP-SLOW paddle or an emergency red flag, stop and go arm motions match.

sec07-card-sec07-R20.question_text: How should you position your car, set speed, and treat lane changes while threaded among cones and drums?
sec07-card-sec07-R20.teaching_text: Holding steady inside one lane until completely clear of barrels prevents clipping workers.

sec07-card-sec07-R21.question_text: Which two fluorescent vest colors help you spot officers, flaggers, and road crews in rain or dusk?
sec07-card-sec07-R21.teaching_text: Bright yellow-green and orange garments cut through fog, twilight, and work-light glare.

sec07-card-sec07-R22.question_text: What emblem marks farm tractors, work rigs, and buggies — and how does it show day versus night?
sec07-card-sec07-R22.teaching_text: Spotting that orange-red triangle warns instantly that the rig ahead creeps below twenty-five miles per hour.

sec07-card-sec07-R24.question_text: What colors form a U.S. highway route marker, and how far does a U.S. route extend?
sec07-card-sec07-R24.teaching_text: Black numerals on a white shield framed in black mark multi-state U.S. highways.

sec07-card-sec07-R25.question_text: What highway network do red-and-blue shield markers identify?
sec07-card-sec07-R25.teaching_text: White numbers on blue crowned in red identify controlled-access interstate highways coast to coast.

sec07-card-sec07-R26.question_text: What happens if you stay in a lane beneath a yellow MUST EXIT or EXIT ONLY interstate sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R26.teaching_text: That through lane drops straight onto the off-ramp unless you signal and merge out early.

sec07-card-sec07-R28.question_text: How close together stand Tennessee's urban interstate reference markers — and in which five cities?
sec07-card-sec07-R28.teaching_text: Tenth-mile posts in Nashville, Knoxville, Memphis, Jackson, and Chattanooga pinpoint crashes for nine-one-one.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: From top to bottom on a vertical signal head, in what order do red, yellow, and green sit?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Standardizing red at the top lets color-blind drivers identify STOP immediately by bulb position.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: Under what three conditions may you turn right at a steady red light in Tennessee?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Rolling through a right-on-red draws a ticket — stop behind the line, check signs, yield walkers and cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: What does a steady yellow traffic light mean — and when is continuing through allowed?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Brake smoothly if safe; only continue carefully when already inside the intersection.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: For at least how many seconds must a yellow signal shine before turning red under Tennessee law?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Tennessee sets a statutory three-second floor so approaching drivers aren't trapped by instant reds.

sec07-card-sec07-R29.question_text: Which cross-street driver mistake makes flooring the gas on a late yellow especially deadly?
sec07-card-sec07-R29.teaching_text: Impatient cross-street drivers rolling early on green T-bone late yellow-runners right inside the intersection.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: Even on a circular green light, which three groups still earn your yield?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Circular green gives unprotected left-turners zero priority over oncoming straight traffic or crosswalks.

sec07-card-sec07-R30.question_text: Why shouldn't you creep into a jammed intersection before your exit lane opens?
sec07-card-sec07-R30.teaching_text: Getting trapped inside the box when your light turns red gridlocks cross traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: What right does a green turn arrow grant — and what yield duty still remains?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Opposing traffic faces red, though you still yield to any pedestrian finishing their crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: What do a yellow turn arrow and a steady red turn arrow each require?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Unlike right-on-circular-red, a steady red arrow in your turn lane bans turning completely.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: What must you yield to before turning left on a flashing yellow arrow?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Flashing yellow arrows permit left turns only through safe gaps after clearing crosswalks.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: Contrast a flashing red intersection beacon against a flashing yellow beacon?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: Treat flashing red identically to a stop sign, while flashing yellow calls for cautious slowing.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.question_text: How does Tennessee law require you to treat an intersection whose traffic lights are completely dark?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.teaching_text: Never blow through an unpowered signal assuming main-road priority — every direction stops.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.question_text: When two vehicles halt simultaneously at an all-way stop, which driver yields?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.teaching_text: Yielding to the vehicle on your right breaks simultaneous arrival ties cleanly.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.question_text: Besides people walking on foot, whom else does Tennessee law classify as a pedestrian?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.teaching_text: Both manual and motorized wheelchair users hold full pedestrian crosswalk rights across Tennessee roadways.

sec07-card-sec07-R31.question_text: What should a pedestrian already mid-street do before DON'T WALK appears — and how are some WALK phases triggered?
sec07-card-sec07-R31.teaching_text: Clearing the curb promptly keeps intersections smooth, and actuated poles wait for a button press.

sec07-card-sec07-R32.question_text: On which two kinds of roadways do overhead lane-control signals appear most often?
sec07-card-sec07-R32.teaching_text: Overhead green arrows and red X's flip rush-hour lanes and mark open toll booths.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.question_text: Which paint color belongs on your right versus your left — and what if yellow sits on your right?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.teaching_text: Reversed edge-line colors warn immediately that you have entered a ramp or divided roadway backward.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.question_text: What fundamental traffic split do yellow pavement lines always indicate?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.teaching_text: Crossing a yellow stripe always puts oncoming headlights in the lane beside you.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.question_text: When may you cross a single broken yellow center line?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.teaching_text: Dashed yellow permits overtaking from either side whenever sightlines and oncoming traffic allow.

sec07-card-sec07-F42.question_text: While passing across double solid yellow lines is banned, what turn across them stays legal when safe?
sec07-card-sec07-F42.teaching_text: Don't miss this distinction — turning left into a driveway or side road may cross solid yellow safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F43.question_text: Along a paired solid-and-broken yellow center line, when may YOU pass — and when must you finish?
sec07-card-sec07-F43.teaching_text: Only the lane bordering dashes may overtake, tucked safely back before solid paint resumes.

sec07-card-sec07-F44.question_text: Contrast broken white, single solid white, and double solid white lines between same-way lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F44.teaching_text: Dashed white allows shifts, single solid discourages weaving, and double solid white forbids crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-R34.question_text: Besides dividing opposing traffic, what fixed travel-path hazards do yellow lines outline?
sec07-card-sec07-R34.teaching_text: Yellow striping steers tires around concrete bridge supports sitting near center medians.

sec07-card-sec07-F45.question_text: Which pedestrians at a corner earn your yield — even where zero white crosswalk stripes exist?
sec07-card-sec07-F45.teaching_text: Every street corner connects sidewalks into a legal crosswalk whether painted white or bare asphalt.

sec07-card-sec07-F46.question_text: Rank the three exact stopping landmarks in order — stop line, crosswalk, or bare corner?
sec07-card-sec07-F46.teaching_text: Halt behind the stop bar first, else before the crosswalk, else short of the intersecting street edge.

sec07-card-sec07-F47.question_text: Contrast a lane painted with a curved arrow plus ONLY against a lane showing combined straight-and-curved arrows?
sec07-card-sec07-F47.teaching_text: Going straight out of an ONLY turn pocket cuts across turning traffic beside you.

sec07-card-sec07-R36.question_text: What rule separates single-headed pavement arrows from double- or triple-headed pavement arrows?
sec07-card-sec07-R36.teaching_text: One arrowhead permits solely that direction, whereas twin or triple heads share movements.

sec07-card-sec07-R35.question_text: How are Tennessee HOV lanes marked on pavement or separated — and what two facts do roadside signs post?
sec07-card-sec07-R35.teaching_text: Painted diamonds or barriers mark the lane while signs state passenger minimums and active hours.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: What must you do if a traffic officer waves you through a red light or orders another normally illegal move?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Live directions from an officer managing a crash or funeral procession override painted lines, signs, and red lights every time.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: Why is coasting downhill in neutral or holding the clutch pedal down illegal and unsafe?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Disengaging engine braking on a grade lets gravity build runaway speed and strips away instant throttle response in an emergency.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: Which direction do you travel around Tennessee traffic circles, roundabouts, and town squares?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Because Tennessee traffic keeps right, every roundabout, rotary, and courthouse square flows counterclockwise to the right.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: Between what evening and morning times does Tennessee law require your headlights to stay on?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Dusk and dawn shadows hide dark cars before total darkness falls, locking in those thirty-minute buffers at both ends.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: Besides nighttime hours, what visibility limit and weather condition require turning on your headlights?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Whenever fog cuts clear sight below two hundred feet—or rain, mist, or snow keeps wipers moving—headlights must come on.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: Within what distance of an oncoming car or a vehicle ahead of you must you dim your high beams?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Tennessee sets the exact same five-hundred-foot cutoff both for approaching headlights and for taillights you are following.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: Which lights are illegal to drive with by themselves in poor visibility or when high beams must be dimmed?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Parking lamps and auxiliary fog beams fail to light the road far enough ahead and can dazzle approaching traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: Although driving on parking lights alone is illegal, when are parking lights actually required?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: When parked or stopped along a road or shoulder in low visibility, parking lamps warn approaching drivers where your car sits.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: For standard vehicles in Tennessee, which two colors are legal for steady front-facing lights?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Decorative blue, red, or green forward lamps confuse drivers at night into mistaking ordinary cars for emergency responders or taillights.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: For ordinary vehicles, what is the only flashing front-facing light setup allowed under Tennessee law?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Aftermarket strobes and grille flashers are banned on civilian cars so real emergency vehicles stay unmistakable.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: How must a truck or trailer carry loose material or trash that could blow or fall onto the road?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Flying gravel, mulch, or trash shatters windshields and forces dangerous swerves at highway speeds unless sealed under a tarp.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: What fine range and cleanup hours can a Tennessee court impose for highway littering?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Tossing trash can cost fifty to three thousand dollars, forty hours picking up roadside litter, and eight recycling-center hours.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: What two passing or lane moves are forbidden around a funeral procession on a two-lane Tennessee road?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Unless a traffic officer waves you around, overtaking a funeral line on two lanes or wedging between its cars breaks state law.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: Even where no minimum speed sign is posted, when does driving slowly violate Tennessee law?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Dropping below a posted minimum in clear weather—or creeping slow enough anywhere to bottle up normal flow—is illegal.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: At what speed below the limit do you count as a slow-moving vehicle, and how many trailing cars require pulling off?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Stacking five or more frustrated drivers behind a car creeping ten-plus under tempts risky head-on passing unless you yield space.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: Under which three roadway conditions is driving below a posted minimum speed limit permitted?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Minimum-speed signs assume dry open pavement, never forcing you to overdrive slick rain, gridlock, or broken road surfaces.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: Is Tennessee's Basic Speed Rule a statute or a safety principle, and can you violate it below the posted limit?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Doing fifty-five on glare ice inside a fifty-five zone still violates this core principle because conditions demand far less speed.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: Under the Basic Speed Rule, how far ahead must you always be able to bring your vehicle to a stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Outrunning your headlights at night or flying blind over a hill crest leaves zero room if a stalled car sits ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: Which roadway, environment, and personal factors shape your safe speed under the Basic Speed Rule?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Safe pace shifts constantly with traffic density, foot traffic, pavement grip, lane width, weather visibility, and your own alertness.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: If the driver ahead slams on the brakes and you rear-end them while driving under the speed limit, what does that prove?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Staying under the posted number never excuses hitting a braking car—either your speed beat conditions or your gap shrank.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.question_text: How does the manual compare the crash risk of overly slow drivers against speeders?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.teaching_text: Big speed gaps trigger sudden braking and lane-weaving around slow cars, so match traffic flow within the legal cap.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: When no other speed sign is posted, what is the default limit on primary and secondary Tennessee state and federal highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Two-lane and multi-lane state or federal routes default to fifty-five miles per hour whenever local signs do not say otherwise.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: What is Tennessee's maximum rural interstate speed limit compared with typical congested urban interstate stretches?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Open rural interstates top out at seventy miles per hour, whereas dense city interstates drop typically to fifty-five for tighter merges.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: In normal uncongested flow, what are the minimum legal speeds in the far-left interstate lane versus the right lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Exam favorite—Tennessee enforces a ten-mile-per-hour higher floor in the far-left passing lane than in outer right lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.question_text: What should you do if driving at the interstate's minimum speed feels too fast for you or your vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.teaching_text: Creeping below forty-five on a seventy-mile-per-hour freeway invites high-energy rear-end crashes, so stick to lower-speed highways.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.question_text: Which three levels of government set speed limits on their respective roads, and what limits are common in neighborhoods?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.teaching_text: Each jurisdiction posts limits for its own streets, frequently capping residential neighborhoods around twenty-five or thirty-five round the clock.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: How does Tennessee law classify speeding in a school zone, and how many points land on your record?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Speeding past school signs is treated automatically as reckless driving, dropping six instant points and triggering a state warning letter.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.question_text: During which three student periods do reduced school-zone speed limits apply?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.teaching_text: Drivers remember morning drop-off and afternoon bell times, yet mid-day recess activates reduced school-zone limits too.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: What minimum and maximum fine range does Tennessee law set for speeding through an active highway work zone?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Speeding past road crews starts at a steep two-hundred-fifty-dollar floor and climbs up to five hundred dollars.

sec08-card-sec08-R16.question_text: Beyond highway paving, what roadside jobs count as work zones, and what visual cues mark them?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.teaching_text: Line crews, tree trimmers, and surveyors get full work-zone protection marked by orange or yellow-green signs, strobes, and high-vis vests.

sec08-card-sec08-R17.question_text: How many deaths, injuries, and property-damage crashes did the manual report for Tennessee work zones in twenty twenty-one?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.teaching_text: Twenty-six deaths, eleven hundred five injuries, and three thousand ten property wrecks in one year show why work-zone limits save lives.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: How should you apply the brakes in everyday driving, and what two hazards come from slamming them late?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Jamming the pedal at the last second locks tires into a skid and catches trailing drivers with no time to react.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: In a vehicle without anti-lock brakes, how do you recover if your wheels lock into a skid?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Lifting off the pedal lets locked tires roll again so steering in the direction the rear is sliding straightens the car.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: How should you brake and steer during a sudden emergency stop in a vehicle equipped with anti-lock brakes?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Keeping steady hard pressure lets ABS pulse the brakes automatically so your front tires can still steer around the obstacle.

sec08-card-sec08-R20.question_text: What pedal feel is normal when anti-lock brakes engage, and what mistake shuts the system off?
sec08-card-sec08-R20.teaching_text: Startled drivers feel rapid pulsing or hear grinding and let up, which immediately cancels anti-lock braking right when needed.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: What is the difference between covering the brake and riding the brake, and which one is safe?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Hovering your foot just above the pedal shaves reaction time safely, whereas resting weight on the pedal is a bad habit.

sec08-card-sec08-R21.question_text: Which two mechanical and traffic problems happen when you ride the brake pedal?
sec08-card-sec08-R21.teaching_text: Constant friction overheats and wears brake linings prematurely while keeping your brake lights lit so drivers behind ignore real stops.

sec08-card-sec08-R18.question_text: How many independent ways of applying the brakes must every legal passenger car have?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.teaching_text: If hydraulic foot brakes fail, a separate mechanical or electric parking brake gives you a backup way to slow down.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.question_text: Before downshifting to slow a manual-transmission car for a stop, what should you do for drivers behind you?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.teaching_text: Engine braking slows your car without lighting the taillights, so a quick brake-light flash warns trailing traffic first.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: What driving mistake causes most rear-end collisions and also shrinks your view ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Crowding a bumper steals both your stopping time and your forward sightline past the vehicle in front of you.

sec08-card-sec08-R22.question_text: How does Tennessee statute define illegal tailgating?
sec08-card-sec08-R22.teaching_text: Legal spacing stretches dynamically—what is reasonable in dry slow traffic turns illegal when speed, volume, or rain increases.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: How do you measure your following distance using Tennessee's two-second rule?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Pick a shadow or signpost—reaching that spot before counting two full seconds after the car ahead means you are tailgating.

sec08-card-sec08-R23.question_text: What should you do right after a fixed-point count shows you are under two seconds behind the car ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-R23.teaching_text: Gently backing off the gas opens space smoothly without startling drivers behind, then a fresh marker confirms at least two seconds.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: In which four driving situations should you double your following gap to at least four seconds?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Wet pavement, limited night sightlines, seventy-mile-per-hour momentum, and quick-stopping motorcycles all demand double the normal two-second cushion.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: Which three sequential stages make up total stopping time, and how long is average reaction time?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Your car rolls huge distances while your brain spots trouble and takes two-thirds of a second just to move your foot.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: In the manual's seventy-mile-per-hour deer example, how far does the car travel before braking starts and before stopping completely?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Traveling more than a football field—four hundred eighteen feet—before stopping explains why overdriving night headlights at seventy is deadly.

sec08-card-sec08-R24.question_text: Which five road and vehicle conditions change how many feet your car needs to stop?
sec08-card-sec08-R24.teaching_text: Worn tread, weak shock absorbers, slick asphalt, or a heavy trailer load all stretch stopping distance well past dry-road averages.

sec08-card-sec08-R25.question_text: According to the National Safety Council figure in the manual, about how many feet does a light car need to stop from fifty miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-R25.teaching_text: Even at a moderate fifty miles per hour, a light passenger car eats roughly twenty car lengths—two hundred feet—to stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: In exact priority order, where must you bring your front bumper to a halt at a stop sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Halt at the painted stop bar first, or before the crosswalk edge, or at a sightline point before nosing into cross-traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: How does Tennessee law define a stop, and does that apply before turning right on red?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Wheels must reach zero rotation—including before any permitted right turn on red—or you just ran the control.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: What visual cue tells you that you left enough space when stopped behind another car in traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Leaving pavement visible beneath their back tires prevents a domino bump if rear-ended and lets you steer out around stalls.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: What two consequences can rolling slowly through a stop sign cost a Tennessee driver or applicant?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Coasting through at two miles per hour earns licensed drivers a citation and hands road-test applicants an automatic fail.

sec08-card-sec08-R26.question_text: After making your full legal stop, what should you do if bushes or parked cars block your view of cross traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-R26.teaching_text: Let pedestrians clear the crosswalk completely, then inch out carefully until you can check both ways before pulling out.

sec08-card-sec08-R27.question_text: Once the car ahead of you stops at a stop sign and drives off, may you follow right through behind it?
sec08-card-sec08-R27.teaching_text: Piggybacking through behind the lead car skips your own required stop at the line and blindsides cross-traffic taking their turn.

sec08-card-sec08-R28.question_text: What physical sensation inside the car tells examiners and officers that your vehicle came to a complete stop?
sec08-card-sec08-R28.teaching_text: When forward motion truly hits zero, weight rocks slightly back onto the rear springs in a distinct little settle.

sec08-card-sec08-R29.question_text: How must you treat a stop paddle or hand signal from a construction flagger compared with a police officer?
sec08-card-sec08-R29.teaching_text: Construction flaggers hold legal traffic-control authority in work zones, often protecting one-lane alternating traffic you cannot see.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: How fast should you approach a railroad crossing, and when is it safe to drive across multiple tracks?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Approach slow enough to halt short of the first rail, and verify a passing train is not hiding a second train.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: Within what exact distance range from the nearest rail must you stop when a train approaches?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Stopping closer than fifteen feet risks overhang impact or derailment debris, and stopping on the rails themselves is a death trap.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: How far out must trains blow their horn, and which four crossing warnings forbid driving onto the tracks?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: A locomotive blasts at fifteen hundred feet, and red flashers, dropping gates, a flagger, or a visible train mean stay back.

sec08-card-sec08-R30.question_text: Which four pavement markings appear ahead of railroad tracks, and how are rail-signal violations penalized?
sec08-card-sec08-R30.teaching_text: Blowing past rail flashers or painted stop bars carries the exact same ticket penalties as running standard intersection traffic signals.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: Which three groups of vehicles must stop at every railroad crossing even when no train or flashing light is present?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Never tailgate school or church buses, taxis, passenger vans for hire, or hazmat tankers near tracks because law forces their stop.

sec08-card-sec08-R31.question_text: How do buses and hazmat tankers signal behind them as they prepare for a mandatory railroad-crossing stop?
sec08-card-sec08-R31.teaching_text: Watch for buses easing right with brake lamps lit and fuel tankers hitting four-way hazard flashers ahead of tracks.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: When meeting or trailing a school or church bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, how long must you remain stopped?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Kids cross blind in front of the hood, so stay frozen until the stop sign folds in and the bus rolls.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: What do flashing yellow lights on a school bus tell drivers, and how should you respond?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Amber bus flashers work just like a yellow traffic signal—never gun the gas to beat the red stop arm.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: What criminal offense grade and fine range hit a driver who illegally passes a stopped school bus?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Blowing past a school bus stop arm is no minor civil ticket—it is a Class A misdemeanor costing two-fifty to one thousand.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.question_text: When may oncoming traffic keep moving cautiously past a stopped school bus, and how does a shared center turn lane count?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.teaching_text: Huge exam trap—painted five-lane center turn lanes are NOT physical barriers, so oncoming lanes must stop completely.

sec08-card-sec08-R32.question_text: Why is passing a stopped school bus on the right especially deadly, and what three cues allow proceeding?
sec08-card-sec08-R32.teaching_text: Bus doors open onto the right side, so hold until the bus moves, its signals shut off, or the driver waves.

sec08-card-sec08-R33.question_text: Who must stop when a school bus halts right at an intersection to load or unload students?
sec08-card-sec08-R33.teaching_text: Students step off and cross diagonally or sideways into cross streets, freezing traffic from all four directions.

sec08-card-sec08-R45.question_text: How do stopping and passing rules for a public transit bus differ from a school bus?
sec08-card-sec08-R45.teaching_text: City transit coaches have no stop-arm mandate, though riders often step out from the front bumper to jaywalk across.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.question_text: Where do more crashes happen than anywhere else, and what share of total and fatal crashes involve them?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.teaching_text: Crossing paths pack one-third of every wreck and over one-fifth of traffic deaths into intersections.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.question_text: What scanning sequence should you use before entering an intersection, and whom should you check twice for?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.teaching_text: Cross-traffic from your left reaches your door first, and slim bikes, motorcycles, and walkers vanish easily on a single glance.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.question_text: Where should your speed be lowest at an intersection, and what lane and passing rules apply?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.teaching_text: Pick your proper lane early, reach lowest speed right before the threshold, and never overtake another car inside an intersection.

sec08-card-sec08-F39.question_text: Is getting trapped inside an intersection after the light changes ever legal if no 'Do Not Block' sign is posted?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.teaching_text: Gridlocking cross-traffic after your green ends breaks state law everywhere, with or without a warning sign.

sec08-card-sec08-F40.question_text: Does Tennessee law ever grant a driver the right-of-way?
sec08-card-sec08-F40.teaching_text: Statutes state who must give way, never handing anyone a license to plow ahead when yielding prevents a wreck.

sec08-card-sec08-F41.question_text: In a marked school zone with warning flashers blinking, what is your duty when a pedestrian enters any crosswalk?
