sec08-card-sec08-F41.teaching_text: Rolling behind a child halfway across violates Tennessee's flashing school-zone rule—wait until they clear the crosswalk.

sec08-card-sec08-F42.question_text: What cues identify blind or deaf pedestrians with service animals, and how far back must you stop without honking?
sec08-card-sec08-F42.teaching_text: Spot a white or red-tipped cane, guide dog, or blaze-orange hearing-dog leash and halt ten-plus feet back in silence.

sec08-card-sec08-R37.question_text: When must you yield to walkers on corners or sidewalks, and when is driving on a sidewalk legal?
sec08-card-sec08-R37.teaching_text: Walkers crossing on green or along sidewalks across driveways have priority, and sidewalks may never be driven along—only crossed.

sec08-card-sec08-R38.question_text: In which three everyday areas must you slow down and watch with extreme caution for playing children?
sec08-card-sec08-R38.teaching_text: Chasing a ball or riding a scooter makes young kids bolt from driveways without ever glancing toward traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F43.question_text: To whom must you yield when turning left at an intersection versus pulling out of an alley or driveway?
sec08-card-sec08-F43.teaching_text: Left turns wait for oncoming straight and right-turning cars, while driveway exits wait for everything moving on the street.

sec08-card-sec08-R39.question_text: Alongside roundabouts, curb pull-outs, and highway merges, what unusual emergency-station move requires yielding?
sec08-card-sec08-R39.teaching_text: Huge ladder trucks and ambulances backing blind into firehouse bays rely on street traffic stopping well clear.

sec08-card-sec08-F44.question_text: Who goes first at an all-way stop, and what tie-breaker applies both there and at uncontrolled intersections?
sec08-card-sec08-F44.teaching_text: Arrival order governs multi-way stops, and simultaneous arrivals—or unsigned crossroads—always yield to the driver on the right.

sec08-card-sec08-R40.question_text: Whom must you let clear even after your light turns green, and who yields at a T-intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-R40.teaching_text: A green bulb never lets you hit cars still clearing the box, and terminating T-street traffic yields both ways.

sec08-card-sec08-F45.question_text: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with a siren, air horn, or flashing red or blue lights?
sec08-card-sec08-F45.teaching_text: Clear a center path immediately by pulling against the right curb and staying halted until it passes or police wave.

sec08-card-sec08-R41.question_text: May a private civilian vehicle carry or flash blue—or blue and red—emergency lights?
sec08-card-sec08-R41.teaching_text: Tennessee reserves blue and blue-red emergency strobes strictly for authorized law-enforcement and emergency responders.

sec08-card-sec08-R42.question_text: Which three actions are illegal around a fire truck answering an alarm or working at a fire scene?
sec08-card-sec08-R42.teaching_text: Trailing fire engines blocks backup rigs, entering the fire block traps crews, and driving over pressurized hoses bursts water lines.

sec08-card-sec08-R43.question_text: What should you do for an approaching emergency vehicle if you are already inside an intersection versus stopped at a red light?
sec08-card-sec08-R43.teaching_text: Finish crossing before pulling right without blocking side streets, and if stopped on red, stay put even when green appears.

sec08-card-sec08-R34.question_text: Where should you position and stop your car when a police officer signals you with blue lights or a siren?
sec08-card-sec08-R34.teaching_text: Pulling snug to the right shoulder away from cross-streets protects both your car and the officer walking up.

sec08-card-sec08-R35.question_text: Which five safety steps should you and your passengers follow during a Tennessee traffic stop?
sec08-card-sec08-R35.teaching_text: Keep hands on the wheel, passenger hands in sight, stay seated, turn on cabin lights at night, and disclose armed carry.

sec08-card-sec08-R36.question_text: Why should you skip roadside arguments with officers, and what may you do if an unmarked car flashes lights at you?
sec08-card-sec08-R36.teaching_text: Judges—not roadsides—settle tickets, and driving slowly to a well-lit populated lot verifies an unmarked stop safely.

sec08-card-sec08-R44.question_text: What must you do when a metro transit bus signals to pull back into traffic from a curbside stop?
sec08-card-sec08-R44.teaching_text: Letting a signaling public transit coach merge back smoothly keeps schedules moving and prevents wide-bus sideswipes.

sec08-card-sec08-F46.question_text: On multi-lane roads, what does Tennessee's Move Over Law require near stopped flashing emergency, utility, maintenance, or tow rigs?
sec08-card-sec08-F46.teaching_text: Shifting one lane away—or slowing safely when boxed in—protects roadside crews working inches from highway traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R46.question_text: What road layout and vehicle location trigger the lane-change duty under this chapter's Move Over rule?
sec08-card-sec08-R46.teaching_text: You need at least two same-direction lanes to vacate the near lane for a flashing rig stopped on your side.

sec08-card-sec08-R47.question_text: Which five bad habits does the manual call out as the most common turning faults?
sec08-card-sec08-R47.teaching_text: Skipping blinkers, blinking too late, failing to scan hazards, starting in the wrong lane, or swinging wide cause intersection crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-R48.question_text: Which lane should you start and finish a turn in, and does turning on your blinker give you right-of-way?
sec08-card-sec08-R48.teaching_text: Start in the lane nearest your turn, finish in the nearest legal lane, and remember blinkers announce intent—never priority.

sec08-card-sec08-R49.question_text: When do hand signals help most, when do they fall short, and where should your hand be mid-turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R49.teaching_text: Arm signals cut through blinding glare or dense traffic yet vanish after dark, and pulling inside restores two-hand steering.

sec08-card-sec08-R50.question_text: How can you alert trailing drivers before braking to a stop, and what must you verify after gentle turns?
sec08-card-sec08-R50.teaching_text: A few light brake-pedal taps catch distracted eyes behind you, and canceling a stuck blinker stops false turn cues.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: Which two lettered sections of the Tennessee manual supply questions for both the learner permit test and the driver license test?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Focusing your study sessions on those two core sections covers every written permit and license question.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: Why can't reading the manual alone teach you to drive — and what two things actually build skill?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Book knowledge teaches the rules, while coached behind-the-wheel hours build muscle memory and judgment.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: How are Tennessee's online practice tests organized, and which manual chapters feed the Guidelines for Driving test?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Pairing each topic quiz with its matching handbook chapters lets you drill weak spots right after reading.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: Which four chapters feed Rules of the Road — and which single chapters match Signs and Alcohol?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Four separate handbook chapters feed Rules of the Road, making it much wider than single-chapter topic quizzes.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: Before opening the driver's door, what should you walk around the vehicle looking for?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Toddlers, family pets, and bikes sit hidden below window height where mirrors never show them.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: Which five vehicle condition items — from glass to pavement drips — belong in your outside walk-around?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Spotting a low tire or fresh fluid puddle before starting prevents roadside breakdowns miles later.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: Right after sitting down inside, what should you do with the key, the doors, and unfamiliar controls?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Locking up for security and mapping every switch, gauge, and pedal keeps eyes forward once rolling.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: Which eight everyday and emergency controls must you locate before you ever need them in traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Fumbling for defrosters, four-way flashers, or dimmer stalks during a sudden downpour pulls eyes off lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: Why must you never drive with your seat reclined or even partly reclined?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Leaning back drops your sightline below the hood and slows emergency steering and braking reach.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: How should you set seat distance so your right foot moves smoothly between gas and brake?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Pivoting on your planted heel shifts from accelerator to brake faster than lifting your whole leg.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: What seating or steering-column mistake makes turning the wheel awkward?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Jamming your chest right up against the rim blocks smooth arm motion during sharp turns.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: Through which glass panels and mirrors must a properly adjusted driver's seat give a clear view?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Sitting high and upright opens sightlines across front glass, both side windows, and all three mirrors.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: Roughly how many inches should separate your body from the steering wheel — and why does airbag aim matter?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Giving the hub ten to twelve inches aims an inflating airbag squarely at your chest instead of your chin.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: Relative to your shoulders, how high may the top of the steering wheel sit?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Tilting the rim above shoulder height blocks forward sight and aims airbags upward toward your face.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: How high should you raise your head restraint, and what rear-impact injury does it prevent?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Catching the back of your skull evenly stops violent neck snap when struck from behind.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: At what exact point in cabin setup should you adjust all three rearview mirrors, and with what goal?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Setting mirrors before adjusting your seat throws every angle off the moment you slide the chair.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: How should you aim the inside rearview mirror, and what tiny rear landmark shows at its edge?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Angling slightly toward the right rear post widens your view of the right-side blind zone.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: Where do you lean your head — and what shows at the inner mirror edge — when setting the left outside mirror?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Swinging the left glass wide until your own door disappears while seated upright shrinks side blind spots.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: Where do you hold your head — and what shows at the inner edge — when aiming the right outside mirror?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Leaning above the console aims the passenger mirror outward into the adjacent lane instead of your own fender.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: As an overtaking car exits your inside mirror on the left, what should appear simultaneously in your left outside mirror?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Seamless handoff from center mirror to side mirror proves cars cannot vanish between views.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: If leaning slightly back still shows lots of your car's rear corners in the outside mirrors, how should you adjust them?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Watching your own paint wastes half the glass that should cover neighboring lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: When your car lacks power or remote mirror switches, how can you aim the right-side mirror accurately?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Having a partner nudge the passenger glass while you hold position over the console nails the angle.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: Where should you get comfortable with wide-angle mirror settings before merging into live traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Watching passing cars from a parked curb spot trains your eyes on the new handoff safely.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: Even with wide-set mirrors, why must you still turn your head before turning or changing lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Small motorcycles, cyclists, or angled cars can still hide outside mirror coverage until you look.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: How should your lap and shoulder belts fit, and who must be secured before you shift out of park?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Confirming every passenger and child seat is clicked before rolling prevents cabin ejections.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: What legal consequence can follow failing to buckle yourself or secure passengers in required child seats?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Tennessee officers write primary citations when drivers or young passengers ride unrestrained.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: Compare pedal and gear positions for starting an automatic car versus starting a manual-transmission car?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Depressing the clutch with the parking brake set keeps a stick-shift car from lurching on crank.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: When you turn the ignition to ON, which dashboard indicators should you scan for warnings?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Glowing warning icons at startup flag brake, airbag, or low-fuel trouble while you are still parked.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Besides night and storms, how much farther away do low-beam headlights make your vehicle visible in normal daylight?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Doubling your daytime visibility range gives oncoming two-lane drivers crucial extra seconds to spot you.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: What do R, D, and O stand for on an automatic shifter — and where does overdrive belong?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Overdrive saves fuel on open interstates with steady cruising and minimal stop-and-go braking.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: In which three tough driving situations should you select automatic lower gears marked L, two, or one?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Engine compression holds speed steady down Smoky Mountain grades without cooking brake pads.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: How can a manual transmission spare your brakes when descending a steep hill?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Dropping into a lower gear uses engine drag to check downhill speed without overheating brakes.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: During which three driving moments — including what stopping speed — must you press a manual clutch all the way down?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Pushing the clutch in below ten miles per hour keeps the engine from stalling as wheels halt.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: What is Tennessee's law on coasting in neutral — and where shouldn't your left foot rest between shifts?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Neutral disconnects engine control on hills, while resting on the clutch pedal burns out the disc.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: Why must you NEVER turn the ignition key to LOCK while a vehicle is still moving?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Clicking the steering-column pin shut mid-roll freezes your front wheels along their path.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: How firmly should both hands hold the wheel, and which two casual arm habits should you avoid?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: White-knuckle tension tires muscles, while hanging an elbow out the window sacrifices instant steering.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: How should your elbows look when your palm reaches the top of the steering wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Stiff locked arms transmit crash impact into shoulder joints and slow quick steering arcs.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: For which three column or dash controls will one hand briefly leave its normal steering spot?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Flicking a stalk with fingertips lets your hand return right back to the wheel rim.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: Beyond losing steering leverage, what catastrophic injury risks hitting an arm hung out the window?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Close mirror-to-mirror brushes or rollovers crush or sever limbs resting outside the door frame.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: Where should your central gaze aim while steering, and what job does your peripheral side vision perform?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Hands follow eyes naturally down your intended path while peripheral sight tracks lane stripes.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: At which clock numbers do your left and right hands belong on the wheel — and why?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: Lower nine-and-three placement keeps forearms clear of an inflating airbag's blast zone.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: Instead of letting the rim spin loose through your fingers after a turn, how should you straighten out?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Controlled counter-steering builds the exact muscle habit needed to catch snow and ice skids.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: Why does the manual allow crossing your wrists slightly in a turn while banning crossing your arms?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Crossed forearms tangle sleeves or bracelets and slam directly into your face if airbags fire.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: Which steering technique does Tennessee recommend, and what two advantages set it apart?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Feeding the rim smoothly from hand to hand prevents oversteering and airbag arm strikes.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: To which clock numbers do your hands travel during a push-pull left turn versus a right turn?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: Pulling down one side while pushing up the opposite side feeds the wheel without crossing arms.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: What happens to your hands during hand-over-hand steering, and how must you manage speed when using it?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Crossing hands at twelve o'clock briefly leaves one hand holding the rim, suited only to slow turns.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.question_text: Where do you grip and pull the rim during a hand-over-hand right turn before returning to nine and three?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.teaching_text: Repeating controlled one-to-five pulls then settling back at nine and three keeps sharp turns tidy.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.question_text: Which three mistakes trip up new drivers most often when reversing?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.teaching_text: Rear-end swing amplifies tiny wheel inputs, turning hurried reverse speed into scraped fenders.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.question_text: Where do your left hand, right arm, and eyes go to reverse — and which way turns the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.teaching_text: Turning the top of the wheel toward the side you want the tail to go keeps reverse intuitive.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.question_text: What speed and eye discipline belong throughout every backing maneuver?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.teaching_text: Snapping your head forward before the car halts misses pedestrians stepping behind your bumper.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.question_text: How far ahead should you aim your eyes when pulling away from a stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.teaching_text: Aiming a full block ahead toward a reference point keeps new drivers tracking straight.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.question_text: Walk through your checks, signal, and pedal touch right before pulling forward from a curb?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.teaching_text: Checking all sides and signaling before leaving the curb alerts approaching cyclists and cars.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.question_text: Which collision type tops Tennessee crash statistics every single year?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.teaching_text: Smooth, planned braking warns drivers behind early enough to cut Tennessee's number-one wreck.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.question_text: Put the mirror check and three foot movements of a smooth stop in order?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.teaching_text: Glancing at mirrors before squeezing steady brake pressure spares trailing cars panic stops.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.question_text: Where must your bumper stop at a stop sign or red signal — with markings versus without?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.teaching_text: Stopping short of painted lines keeps crosswalks open; without paint, stop where cross-road sight opens.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.question_text: Within how many inches of the curb must you park in Tennessee?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.teaching_text: Leaving your tail sticking farther than eighteen inches into the street clips passing mirrors.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.question_text: Once basic vehicle handling feels automatic, what single habit matters most for safety?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.teaching_text: Experienced drivers rarely crash from clumsy hands — wandering attention causes their wrecks.

sec05-card-sec05-F42.question_text: Why can't your senses detect deadly carbon monoxide — and which three situations commonly leak it into cabins?
sec05-card-sec05-F42.teaching_text: Colorless, odorless, tasteless exhaust sneaks in through leaky pipes, running heaters, or bumper-to-bumper fumes.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.question_text: Which two enclosed engine-running situations risk fatal carbon monoxide buildup?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.teaching_text: Warming up inside a shut garage or running climate control parked with closed glass traps lethal gas.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.question_text: Which three maintenance, listening, and vent habits guard against carbon monoxide poisoning?
sec05-card-sec05-R18.teaching_text: Loud underbody roaring flags a cracked pipe, and shutting fresh-air vents blocks tailpipe fumes in jams.

sec05-card-sec05-F44.question_text: Which two physical holding and messaging actions does the Hands Free Tennessee law forbid?
sec05-card-sec05-F44.teaching_text: Cradling a phone on your knee or shoulder counts as holding with a body part.

sec05-card-sec05-R20.question_text: What seat-position reach and three video actions also violate Tennessee's hands-free law?
sec05-card-sec05-R20.teaching_text: Lunging out of your belted posture for a dropped phone or watching clips draws a citation.

sec05-card-sec05-R19.question_text: What fine and court-cost caps — plus which responder exemptions — came with Tennessee's two thousand nine texting statute?
sec05-card-sec05-R19.teaching_text: Know those statutory caps — up to fifty dollars plus ten dollars court costs, with on-duty responders exempt.

sec05-card-sec05-F45.question_text: When school-zone warning flashers are active, what phone rule applies to moving drivers aged eighteen and older?
sec05-card-sec05-F45.teaching_text: Active yellow school flashers ban adult handheld calls right where children cross.

sec05-card-sec05-R21.question_text: Does the school-zone hands-free allowance cover drivers under eighteen — and how is teen handheld use classified?
sec05-card-sec05-R21.teaching_text: Drivers under eighteen get zero school-zone phone exception and face a delinquent-act violation.

sec05-card-sec05-F46.question_text: Which screens are banned inside the driver's view while moving — and which three functional displays stay legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F46.teaching_text: Entertainment video blinds attention, whereas GPS maps, backup cameras, and car-info displays aid driving.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: At least how many feet ahead of a turn or lane change must you switch on your turn signal in Tennessee?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Flipping your blinker right as you yank the wheel gives surrounding drivers zero time to adjust speed or space.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: When your driveway or turn sits right past an intersection, when should you click on your turn signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Signaling too early tricks cross-street drivers into pulling out right in front of you because they think you are turning early.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Which two well-meaning blinker habits does the Tennessee manual tell you never to use?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Blinkers exist solely to announce your own move—waving cars around or echoing traffic ahead misleads oncoming drivers.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: Why must you signal every direction change even when the street looks completely deserted?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: The cyclist, motorcycle, or car tucked silently inside your blind spot is the exact hazard a habit blinker warns.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How long should you run your turn signal before pulling away from a parked spot at the curb?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Approaching drivers assume curbside cars are empty unless a steady blinker gives clear advance notice before your nose moves.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: When should you get into your turn lane and pick your gear, and how should throttle feel through the corner?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Settling lane position and downshifting beforehand—even earlier on fast roads—lets light steady throttle stabilize your tires mid-turn.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: Where must you wait if backed-up traffic ahead could trap you mid-turn when the signal changes?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Pulling halfway into the box behind a clogged side street leaves your car blocking cross-traffic when red hits.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: What is the right play if you realize at the last moment that you are in the wrong lane for your turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Cutting suddenly across lanes at an intersection causes sideswipes, whereas driving one extra block fixes the mistake safely.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: Why must your front wheels stay pointed straight ahead while waiting for an opening to turn left?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: If a distracted driver taps your rear bumper while your tires point left, you roll straight into head-on traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: Which braking, clutch, and gearshift actions should you avoid once you are actually turning inside an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Braking mid-corner upsets tire grip, and pressing the clutch or hunting gears mid-intersection risks stalling across live lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: When you and an oncoming driver both turn left at the same intersection, how should your paths pass each other?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Turning in front—to the left—of each other keeps sightlines open instead of looping blindly behind the other car.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: How far forward into an intersection should you roll with straight wheels before starting to steer left?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Turning the wheel too soon clips the cross-street's oncoming left-turn lane instead of squaring neatly into yours.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: From which lane do you start a left turn on a two-way street, and which lane must you enter?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Start right beside your center line and finish immediately right of the new center line—never drifting wide outside.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: If you are waiting behind the line to turn left and the signal turns yellow, what must you do?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Pulling out as yellow appears pits you against oncoming drivers trying to beat the light right as red hits.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: How can you tell instantly from center lane-line colors whether a street carries two-way or one-way traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Yellow stripes always divide opposing directions, whereas white dashed lines mean every lane beside you flows one direction.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: Which lane must you turn into when making a left turn onto a one-way street?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: With zero oncoming traffic on the cross street, your closest legal target lane hugs the far-left curb.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: When driving on a one-way street, which lane must you use to set up a left turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Starting a left turn from a middle one-way lane cuts straight across vehicles continuing forward along the left curb.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: What lane rule governs dedicated left-turn lanes and side-by-side multiple turn lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Drifting sideways mid-intersection inside dual turn lanes sideswipes the car turning inches off your fender.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: How do you execute a left turn from a one-way street onto a two-way street, and when may you move right?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Square into the lane immediately right of the yellow center stripe first, then signal and check before shifting right.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: When is turning left on a red light from a one-way street onto a two-way street legal?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Turning left onto a two-way street on red forces you across live cross-traffic flowing from your left.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: Under what exact street combination and conditions is turning left on a red light legal in Tennessee?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: When one one-way feeds left onto another one-way, no opposing lane is crossed—so stop, yield, and check signs.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: Which two red-light turns does Tennessee allow unless prohibited by a sign, and what must you do first?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Both standard right turns on red and one-way-to-one-way left turns require a zero-motion stop and full yielding first.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: When may drivers in a second adjacent lane make the same turn as the curb or inside lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Never invent a second turn lane on your own unless overhead signs or painted turn arrows authorize it.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: What purpose do curved white channel lines and pavement arrows serve inside wide intersections?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Following dotted white guide arcs keeps side-by-side turning traffic aligned cleanly into each driver's matching exit lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: How should you position your car before and after making a standard right turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Approach snug near the right edge without swinging left and land squarely inside the nearest right-hand lane.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: Why is swinging wide to the left right before making a right turn dangerous?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Pulling left tricks the driver behind into thinking you are turning left, tempting them to shoot up your right side.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: Which four traffic and vulnerable-user conflicts must you scan for before turning right?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Watch cross-street cars, oncoming left-turners aiming at the same lane, crosswalk walkers, and cyclists along your right fender.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: Why must you never squeeze past a large truck or bus on the right near an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Tractor-trailers must swing left first to clear corners, then their trailer wheels cut right across that open curb gap.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: Which direction does traffic move inside a roundabout, and who yields at the entrance?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Entering drivers always wait for cars already circling counterclockwise from their left before slipping into a safe gap.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: What posted speed range, passing rule, and exit-blinker rule govern driving inside a roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Cruise calmly around fifteen to twenty-five, never overtake inside multi-lane rings, and blink right so waiting drivers read your exit.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: Which three safety and neighborhood goals prompt cities to install roundabouts?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Curved geometry lowers speeds naturally, eliminates high-energy T-bone angles, and discourages fast shortcutting through quiet streets.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.question_text: Which side of the raised splitter island do you pass when entering a roundabout, and when may you stop inside?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.teaching_text: Raised islands channel cars right, and stopping unprompted inside the circle triggers instant rear-end chain reactions.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.question_text: What conflict must you watch for in a multi-lane roundabout, and what should you do if you miss your exit?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.teaching_text: Never cut sharply across an inside car's bow—give exiting inner-lane traffic room, or simply loop around one extra lap.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: At what controlled intersections and below what clear sight distance are U-turns illegal in Tennessee?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Flipping around at a traffic light, near an officer, or with less than five hundred feet of view invites T-bones.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: Where else are U-turns banned on city streets, and what safer alternative does the manual recommend?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Spinning around mid-block between city intersections surprises traffic from driveways and lanes—looping around the block is safer.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.question_text: Can Tennessee cities or towns outlaw U-turns across all of their municipal streets?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.teaching_text: Local ordinances can forbid U-turns across an entire municipality even where individual intersection signs are absent.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: Are U-turns allowed on interstates, and who is permitted to use paved median crossovers there?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Slowing to turn into a seventy-mile-per-hour fast lane is deadly, restricting gravel or paved turnarounds strictly to official rigs.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.question_text: What must you do if you blow past your interstate exit or get caught in a freeway backup?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.teaching_text: Cutting across grassy medians or reversing up a shoulder is illegal and causes catastrophic wrong-way or high-speed wrecks.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: How much roadway space must you leave oncoming vehicles on a narrow road with no painted center line?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Without yellow paint to split lanes, hugging your right edge gives approaching vehicles a full safe half.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: Which paint color belongs on your left versus your right, and what does seeing yellow on your right mean?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Spotting yellow along your right door means you are facing head-on oncoming traffic and must pull off immediately.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.question_text: Which four situations allow driving left of the center line, and which side should pass a road crash?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.teaching_text: Stay right of center outside those four exceptions, and steer right around crash scenes whenever room allows.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: What is the sole legal purpose of the middle lane on a two-way street with three or five lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Using a center turn lane as a through-travel or passing lane sets up a head-on collision with opposing turners.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: Which roadway of a divided highway must you drive on, and where is crossing the median legal?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Keep the median strip to your left and cross only at paved intersections, authorized openings, or under officer direction.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: What urgent warning are raised lane reflectors sending if they glow red in your headlights?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Highway markers shine white or yellow with traffic and flash bright red only to drivers heading into oncoming lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.question_text: How do center and lane markings differ between a two-lane highway and an undivided four-lane highway?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.teaching_text: Two-lane roads use a broken yellow where passing is open, while four-lane highways split directions with double solid yellow.

sec09-card-sec09-R20.question_text: How do public median crossovers on four-lane divided highways differ from interstates?
sec09-card-sec09-R20.teaching_text: Divided four-lane routes provide paved public turnouts, whereas controlled-access interstates ban civilian median crossings completely.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.question_text: Where must you wait if another car is already stopped inside a divided-highway median crossover?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.teaching_text: Pulling into a tight median gap behind another car leaves your tail jutting into fast lanes or blocks sightlines.

sec09-card-sec09-R21.question_text: What does a pavement marking combining a straight arrow and a turn arrow allow, and what yield rules apply?
sec09-card-sec09-R21.teaching_text: Shared-option lanes let you proceed straight or turn, following standard right-of-way rules unless a green arrow protects you.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: What is prohibited in a shared center turn lane, and what is the maximum distance you may travel inside it?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Cruising past three hundred feet or overtaking traffic inside a two-way left-turn lane risks a head-on wreck.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: When two opposing drivers want the same stretch of a shared center turn lane, who has priority?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Whoever enters the painted center turn box first holds position—never nose head-on into an occupied pocket.

sec09-card-sec09-R22.question_text: When should you pull into a shared center turn lane, what shortcut is banned, and how can side-street turners use it?
sec09-card-sec09-R22.teaching_text: Pull in right before your driveway—never riding early toward a distant light—though side-street lefts may shelter there before merging.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: What does each overhead symbol—green arrow, red X, flashing yellow X, and steady yellow X—mean over a reversible lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Green opens travel, red X bans entry, flashing yellow X restricts to turns, and steady yellow X warns to vacate.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: Which three groups may travel in a white-diamond reserved lane, and when may an ordinary solo car enter one?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Solo drivers stay out of diamond lanes except during the final half-block needed to execute a legal turn.

sec09-card-sec09-R23.question_text: What occupancy minimum and schedule info do HOV-two signs communicate?
sec09-card-sec09-R23.teaching_text: Check the sign's days and clock window—during active enforcement, at least two occupants must sit inside the vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: What exact sequence of checks and signals should you follow every time you change lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: Mirrors alone leave dangerous side blind zones—adding your blinker and a real over-the-shoulder check prevents sideswipes.

sec09-card-sec09-R24.question_text: How should you respond when a driver slightly ahead in the next lane clicks on a blinker to merge over?
sec09-card-sec09-R24.teaching_text: Gassing up to close the gap or changing lanes simultaneously turns a routine merge into a high-speed bump.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: Before pulling out to pass on a two-lane road, how should you treat any oncoming car visible in the distance?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: Two cars closing at fifty-five eat over one hundred sixty feet every second, making visible headlights closer than they look.

sec09-card-sec09-R25.question_text: What crash happens if you cut back in too early after passing versus waiting too long?
sec09-card-sec09-R25.teaching_text: Slicing right too early clips the passed bumper, while staying left too long meets opposing traffic bumper-to-bumper.

sec09-card-sec09-R26.question_text: Why must you never nose across the center line just to peek past the vehicle ahead before passing?
sec09-card-sec09-R26.teaching_text: Drop back for a clean angle instead—poking half your hood across yellow puts you blind into oncoming headlights.

sec09-card-sec09-R27.question_text: Why does the manual warn against passing at night on unfamiliar two-lane roads?
sec09-card-sec09-R27.teaching_text: Darkness hides dips, curves, and solid yellow line starts until you are already committed beside the other car.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: When is it safe to pull back into the right lane after passing a car, and what final step finishes the pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Wait until both headlights—the entire front of the passed car—appear inside your center rearview mirror, then cancel your blinker.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: Is passing several cars in one move legal in Tennessee, and what hundred-foot clearance rule applies?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: Multi-car passes are discouraged and safe only when you tuck back right at least one hundred feet before solid yellow or oncoming cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.question_text: Under which two roadway conditions may you legally pass on the right, and what surface rule never bends?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.teaching_text: Overtake on the right only past a left-turning car or on multi-lane roads—dropping tires onto gravel or shoulder is illegal.

sec09-card-sec09-R28.question_text: Which three special lanes are illegal for right-side passing, and who gets blamed if the car ahead turns right?
sec09-card-sec09-R28.teaching_text: Shooting up a bike, parking, or signal-approach emergency lane puts crash blame squarely on the right-side passer.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.question_text: Around which six roadway features is passing prohibited because sightlines or escape room vanish?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.teaching_text: Curves, hill crests, intersections, train tracks, tunnels, viaducts, and narrow bridges all hide oncoming traffic or trap you left.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.question_text: Why must you never overtake a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.teaching_text: That halted SUV is blocking your view of a pedestrian stepping right into your lane—a classic fatal mistake.

sec09-card-sec09-R29.question_text: What center-line marking and bus signal strictly forbid passing?
sec09-card-sec09-R29.teaching_text: Either a solid yellow stripe bordering your lane or a school or church bus flashing red with its arm out locks passing.

sec09-card-sec09-R30.question_text: About how far back should you stop for a crosswalk on a multi-lane street, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-R30.teaching_text: Halting roughly thirty feet back lets drivers in adjacent lanes see pedestrians early instead of screening them behind your hood.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.question_text: Does passing a 'Do Not Pass' zone's end sign mean it is automatically safe to pull out and pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.teaching_text: Broken paint returning only means road geometry opened up—you still have to verify zero oncoming cars.

sec09-card-sec09-R31.question_text: Even inside a marked no-passing zone, when may you legally cross a solid yellow line?
sec09-card-sec09-R31.teaching_text: No-passing stripes ban overtaking moving traffic, not turning left across the road into or out of driveways, alleys, or streets.

sec09-card-sec09-R32.question_text: What does Tennessee law say about using the right shoulder to pass or weaving back and forth through lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-R32.teaching_text: Paved shoulders hold stalled cars and debris, and aggressive lane-weaving surprises surrounding traffic from unpredictable angles.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.question_text: What three duties apply to you while another driver is passing your vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.teaching_text: Speeding up out of pride traps the passer inside oncoming lanes and turns a legal overtake into a deadly emergency.

sec09-card-sec09-R33.question_text: If an oncoming car pops over a hill while someone is halfway past you, what should you do?
sec09-card-sec09-R33.teaching_text: Braking gently lets the passing car tuck quickly in front of you instead of meeting oncoming headlights head-on.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.question_text: At least how many feet of side clearance does Tennessee law require when passing a bicyclist riding your direction?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.teaching_text: Hold at least three full feet of side air all the way past so mirror gusts or wobbles never clip handlebars.

sec09-card-sec09-R34.question_text: In which two tight situations must you wait behind a bicyclist instead of trying to squeeze past?
sec09-card-sec09-R34.teaching_text: Threading between a rider and oncoming headlights—or pinching them against parked car doors—leaves zero survival margin.

sec09-card-sec09-F42.question_text: How can you tell instantly whether a tractor-trailer driver can see your car, and why avoid cruising beside one?
sec09-card-sec09-F42.teaching_text: If you cannot spot the rig's side mirrors, you are invisible inside a huge No-Zone along the trailer.

sec09-card-sec09-R35.question_text: Why is pulling right in front of a heavy truck or bus and braking so dangerous?
sec09-card-sec09-R35.teaching_text: Eighty-thousand-pound rigs need far longer to shed speed than cars and cannot stop inside a stolen front gap.

sec09-card-sec09-R36.question_text: How do flat roads, uphill climbs, and downhill grades change passing a heavy truck, and what speed cap stays firm?
sec09-card-sec09-R36.teaching_text: Heavy rigs lose speed climbing hills and gain momentum coasting down, yet passing never excuses breaking the posted speed limit.

sec09-card-sec09-F43.question_text: What is the only reason to back into a live travel lane, and why should road-test applicants drill backing?
sec09-card-sec09-F43.teaching_text: Backing into traffic is banned outside parallel parking, and sloppy reversing fails more new Tennessee applicants than any other skill.

sec09-card-sec09-R37.question_text: What check comes before entering your car to back up, and how should you look once reversing?
sec09-card-sec09-R37.teaching_text: Inspect behind the bumper first, then turn to look directly out the rear window—never leaning out an open door.

sec09-card-sec09-F44.question_text: Which two high-conflict places are explicitly illegal to back into or reverse along?
sec09-card-sec09-F44.teaching_text: Reversing out of a corner driveway into an intersection—or backing along an interstate—meets cross or freeway traffic blind.

sec09-card-sec09-R38.question_text: May you stop inside a moving travel lane if you get lost, drop off a friend, or feel car trouble starting?
sec09-card-sec09-R38.teaching_text: Halting mid-lane invites high-speed rear-end crashes—coast or drive clear onto a shoulder or lot before stopping.

sec09-card-sec09-R51.question_text: Which way does your front bumper swing as you steer while backing out of an angled parking space, and when do you recheck?
sec09-card-sec09-R51.teaching_text: Turning the wheel right swings your front left fender toward the neighboring car, and clearing adjacent bumpers unlocks cross-aisle sight.

sec09-card-sec09-F45.question_text: What wheel-placement, open-road width, and visibility distances apply when parking outside city limits?
sec09-card-sec09-F45.teaching_text: Get all four tires off the asphalt, leave eighteen feet of clear road, and stay visible two hundred feet each way.

sec09-card-sec09-R39.question_text: What brake and transmission habit should you use every single time you park?
sec09-card-sec09-R39.teaching_text: Engaging the parking brake alongside Park—or in-gear on manuals—prevents runaway rollaways on slopes or near playgrounds.

sec09-card-sec09-R40.question_text: What does Tennessee law say about leaving an unattended parked car running, and what two steps secure it?
sec09-card-sec09-R40.teaching_text: Walking into a store with the engine idling is illegal and invites instant theft or rollaway crashes.

sec09-card-sec09-R41.question_text: Which three actions are mandatory whenever you pull out of a parallel or lot parking space?
sec09-card-sec09-R41.teaching_text: Parked vehicles hold zero right-of-way—scan mirrors and blind spots, blink your intent, and wait for moving cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F46.question_text: Which way do you turn your front wheels when parking downhill, on any curbless hill, or uphill with a curb?
sec09-card-sec09-F46.teaching_text: Only uphill with a curb turns left so the tire catches concrete—downhill or curbless slopes turn right off-road.

sec09-card-sec09-F47.question_text: How many feet must you stay clear when parking near a fire hydrant, crosswalk, stop sign or signal, and railroad crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-F47.teaching_text: Lock in that clean staircase—fifteen from hydrants, twenty from crosswalks, thirty from signals or stops, fifty from tracks.

sec09-card-sec09-R42.question_text: Is stopping side-by-side next to a curbed car ever legal, and when should four-way flashers come on after dark?
sec09-card-sec09-R42.teaching_text: Hazard lights never legalize double-parking in a travel lane—save four-way flashers for breakdowns or true night hazards.

sec09-card-sec09-R43.question_text: Which everyday access points, structures, and freeway spots ban non-emergency parking?
sec09-card-sec09-R43.teaching_text: Blocking driveways, intersections, fire lanes, sidewalks, bridges, tunnels, or freeway ramps traps traffic or emergency crews.

sec09-card-sec09-R44.question_text: How far must you park from a fire-station driveway on the same side of the street versus across the street?
sec09-card-sec09-R44.teaching_text: Wide-turning ladder engines need twenty feet beside the bay doors and seventy-five feet across the street to swing out.

sec09-card-sec09-R45.question_text: Which three levels of stopping or loading restrictions can painted curbs establish?
sec09-card-sec09-R45.teaching_text: Curb colors separate quick passenger drop-offs, commercial loading with the driver present, and total no-stopping fire zones.

sec09-card-sec09-R46.question_text: How do you line up beside the forward car and angle back when starting a parallel park?
sec09-card-sec09-R46.teaching_text: Match bumpers at least two feet apart, then steer sharply right while reversing slowly to a forty-five-degree entry angle.

sec09-card-sec09-R47.question_text: Within how many inches of the curb must a completed parallel park sit, and what comes before opening your door?
sec09-card-sec09-R47.teaching_text: Parking farther out than eighteen inches crowds the travel lane, and checking behind saves your door and passing cyclists.

sec09-card-sec09-R48.question_text: If your car dies and cannot roll off the pavement, which four steps warn traffic and secure the vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-R48.teaching_text: Pop the hood or tie cloth on the left handle or antenna, run four-way flashers, and lock the cabin.

sec09-card-sec09-R49.question_text: Is walking along a Tennessee interstate legal if your car breaks down?
sec09-card-sec09-R49.teaching_text: Pedestrians on seventy-mile-per-hour shoulders face extreme danger, so stay buckled inside unless fire or immediate peril forces evacuation.

sec09-card-sec09-R50.question_text: Who may legally use an accessible parking space, and what penalties hit violators?
sec09-card-sec09-R50.teaching_text: Borrowing grandma's placard while she stays home is a misdemeanor bringing a hundred-dollar fine and a towed car.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: Why does driving after dark turn extra hazardous along poorly lit highways and rural roads?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Headlight beams reach only a fraction of daylight view, hiding animals, unlit cars, and dark-clothed walkers.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: How do your odds of a serious crash at night compare with daytime driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Fewer cars on the road never makes night safer because fatigue, glare, and limited sight multiply severe wrecks.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: Which three specific visual skills weaken once daylight fades?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Because reaction time starts with your eyes, weakened depth, color, and side vision delay every steering move.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: Which two nights of the week record more fatal traffic crashes than any other days?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Late weekend traffic mixes tired drivers, unfamiliar routes, and impaired motorists into the week's highest fatality spike.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: What is the foundational speed rule for driving safely after dark?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Going too fast to stop inside your lit path guarantees hitting any stalled car or deer before stopping.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: How must your stopping distance compare with sight distance at night, and what car factors matter?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Weak bulbs or spongy brakes lengthen stopping runs, demanding even slower night speeds to stay inside view.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: Where should your eyes scan beyond your main beams while driving after dark?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Sweeping past beam tips and glancing side to side catches dark silhouettes, road edges, and oncoming glow.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: Where should you look instead of staring straight into bright oncoming headlights?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Staring into high-intensity lamps temporarily blinds your retinas, whereas tracking the right stripe keeps lane control.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: Why should you avoid flashing your high beams to warn another motorist?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Blasting brights back at an oncoming driver leaves two blinded drivers closing on each other at highway speed.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: At least how far ahead must Tennessee headlights reveal a person on the highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Dirty lenses or droopy aim slash illumination short of Tennessee's mandatory two-hundred-foot standard.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: Why must headlights stay in peak working order to meet legal seeing distance?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Light intensity drops off steeply over distance, so aging bulbs lose far-field visibility long before burning out.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: Which two resources can help ensure your headlights are aimed accurately?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Proper vertical and horizontal alignment puts light onto your lane instead of into oncoming windshields.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: What happens to your eyes and road vision during glare recovery time after bright lights pass?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Contracted pupils take precious seconds to reopen to darkness, leaving you driving nearly blind past the glare.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: Does sharp daytime vision speed glare recovery, and which drivers usually recover slowest?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Twenty-twenty acuity offers zero immunity against slow pupil rebound as drivers age or feel run-down.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: What cleaning habits help cut down night glare on windshields, glasses, and lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Interior film and road grime scatter oncoming headlight beams into a hazy veil across the glass.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: What is the effect of headlights aimed too high or too far outward?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Wasted upward beams miss the asphalt ahead while dazzling drivers approaching or checking rearview mirrors.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: Within what distance must you dim high beams when meeting or following another vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: High beams reflect just as harshly off a lead car's mirrors as they hit an oncoming windshield.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: Which beam setting belongs in cities and towns, and what curve habit protects oncoming traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Swinging around a right-hand bend sweeps high-beam cones straight across the oncoming lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: Why must you never leave full headlights burning while parked at night, even briefly?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Approaching motorists steer toward or beside lit headlights assuming the lane continues moving there.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: When do lit headlights on a parked vehicle create the worst deception for approaching drivers?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: White beams sitting on the left shoulder trick oncoming drivers into steering off the road to pass right.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: Which two lighting systems should stay on if you must park beside a highway at night?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Amber hazards and low-glare marker lamps flag your stopped car without blinding passing traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: When is stopping allowed on an interstate shoulder versus on an entrance or exit ramp?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: High-speed traffic leaves shoulders strictly for emergencies and ramps strictly for mechanically disabled vehicles.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: Why must you drop speed at the very first sign of rain?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Water stretches braking distances immediately and turns brisk cornering into sudden four-wheel skids.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: Why are roads usually slickest during the first minutes after rain begins?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Light early moisture floats accumulated exhaust oil and road dust before heavier downpours rinse it away.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: Why should you wait a few seconds after raindrops start before switching on windshield wipers?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Sweeping dry blades over dusty glass smears a milky paste right across your line of sight.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: Which two climate controls keep windows and mirrors clear during damp or stormy weather?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Air conditioning dehumidifies cabin air rapidly so interior moisture stops fogging cold glass.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: How should you adjust turn signaling and braking timing during rainy weather?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Drivers behind you also face longer wet stopping distances and need extra seconds to react smoothly.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.question_text: Why does rain starting on a hot day make asphalt extraordinarily slick at first?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.teaching_text: Baked asphalt sweats oil to the surface, creating a skating rink until sustained rain washes it clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: Which headlight setting must you use in fog or mist, and why are high beams dangerous?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Suspended water droplets act like millions of tiny mirrors reflecting high-beam glare straight back at you.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: What is the safest overall decision regarding driving in thick fog or wildfire smoke?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Tennessee valleys see sudden temperature fog and brush-fire smoke year-round where zero visibility causes chain pileups.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: If you cannot avoid driving in fog or smoke, which light combinations are required or banned?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: Cruising on dim parking or fog lamps alone fails to light taillights and hides your car.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: Why should you silence or lower the radio and stay off your phone in fog or smoke?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: When eyes lose range in thick haze, your ears help detect tire noise, horns, and sirens.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: Which lane, passing, crossing, and stopping rules keep you safer inside fog?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Pulling out to pass or stopping mid-lane in whiteout haze triggers instant head-on or rear-end hits.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: What should you do if fog grows so thick that you lose sight of the road edge?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: Clearing the travel lane completely keeps blindly creeping traffic from plowing into your rear bumper.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: What personal safety step should you take if your car breaks down or stalls in fog or smoke?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Approaching drivers following taillights in zero visibility often steer straight into a stopped vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: Besides postponing travel until fog lifts, what roadside controls should you watch for in fog zones?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: Mountain passes and river bridges post automated fog beacons and speed drops when pileup risk spikes.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: During which three daytime weather conditions does Tennessee law require turning on low-beam headlights?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: Daytime running lamps leave dark rear ends unlit, whereas full low beams switch taillights on too.

sec11-card-sec11-R38.question_text: Why should you switch headlights on whenever bad weather cuts visibility?
sec11-card-sec11-R38.teaching_text: Headlights in gloom work as visibility beacons for oncoming motorists long before lighting your own path.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: What happens between your tires and the road during hydroplaning, and why is it unstable?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: Riding on a water wedge leaves zero friction, so a tiny steering nudge or wind gust spins you.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: How must you slow down if your tires start hydroplaning on standing water?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: Lifting smoothly off the accelerator lets tires sink back through water without locking into a spin.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.question_text: How severely can hydroplaning multiply stopping distance and affect steering?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.teaching_text: Needing three times normal braking room with dead steering leaves zero escape from tailgating.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: Does hydroplaning happen only at freeway speeds, or can it occur slower?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Deep puddles and worn tire treads can float wheels even at moderate town speeds.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: What tire condition defines a skid, and what driver mistake triggers it?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: Blaming slick pavement misses the controllable root cause of carrying too much speed for road grip.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: What should your feet and hands do if your car's rear end slides left in a skid?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: Pointing front wheels down your intended travel line realigns the sliding rear without locking tires.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.question_text: What steering adjustment is crucial the moment a skidding vehicle begins straightening out?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.teaching_text: Holding recovery lock too long whips the tail past center into a violent opposite-way spin.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.question_text: How should you steer right after catching the main slide of a skid?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.teaching_text: Gentle micro-adjustments settle lingering pendulum sway cleanly until all four tires track straight down the lane.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.question_text: What proactive habit is the single best defense against ever entering a skid?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.teaching_text: Shedding speed long before intersections and curves keeps traction demands inside tire grip limits.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: What must you do immediately if your right wheels drop off the paved roadway edge?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Yanking the wheel against a pavement lip slingshots the car sideways across oncoming lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: How should you brake and when should you steer back onto pavement after a wheel drop-off?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: Slowing gently with clear traffic lets tires climb the pavement edge without snapping sideways.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.question_text: What is the primary job of painted edge rumble stripes, and what is the buzz-and-shake?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.teaching_text: Angled grooves drain water so headlights reflect brightly off wet edge paint while vibration adds warning.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.question_text: Which thunderstorm hazard kills more people each year than lightning, wind, or hail?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.teaching_text: Underestimating water across low roadways traps motorists inside buoyant cars swept off the pavement.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.question_text: What depth of fast-moving floodwater knocks down an adult versus sweeps away most cars?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.teaching_text: Moving water packs immense lateral force well before reaching hubcap or door-sill height.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.question_text: Why do heavy pickups and SUVs still fail to protect drivers in flooded roadways?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.teaching_text: Sealed vehicle bodies act like boats once water rises just six to twelve extra inches.

sec11-card-sec11-R21.question_text: What often happens once floodwater sweeps a car downstream, leaving only seconds to escape?
sec11-card-sec11-R21.teaching_text: Currents flip floating vehicles quickly, trapping panicked occupants who stay buckled inside rising water.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.question_text: Why does Turn Around, Don't Drown warn against trusting shallow-looking floodwater?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.teaching_text: Muddy surface water hides collapsed culverts and deep craters where pavement used to sit.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.question_text: What two legal and financial penalties can hit a driver who knowingly bypasses flood barricades?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.teaching_text: Ignoring posted flood warnings risks first-responder lives, triggering criminal charges and full rescue reimbursement.

sec11-card-sec11-R22.question_text: How shallow can water be when you lose car control, and what depth floats most vehicles?
sec11-card-sec11-R22.teaching_text: Tires lose steering bite in half a foot of water, long before two feet floats the chassis.

sec11-card-sec11-R23.question_text: What must you do immediately if your vehicle stalls inside floodwater?
sec11-card-sec11-R23.teaching_text: No vehicle is worth drowning for when flash-flood levels can surge another foot in seconds.

sec11-card-sec11-R24.question_text: Which road features collect floodwater fastest, and when are hidden floods hardest to spot?
sec11-card-sec11-R24.teaching_text: Underpasses, creek bridges, and dark rural dips fill rapidly before drivers see water across asphalt.

sec11-card-sec11-R25.question_text: What simple in-car habit keeps you informed during severe thunderstorms?
sec11-card-sec11-R25.teaching_text: Local weather bulletins warn of flash floods, hail cores, and tornado tracks ahead of your route.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.question_text: What must you do instead of trying to outrun a visible tornado in your car?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.teaching_text: Tornado winds toss vehicles easily, so lying face-down in a low ditch shields against flying debris.

sec11-card-sec11-R45.question_text: According to the Tennessee manual, where should you seek shelter during a hailstorm or sleet?
sec11-card-sec11-R45.teaching_text: Tennessee's study guide specifically pairs hailstorms and sleet with pulling beneath an overpass or bridge.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.question_text: How should you position and adjust speed when a large truck or bus passes on your left?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.teaching_text: Bow-wave air gusts push light passenger cars sideways unless you add right-side cushion and drop speed.

sec11-card-sec11-R26.question_text: Which four vehicle profiles struggle most in strong crosswinds and need slower speeds?
sec11-card-sec11-R26.teaching_text: Tall slab sides catch wind like sails while light curb weights get shoved across lane stripes.

sec11-card-sec11-R27.question_text: Where along a highway do sudden crosswind gusts hit hardest?
sec11-card-sec11-R27.teaching_text: Emerging from rock cuts, tree lines, or overpasses exposes your side panels instantly to full gusts.

sec11-card-sec11-R28.question_text: How do you keep a towed trailer from jackknifing in the wind wake of a passing truck?
sec11-card-sec11-R28.teaching_text: Light forward pull restores tension on the hitch and straightens trailer oscillation safely.

sec11-card-sec11-R29.question_text: How do strong headwinds versus strong tailwinds change throttle, steering, and braking needs?
sec11-card-sec11-R29.teaching_text: Pushing air adds speed from behind, stretching stopping distances unless you ease off and brake earlier.

sec11-card-sec11-R30.question_text: When is sun glare worst ahead, and which three tools help cut it down?
sec11-card-sec11-R30.teaching_text: Low-horizon morning and late-afternoon rays turn dusty windshields opaque without clean glass and visors.

sec11-card-sec11-R31.question_text: Why must you stay extra defensive even when low sun shines comfortably from behind you?
sec11-card-sec11-R31.teaching_text: Drivers looking straight past your car into low sun can miss both your turn signals and silhouette.

sec11-card-sec11-R32.question_text: How should your gear, front wheels, and gas pedal be set when starting out of mud or snow?
sec11-card-sec11-R32.teaching_text: Angled or spinning tires dig deeper ruts and polish snow into slick ice beneath the tread.

sec11-card-sec11-R33.question_text: After creeping forward as far as possible in mud or snow, how do you rock the car free?
sec11-card-sec11-R33.teaching_text: Rhythmic forward-and-back rolling lengthens packed tracks inches at a time until momentum carries out.

sec11-card-sec11-R34.question_text: What safety rule applies before wedging boards or branches under tires stuck in deep mud or snow?
sec11-card-sec11-R34.teaching_text: Spinning treads can hurl wood planks backward like projectiles or pull hands toward moving tires.

sec11-card-sec11-R35.question_text: Where and when should you install tire chains to avoid getting stuck?
sec11-card-sec11-R35.teaching_text: Putting chains on dry shoulder space before hitting deep snow beats wrestling cold metal while stuck.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.question_text: Why do tree-shaded or building-shaded road sections hide surprise ice on cold wet days?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.teaching_text: Blocked winter sunlight leaves cold shadow strips glazed long after surrounding pavement looks bone-dry.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.question_text: Why do highway bridges and overpasses ice over earlier than solid-ground roads?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.teaching_text: Cold air circulates both above and beneath elevated bridge decks, chilling concrete long before insulated earth.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.question_text: How does traction on ice right near the freezing point compare with much colder sub-zero ice?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.teaching_text: A microscopic film of liquid meltwater on thirty-two-degree ice lubricates tires far worse than dry cold ice.

sec11-card-sec11-R36.question_text: What are the three classic driver overreactions on snow-covered or icy roads?
sec11-card-sec11-R36.teaching_text: Aggressive gas, brake, or steering inputs snap fragile winter tire grip instantaneously.

sec11-card-sec11-R37.question_text: What must you clear off before winter driving, and what tool belongs in the car?
sec11-card-sec11-R37.teaching_text: Peeking through a tiny scraped porthole blinds you completely to cross traffic and lane edges.

sec11-card-sec11-R39.question_text: How should you pull away from a stop and hold pace on snow or ice?
sec11-card-sec11-R39.teaching_text: Spinning tires polish snow slick while crawling too slowly can stall you on uphill grades.

sec11-card-sec11-R40.question_text: What helps carry a vehicle through deeper snow, and what improves winter steering?
sec11-card-sec11-R40.teaching_text: Stopping mid-drift strands tires, whereas steady momentum plus deep front tread keeps the nose tracking.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.question_text: What happens to steering control if continuous hard braking locks your front wheels on ice?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.teaching_text: Tires must roll to turn a vehicle, so locked front wheels slide straight ahead regardless of steering.

sec11-card-sec11-F41.question_text: On snow or ice without pumping, how do you modulate brake pressure near wheel lockup?
sec11-card-sec11-F41.teaching_text: Threshold squeeze keeps maximum rolling deceleration without locking tires into an uncontrollable sled.

sec11-card-sec11-F42.question_text: How should you press the pedal with antilock brakes during an icy emergency stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F42.teaching_text: ABS computers pulse wheel valves automatically only while your foot holds firm steady pedal pressure.

sec11-card-sec11-R41.question_text: How far can stopping stretch from just twenty miles per hour on a low-traction icy surface?
sec11-card-sec11-R41.teaching_text: Needing two-thirds of a football field to stop from neighborhood speed shows why tailgating fails on ice.

sec11-card-sec11-R42.question_text: How can road conditions flip abruptly between the sunny side and shady side of a winter hill?
sec11-card-sec11-R42.teaching_text: Cresting briskly off wet sunlit asphalt onto hidden north-slope glare ice catches drivers mid-descent.

sec11-card-sec11-R43.question_text: Besides bridges freezing early, what icy trap can lurk right behind a car stopped ahead?
sec11-card-sec11-R43.teaching_text: Warm exhaust and spinning tires glaze approaches where stopped cars idle, sliding late brakers into bumpers.

sec11-card-sec11-R44.question_text: What does stop-and-go traffic do to fresh snow, and where can your tires find better bite?
sec11-card-sec11-R44.teaching_text: Repeated tire polishing turns wheel tracks mirror-slick while unpacked edges alongside still offer texture.

sec17-card-sec17-R01.question_text: How does the manual describe earning a driver license as a teen steps toward adulthood?
sec17-card-sec17-R01.teaching_text: Treating licensing as a casual birthday perk ignores the real crash stakes facing brand-new solo drivers.

sec17-card-sec17-F01.question_text: What is the single most important thing a supervising adult can do while teaching someone to drive?
sec17-card-sec17-F01.teaching_text: Beginners absorb what they watch for years from the passenger seat far more than lectures.

sec17-card-sec17-F02.question_text: How do teens frequently justify bad road-test habits like rolling stops to license examiners?
sec17-card-sec17-F02.teaching_text: Shortcuts parents take daily show up directly as point deductions on a teen's road test.

sec17-card-sec17-F04.question_text: Which two traffic choices are shaped directly by a new driver's behind-the-wheel attitude?
sec17-card-sec17-F04.teaching_text: Mindset determines whether a novice shares lanes calmly or treats merges and yellow lights like races.

sec17-card-sec17-F05.question_text: Which three personal qualities make a supervising adult an effective driving mentor?
sec17-card-sec17-F05.teaching_text: Calm, respectful coaching paired with cleaning up your own habits protects a teen's long-term safety.

sec17-card-sec17-R02.question_text: What sequence does Tennessee's graduated program establish for beginners of any age?
sec17-card-sec17-R02.teaching_text: Mastering signs and right-of-way rules on paper before entering live lanes prevents mid-intersection confusion.
sec17-card-sec17-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Book study first, supervised driving next

visual_sync.text_span: Book study first, supervised driving next

sec17-card-sec17-F03.question_text: How many days must an applicant under eighteen hold a learner permit before taking the road test?
sec17-card-sec17-F03.teaching_text: Graduated law locks in a full six-month supervised window before any minor can test for solo driving.

sec17-card-sec17-F06.question_text: How can narrating your own thoughts aloud while driving coach a passenger learner safely?
sec17-card-sec17-F06.teaching_text: Pointing out tricky signs, stale yellows, and two-second counts builds hazard awareness before the learner touches the wheel.

sec17-card-sec17-R03.question_text: How should a parent or mentor react when narration prompts friendly critique of their own driving?
sec17-card-sec17-R03.teaching_text: Laughing and owning a mistake proves rules apply to everyone and sharpens the learner's eye.

sec17-card-sec17-R05.question_text: What active role must a mentor maintain from the front passenger seat during practice drives?
sec17-card-sec17-R05.teaching_text: Scanning ahead faster than your novice lets you cue gentle corrections before hazards turn urgent.

sec17-card-sec17-F07.question_text: Why must mentors map out every practice drive beforehand rather than wandering aimlessly?
sec17-card-sec17-F07.teaching_text: Wandering without a plan can dump an early beginner straight onto a multi-lane highway rush.

sec17-card-sec17-R07.question_text: Why should a driving mentor keep spoken commentary brief while the beginner is behind the wheel?
sec17-card-sec17-R07.teaching_text: Every extra sentence competes with mirrors, pedals, and signs for a beginner's limited mental bandwidth.

sec17-card-sec17-F14.question_text: How should a mentor time route directions and choose pedal or control words?
sec17-card-sec17-F14.teaching_text: Calling turns early and sticking to one term like gas pedal avoids last-second confusion.

sec17-card-sec17-F15.question_text: Why must a mentor respond calmly instead of yelling or fussing over routine beginner mistakes?
sec17-card-sec17-F15.teaching_text: Panicked shouting spikes adrenaline and makes a nervous teen more likely to freeze or hit the wrong pedal.

sec17-card-sec17-F16.question_text: What should a mentor and learner do right after a serious behind-the-wheel mistake?
sec17-card-sec17-F16.teaching_text: Parking promptly while details stay fresh lets both of you walk through the safest fix calmly.

sec17-card-sec17-F08.question_text: Why must hand-and-foot coordination be solid before a beginner ever enters live street traffic?
sec17-card-sec17-F08.teaching_text: In a sudden scare, a novice still hunting for the brake can mash the accelerator instead.

sec17-card-sec17-R04.question_text: What single foundation should the earliest behind-the-wheel sessions focus on building?
sec17-card-sec17-R04.teaching_text: Smooth starting, stopping, and steering must feel natural before adding cross-traffic decisions.

sec17-card-sec17-F09.question_text: Where is the ideal place to run phase-one beginner driving practice?
sec17-card-sec17-F09.teaching_text: An open, traffic-free lot lets a beginner learn steering radius and brake feel with zero collision pressure.

sec17-card-sec17-F10.question_text: Which foundational cabin, pedal, backing, and lane-holding skills belong inside phase one?
