sec16-card-sec16-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Red-tipped white cane or guide dog

visual_sync.text_span: Red-tipped white cane or guide dog

sec16-card-sec16-R06.question_text: May pedestrians walk in the street alongside an available sidewalk?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.teaching_text: Tennessee law requires using provided sidewalks rather than stepping into vehicle travel lanes.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.question_text: On which side and in what formation should pedestrians walk when no sidewalk exists?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.teaching_text: Facing oncoming cars lets walkers see approaching vehicles directly and step clear if a driver drifts.
sec16-card-sec16-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Left edge facing traffic, single file

visual_sync.text_span: Left edge facing traffic, single file

sec16-card-sec16-R08.question_text: Why is wearing headphones risky while walking or jogging along busy streets?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.teaching_text: Blocking out horns, sirens, and tire noise steals precious seconds when a vehicle swerves or backs nearby.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.question_text: What four-part look sequence should a pedestrian complete at the curb before stepping out?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.teaching_text: Adding an over-the-shoulder check catches right- or left-turning cars swinging into the crosswalk from behind.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.question_text: Why should pedestrians waiting at an intersection corner step back when a bus or truck turns right?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.teaching_text: Long wheelbases track inward during tight right turns, sweeping trailer tires right across the sidewalk corner.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.question_text: Why must a pedestrian never cut behind a truck that is backing up?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.teaching_text: Solid trailer boxes create a massive rear blind zone where someone on foot disappears completely.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.question_text: What clothing should night walkers wear, and what handheld item gives the best visibility?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.teaching_text: Dark clothes vanish beyond low beams, whereas reflective trim and a live flashlight beam alert drivers early.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.question_text: Does a green traffic light or white walk signal guarantee that stepping into the street is safe?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.teaching_text: Distracted red-light runners and turning cars ignore signals, so look first even when it is your turn.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.question_text: What should you do if the don't-walk signal begins flashing after you are already halfway across?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.teaching_text: Signal timing builds in clearance seconds so pedestrians already in the street can finish crossing without turning back.

sec16-card-sec16-R12.question_text: During which three signal phases are pedestrians barred from starting across unless a walk signal faces them?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.teaching_text: Stepping off on yellow, red, or protected green turn arrows puts walkers straight into turning or cross-street traffic.

sec16-card-sec16-R13.question_text: Why does the law forbid pedestrians from stepping off a curb directly in front of a close-approaching vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-R13.teaching_text: Physics sets minimum braking distance, so darting closely ahead of a moving car creates an unavoidable collision.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.question_text: Which two turning mistakes by motorists cause the majority of car-bicycle collisions?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.teaching_text: Left-hooking an oncoming cyclist or right-hooking a rider beside your fender accounts for most intersection bike wrecks.
sec16-card-sec16-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Turning left or right across riders

visual_sync.text_span: Turning left or right across riders

sec16-card-sec16-F11.question_text: How should you time a left turn with an oncoming cyclist or a right turn with a cyclist on your right?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.teaching_text: Bicycles often travel faster than drivers judge, so waiting lets the rider clear your turn path safely.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.question_text: What legal status do bicyclists hold on most Tennessee streets, and from which highways are they barred?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.teaching_text: Cyclists carry standard vehicle rights and duties everywhere except limited-access interstates, expressways, and posted roads.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.question_text: On which side and in what direction must bicyclists ride on Tennessee roadways?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.teaching_text: Riding against traffic surprises turning drivers, so cyclists travel right-side with traffic while dodging curb hazards.

sec16-card-sec16-R14.question_text: Why is a bicyclist riding properly when moving toward lane center alongside a row of parked cars?
sec16-card-sec16-R14.teaching_text: A suddenly opened car door can knock a cyclist into moving traffic unless the rider leaves door clearance.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.question_text: How much side clearance and what pace does Tennessee law require when overtaking a bicycle?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.teaching_text: Buzzing close past handlebars creates wind wobble and clips mirrors, making three full feet mandatory until clear.
sec16-card-sec16-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Pass slowly with three feet minimum

visual_sync.text_span: Pass slowly with three feet minimum

sec16-card-sec16-F15.question_text: What should you do instead of squeezing between a bicyclist and an oncoming car on a two-lane road?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.teaching_text: Threading the needle between oncoming traffic and a cyclist leaves zero room for a gust or pothole swerve.

sec16-card-sec16-R15.question_text: How do you handle sharing a left-turn lane with a cyclist versus preparing for a right turn near bikes?
sec16-card-sec16-R15.teaching_text: Trailing behind through left turns and merging smoothly before right turns prevents pinching cyclists against curbs.

sec16-card-sec16-R16.question_text: In which two tight street setups must you hold back instead of overtaking a bicycle?
sec16-card-sec16-R16.teaching_text: Forcing a pass where pavement narrows crowds the rider straight into curbs or opening doors.

sec16-card-sec16-R17.question_text: How should you alert an unaware cyclist before overtaking on a narrow road?
sec16-card-sec16-R17.teaching_text: A loud close horn blast can startle a rider into wobbling sideways right into your path.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.question_text: May motorists use a signed and marked bicycle-only lane to turn, pass, or park?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.teaching_text: Dedicated bike lanes reserve safe pavement for two-wheeled riders and ban motor-vehicle turning, passing, or parking.
sec16-card-sec16-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Never turn, pass, or park inside

visual_sync.text_span: Never turn, pass, or park inside

sec16-card-sec16-R20.question_text: How must you set your headlights at night when meeting an oncoming bicyclist?
sec16-card-sec16-R20.teaching_text: High-beam glare blinds an oncoming cyclist just as badly as an oncoming motorist, hiding potholes and curb edges.

sec16-card-sec16-R18.question_text: How does a rider signal a left turn versus the two ways to signal a right turn by hand?
sec16-card-sec16-R18.teaching_text: Test questions check both legal right-turn hand options: left arm angled upward or right arm extended straight.
sec16-card-sec16-R18.must_match_memory_hook: Left straight; right bent-up or straight

visual_sync.text_span: Left straight; right bent-up or straight

sec16-card-sec16-R19.question_text: What arm and palm position signals that a rider or driver is slowing down or stopping?
sec16-card-sec16-R19.teaching_text: Extending the left arm bent ninety degrees downward with an open rear-facing palm warns followers before speed drops.

sec16-card-sec16-R21.question_text: In which three situations may a bicyclist legally occupy the entire traffic lane?
sec16-card-sec16-R21.teaching_text: Potholes, glass, parked doors, overtaking slower traffic, or lanes too skinny to share justify taking center lane.
sec16-card-sec16-R21.must_match_memory_hook: Passing, road hazards, or narrow lanes

visual_sync.text_span: Passing, road hazards, or narrow lanes

sec16-card-sec16-R22.question_text: Which three protective habits does the manual stress for bicycle riders?
sec16-card-sec16-R22.teaching_text: Slipping right beside a bus or truck at an intersection puts a cyclist directly into a wide-turn crush zone.
sec16-card-sec16-R22.must_match_memory_hook: Wear helmets, ride right, avoid curb-squeezing

visual_sync.text_span: Wear helmets, ride right, avoid curb-squeezing

sec16-card-sec16-F17.question_text: What front and rear lighting or reflector visibility distance does Tennessee law require on bicycles at night?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.teaching_text: Both the white forward lamp and rear red reflector or lamp must shine clearly from five hundred feet away.
sec16-card-sec16-F17.must_match_memory_hook: White front, red rear, five-hundred feet

visual_sync.text_span: White front, red rear, five-hundred feet

sec16-card-sec16-R23.question_text: Why must drivers expect sudden turns and wobbles whenever children ride bicycles nearby?
sec16-card-sec16-R23.teaching_text: Kids lack adult gap judgment and balance control, making sudden swerves across lanes common in neighborhoods.
sec16-card-sec16-R23.must_match_memory_hook: Young riders misjudge speed and traffic

visual_sync.text_span: Young riders misjudge speed and traffic

sec16-card-sec16-R24.question_text: From which concealed roadside spots can bicycles emerge abruptly into traffic?
sec16-card-sec16-R24.teaching_text: Scanning past parked SUVs and hedges gives you early brake readiness before a hidden wheel rolls out.

sec16-card-sec16-R25.question_text: What does an orange or red pennant mounted on a bicycle often tell approaching drivers?
sec16-card-sec16-R25.teaching_text: Slowing early matters because a hearing-impaired cyclist may never hear your engine or a gentle horn tap.

sec16-card-sec16-R26.question_text: How does a motorcycle's slim outline affect a car driver's eyes in traffic?
sec16-card-sec16-R26.teaching_text: Narrow handlebars look farther away and slower than wide car bumpers, causing drivers to pull out too late.
sec16-card-sec16-R26.must_match_memory_hook: Slim profile hides speed and distance

visual_sync.text_span: Slim profile hides speed and distance

sec16-card-sec16-F18.question_text: What error by automobile drivers causes two-thirds of car-motorcycle collisions?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.teaching_text: Two out of three car-bike crashes happen when a driver turns left right across a rider's path.
sec16-card-sec16-F18.must_match_memory_hook: Turning across an unseen oncoming motorcycle

visual_sync.text_span: Turning across an unseen oncoming motorcycle

sec16-card-sec16-F19.question_text: How much lane width belongs to a motorcycle, and may a car drive beside one in the same lane?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.teaching_text: Riders shift left and right inside their lane to dodge oil slicks and potholes, making lane sharing illegal.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.question_text: Why must you avoid passing a motorcycle too closely or at excessive speed?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.teaching_text: Your car's wake pushes a light two-wheeled bike sideways, so change lanes completely at controlled speed.
sec16-card-sec16-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Wind gusts shove riders off balance

visual_sync.text_span: Wind gusts shove riders off balance

sec16-card-sec16-F21.question_text: At least how many seconds of following distance must you maintain behind a motorcycle?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.teaching_text: Motorcycles downshift and stop briskly without always flashing brake lights first, needing full two-second cushions.
sec16-card-sec16-F21.must_match_memory_hook: Keep at least two seconds back

visual_sync.text_span: Keep at least two seconds back

sec16-card-sec16-R27.question_text: Why are blind-spot head checks especially critical for spotting motorcycles before changing lanes?
sec16-card-sec16-R27.teaching_text: A compact bike fits entirely inside a car's side mirror blind zone unless you turn your head first.
sec16-card-sec16-R27.must_match_memory_hook: Motorcycles vanish easily inside blind spots

visual_sync.text_span: Motorcycles vanish easily inside blind spots

sec16-card-sec16-R28.question_text: Why should you wait at an intersection until a motorcyclist's actual turn or straight move becomes unmistakable?
sec16-card-sec16-R28.teaching_text: Many motorcycle turn signals do not self-cancel, so trusting a blinking light alone causes intersection t-bones.
sec16-card-sec16-R28.must_match_memory_hook: Confirm rider's move before pulling out

visual_sync.text_span: Confirm rider's move before pulling out

sec16-card-sec16-R29.question_text: Why is a motorcycle harder to judge after dark, and what beam courtesy still applies?
sec16-card-sec16-R29.teaching_text: One headlight or taillight merges into background car lights, and high-beam glare blinds riders through helmet visors.
sec16-card-sec16-R29.must_match_memory_hook: Single lamp blends; dim high beams

visual_sync.text_span: Single lamp blends; dim high beams

sec16-card-sec16-R30.question_text: Which five weather, wind, or bridge surfaces make stability hardest for motorcyclists?
sec16-card-sec16-R30.teaching_text: Steel bridge grates, wet paint, angled rail tracks, and wind gusts unsettle two tires, requiring extra following room.
sec16-card-sec16-R30.must_match_memory_hook: Rain, crosswinds, truck gusts, rails, grates

visual_sync.text_span: Rain, crosswinds, truck gusts, rails, grates

sec16-card-sec16-R31.question_text: Which road vehicles accelerate fastest off the line, and which accelerate slowest?
sec16-card-sec16-R31.teaching_text: Power-to-weight lets motorcycles leap ahead rapidly while heavy trucks and buses build highway speed slowly.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.question_text: In fatal collisions involving passenger cars and large trucks, who suffers seventy-eight percent of the deaths?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.teaching_text: Massive weight mismatches mean nearly four out of five fatalities fall on the smaller car's driver and riders.

sec16-card-sec16-R33.question_text: What single piece of safety equipment provides your strongest protection in a crash with a large truck?
sec16-card-sec16-R33.teaching_text: Staying strapped inside the survival cage stops ejection during violent heavy-truck impacts.
sec16-card-sec16-R33.must_match_memory_hook: Buckling your safety belt protects most

visual_sync.text_span: Buckling your safety belt protects most

sec16-card-sec16-F23.question_text: How can you tell instantly whether a large truck's driver can see your car?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.teaching_text: If you cannot spot the trucker's face in their side mirror, your car sits hidden inside a blind zone.
sec16-card-sec16-F23.must_match_memory_hook: No driver reflection means you're invisible

visual_sync.text_span: No driver reflection means you're invisible

sec16-card-sec16-F24.question_text: Up to how much can a loaded semi weigh, and how does fifty-five-mile-per-hour stopping compare between cars and semis?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.teaching_text: Stopping at fifty-five jumps from roughly two hundred forty feet in a car past four hundred fifty feet for semis.
sec16-card-sec16-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Eighty thousand pounds; four-fifty-foot truck stops

visual_sync.text_span: Eighty thousand pounds; four-fifty-foot truck stops

sec16-card-sec16-R34.question_text: Roughly what share of American communities rely solely on trucks for freight, and how long can rigs stretch?
sec16-card-sec16-R34.teaching_text: Passing a combination longer than seventy feet takes far more road than overtaking an ordinary sedan.
sec16-card-sec16-R34.must_match_memory_hook: Seventy-seven percent communities; over seventy feet

visual_sync.text_span: Seventy-seven percent communities; over seventy feet

sec16-card-sec16-F25.question_text: Why do large trucks swing left before turning right, and why must you never slip beside them?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.teaching_text: Sneaking into the right-hand gap as a semi swings left traps your car beneath the turning trailer.
sec16-card-sec16-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Wide setups hide right-side blind zones

visual_sync.text_span: Wide setups hide right-side blind zones

sec16-card-sec16-R32.question_text: Why is darting sharply in front of a moving bus or tractor-trailer so dangerous?
sec16-card-sec16-R32.teaching_text: Heavy rigs cannot shed speed fast enough when a car steals their front buffer.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.question_text: When may you pull back ahead of a passed truck, and what must your speed do afterward?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.teaching_text: Waiting until the entire cab grill fills your rearview mirror and holding speed keeps forty tons off your bumper.
sec16-card-sec16-F26.must_match_memory_hook: See whole cab front; keep pace

visual_sync.text_span: See whole cab front; keep pace

sec16-card-sec16-F27.question_text: Which four areas around a tractor-trailer make up its blind spots, and how far back does the rear one stretch?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.teaching_text: Riding anywhere inside that two-hundred-foot rear wake or alongside the trailer hides you from the cab.
sec16-card-sec16-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Front, both sides, two-hundred feet back

visual_sync.text_span: Front, both sides, two-hundred feet back

sec16-card-sec16-R36.question_text: How many feet directly ahead of a conventional long-hood bumper can disappear from the trucker's view?
sec16-card-sec16-R36.teaching_text: Squeezing tight ahead of a tall radiator hood puts a compact car completely below the trucker's sightline.
sec16-card-sec16-R36.must_match_memory_hook: Ten to twenty feet hidden ahead

visual_sync.text_span: Ten to twenty feet hidden ahead

sec16-card-sec16-R35.question_text: How should you take an upcoming highway exit when traveling near a truck or bus?
sec16-card-sec16-R35.teaching_text: Sprinting ahead just to dive across a semi's nose onto an exit ramp risks a high-speed underride crash.
sec16-card-sec16-R35.must_match_memory_hook: Ease off and exit behind trucks

visual_sync.text_span: Ease off and exit behind trucks

sec16-card-sec16-R38.question_text: How does a truck's or bus's large size trick approaching drivers into misjudging its speed?
sec16-card-sec16-R38.teaching_text: Optical scale makes big rigs look leisurely even at highway speed, tempting risky left turns across their path.
sec16-card-sec16-R38.must_match_memory_hook: Large vehicles appear slower than reality

visual_sync.text_span: Large vehicles appear slower than reality

sec16-card-sec16-R39.question_text: What does a truck or bus driver communicate by blinking headlights after you overtake them?
sec16-card-sec16-R39.teaching_text: Even with a courteous flash, verify the cab's full front in your mirror before merging right.
sec16-card-sec16-R39.must_match_memory_hook: Clear to return once mirror confirms

visual_sync.text_span: Clear to return once mirror confirms

sec16-card-sec16-R37.question_text: Which lane should you vacate when passing a highway commercial weigh station, and why?
sec16-card-sec16-R37.teaching_text: Loaded rigs leaving scale ramps accelerate slowly and need an open right lane to rejoin highway flow.
sec16-card-sec16-R37.must_match_memory_hook: Clear right lane for merging trucks

visual_sync.text_span: Clear right lane for merging trucks

sec02-card-sec02-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Original live seal, never photocopied stamp

sec02-card-sec02-F26.question_text: Within how many days of establishing Tennessee residency must an out-of-state driver switch to a Tennessee license?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.teaching_text: Driving past day thirty on your former state's card after moving to Tennessee violates state residency licensing law.
sec02-card-sec02-F26.must_match_memory_hook: Switch licenses within thirty residency days

visual_sync.text_span: Switch licenses within thirty residency days

sec02-card-sec02-F27.question_text: Which screening must every single new or returning Tennessee resident complete at the Driver Service Center?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.teaching_text: Even when your valid out-of-state card waives written and road exams, nobody skips the counter vision check.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.question_text: How long must an out-of-state license be expired before a new resident has to take all three Tennessee exams?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.teaching_text: Letting a former state's license stay lapsed beyond six months forfeits reciprocity and requires written, road, and vision testing.
sec02-card-sec02-F28.must_match_memory_hook: Expired past six months triggers retesting

visual_sync.text_span: Expired past six months triggers retesting

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: How does the thirty-day newcomer rule differ from the six-month rule for out-of-state licenses?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: Written exams pair these numbers to see if you confuse the thirty-day transfer deadline with the six-month expiration retest trigger.
sec02-card-sec02-R10.must_match_memory_hook: Thirty days switches, six months retests

visual_sync.text_span: Thirty days switches, six months retests

sec02-card-sec02-F29.question_text: Which exams must new residents arriving from another country pass, and what happens to their foreign license?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.teaching_text: Unlike domestic transfers who surrender old state cards, international arrivals take full Tennessee testing while keeping their home credential.
sec02-card-sec02-F29.must_match_memory_hook: All three exams, keep foreign card

visual_sync.text_span: All three exams, keep foreign card

sec02-card-sec02-F30.question_text: When does a United States Armed Forces member's Tennessee license remain valid beyond its printed expiration date?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.teaching_text: Service members stationed out of state keep valid driving privileges automatically as long as the license was never suspended or surrendered.
sec02-card-sec02-F30.must_match_memory_hook: Active duty outside Tennessee, clean status

visual_sync.text_span: Active duty outside Tennessee, clean status

sec02-card-sec02-F32.question_text: How can active-duty troops stationed outside Tennessee mark their license to show it does not expire?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.teaching_text: Adding Code thirty prevents out-of-state police or rental counters from mistaking a printed expiration date for an invalid card.
sec02-card-sec02-F32.must_match_memory_hook: Show military orders, add Code thirty

visual_sync.text_span: Show military orders, add Code thirty

sec02-card-sec02-F33.question_text: How soon must troops renew after discharge or reassignment back to Tennessee, and how is Fort Campbell treated?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.teaching_text: Being assigned to Fort Campbell counts as returning to Tennessee, starting the sixty-day renewal clock just like separation from service.
sec02-card-sec02-F33.must_match_memory_hook: Sixty days back; Fort Campbell counts

visual_sync.text_span: Sixty days back; Fort Campbell counts

sec02-card-sec02-R12.question_text: Which two military-connected groups are excluded from using Tennessee's active-duty license extension?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.teaching_text: Spouses, dependents, and National Guard members must renew on normal schedules rather than relying on active-duty extensions.
sec02-card-sec02-R12.must_match_memory_hook: National Guard and military dependents excluded

visual_sync.text_span: National Guard and military dependents excluded

sec02-card-sec02-F24.question_text: How long do Tennessee licenses for drivers over twenty-one last since two thousand sixteen, and how did expiration dates change?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.teaching_text: Assuming your card still expires on your birthday can catch you off guard because eight-year terms count from issuance date.
sec02-card-sec02-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Eight years from issue, off birthdays

visual_sync.text_span: Eight years from issue, off birthdays

sec02-card-sec02-F35.question_text: When did pre-two-thousand-sixteen Class D licenses expire compared with the standard term of a learner permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.teaching_text: Knowing that learner permits run only twelve months from issuance prevents teens from letting supervised practice privileges lapse.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.question_text: On the eight-year fee chart, what do a Class D license at sixteen and a minor's one-year permit at fifteen cost?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.teaching_text: Knowing exact counter fees keeps teen permit applicants at fifteen and new Class D drivers at sixteen ready on test day.
sec02-card-sec02-F31.must_match_memory_hook: Twenty-eight Class D, ten-fifty teen permit

visual_sync.text_span: Twenty-eight Class D, ten-fifty teen permit

sec02-card-sec02-R11.question_text: How does the one-year learner permit fee differ between applicants under eighteen and applicants over eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.teaching_text: Graduated teen processing makes an under-eighteen learner permit ten dollars and fifty cents versus five dollars and fifty cents for adults.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: Which six payment methods are accepted at Tennessee Driver Service Centers?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Bringing an unsupported card brand can stall checkout since centers take only MasterCard, Visa, Discover, cash, checks, and money orders.
sec02-card-sec02-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Cash, check, money order, three cards

visual_sync.text_span: Cash, check, money order, three cards

sec02-card-sec02-F34.question_text: Where can lost credentials be replaced, and which two temporary cards can never be replaced online?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.teaching_text: Temporary driver and identification holders must visit a center in person because online duplicate portals block temporary credentials.
sec02-card-sec02-F34.must_match_memory_hook: Centers or online, never temporary credentials

visual_sync.text_span: Centers or online, never temporary credentials

sec02-card-sec02-F36.question_text: How far ahead of expiration does Tennessee mail a courtesy renewal notice, and is that notice required to renew?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.teaching_text: Missing a mailed reminder never excuses an expired license because you can renew on time without bringing the notice.
sec02-card-sec02-F36.must_match_memory_hook: Eight to ten weeks; optional notice

visual_sync.text_span: Eight to ten weeks; optional notice

sec02-card-sec02-F37.question_text: How do late renewal penalties escalate past thirty days, past six months, and past five years expired?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.teaching_text: Ignoring an expired card climbs from small five- and ten-dollar late fees into retaking vision, written, and road tests at five years.
sec02-card-sec02-F37.must_match_memory_hook: Five dollars, ten dollars, full retest

visual_sync.text_span: Five dollars, ten dollars, full retest

sec02-card-sec02-F38.question_text: How much grace time do you get to keep driving after your Tennessee license expires, and what penalty applies?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.teaching_text: Test questions bust the thirty-day grace-period myth: late fees wait thirty days, while legal driving stops the midnight your card expires.
sec02-card-sec02-F38.must_match_memory_hook: Zero grace period, unlicensed driving penalties

visual_sync.text_span: Zero grace period, unlicensed driving penalties

sec02-card-sec02-R14.question_text: At what age may drivers choose a non-photo license remotely, and why might keeping a photo card still help?
sec02-card-sec02-R14.teaching_text: Skipping a photo at sixty works for local driving, yet airlines, trains, and cruise lines expect government photo identification.
sec02-card-sec02-R14.must_match_memory_hook: Sixty skips photo; travel needs one

visual_sync.text_span: Sixty skips photo; travel needs one

sec02-card-sec02-F39.question_text: How soon must you report a residential address change, even if postal or emergency renumbering caused it?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.teaching_text: Even if you never packed a box, a street rename or postal change must reach the state within ten days.
sec02-card-sec02-F39.must_match_memory_hook: Report within ten days, even renumbering

visual_sync.text_span: Report within ten days, even renumbering

sec02-card-sec02-F40.question_text: What address details must appear on your Tennessee license, and why is a post office box alone refused?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.teaching_text: Licensing records must tie every driver to an actual house or apartment street address rather than a mail-only box.
sec02-card-sec02-F40.must_match_memory_hook: Physical street address, never post box

visual_sync.text_span: Physical street address, never post box

sec02-card-sec02-R15.question_text: When your address changes, what must be updated within ten days, and what does not have to be replaced?
sec02-card-sec02-R15.teaching_text: Written exams test that updating your official state record within ten days satisfies the law without buying a new plastic license.
sec02-card-sec02-R15.must_match_memory_hook: Update state file; keep plastic card

visual_sync.text_span: Update state file; keep plastic card

sec02-card-sec02-R16.question_text: How does the federal Driver Privacy Protection Act guard personal details on your Tennessee driving record?
sec02-card-sec02-R16.teaching_text: Federal law shields your home address and personal record details from public release unless you grant express permission.
sec02-card-sec02-R16.must_match_memory_hook: Blocks personal data release without consent

visual_sync.text_span: Blocks personal data release without consent

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: May a Tennessee officer pull you over and ticket you SOLELY for a safety-belt or child-restraint violation?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Unlike secondary-enforcement states, Tennessee police do not need another traffic infraction to pull unbelted cars over.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: Which front-row occupants must wear a safety belt whenever a vehicle is moving in Tennessee?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Once the wheels roll, everyone riding in the front row must stay buckled regardless of age.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: Under what age must back-seat passengers always wear safety belts in Tennessee?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Minors sixteen and younger must buckle up even when riding in the rear row.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: When the driver holds a learner permit or intermediate license, which back-seat age group must wear safety belts?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Graduated licensing explicitly requires back-seat riders aged four through seventeen to stay belted behind teen drivers.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: Compare Tennessee's general back-seat belt age rule against the rule for permit and intermediate drivers?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: General law covers under-seventeen rear riders, while permit and intermediate drivers add age seventeen too.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What historic national first did Tennessee achieve in child passenger safety legislation?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Tennessee pioneered mandatory car seats and boosters before any other state in the country.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: Which two groups of young children — by age OR weight — must ride in a rear-facing car seat?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Notice the word OR — a ten-month-old over twenty pounds or a light one-year-old still faces backward.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What age range AND weight requirement place a child into a forward-facing car seat?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Both thresholds must align — at least age one through three AND weighing over twenty pounds.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: What age span AND height cutoff require a child to use a belt-positioning booster seat?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Boosters lift kids aged four through eight under four feet nine inches so adult belts fit.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: Walk through all three Tennessee child-restraint stages from rear-facing to forward-facing to booster?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Locking the twenty-pound weight split and four-foot-nine booster ceiling solves every child-seat test item.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: In which row must a child in a booster ride when available — and what standards govern seats?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Boosters belong in the rear seat whenever present, installed strictly per federal and manufacturer instructions.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: When a child uses a medically prescribed modified restraint, what document should stay inside that vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Carrying a copy of the physician's prescription in the glovebox proves compliance during any stop.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: Normally, who answers legally for unrestrained children under sixteen — and what dollar fine applies?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: When parents aren't riding along, the driver carries a fifty-dollar fine responsibility under sixteen.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: What shifts legal responsibility off the driver when a child's parent or legal guardian rides as a passenger?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Watch this Tennessee twist — if the child's parent is in the passenger seat, they take the ticket.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: What criminal grade and mandatory class can hit for skipping a required car seat or booster under age nine?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Skipping a car seat or booster under nine or four-foot-nine escalates to a Class C misdemeanor and safety class.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: Contrast when Tennessee's plain fifty-dollar restraint fine applies versus the heavier Class C misdemeanor?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Older unbelted kids under sixteen draw the fifty-dollar fine, whereas missing car seats trigger Class C charges.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: Name the five physical ways safety belts shield your body during a crash?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Keeping you inside while spreading impact across strong pelvic and shoulder bones shields head and spine.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: Even when a severe crash still makes a belted rider touch the wheel or dash, how does the belt help?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Slowing your torso down with the vehicle's crumple zone softens any remaining contact dramatically.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: Which two crash advantages let a belted driver keep handling an unfolding emergency?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Remaining upright and awake behind the wheel lets you steer clear of secondary collisions.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: By what percentages do lap-and-shoulder belts cut death and moderate-to-critical injury for front-seat car occupants?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Cutting front-seat car death risk nearly in half makes clicking your belt an instant lifesaver.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: By what even larger percentages do belts cut death and moderate-to-critical injury for light-truck occupants?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Pickups and SUVs roll more often than sedans, pushing belt survival gains to sixty and sixty-five percent.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: How many times more likely were unbelted crash occupants to die — and to suffer serious injury?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Facing thirty-two times higher odds of dying shows how severely riding unbelted stacks the deck.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: Which single safety behavior contributes to more traffic deaths than any other according to the Tennessee manual?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: No single decision behind the wheel claims more lives nationwide than leaving a seat belt unbuckled.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: How fast does a safety belt release, and how common are crashes ending in fire or deep water?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: One quick click releases a latch in under a second while keeping you conscious beforehand.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: What tiny percentage of crashes actually end in fire or submersion — and why does buckling still help there?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Only half of one percent involve fire or water, where staying conscious lets you unbuckle and escape.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: Compared with riders who stay inside the cabin, how much more likely are ejected occupants to be killed?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Flying through glass onto pavement or under rolling metal quadruples fatal crash risk.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: What fraction does the Tennessee manual give for the chance of being killed once ejected from a vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Facing one-in-eight fatal odds once thrown outside proves why staying belted inside the cage matters.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: When your car is T-boned from the side, which direction do loose items and unbelted passengers slide?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: As the struck car shoves sideways underneath you, inertia throws unbelted bodies straight into the hit.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: How many traffic deaths on Tennessee roads in two thousand sixteen does the manual cite to show why buckling matters?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Remembering one thousand thirty-nine Tennessee crash deaths underscores how many unbelted victims could have survived.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: Where across your lower body should the lap belt sit?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Anchoring low across the pelvis and upper thighs keeps crash force off soft abdominal organs.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: Where must the shoulder belt cross, which two body zones are off-limits, and how tight should it stay?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Routing under an arm crushes ribs, and leaving slack lets the strap slip off your shoulder.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: How should a pregnant driver or passenger position both parts of her safety belt?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Framing the belly — lap strap low beneath, shoulder strap angled above between breasts — protects mother and baby.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: What posture check against the vehicle seat shows a child is finally tall enough for adult belts?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Kids whose legs are too short slouch forward to bend their knees, pushing lap belts onto stomachs.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: Once a child graduates to adult belts, where must the lap and shoulder straps rest — and never go?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Tucking an uncomfortable shoulder strap behind a child's back or under an arm invites spinal injury.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: Which two bones take pressure under 'belts-to-bones' — and what happens if straps touch stomach, face, or neck?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Any belt creeping onto soft belly tissue or rubbing the neck means returning straight to a booster.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.question_text: Where specifically must the lap belt sit once a child moves out of a booster into vehicle belts?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.teaching_text: Keeping the lap strap flat across upper thighs locks it low over strong hip bones.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: What share of otherwise-fatal crashes do properly secured infants survive — and how about toddlers?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Properly installed infant carriers turn three out of four fatal crashes into survivable impacts.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: Out of every ten deaths and ten serious injuries under age four, how many could proper child restraints prevent?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Nearly every fatal or severe crash injury among toddlers and preschoolers becomes preventable once restraints fit properly.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.question_text: Why does your own seat-belt consistency directly shape whether children stay buckled?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.teaching_text: Children mirror adult behavior automatically, making your own click the strongest lesson inside the cabin.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.question_text: What do the manual's two thousand twenty CDC figures identify as the leading cause of fatal injury for ages three to fourteen?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.teaching_text: Traffic crashes outrank other injury causes for school-age kids, keeping car seats and belts vital.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: What pairing delivers the strongest crash protection available in a car, SUV, or truck?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Belts hold you in position while airbags cushion forward momentum across cars, SUVs, and pickups.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: What cabin strikes do airbags prevent, and how fast do they inflate and deflate?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Explosive inflation faster than an eye blink demands sitting ten-plus inches back before impact.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.question_text: More than how many lives does the manual credit airbags with saving between nineteen eighty-seven and two thousand twelve?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.teaching_text: Nearly forty thousand NHTSA-documented saves across twenty-five years prove supplemental airbags work.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: Through what age are children safest riding properly restrained in the back seat — with or without a passenger airbag?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Even without a front airbag, rear seats keep kids twelve and under farthest from frontal crush.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: Where must you avoid installing a child safety seat whenever a vehicle has a rear row?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Passenger airbags deploy at speed built for adult chests, endangering children in safety seats.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.question_text: Where do infants in rear-facing seats belong when a car has a front passenger airbag and a back seat?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.teaching_text: A rear-facing shell rests inches from the dashboard where an inflating airbag strikes hardest.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: If a child MUST ride up front — like in a two-seat pickup with a passenger airbag — what two steps apply?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Pushing the passenger track all the way back maximizes distance from the airbag cover.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: How many inches should adults keep between their breastbone and the airbag cover while wearing both belt straps?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Sitting ten to twelve inches back lets the bag cushion fully instead of punching upward.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: How should you angle an adjustable tilt steering wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Tilting downward aims the steering hub toward your ribcage rather than upward at your chin.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.question_text: Which age group is ALWAYS banned from pickup beds in Tennessee — and where are ages six to twelve banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.teaching_text: Memorize both tiers — under six never rides in beds, and six-to-twelve stays off state and interstate highways.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.question_text: Which two activities allow children in a pickup bed — and what speed ceiling governs parades?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.teaching_text: Organized parades or ceremonies stay capped at twenty miles per hour alongside agricultural farm work.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.question_text: Even off state highways, why might ages six to twelve still be barred from riding in a pickup bed?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.teaching_text: Tennessee cities and counties can extend the six-to-twelve pickup-bed ban onto local streets too.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.question_text: Under what child age, supervisor age, and three risk triggers is leaving a child in a parked public vehicle a crime?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.teaching_text: Dangerous heat, a running engine, or keys left inside make leaving kids under seven unlawful without a thirteen-plus sitter.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.question_text: What misdemeanor class and first-versus-repeat fines punish leaving a child under seven unattended in a car?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.teaching_text: First offenses bring a Class B misdemeanor and two hundred dollars, jumping to five hundred afterward.
sec06-card-sec06-F37.must_match_memory_hook: Class B; two hundred, five hundred

visual_sync.text_span: Class B; two hundred, five hundred

sec06-card-sec06-F38.question_text: On a sunny summer day, how fast can heat inside a parked car start harming a child?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.teaching_text: Greenhouse glass traps solar heat so rapidly that ten minutes of errands turns dangerous.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.question_text: Even on a mild seventy-three-degree day, how hot can an SUV reach in ten and thirty minutes — and at ninety outside?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.teaching_text: Seventy-three outside hits one hundred in ten minutes, while ninety outside rockets to one hundred sixty.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.question_text: Above which temperatures do heat exhaustion and heat stroke set in — and why are kids extra vulnerable?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.teaching_text: Children's still-developing respiratory systems overheat far faster once cabins pass ninety and one hundred five degrees.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.question_text: Why shouldn't even a quick errand tempt you to leave a child behind — and what check belongs at every stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.teaching_text: Quiet sleeping infants in rear-facing carriers get forgotten when routines change unless you check every row.

sec06-card-sec06-R20.question_text: Why must you lock parked cars at home and keep keys and fobs away from children?
sec06-card-sec06-R20.teaching_text: Curious kids climb inside unlocked cars, trap themselves in heat, or shift vehicles into rollaways.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.question_text: What should you do immediately if a child gets locked inside a car or you spot a child or pet left alone?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.teaching_text: Minutes separate heat exhaustion from fatal heat stroke, so dial nine-one-one without hesitation.

sec06-card-sec06-R21.question_text: Under Tennessee child-abuse law, how does knowingly injuring a child shift charges when the victim is six or younger?
sec06-card-sec06-R21.teaching_text: Injuring a child six or younger elevates a Class A misdemeanor straight to a Class D felony.

sec06-card-sec06-R22.question_text: Contrast the jail-and-fine range of a Tennessee Class A misdemeanor against a Class A felony?
sec06-card-sec06-R22.teaching_text: Class A misdemeanors cap under a year and twenty-five hundred dollars, while Class A felonies bring fifteen-to-sixty years.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: Which three surface-street hazards are absent on interstates, and how does traffic get on and off?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Replacing stop signs, red lights, and train tracks with grade-separated ramps lets freeway traffic enter and leave without crossing paths.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: Which deadly crash type have interstates and divided highways largely wiped out, and how is road geometry built?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Separating opposing lanes across medians removes oncoming conflicts while engineered grades avoid steep climbs and blind bends.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: What route details and gauge should you check before rolling onto an interstate, especially in rural areas?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Rural Tennessee interchanges sit miles apart, turning a missed exit or low gas tank into a stranded shoulder emergency.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: What should you do if you are unwilling or unable to maintain at least the interstate's minimum speed?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Rolling onto high-speed lanes below minimum pace creates a dangerous mobile roadblock—use surface highways instead.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: How do you use an interstate entrance ramp and acceleration lane to merge cleanly into freeway traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Matching freeway speed down the acceleration lane before signaling left lets you slip smoothly into gaps without forcing brakes.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: Between a driver entering on an on-ramp and vehicles already cruising on the interstate, who must legally yield?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Vehicles established in freeway lanes never owe the right-of-way to merging ramp cars—adjust speed to fit their gaps.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: Even though ramp traffic must legally yield, what should drivers already on the interstate do near on-ramps?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Shifting left a lane or easing throttle helps merging cars join smoothly and protects your own fender.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: Why must you never stop at the tip of an on-ramp, and how should you time tight traffic gaps instead?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Stopping dead at the merge point triggers ramp rear-ends and leaves zero runway left to accelerate up to seventy.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: What does an interstate 'Lane Added' sign tell both entering ramp drivers and right-lane freeway drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Entering drivers can roll straight ahead without merging immediately, while main-line cars should avoid darting right into them.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: What does an interstate 'Merge' sign tell drivers, unlike a 'Lane Added' sign?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Because the entrance lane is about to pinch off, both ramp and right-lane drivers must watch closely for blending cars.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: What extra allowance should you give heavy trucks and buses accelerating down an interstate entrance ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Loaded tractor-trailers and coaches need far more runway and gap length than passenger cars to climb to freeway speed.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: Which lane stays open for overtaking on multi-lane interstates, and where should you avoid cruising beside other cars?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Save the far-left lane for passing traffic and stagger your position so you never camp inside adjacent blind zones.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: What are the three downsides of constant freeway lane-hopping compared with holding an even speed?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Darting from gap to gap multiplies blind-spot conflict, sparks road rage, and shaves almost zero real arrival time.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: Why should you avoid cruising bunched inside tight clusters of freeway cars?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Driving boxed in on all four sides leaves nowhere to steer if a tire blows or brakes lock ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: What minimum following gap applies on interstates in clear conditions versus storms, darkness, or fast rural stretches?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Two seconds is the bare floor—rain, nighttime glare, or seventy-mile-per-hour rural speed call for four seconds or more.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.question_text: What bad habit triggers many multi-car interstate chain-reaction crashes?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.teaching_text: Higher freeway momentum eats ground fast, turning tight bumpers into instant ten-car chain reactions when traffic checks up.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: How many seconds down the road should your eyes scan while cruising on an interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Looking fifteen to twenty seconds ahead spots brake lights, merging trucks, and exit backups long before panic braking.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: How should you alert fast-approaching drivers behind you when interstate traffic ahead suddenly slows or stops?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Flashing your brake lamps with several gentle taps wakes up zoned-out drivers behind you before you brake hard.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: May you break the posted speed limit just to match faster interstate traffic, and where belong slower drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: 'Going with the flow' is never a legal defense past the sign—keep within limits and use the right lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: Why does Tennessee law outlaw driving too slowly on an interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: A forty-mile-per-hour car inside seventy-mile-per-hour lanes creates violent closing speeds just as hazardous as excessive speeding.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: What is the far-left interstate lane reserved for, and what must you do when a faster vehicle closes behind you?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Camping in the passing lane forces dangerous right-side undertakes, so signal and slide one lane right promptly.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: On multi-lane interstates, drivers in which lanes should stay ready to yield rightward for overtaking traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Only the outermost right slow lane has nowhere farther right to yield—middle and left lanes shift right for faster flow.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: During which weekday rush-hour windows are Tennessee HOV lanes restricted, and which vehicles qualify?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Weekday peaks from seven to nine morning and four to six evening reserve HOV lanes for two-plus carpools, bikes, buses, and responders.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: Does an infant in a car seat count toward HOV occupancy, and may a solo driver duck into the HOV lane to pass?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Every human occupant—including a strapped-in baby—counts toward two-plus, and solo drivers cannot touch HOV lanes at peak even briefly.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: How do HOV lanes operate on weekends and off-peak hours, and what fine hits peak-hour violators?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Outside weekday rush windows anyone can use the lane normally, while peak-hour solo cheating costs fifty dollars plus court fees.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: Where do Tennessee interstate HOV lanes sit, and how do you enter one from an on-ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Because HOV lanes hug the far-left median, merge normally first and step across one lane at a time.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: At peak HOV hours, how does the occupant rule for a bus compare with a motorcycle?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Watch that tricky exam detail—an empty deadheading bus with just a driver fails peak HOV, while a solo motorcyclist qualifies.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: What must you plan early if your exit comes up before the inside HOV lane ends?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: Crossing three or four lanes from the median to a right-hand exit takes calm early lane changes, never a dive-bomb.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: When should you move into the right-hand lane ahead of your planned interstate exit?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Getting settled in the right lane early avoids dangerous last-second swoops across fast multi-lane traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: How far ahead do advance interstate exit signs typically appear, and how does heavy traffic change your timing?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: One-mile warning boards give you your cue, and bumper-to-bumper traffic demands sliding right even earlier.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: When exiting an interstate, at what exact point should you start slowing down?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Braking early inside a seventy-mile-per-hour travel lane invites rear-ends—wait until you enter the deceleration lane, then match ramp signs.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: What pavement marker pattern typically outlines an interstate exit's deceleration lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: A crisp line of white reflectors guides drivers cleanly into the deceleration pocket at night and in rain.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: What are the only two legal reasons to drive onto an interstate's paved shoulder?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Using the breakdown shoulder to sneak past traffic jams risks slamming into stalled cars or roadside workers.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: When is parking on any part of an interstate entrance or exit ramp legal?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Curved ramps have short sightlines where drivers accelerate or brake hard—never stop there to check directions or phones.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: At a standard diamond interchange, where does the exit ramp split off, and how do you turn onto the crossroad?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Diamond exits peel off ahead of the overpass or underpass and meet the surface road at a regular sign or signal.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: Driving along the surface crossroad at a diamond interchange, where do you find the right-turn on-ramp versus the left-turn on-ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Turning left too early before the bridge puts you wrong-way down the off-ramp—cross over or under first for left entries.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: How do you end up going left at a cloverleaf interchange where every ramp exits to the right?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: Pass under or over the crossroad first, then peel onto the looping right-hand ramp that curls two-seventy degrees left.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.question_text: At a cloverleaf interchange, which ramp takes you right onto the cross highway?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.teaching_text: To head right at a cloverleaf, exit onto the outer right-hand slip ramp before reaching the bridge.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.question_text: What traffic-flow advantage does a full cloverleaf interchange provide?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.teaching_text: Replacing left-across-traffic turns with sweeping right-hand loops keeps busy highways flowing without stop lights.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: What makes a weaving interchange one of the riskiest spots on an interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: Accelerating on-ramp cars trying to move left cross paths inside the same short lane with exiting cars slowing right.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.question_text: How should entering and exiting drivers handle conflict inside a weaving interchange?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.teaching_text: Cooperating smoothly—matching gaps and sharing space equally—prevents sideswipes where entry and exit paths crisscross.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: Which three turn-around moves are illegal if you miss your interstate exit?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Missing an exit costs ten extra minutes at the next interchange—backing or cutting medians costs lives.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.question_text: When is a left turn or U-turn ever legal on an interstate, and who may use unmarked median strips?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.teaching_text: Unless an opening is specifically built and signed for public turns, median crossovers belong strictly to responders and TDOT crews.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.question_text: What rules cover unsignaled lane changes, blind-spot cruising, and improvised interstate entries?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.teaching_text: Every lane shift requires a blinker, lingering in blind zones is unsafe, and entering anywhere outside official ramps is illegal.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.question_text: Where is non-emergency stopping or parking allowed along an interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.teaching_text: Pull into rest stops or off-exit plazas for breaks—highway shoulders are reserved strictly for true breakdowns and emergencies.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.question_text: Which four ongoing checks and spacing habits keep long interstate drives trouble-free?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.teaching_text: Signaling early, sweeping mirrors regularly, holding safe time gaps, and glancing at speed and fuel gauges prevent surprises.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.question_text: Which three unexpected living or traffic hazards must you stay alert for even on controlled-access interstates?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.teaching_text: Fences and ramps cannot stop deer, stranded motorists near breakdowns, or impaired wrong-way drivers after dark.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.question_text: What updates appear on overhead TDOT SmartWay Dynamic Message Signs, and what does a blank board mean?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.teaching_text: Electronic SmartWay boards post live crash, work, weather, travel-time, and Amber Alert notices, staying dark when roads run clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.question_text: Why is nighttime driving far deadlier per mile than daytime driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.teaching_text: Drowsiness, headlight-limited vision, and a higher share of alcohol-impaired drivers stack together after sunset.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.question_text: What causes 'interstate hypnosis' on long freeway drives?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.teaching_text: Unchanging straight scenery paired with constant wind, engine, and tire hum lulls your brain into zoned-out drowsiness.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.question_text: Which three actions combat interstate hypnosis, and why must drowsiness trigger an immediate stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.teaching_text: Keep scanning mirrors and signs in a cool cabin, and exit immediately if drowsy—microsleep follows seconds behind.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.question_text: How often should you stop and stretch on long highway trips, and what daily driving cap does the manual advise?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.teaching_text: Stepping out every two hours—or roughly one hundred miles—and capping days at eight hours keeps reaction speed sharp.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.question_text: Which four everyday driver habits cause both interstate crashes and phantom traffic jams?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.teaching_text: Slowing to gawk at opposite-side scenes, crowding bumpers, darting lanes, and zoning out ripple backward into miles of gridlock.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.question_text: How do empty gas tanks and skipped maintenance affect everyone else on an interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.teaching_text: One avoidable stall on a busy urban freeway pinches lanes and triggers secondary rear-end crashes behind the backup.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.question_text: On highways with two or more same-direction lanes, what does the Move Over Law require near flashing stopped work or emergency rigs?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.teaching_text: Putting a full empty lane buffer next to flashing responders, tow rigs, or utility trucks saves roadside lives.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.question_text: Does Move Over apply to left-median shoulders too, and when is slowing in your lane allowed instead of moving over?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.teaching_text: Vacate the lane nearest either shoulder, dropping speed carefully in place only when heavy traffic blocks a safe lane change.

sec10-card-sec10-R21.question_text: Which lane do you shift into when a flashing vehicle sits on the right shoulder versus the left median shoulder?
sec10-card-sec10-R21.teaching_text: Always move away from the flashing vehicle so the lane immediately beside its doors stays clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.question_text: Does Tennessee's Move Over protection extend to ordinary civilian cars and pickups stopped with hazard flashers blinking?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.teaching_text: Tennessee expanded Move Over so a family changing a flat tire with four-way hazards gets the exact same empty-lane protection.

sec10-card-sec10-R22.question_text: Which six categories of official and service fleets are protected under Tennessee's Move Over Law?
sec10-card-sec10-R22.teaching_text: Patrol cars, fire and ambulance units, utility and sanitation trucks, wreckers, TDOT HELP patrols, and road contractors all count.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.question_text: What are your immediate first two moves when your car loses power or blows a tire on an interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.teaching_text: Use remaining momentum promptly to clear live lanes onto the right shoulder or emergency bay and flip on hazards.

sec10-card-sec10-R23.question_text: How do you signal visibly that your broken-down vehicle needs assistance, and where should you wait?
sec10-card-sec10-R23.teaching_text: Popping the hood with a white cloth on the antenna signals distress clearly while waiting away from passing traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-R24.question_text: Why should families stay with a disabled vehicle instead of walking the interstate shoulder for help?
sec10-card-sec10-R24.teaching_text: Keep kids well back from pavement—on-duty officers not answering an urgent call stop routinely for occupied breakdowns.

sec10-card-sec10-R25.question_text: In which four major Tennessee metro areas do yellow TDOT HELP trucks patrol to assist stranded motorists?
sec10-card-sec10-R25.teaching_text: Tennessee's four largest urban freeway networks run dedicated yellow HELP response trucks to clear stalls and assist drivers.

sec10-card-sec10-R26.question_text: What authority do TDOT HELP operators hold over vehicles blocking lanes, and how must you treat their directions?
sec10-card-sec10-R26.teaching_text: HELP crews can relocate obstructing vehicles to restore safe flow, and drivers must follow their traffic directions just like officers.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.question_text: After an interstate crash with no serious injuries or fatalities, what does Tennessee law let you do with a drivable car?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.teaching_text: Leaving drivable cars sitting in seventy-mile-per-hour lanes invites deadly secondary crashes while everyone waits for police.

sec10-card-sec10-R27.question_text: How do Tennessee's stay-at-the-scene duty and TDOT shoulder signs work together after a minor wreck?
sec10-card-sec10-R27.teaching_text: Pulling onto the adjacent shoulder satisfies your legal duty to stay at the scene without blocking fast freeway lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.question_text: Which three actions must you never take after a serious or fatal crash?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.teaching_text: Moving spinal-injury victims risks paralysis, disturbing fatal scenes spoils investigations, and leaving any crash scene is a crime.

sec10-card-sec10-R28.question_text: Which core tire, power, safety, signaling, and document items belong in a suggested roadside emergency kit?
sec10-card-sec10-R28.teaching_text: Packing a good spare, jack, gauge, cables, flashlight, first-aid kit, extinguisher, three reflectors, papers, and phone covers common roadside emergencies.

sec10-card-sec10-R29.question_text: Which extra items should join your emergency kit for winter road trips versus hot summer drives?
sec10-card-sec10-R29.teaching_text: Add a blanket, small portable heater, ice scraper, and snow tires or chains in winter, plus drinking water in summer.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: Which two broad topics are covered in Section C of the Tennessee driver manual?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Written exam questions pull heavily from Section C, pairing personal crash-prevention habits with how to share lanes safely.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: Does your duty to learn traffic rules end once you earn a license, or how long does it last?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Traffic statutes and road designs evolve constantly, leaving every licensed driver responsible for staying current long after test day.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: How does a new driver turn written manual rules into automatic behind-the-wheel habits?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Reading rules once passes a quiz, whereas revisiting the manual while logging real miles locks safe instincts into muscle memory.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: What does aiming high in steering require you to do with your eyes?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Staring right over your front hood hides developing brake lights and lane blockages until smooth reactions are impossible.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: How should you use your eyes instead of staring at a single spot in traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Target fixation blinds you to side-street cars and mirrors, while constant gaze shifts track changing traffic smoothly.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: What spacing habit lets you get the big picture and judge real hazards around your car?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Riding another bumper blocks your forward sightline, whereas a full following gap reveals hazards around the entire traffic pack.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: Where must you keep open space around your car so you always leave yourself an out?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Boxing yourself in beside cars with zero front buffer traps you with nowhere to steer when sudden braking starts.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: Which three vehicle tools help you catch eye contact so drivers and pedestrians notice you?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Assuming another road user sees you is risky until signals, lights, or a brief horn tap confirm eye contact.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: Beyond signaling with horn and lights for eye contact, what should you confirm about nearby drivers and walkers?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Eye contact pairs with reading body language and wheel position so nobody steps or turns across your path unexpectedly.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: Which four ongoing actions define defensive driving before an obstacle or car becomes a crash?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Spotting trouble early and acting ahead of time beats relying on last-second panic braking.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: What should a defensive driver expect from other motorists while keeping their own driving consistent?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: Leaving margin for someone else's bad move while signaling predictable moves yourself keeps two mistakes from colliding.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: Which two attitudes toward fellow road users does the manual rank as the key to safe driving?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Treating lane merges and mistakes with patience defuses conflicts long before they turn into crashes or road rage.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: What financial and legal headaches can hit you even after a minor collision with zero injuries?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Even a fender-bender drains time and money through shop bills, citations, and multi-year insurance rate hikes.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: What assumption should you make about another driver's next move, and what should you keep ready?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Mentally rehearsing where you will brake or steer if a cross-street car pulls out shaves precious reaction time.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: Roughly what percentage of behind-the-wheel road information enters through a driver's eyes?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: Because nine-tenths of driving input is visual, glancing down at a screen or passenger leaves you practically blind.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: Which three mental distractions does the manual warn have zero place behind the wheel?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: Split attention slows hazard recognition just like physical impairment, turning routine traffic slowdowns into sudden emergencies.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: How many seconds—and roughly what city distance—ahead should a defensive driver aim their focus?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: Scanning roughly one city block ahead reveals slowing traffic early enough for smooth braking instead of hard swerves.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: Which three visual clues warn that a parked or stopped car is about to pull into your lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Spotting tailpipe vapor, glowing brake or reverse lamps, or front tires turned outward warns you before the bumper moves.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: What three things should you sweep for from side to side as you travel down a street?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Wide side-to-side scanning catches guide signs early and spots curb-side cars or pedestrians timing a move into your lane.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: Which hidden entrances, terrain features, and surface shifts require extra alertness on rural roads?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Country speeds meet blind hillcrests, concealed farm driveways, narrowing shoulders, and sudden pavement-to-gravel drop-offs.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: In what exact sequence should you look before entering an intersection, and why does that side come first?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: Cross traffic from your left travels in the nearest lane you cross first, making left-right-left essential before rolling out.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: How regularly should you monitor your rearview mirrors, and before what lateral move is a check mandatory?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Skipping mirror checks before moving laterally risks cutting right across a fast-closing car beside your rear quarter.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: Roughly how often should you flick a brief glance to your rearview mirror, and what are you checking for?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Quick ten-second mirror checks catch fast-closing cars or tailgaters early without pulling focus off the lane ahead.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: During which four specific maneuvers or road grades must you check traffic behind your car?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Sudden deceleration or steep downhill truck traffic behind you makes rear awareness critical before slowing, reversing, or shifting lanes.
sec14-card-sec14-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Lane changes, backing, hard braking, downgrades

visual_sync.text_span: Lane changes, backing, hard braking, downgrades

sec14-card-sec14-R09.question_text: What two details about surrounding vehicles let you make fast, safe choices when emergencies pop up?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.teaching_text: Knowing where nearby cars sit and how fast they are closing tells you instantly whether a lane is open.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: Why must you avoid lingering in another vehicle's blind spot?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Cruising beside another driver's rear pillar hides your car from their mirrors right when they decide to change lanes.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: How do you measure the two-second following rule using a roadside object?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Reaching the landmark before finishing one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two proves you are following too close to brake safely.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: To how many seconds should your following gap expand on fast interstates, behind large rigs, or in bad weather?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Slick pavement, highway speeds, and tall trailers blocking sightlines demand at least three to four seconds to react.
sec14-card-sec14-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Stretch gap three to four seconds

visual_sync.text_span: Stretch gap three to four seconds

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: What bad habit causes common rear-end crashes, and where besides normal travel should you leave extra stopped buffer?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: Keeping two seconds rolling plus extra stopped margin on hills, curves, and rail tracks protects against rollbacks and rear-end shoves.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: Which four directions around your car make up a complete defensive safety cushion?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Maintaining breathing room around all four sides guarantees an open lane or braking margin when traffic compresses.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: How should you clear a tailgater on a multi-lane road versus on a single-lane road?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Changing right or gently easing off speed where passing is legal invites an impatient tailgater around safely.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: Why must you never tap or slam your brakes suddenly to scare off a tailgater?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Brake-checking a close follower leaves zero reaction distance and practically guarantees getting slammed from behind.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.question_text: Which two smooth habits help the driver behind you maintain a safe following gap?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.teaching_text: Erratic speed swings and late blinkers surprise trailing drivers, while steady pacing and early signals give smooth warning.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.question_text: What is the real safety goal of communicating in traffic with drivers and pedestrians?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.teaching_text: Clear early signals remove guesswork so nearby motorists and walkers can adjust long before paths cross.
sec14-card-sec14-R10.must_match_memory_hook: Show moves early to avoid crashes

visual_sync.text_span: Show moves early to avoid crashes

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: Which direction changes require a turn signal, and does an apparently empty street let you skip signaling?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Signaling every turn, lane shift, ramp entry, and curb pull protects the unseen bike, walker, or car you missed.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.question_text: What restriction still applies when you speed up or slow down to manage space around your car?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.teaching_text: Finding an open traffic pocket never excuses exceeding the posted speed limit or impeding flow illegally.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: Where inside your lane should you position your car when meeting oncoming traffic on a two-lane road?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Easing slightly right of lane center opens crucial buffer space away from oncoming mirrors and centerline drifters.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.question_text: When splitting the difference between two hazards like parked cars and an oncoming semi, who gets extra space?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.teaching_text: A high-speed oncoming tractor-trailer carries far worse crash force than stationary parked cars, earning the wider margin.
sec14-card-sec14-F26.must_match_memory_hook: Favor extra room from deadlier hazards

visual_sync.text_span: Favor extra room from deadlier hazards

sec14-card-sec14-F27.question_text: How do you handle overtaking a bicyclist when an oncoming car will reach you at the same moment?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.teaching_text: Dealing with hazards one by one prevents squeezing between a vulnerable cyclist and oncoming steel.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.question_text: Which roadside cars and people need extra side clearance, and which age group needs the most?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.teaching_text: Car doors swing open and children dart into traffic without looking, demanding generous lateral room along curbs.

sec14-card-sec14-R18.question_text: What should you add when bushes, sun glare, or umbrellas block sightlines for you or others?
sec14-card-sec14-R18.teaching_text: If hedges or umbrellas hide you from a driver or walker, they can step or pull straight out unexpectedly.
sec14-card-sec14-R18.must_match_memory_hook: Add extra space around blind views

visual_sync.text_span: Add extra space around blind views

sec14-card-sec14-R19.question_text: How should you adjust space around drivers or walkers absorbed in phones, sightseeing, or children?
sec14-card-sec14-R19.teaching_text: Someone staring at a phone or turning toward kids in the back seat often drifts or steps out blindly.

sec14-card-sec14-R20.question_text: Which clues reveal a confused driver or pedestrian who needs extra space?
sec14-card-sec14-R20.teaching_text: Lost motorists hunting street signs brake or dive across lanes without warning when their turn suddenly appears.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.question_text: At least how many seconds of gap do you need to merge or change lanes, and how do you cross multiple lanes?
