sec14-card-sec14-F28.teaching_text: Slicing across multiple lanes in one sweep blindsides drivers in far lanes and triggers multi-car pileups.
sec14-card-sec14-F28.must_match_memory_hook: Four-second gap, one lane per move

visual_sync.text_span: Four-second gap, one lane per move

sec14-card-sec14-R13.question_text: What courteous move should you make on a multi-lane road when ramp traffic is trying to merge?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.teaching_text: Sliding into an open left lane clears the right lane cleanly so entering drivers do not run out of ramp.
sec14-card-sec14-R13.must_match_memory_hook: Move left to open merging space

visual_sync.text_span: Move left to open merging space

sec14-card-sec14-R15.question_text: What three traffic consequences can result from cutting across several lanes at once?
sec14-card-sec14-R15.teaching_text: Even if your bumper misses everyone, forcing startled drivers to swerve can cause secondary crashes behind you.
sec14-card-sec14-R15.must_match_memory_hook: Jams traffic, wrecks you or others

visual_sync.text_span: Jams traffic, wrecks you or others

sec14-card-sec14-F29.question_text: When must you stay out of an intersection even if the traffic light is green?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.teaching_text: Stopping mid-intersection or leaving your bumper overhanging cross lanes traps traffic and creates broadside crash hazards.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.question_text: Roughly how long does passing at fifty-five miles per hour take, and may you break the speed limit to pass?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.teaching_text: Test questions bust the myth that you may briefly exceed posted limits while passing on a two-lane road.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.question_text: What visual check in your rearview mirror tells you it is safe to pull back in after passing a car?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.teaching_text: Seeing both headlights centered in your inside mirror confirms you have cleared the passed car's front bumper.

sec14-card-sec14-R16.question_text: How many vehicles should you generally pass at once, and what space ahead must exist before starting?
sec14-card-sec14-R16.teaching_text: Leapfrogging strings of cars without a guaranteed return pocket traps you head-on when oncoming traffic appears.
sec14-card-sec14-R16.must_match_memory_hook: One vehicle with return gap open

visual_sync.text_span: One vehicle with return gap open

sec14-card-sec14-R17.question_text: Why must you never count on the driver you are passing to create space for your return?
sec14-card-sec14-R17.teaching_text: Distracted or stubborn drivers may hold steady pace, so you need clear space behind your bumper before moving right.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.question_text: How should you react when another driver misjudges a pass and runs low on room?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.teaching_text: Closing the gap to punish a reckless passer risks dragging yourself straight into a multi-car head-on wreck.

sec14-card-sec14-R21.question_text: At which three road features should you slow down and expect abrupt lane merges?
sec14-card-sec14-R21.teaching_text: Drivers running out of pavement at lane drops or dodging debris often swerve over before checking blind spots.

sec14-card-sec14-R22.question_text: Which three roadside situations can push a neighboring driver abruptly into your lane?
sec14-card-sec14-R22.teaching_text: Anticipating neighbors moving over for flashing lights, cones, or ramp cars keeps you out of pinch-point sideswipes.
sec14-card-sec14-R22.must_match_memory_hook: Other mergers, work zones, emergency vehicles

visual_sync.text_span: Other mergers, work zones, emergency vehicles

sec14-card-sec14-R23.question_text: Roughly what share of annual traffic fatalities does the manual link to aggressive driving behaviors?
sec14-card-sec14-R23.teaching_text: Nearly two-thirds of yearly road deaths trace back to aggressive moves like red-light running, tailgating, and right-side passing.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.question_text: Which behaviors—from following distance and horn use to extreme violence—count as aggressive driving?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.teaching_text: Aggression escalates rapidly from impatient tailgating, cutting people off, and rude gestures into criminal violence.

sec14-card-sec14-R24.question_text: How are police departments and auto insurers responding to aggressive drivers?
sec14-card-sec14-R24.teaching_text: Aggressive citations bring heavy enforcement penalties alongside steep insurance surcharges or policy cancellation.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.question_text: What three emotional and attention rules keep you from escalating a road-rage confrontation?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.teaching_text: Even glaring back or tapping the horn feeds a confrontation, whereas calm eyes forward starve road rage instantly.

sec14-card-sec14-R25.question_text: Which five everyday driving habits keep you out of road-rage triggers?
sec14-card-sec14-R25.teaching_text: Driving within limits, leaving buffer room, and passing only when necessary prevents triggering hostile drivers around you.
sec14-card-sec14-R25.must_match_memory_hook: Relaxed, lawful speed, space, needed passes

visual_sync.text_span: Relaxed, lawful speed, space, needed passes

sec14-card-sec14-F35.question_text: How should you respond around an angry driver instead of taking bad traffic behavior personally?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.teaching_text: Backing off and refusing to take rude driving personally keeps an unstable motorist safely away from your car.

sec14-card-sec14-R27.question_text: What does the manual warn about a motorist who habitually gets angry behind the wheel?
sec14-card-sec14-R27.teaching_text: Chronic behind-the-wheel anger clouds judgment until changing that mindset becomes the only way to prevent a wreck.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.question_text: Where should you drive if another motorist starts following you aggressively?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.teaching_text: Leading a hostile driver home isolates you, while a police station or busy public place brings immediate witnesses and help.
sec14-card-sec14-F36.must_match_memory_hook: Head to police or public help

visual_sync.text_span: Head to police or public help

sec14-card-sec14-R26.question_text: What detail should you note and what action should you take if someone harasses you in traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-R26.teaching_text: Giving dispatchers an accurate license plate lets officers intercept a dangerous driver rather than engaging them yourself.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.question_text: Does bad weather cause most traffic collisions, or in what weather do most crashes actually occur?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.teaching_text: Sunny skies breed complacency and higher speeds, catching drivers off guard on test questions expecting snow or fog.
sec15-card-sec15-F01.must_match_memory_hook: Most crashes happen in clear weather

visual_sync.text_span: Most crashes happen in clear weather

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: How do many motorists react right before an impending crash, and why is that reaction wrong?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.teaching_text: Panicking and doing nothing surrenders control when steering or braking can almost always dodge or soften the impact.
sec15-card-sec15-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Never freeze; act to reduce impact

visual_sync.text_span: Never freeze; act to reduce impact

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: What are the three physical actions a driver can use to avoid an impending collision?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.teaching_text: Remembering all three evasive tools prevents locking onto brakes alone when steering around or accelerating clears danger.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: Why should you check your vehicle owner's manual regarding your car's braking system?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.teaching_text: Knowing before an emergency whether your car carries antilock brakes ensures you apply the right pedal technique.
sec15-card-sec15-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Know how your antilock system stops

visual_sync.text_span: Know how your antilock system stops

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: How should you use the brake pedal during a sudden emergency stop with antilock brakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.teaching_text: Lifting your foot when the antilock pedal pushes back shuts off computerized braking and stretches stopping distance.
sec15-card-sec15-F04.must_match_memory_hook: Stomp firmly and hold steady pressure

visual_sync.text_span: Stomp firmly and hold steady pressure

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: How hard should you press the pedal in an emergency stop when your car lacks antilock brakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.teaching_text: Threshold braking delivers maximum stopping power without locking non-antilock tires into an uncontrollable slide.
sec15-card-sec15-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Press hard just short of lockup

visual_sync.text_span: Press hard just short of lockup

sec15-card-sec15-F06.question_text: What pedal action restores rolling grip if your wheels lock up without antilock brakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.teaching_text: Releasing pressure lets locked tires roll and regain traction before you reapply firm braking repeatedly until stopped.
sec15-card-sec15-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Ease off briefly, then squeeze again

visual_sync.text_span: Ease off briefly, then squeeze again

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: How does steering control during hard emergency braking differ with antilock brakes versus without them?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.teaching_text: Rolling tires steer where pointed, whereas locked non-antilock wheels slide straight ahead regardless of steering input.
sec15-card-sec15-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Antilock keeps steering; locked wheels slide

visual_sync.text_span: Antilock keeps steering; locked wheels slide

sec15-card-sec15-F22.question_text: Why must you never pump an antilock brake pedal when you feel rapid pulsing underfoot?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.teaching_text: That rapid vibration means antilock valves are already cycling brakes far faster than any human foot can pump.
sec15-card-sec15-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Never pump; system pulses faster automatically

visual_sync.text_span: Never pump; system pulses faster automatically

sec15-card-sec15-R13.question_text: What happens if rattle or vibration startles you into easing off an antilock brake pedal?
sec15-card-sec15-R13.teaching_text: Startled drivers who lift off noisy pulsing pedals throw away the antilock system's emergency braking advantage.
sec15-card-sec15-R13.must_match_memory_hook: Easing off ruins antilock stopping power

visual_sync.text_span: Easing off ruins antilock stopping power

sec15-card-sec15-F24.question_text: Does having antilock brakes justify following closer or driving more aggressively?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.teaching_text: Antilock brakes preserve steering control during stops, yet they cannot defy physics when speed or tailgating erases space.
sec15-card-sec15-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Never drive more aggressively with antilock

visual_sync.text_span: Never drive more aggressively with antilock

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: Why should you steer around an obstacle rather than rely on braking alone when stopping room runs short?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.teaching_text: At highway speeds stopping distance stretches far past swerving distance, making controlled steering your fastest escape.
sec15-card-sec15-F08.must_match_memory_hook: Cars turn faster than they stop

visual_sync.text_span: Cars turn faster than they stop

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: Where on the steering wheel should your hands sit for quick evasive steering and airbag safety?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Holding nine and three gives balanced leverage for sharp maneuvers while keeping forearms clear of deploying airbags.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: How do your right and left hands move on the wheel during a quick evasive turn to the left?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.teaching_text: Swinging the right hand from three toward nine while sliding the left low keeps firm two-handed control.
sec15-card-sec15-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Right swings across; left slides low

visual_sync.text_span: Right swings across; left slides low

sec15-card-sec15-R03.question_text: What steering sequence brings your car straight into the lane after swerving left past a hazard?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.teaching_text: Prompt counter-steering back into your lane and straightening smoothly stops the car from shooting off the opposite shoulder.
sec15-card-sec15-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Steer right, straighten left, reset hands

visual_sync.text_span: Steer right, straighten left, reset hands

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: Why must you stay poised to steer immediately after dodging an initial road hazard?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: Overcorrecting or relaxing after clearing the first obstacle sends drivers spinning into oncoming lanes or roadside trees.
sec15-card-sec15-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Stay controlled to prevent secondary crashes

visual_sync.text_span: Stay controlled to prevent secondary crashes

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: What advantage do antilock brakes provide when you must swerve and slow down simultaneously?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Because antilock sensors stop wheel lockup, you can hold hard brake pressure while steering cleanly around trouble.
sec15-card-sec15-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Steer and brake together without skidding

visual_sync.text_span: Steer and brake together without skidding

sec15-card-sec15-F12.question_text: In what order must you handle the brake pedal and steering wheel for a quick turn without antilock brakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.teaching_text: Trying to yank the wheel while non-antilock brakes stay clamped locks front tires so the car plows straight.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.question_text: How does braking right before releasing to turn help a car without antilock brakes corner faster?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.teaching_text: Brief straight-line braking cuts speed and presses weight onto front steering tires right before you release and turn.
sec15-card-sec15-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Braking shifts grip onto front tires

visual_sync.text_span: Braking shifts grip onto front tires

sec15-card-sec15-F13.question_text: What two mistakes cause front tires to lose steering bite and plow straight forward?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.teaching_text: Easing off locked brakes and avoiding extreme wheel angles restores front-tire rolling grip so the car actually turns.
sec15-card-sec15-F13.must_match_memory_hook: Locked front brakes or over-cranked steering

visual_sync.text_span: Locked front brakes or over-cranked steering

sec15-card-sec15-F14.question_text: When forced to choose between leaving the roadway and hitting an oncoming vehicle head-on, which is safer?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.teaching_text: Head-on collisions combine both vehicles' speeds into catastrophic force, making controlled off-road escape far more survivable.
sec15-card-sec15-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Drive off-road rather than hit head-on

visual_sync.text_span: Drive off-road rather than hit head-on

sec15-card-sec15-F15.question_text: In what crash setup is speeding up the safest choice, and what should follow once clear?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.teaching_text: When space ahead is open and another car is closing on your side or rear, brisk acceleration clears impact.
sec15-card-sec15-F15.must_match_memory_hook: Accelerate past side or rear hits

visual_sync.text_span: Accelerate past side or rear hits

sec15-card-sec15-F23.question_text: What severe danger comes from jerking the steering wheel violently during an emergency?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.teaching_text: Violent steering snaps weight sideways, flipping top-heavy vehicles or flinging cars into poles and oncoming lanes.
sec15-card-sec15-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Jerking triggers rollovers or off-road wrecks

visual_sync.text_span: Jerking triggers rollovers or off-road wrecks

sec15-card-sec15-R14.question_text: How do you combine antilock braking and steering all the way past a sudden obstacle?
sec15-card-sec15-R14.teaching_text: Keep firm brake pressure while guiding the car around the obstacle and continuing into a safe lane spot.
sec15-card-sec15-R14.must_match_memory_hook: Hold brake, steer past to safety

visual_sync.text_span: Hold brake, steer past to safety

sec15-card-sec15-R15.question_text: Where and at what speed does the manual suggest practicing antilock panic stops and swerves?
sec15-card-sec15-R15.teaching_text: Practicing twenty-mile-per-hour hard stops around a harmless cardboard box in an open curb-free lot removes first-time pedal shock.
sec15-card-sec15-R15.must_match_memory_hook: Empty lot around twenty miles hourly

visual_sync.text_span: Empty lot around twenty miles hourly

sec15-card-sec15-F16.question_text: Which season brings the highest risk of deer collisions, and what two seasonal triggers cause it?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.teaching_text: Fall breeding and hunting activity push deer across highways far more often than calmer summer or winter months.
sec15-card-sec15-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Autumn mating and hunting stir deer

visual_sync.text_span: Autumn mating and hunting stir deer

sec15-card-sec15-F17.question_text: Which animal accounts for the most dangerous and expensive wildlife collisions on highways?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.teaching_text: Adult deer stand tall enough to smash over hoods into windshields, causing severe injuries and heavy vehicle damage.
sec15-card-sec15-F17.must_match_memory_hook: Deer cause costliest, deadliest animal crashes

visual_sync.text_span: Deer cause costliest, deadliest animal crashes

sec15-card-sec15-F18.question_text: At what two times of day and near which two landscape features should you watch hardest for deer?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.teaching_text: Low twilight visibility coincides right when deer leave wooded cover and stream banks to feed near roadsides.
sec15-card-sec15-F18.must_match_memory_hook: Dusk and dawn near woods, water

visual_sync.text_span: Dusk and dawn near woods, water

sec15-card-sec15-F19.question_text: What should you expect immediately whenever a single deer crosses or stands near the road?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.teaching_text: Accelerating right after one deer clears the lane often hits the second or third herd member bolting behind it.
sec15-card-sec15-F19.must_match_memory_hook: One deer means others trail close

visual_sync.text_span: One deer means others trail close

sec15-card-sec15-R05.question_text: Are animal collisions limited to autumn nights and deer, or when and with what animals can they happen?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.teaching_text: Dogs, rabbits, opossums, and daytime deer can dart onto pavement year-round even outside peak autumn twilight.
sec15-card-sec15-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Any animal, any season, any hour

visual_sync.text_span: Any animal, any season, any hour

sec15-card-sec15-R06.question_text: Has any device or barrier proven completely foolproof at keeping deer and wildlife off highways?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.teaching_text: Relying on hood whistles or roadside fencing fails because nothing keeps wild animals completely off roadways.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.question_text: What three habits—using signs, scanning, and nighttime lighting—help you spot deer before they jump out?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.teaching_text: Using high beams whenever oncoming lanes are empty lights ditches far earlier in marked deer-crossing corridors.
sec15-card-sec15-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Heed signs, scan wide, high beams

visual_sync.text_span: Heed signs, scan wide, high beams

sec15-card-sec15-R08.question_text: What glowing clue along dark roadsides reveals a deer standing near the pavement?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.teaching_text: Two tiny points of reflected eye shine in roadside brush appear long before the animal's dark coat shows up.
sec15-card-sec15-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Headlight beams reflecting off deer eyes

visual_sync.text_span: Headlight beams reflecting off deer eyes

sec15-card-sec15-R09.question_text: Which three steps should you take when you spot an animal ahead with time to react?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.teaching_text: Tapping brakes flashes rear warning lamps for trailing cars while slowing and sounding the horn urges the animal clear.
sec15-card-sec15-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Slow down, tap brakes, honk horn

visual_sync.text_span: Slow down, tap brakes, honk horn

sec15-card-sec15-R10.question_text: Why can flashing your headlights at a deer in the roadway backfire?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.teaching_text: Deer fixate on bright beams, so strobing headlights often locks them motionless right in your lane.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.question_text: How firmly should you brake for an animal when your mirror shows nobody following closely behind?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.teaching_text: With clear space behind you, strong straight-line braking cuts impact speed rapidly while avoiding a sideways skid.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.question_text: Why must you hold your lane rather than swerve when striking an animal cannot be avoided?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.teaching_text: Swerving at highway speed trades a survivable bumper strike for rolling into trees, ditches, or oncoming traffic.
sec15-card-sec15-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Never swerve; stay straight on pavement

visual_sync.text_span: Never swerve; stay straight on pavement

sec15-card-sec15-F21.question_text: Whom must you notify after a collision with a deer or livestock?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.teaching_text: Large carcasses block dark lanes for trailing motorists, and insurance or accident laws require an official police report.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.question_text: What courteous step should you take if you accidentally strike a household pet near homes?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.teaching_text: Letting nearby owners know promptly gives an injured pet a chance at care instead of leaving families searching.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.question_text: What single root cause drives most traffic collisions, led by which three driver mistakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.teaching_text: Mechanical failures are rare compared with human speeding, wandering focus, and panicked evasive moves.
sec15-card-sec15-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Human error; speed, inattention, bad swerves

visual_sync.text_span: Human error; speed, inattention, bad swerves

sec15-card-sec15-F26.question_text: Which three connected elements make up the highway safety system?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.teaching_text: Neglecting personal alertness, car maintenance, or changing road conditions breaks the safety triangle behind most wrecks.

sec15-card-sec15-R17.question_text: Which three commitments separate a responsible driver from a careless one?
sec15-card-sec15-R17.teaching_text: Safe driving starts before turning the key through mechanical upkeep, lawful habits, and courtesy in traffic.
sec15-card-sec15-R17.must_match_memory_hook: Maintain vehicle, obey laws, respect others

visual_sync.text_span: Maintain vehicle, obey laws, respect others

sec15-card-sec15-R18.question_text: Roughly how many reported Tennessee crashes each year does the manual trace to poor driving habits?
sec15-card-sec15-R18.teaching_text: Seeing one hundred sixty thousand preventable state crashes yearly proves routine bad habits cause massive real-world damage.
sec15-card-sec15-R18.must_match_memory_hook: One hundred sixty thousand yearly crashes

visual_sync.text_span: One hundred sixty thousand yearly crashes

sec15-card-sec15-R19.question_text: Which four personal conditions show a motorist is physically and mentally fit to drive?
sec15-card-sec15-R19.teaching_text: Checking eyesight, sleep, sobriety, and physical plus emotional steadiness prevents impaired reactions before leaving the driveway.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.question_text: How can everyday states like worry, frustration, fatigue, anger, or a head cold affect your driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.teaching_text: Slower reflexes and distracted thoughts from a bad mood or common cold degrade safety much faster than drivers realize.
sec15-card-sec15-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Everyday moods and colds impair safety

visual_sync.text_span: Everyday moods and colds impair safety

sec15-card-sec15-R26.question_text: What should you do when a stiff neck, coughing spell, or sore leg makes physical control uncomfortable?
sec15-card-sec15-R26.teaching_text: A stiff neck stops blind-spot head checks and a sore leg slows braking, making a substitute driver safer.

sec15-card-sec15-F33.question_text: Under what two medical conditions may a Tennessee resident with epilepsy hold driving privileges?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.teaching_text: Test questions check the exact six-month seizure-free period paired with ongoing physician supervision.
sec15-card-sec15-F33.must_match_memory_hook: Doctor's care plus six seizure-free months

visual_sync.text_span: Doctor's care plus six seizure-free months

sec15-card-sec15-R27.question_text: When must a driver taking insulin for diabetes stay out from behind the wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-R27.teaching_text: Skipping a meal or feeling shaky risks sudden diabetic shock or blackout mid-traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-R28.question_text: Which heart, blood-pressure, or circulation patients must not drive, and whom should treated heart patients consult?
sec15-card-sec15-R28.teaching_text: Fainting or cardiac episodes at highway speed endanger everyone, requiring clear physician guidance before driving.
sec15-card-sec15-R28.must_match_memory_hook: No blackout risk; consult your doctor

visual_sync.text_span: No blackout risk; consult your doctor

sec15-card-sec15-F34.question_text: How should you handle strong anger before driving, and how do impatient drivers beat the urge to speed?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.teaching_text: Leaving early removes clock pressure so routine red lights and slow traffic stop tempting risky speed.
sec15-card-sec15-F34.must_match_memory_hook: Cool off first; leave extra time

visual_sync.text_span: Cool off first; leave extra time

sec15-card-sec15-R29.question_text: Can years of driving experience make someone safe behind the wheel when buzzed on alcohol or drugs?
sec15-card-sec15-R29.teaching_text: Skill never overrides chemical slowing of vision, judgment, and brake reflexes from alcohol or drugs.

sec15-card-sec15-R20.question_text: How does darkness affect every driver's eyesight, and what oncoming light adds extra trouble?
sec15-card-sec15-R20.teaching_text: Even sharp daytime vision loses contrast and depth after dark while oncoming headlights temporarily dazzle eyes.
sec15-card-sec15-R20.must_match_memory_hook: Darkness dims everyone; glare blinds worse

visual_sync.text_span: Darkness dims everyone; glare blinds worse

sec15-card-sec15-R21.question_text: What sensible habit should you adopt if you have difficulty seeing clearly at night?
sec15-card-sec15-R21.teaching_text: Planning errands in daylight and slowing with extra caution on unavoidable night trips cuts glare-related crashes.

sec15-card-sec15-R22.question_text: During which two highway maneuvers does judging vehicle speed and distance matter most?
sec15-card-sec15-R22.teaching_text: Misjudging closing speed on an expressway merge or a two-lane pass creates high-speed sideswipes or head-on collisions.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.question_text: How often does the manual recommend having an eye specialist examine your vision?
